requirements.section: Intro paragraphs, Glossary, and Sign in
requirements.requirement: The product names itself Silicon Present in the web and in the CLI.
requirements.quote: the entire Silicon Present
requirements.acceptance: A signed-out browser opening the web's / sees the product named 'Silicon Present' (page title and landing page), and `present --help` names 'Silicon Present' in its first line; neither calls the product by any other name.

requirements.section: Intro paragraphs, Glossary, and Sign in
requirements.requirement: The web editor is served at present.teamofsilicons.com.
requirements.quote: the web editor at `present.teamofsilicons.com`
requirements.acceptance: Production smoke test: a signed-out browser at https://present.teamofsilicons.com/ gets the Silicon Present landing page over HTTPS; after c:ada signs in through Silicon Accounts she lands back on https://present.teamofsilicons.com/decks, and /decks/<id> opens the editor on that same host.

requirements.section: Intro paragraphs, Glossary, and Sign in
requirements.requirement: The command-line tool is invoked as `present`.
requirements.quote: the `present` CLI
requirements.acceptance: Building/installing crates/present-cli yields one executable named `present` on PATH; `present --help` exits 0 and lists its commands (login, new, read, render, comment, start, ...), and every step of the CLI end-to-end suite runs through that `present` binary.

requirements.section: Intro paragraphs, Glossary, and Sign in
requirements.requirement: A Carbon can make slides in the web editor: create a deck, add slides and fill them.
requirements.quote: Carbons and Silicons make, present and comment on slides together
requirements.acceptance: c:ada signs in on the web, creates a deck from /decks, and in /decks/<id> adds three slides and types a title on each; after a reload the three slides show with their titles, and GET /v1/decks/<id>/content?format=json returns them in order.

requirements.section: Intro paragraphs, Glossary, and Sign in
requirements.requirement: A Silicon can build a complete deck entirely by itself through the `present` CLI, with no Carbon and no web step.
requirements.quote: a Silicon can build a whole deck itself, through the CLI
requirements.acceptance: Signed in only as si:designer (`present login --slt-stdin`) and with no Carbon involved, the Silicon runs `present new 'Q4'`, several `present slide add <deck> --layout ... --title ...`, `present add text|image|shape|table|chart|video|html ...`, `present slide notes <deck> 1 '...'` and `present theme <deck> Ivory`; `present read <deck>` then shows every slide, all seven element kinds, the notes and the theme it set, and GET /v1/decks/<id> shows si:designer as owner and creator.

requirements.section: Intro paragraphs, Glossary, and Sign in
requirements.requirement: Building a deck through the CLI takes a Silicon no more effort than building it in the web editor takes a Carbon: each step is a single `present` command with plain inputs.
requirements.quote: as easily as a Carbon does in the web editor
requirements.acceptance: The same deck is built twice: by c:ada in the web editor (new deck, slide with a layout, text box, image, shape, table, chart, speaker notes, theme) and by si:designer with `present`. The Silicon uses no more `present` commands than c:ada used editor actions; each command is found from `present --help` / `present <command> --help` and takes only text, numbers, file paths or ids/numbers printed by earlier commands; no step needs Yjs, base64 or resending the whole deck; and `present read` shows both decks with the same content.

requirements.section: Intro paragraphs, Glossary, and Sign in
requirements.requirement: Silicons use Silicon Present first-hand: a Silicon signs in as itself and everything it does is attributed to its own si:id, never to a Carbon.
requirements.quote: Silicons are first-hand users
requirements.acceptance: si:designer signs in with its own Silicon Accounts short-lived token (`silicon-accounts login --app present -q | present login --slt-stdin`); `present whoami --json` shows kind silicon and id si:designer; after it creates and edits a deck, GET /v1/decks/<id> shows owner and creator si:designer and `present versions <deck>` lists si:designer as the author, with no Carbon named anywhere.

requirements.section: Intro paragraphs, Glossary, and Sign in
requirements.requirement: A Carbon can present a deck from the web, including a deck a Silicon made.
requirements.quote: Carbons will mostly review and present them
requirements.acceptance: si:designer builds a three-slide deck with `present` and shares it with c:ada as viewer (`present share <deck> c:ada --role viewer`); c:ada opens /decks/<id>/present in the web, slide 1 fills the screen, and the arrow key moves through slides 2 and 3 in order, each showing the content `present read <deck>` lists for it.

requirements.section: Intro paragraphs, Glossary, and Sign in
requirements.requirement: A Silicon can present a deck through the CLI.
requirements.quote: Carbons and Silicons make, present and comment on slides together
requirements.acceptance:
si:designer runs `present start ` (it prints a presentation id and a follow link), then `present next` and `present goto 3`; GET /v1/presentations/

reports slide 3; after `present stop`, the presentation's live stream (GET /v1/presentations/

/live) sends `ended`.

requirements.section: Intro paragraphs, Glossary, and Sign in
requirements.requirement: A Carbon can comment on slides from the web.
requirements.quote: Carbons and Silicons make, present and comment on slides together
requirements.acceptance: c:ada, commenter on a deck, opens /decks/<id>, places a comment on slide 2 and posts 'Tighten this'; after a reload the thread shows on slide 2, and GET /v1/decks/<id>/threads returns it with author c:ada.

requirements.section: Intro paragraphs, Glossary, and Sign in
requirements.requirement: A Silicon can comment on slides through the CLI.
requirements.quote: Carbons and Silicons make, present and comment on slides together
requirements.acceptance: si:designer, commenter on a deck, runs `present comment <deck> --slide 2 'Numbers updated'`; `present comments <deck>` lists the new thread under slide 2 with author si:designer, and GET /v1/decks/<id>/threads returns it.

requirements.section: Intro paragraphs, Glossary, and Sign in
requirements.requirement: A Carbon in the web editor and a Silicon in the CLI make the same deck together: each one's edits reach the other.
requirements.quote: Carbons and Silicons make, present and comment on slides together
requirements.acceptance: c:ada shares her deck with si:designer as editor; si:designer runs `present add text <deck> 1 'From the Silicon'` and the text appears on slide 1 in c:ada's /decks/<id>; c:ada types 'From the Carbon' into a text box on slide 2 and `present read <deck>` then shows it on slide 2; the deck holds both edits.

requirements.section: Intro paragraphs, Glossary, and Sign in
requirements.requirement: Carbons and Silicons comment in the same threads: a reply from either one shows up in the thread for the other.
requirements.quote: Carbons and Silicons make, present and comment on slides together
requirements.acceptance: c:ada comments on slide 2 in /decks/<id>; si:designer finds the thread with `present comments <deck>` and runs `present reply <thread> 'Done'`; c:ada's thread on slide 2 shows the reply from si:designer. Then si:designer starts a thread with `present comment <deck> --deck 'Ready for review'`, c:ada replies in the web, and `present comments <deck> --json` shows her reply in that thread.

requirements.section: Intro paragraphs, Glossary, and Sign in
requirements.requirement: Carbons and Silicons present to each other: a Carbon in the web can follow a presentation a Silicon gives through the CLI.
requirements.quote: Carbons and Silicons make, present and comment on slides together
requirements.acceptance: si:designer runs `present start <deck>` and hands the printed follow link to c:ada (viewer on the deck); c:ada opens /p/<presentation> and sees slide 1; si:designer runs `present next`, then `present goto 3`, and c:ada's page moves to slide 2 and then slide 3 without her doing anything.

requirements.section: Intro paragraphs, Glossary, and Sign in
requirements.requirement: Silicon Present has the features people expect from Google Slides or PowerPoint.
requirements.quote: It has everything people expect from Google Slides or PowerPoint.
requirements.acceptance: Parity smoke test (each feature's detailed checks live with its own section): in the web editor c:ada creates a deck, picks a layout and a theme, adds text, an image, a shape, a table, a chart and a video, reorders slides in the slide sorter, writes speaker notes, undoes a change, presents it, and downloads it as .pptx (GET /v1/decks/<id>/export?format=pptx); every step works inside Silicon Present and the .pptx opens in LibreOffice with the same slides.

requirements.section: Intro paragraphs, Glossary, and Sign in
requirements.requirement: Besides ordinary elements, the same slide can hold live HTML.
requirements.quote: Slides can also hold live HTML
requirements.acceptance: si:designer runs `present add text <deck> 1 'Title'` and `present add html <deck> 1 --html w.html --css w.css --js w.js --x 960 --y 200 --w 800 --h 600`; `present read <deck>` and GET /v1/decks/<id>/content?format=json list both elements on slide 1 (kinds text and html), and c:ada's /decks/<id> shows both on the slide.

requirements.section: Intro paragraphs, Glossary, and Sign in
requirements.requirement: HTML on a slide renders: its markup and CSS are drawn on the slide the way a browser draws a web page.
requirements.quote: live HTML that renders, animates and runs JS
requirements.acceptance:
si:designer adds an html element with `

Hello

` and CSS `.t{color:#c00;font-size:120px}`; in c:ada's /decks/ Playwright finds a visible red 'Hello' heading inside the element's frame, and `present render 1 -o s1.png` shows red 'Hello' text inside the element's box.

requirements.section: Intro paragraphs, Glossary, and Sign in
requirements.requirement: HTML on a slide animates: its CSS and JS animations play on the slide.
requirements.quote: live HTML that renders, animates and runs JS
requirements.acceptance: si:designer adds an html element whose CSS moves a box from left:0 to left:600px over 3 s; in c:ada's /decks/<id> Playwright reads the box's position inside the element's frame at about 0.5 s and 2.5 s and finds it has moved; `present render <deck> 1 --at 500` and `present render <deck> 1 --at 2500` give images with the box in different places.

requirements.section: Intro paragraphs, Glossary, and Sign in
requirements.requirement: HTML on a slide runs its JS.
requirements.quote: live HTML that renders, animates and runs JS
requirements.acceptance: si:designer adds an html element whose JS sets `document.body.textContent = 'ran ' + (1 + 1)`; c:ada's /decks/<id> shows 'ran 2' inside the element's frame, and `present render <deck> 1 -o s1.png` shows 'ran 2' in the element's box.

requirements.section: Intro paragraphs, Glossary, and Sign in
requirements.requirement: A slide can be anything a web page can be: an HTML element can cover the whole slide and behave as a full, interactive web page.
requirements.quote: so a slide can be anything a web page can be
requirements.acceptance: si:designer adds an html element at 0,0,1920,1080 holding a canvas drawing, an inline SVG and a button whose click handler increments a counter; in c:ada's /decks/<id> and /decks/<id>/present the element covers the whole slide, the canvas and SVG are drawn, and clicking the button in present mode increments the counter, just as the same HTML does when opened directly in a browser.

requirements.section: Intro paragraphs, Glossary, and Sign in
requirements.requirement: A Carbon can review a deck a Silicon made: it opens in the web with every slide and element the Silicon built.
requirements.quote: Carbons will mostly review and present them
requirements.acceptance: si:designer builds a deck with `present` (text, image, shape, table, chart and html elements over several slides) and shares it with c:ada as commenter; c:ada opens /decks/<id> and sees every slide in the order `present read <deck>` lists them, each element where `present read` places it, and each slide looking the same as `present render <deck> <n>`.

requirements.section: Intro paragraphs, Glossary, and Sign in
requirements.requirement: Commenting is effortless for Carbons in the web.
requirements.quote: commenting has to be effortless for Carbons
requirements.acceptance: c:ada, commenter on a deck, opens /decks/<id> and clicks once on a point of slide 2: a comment box opens right at that point with no button or menu first; she types 'Too busy' and submits; GET /v1/decks/<id>/threads shows a new thread by c:ada anchored to that point of slide 2 (kind point), and it shows there on the slide.

requirements.section: Intro paragraphs, Glossary, and Sign in
requirements.requirement: Every deck, however it was made (web editor, CLI or an opened file) and by whom, is a comfortable place for a Silicon to work through the CLI.
requirements.quote: every deck has to be a comfortable place for a Silicon to work
requirements.acceptance: c:ada builds one deck in the web editor and opens a .pptx as a second one (POST /v1/imports from the web), and shares both with si:designer as editor. On each, si:designer runs `present read <deck> --comments` (plain readable text of every slide, element, position and note, no raw Yjs or base64), `present render <deck> 1 -o s1.png` (a non-blank image), `present replace <deck> 1 --find '<passage>' --replace '<new>'` (only that passage changes) and `present comment <deck> --slide 1 '...'`; every command succeeds and c:ada sees the edit and the comment in the web.

requirements.section: Intro paragraphs, Glossary, and Sign in
requirements.requirement: Everything Silicon Present shows calls a Carbon a 'Carbon'.
requirements.quote: Every human account is called a carbon.
requirements.acceptance: Crawl every web page signed out and signed in (/, /sign-in, /decks, /decks/<id>, /decks/<id>/history, /decks/<id>/present, /decks/<id>/presenter, /p/<presentation>, /transfers, /trash), run `present --help` and `present <command> --help` for every command, and provoke common errors through the API and the CLI (sign_in_required, 403, 404): every reference to a Carbon uses the word 'Carbon', and the strings 'human' and 'user account' appear nowhere.

requirements.section: Intro paragraphs, Glossary, and Sign in
requirements.requirement: Everything Silicon Present shows calls a Silicon a 'Silicon'.
requirements.quote: Our AI Agent account is referred to as a Silicon.
requirements.acceptance: In the same crawl of web pages, CLI help and API/CLI errors as GLOS-01, every reference to a Silicon uses the word 'Silicon', and 'AI agent', 'agent account' and 'bot' never name a Silicon.

requirements.section: Intro paragraphs, Glossary, and Sign in
requirements.requirement: A single presentation is called a deck wherever the web and the CLI name it.
requirements.quote: `Deck` - A single presentation in Silicon Present.
requirements.acceptance: The web lists presentations at /decks and its headings and actions say 'deck' (for example when creating a new one); CLI help names what `present new`, `present list` and `present read` act on a 'deck' (`<deck>`); no web page or CLI help calls a deck a 'file', 'document' or 'project'.

requirements.section: Intro paragraphs, Glossary, and Sign in
requirements.requirement: A deck is made of slides, each one page, kept in a set order.
requirements.quote: `Slide` - One page of a deck.
requirements.acceptance: si:designer adds slides titled A, B and C with `present slide add`; GET /v1/decks/<id>/content?format=json returns slides A, B, C in that order, `present read <deck>` prints them as slides 1-3, and c:ada's /decks/<id> shows three pages in the same order; after `present slide move <deck> 3 --first` all three show C, A, B.

requirements.section: Intro paragraphs, Glossary, and Sign in
requirements.requirement: Text can be placed on a slide as an element.
requirements.quote: `Element` - Anything placed on a slide: text, an image, a shape, a table, a chart, a video, or an HTML element.
requirements.acceptance: si:designer runs `present add text <deck> 1 'Revenue grew 40%'`; GET /v1/decks/<id>/content?format=json has a kind text element on slide 1 with that text and c:ada's /decks/<id> shows it on the slide; a text box c:ada adds in the editor appears in `present read <deck>` as a text element.

requirements.section: Intro paragraphs, Glossary, and Sign in
requirements.requirement: An image can be placed on a slide as an element.
requirements.quote: `Element` - Anything placed on a slide: text, an image, a shape, a table, a chart, a video, or an HTML element.
requirements.acceptance: si:designer runs `present add image <deck> 1 photo.png`; the content JSON has a kind image element whose src is asset:<id>, and the picture shows on slide 1 in c:ada's /decks/<id>; an image c:ada inserts in the editor appears in `present read <deck>` as an image element.

requirements.section: Intro paragraphs, Glossary, and Sign in
requirements.requirement: A shape can be placed on a slide as an element.
requirements.quote: `Element` - Anything placed on a slide: text, an image, a shape, a table, a chart, a video, or an HTML element.
requirements.acceptance: si:designer runs `present add shape <deck> 1 ellipse --fill '#2f5bea'`; the content JSON has a kind shape element with shape ellipse, and a blue ellipse shows on slide 1 in c:ada's /decks/<id>; a shape c:ada draws in the editor appears in `present read <deck>`.

requirements.section: Intro paragraphs, Glossary, and Sign in
requirements.requirement: A table can be placed on a slide as an element.
requirements.quote: `Element` - Anything placed on a slide: text, an image, a shape, a table, a chart, a video, or an HTML element.
requirements.acceptance: si:designer runs `present add table <deck> 1 --rows 2 --cols 2 --cell 0,0=Q3 --cell 0,1=Q4 --cell 1,0=10 --cell 1,1=14`; the content JSON has a kind table element with those four cells, and c:ada's /decks/<id> shows a 2x2 table holding them; a table c:ada inserts in the editor appears in `present read <deck>` with its cells.

requirements.section: Intro paragraphs, Glossary, and Sign in
requirements.requirement: A chart can be placed on a slide as an element.
requirements.quote: `Element` - Anything placed on a slide: text, an image, a shape, a table, a chart, a video, or an HTML element.
requirements.acceptance: si:designer runs `present add chart <deck> 1 --type column --labels Q1,Q2 --series 'Revenue=10,12'`; the content JSON has a kind chart element with that data, and c:ada's /decks/<id> shows a column chart with two bars; a chart c:ada inserts in the editor appears in `present read <deck>`.

requirements.section: Intro paragraphs, Glossary, and Sign in
requirements.requirement: A video can be placed on a slide as an element.
requirements.quote: `Element` - Anything placed on a slide: text, an image, a shape, a table, a chart, a video, or an HTML element.
requirements.acceptance: si:designer runs `present add video <deck> 1 demo.mp4`; the content JSON has a kind video element whose src is asset:<id>, and c:ada's /decks/<id> shows a video on slide 1 that plays; a video c:ada inserts in the editor appears in `present read <deck>`.

requirements.section: Intro paragraphs, Glossary, and Sign in
requirements.requirement: An HTML element can be placed on a slide as an element.
requirements.quote: `Element` - Anything placed on a slide: text, an image, a shape, a table, a chart, a video, or an HTML element.
requirements.acceptance: si:designer runs `present add html <deck> 1 --html w.html --x 100 --y 100 --w 800 --h 400`; the content JSON lists a kind html element among slide 1's elements with that position and size, `present read <deck>` shows it, and c:ada's /decks/<id> shows the HTML on the slide.

requirements.section: Intro paragraphs, Glossary, and Sign in
requirements.requirement: An HTML element is made of its own HTML, CSS and JS, held as three separate parts.
requirements.quote: `HTML element` - An element made of HTML, CSS and JS
requirements.acceptance: si:designer runs `present add html <deck> 1 --html w.html --css w.css --js w.js`; GET /v1/decks/<id>/content?format=json shows the element (kind html) with html, css and js equal to the three files; `present set <deck> 1 <element> css=@new.css` changes only css, leaving html and js as they were, and c:ada's /decks/<id> shows the new styling.

requirements.section: Intro paragraphs, Glossary, and Sign in
requirements.requirement: An HTML element runs live in place on the slide, inside its own box, not as a still picture and not in a separate window.
requirements.quote: renders and runs live on the slide
requirements.acceptance: si:designer adds an html element at x=100, y=100, w=800, h=400 whose JS increments an on-screen counter every 500 ms; in c:ada's /decks/<id> Playwright finds the element's live frame placed over exactly that box of the slide (scaled to the canvas), the counter reads higher 2 s later, and no new window or tab opens.

requirements.section: Intro paragraphs, Glossary, and Sign in
requirements.requirement: A folder can hold decks.
requirements.quote: `Folder` - A place to keep decks and other folders together.
requirements.acceptance: si:designer runs `present folder new 'Clients'` and `present move <deck> <folder>`; `present list --folder <folder>` and GET /v1/decks?scope=mine&folder=<folder> list the deck. c:ada makes a folder from /decks in the web, moves a deck into it, and sees the deck inside that folder.

requirements.section: Intro paragraphs, Glossary, and Sign in
requirements.requirement: A folder can hold other folders.
requirements.quote: `Folder` - A place to keep decks and other folders together.
requirements.acceptance: si:designer runs `present folder new 'Acme' --parent <clients>`; `present folder list --parent <clients>` lists 'Acme', and a deck moved into 'Acme' is listed by `present list --folder <acme>`. c:ada nests one folder inside another from /decks in the web and reaches a deck by opening the outer folder, then the inner one.

requirements.section: Intro paragraphs, Glossary, and Sign in
requirements.requirement: A deck can belong to a Carbon or to a Silicon: Silicons own decks just as Carbons do.
requirements.quote: `Owner` - The Carbon or Silicon a deck or folder belongs to.
requirements.acceptance: c:ada creates a deck in the web and si:designer creates one with `present new 'Mine'`; GET /v1/decks/<id> shows owner c:ada for the first and owner si:designer for the second, and each deck appears among its owner's own decks (/decks in the web for c:ada, `present list` for si:designer).

requirements.section: Intro paragraphs, Glossary, and Sign in
requirements.requirement: A folder can belong to a Carbon or to a Silicon: Silicons own folders just as Carbons do.
requirements.quote: `Owner` - The Carbon or Silicon a deck or folder belongs to.
requirements.acceptance: c:ada creates a folder from /decks in the web and si:designer creates one with `present folder new 'Work'`; GET /v1/folders/<id> shows owner c:ada and owner si:designer respectively, and each folder appears among its owner's own folders (`present folder list` for si:designer).

requirements.section: Intro paragraphs, Glossary, and Sign in
requirements.requirement: Every deck has exactly one owner at all times.
requirements.quote: Every deck and folder has exactly one owner.
requirements.acceptance: Across a deck's life (created by c:ada, shared with si:designer as editor, offered with `present transfer <deck> si:designer` and accepted with `present transfers accept <id>`), plus a deck si:designer creates inside a folder c:ada shared with it as editor: GET /v1/decks/<id> always reports exactly one owner (one account, never empty, never a list); editors never appear as owners in `present access <deck>` or the web's share dialog; after the transfer only si:designer is owner; the deck made in c:ada's folder has c:ada as its only owner; and removing the owner's access (`present unshare <deck> <owner>`) is refused.

requirements.section: Intro paragraphs, Glossary, and Sign in
requirements.requirement: Every folder has exactly one owner at all times.
requirements.quote: Every deck and folder has exactly one owner.
requirements.acceptance: Across a folder's life (created by c:ada, shared with si:designer as editor via `present share <folder> si:designer --role editor --folder`, transferred with `present transfer <folder> si:designer --folder` and accepted), plus a subfolder si:designer creates inside it before the transfer: GET /v1/folders/<id> always reports exactly one owner; editors never appear as owners in `present access <folder> --folder` or the web's share dialog; after the transfer only si:designer is owner; and removing the owner's access is refused.

requirements.section: Intro paragraphs, Glossary, and Sign in
requirements.requirement: A comment can be attached to a whole deck.
requirements.quote: `Comment` - A note attached to a deck, a slide, or a part of a slide.
requirements.acceptance: si:designer runs `present comment <deck> --deck 'Looks great overall'`; GET /v1/decks/<id>/threads shows a thread with anchor kind deck, `present read <deck> --comments` shows it against the deck as a whole, and c:ada sees it in the web as a comment on the whole deck, not on any slide.

requirements.section: Intro paragraphs, Glossary, and Sign in
requirements.requirement: A comment can be attached to a slide.
requirements.quote: `Comment` - A note attached to a deck, a slide, or a part of a slide.
requirements.acceptance: si:designer runs `present comment <deck> --slide 2 'Cut this slide?'`; GET /v1/decks/<id>/threads shows a thread with anchor kind slide on slide 2, and c:ada sees it on slide 2 in /decks/<id>.

requirements.section: Intro paragraphs, Glossary, and Sign in
requirements.requirement: A comment can be attached to a part of a slide.
requirements.quote: `Comment` - A note attached to a deck, a slide, or a part of a slide.
requirements.acceptance: c:ada clicks a point on slide 2 in /decks/<id> and comments; si:designer runs `present comment <deck> --slide 2 --area 100,100,600,400 'Simplify'` and `present comment <deck> --slide 2 --element <element> 'Wrong colour'`; GET /v1/decks/<id>/threads shows anchors of kind point, area and element on slide 2 with their coordinates or element, and each shows on that spot of the slide in the web and next to what it is on in `present read <deck> --comments`.

requirements.section: Intro paragraphs, Glossary, and Sign in
requirements.requirement: A comment and its replies form one thread.
requirements.quote: A comment and its replies are a `thread`.
requirements.acceptance: c:ada comments on slide 1 in the web; si:designer replies twice with `present reply <thread> '...'`; GET /v1/decks/<id>/threads returns one thread whose comments are c:ada's comment followed by the two replies in order; the web shows them together as one thread and `present comments <deck>` prints them under one thread id.

requirements.section: Intro paragraphs, Glossary, and Sign in
requirements.requirement: Carbons sign in to the web through Silicon Accounts.
requirements.quote: Signing in and signing up are handled entirely by Silicon Accounts.
requirements.acceptance: c:ada, who already has a Silicon Accounts account, clicks Sign in on the web's / (or opens /sign-in); the browser goes to the Silicon Accounts hosted pages on the Accounts origin, she enters her email and the emailed code there, and /auth/callback returns her to /decks signed in as c:ada.

requirements.section: Intro paragraphs, Glossary, and Sign in
requirements.requirement: A Carbon who has no account signs up through Silicon Accounts, not through Silicon Present.
requirements.quote: Signing in and signing up are handled entirely by Silicon Accounts.
requirements.acceptance: An email with no Silicon Accounts account starts sign-in from the web's /; the Silicon Accounts hosted pages take it through creating the account ('Create account', 'Finish setup'); it comes back to Silicon Present's /decks signed in as the new c:id, and Silicon Present never showed a sign-up form of its own.

requirements.section: Intro paragraphs, Glossary, and Sign in
requirements.requirement: Silicons sign in to the `present` CLI through Silicon Accounts.
requirements.quote: Signing in and signing up are handled entirely by Silicon Accounts.
requirements.acceptance: si:designer pipes a Silicon Accounts short-lived token into the CLI (`silicon-accounts login --app present -q | present login --slt-stdin`); `present whoami --json` shows kind silicon and id si:designer; `present login --slt not-a-token` is refused with an error; the CLI never asks for a Silicon Present password or key.

requirements.section: Intro paragraphs, Glossary, and Sign in
requirements.requirement: A Carbon who signs in to the `present` CLI does so through Silicon Accounts.
requirements.quote: Signing in and signing up are handled entirely by Silicon Accounts.
requirements.acceptance: `present login` with no token shows a code and the Silicon Accounts address to approve it at; c:ada approves the code on the Silicon Accounts site in a browser; the command finishes and `present whoami --json` shows kind carbon and id c:ada; the CLI never asks her for a password.

requirements.section: Intro paragraphs, Glossary, and Sign in
requirements.requirement: Silicon Present has no sign-in or sign-up of its own: it never asks for or stores a password, and never creates or signs in an account itself.
requirements.quote: handled entirely by Silicon Accounts
requirements.acceptance: No web page (including /sign-in) has a password field or a Silicon Present sign-up form, and /sign-in only sends the browser to Silicon Accounts; the service exposes no sign-in, sign-up or password routes (e.g. POST /v1/login and /v1/signup return 404); migrations/ define no password or credential columns (the accounts table only caches uuid, c:id/si:id, name, pfp and email); and the CLI keeps only Silicon Accounts tokens in {home}/.present/state.json.

requirements.section: Intro paragraphs, Glossary, and Sign in
requirements.requirement: The service accepts only Silicon Accounts access tokens as proof of who is calling.
requirements.quote: Signing in and signing up are handled entirely by Silicon Accounts.
requirements.acceptance: With a valid Silicon Accounts access token for Silicon Present, GET /v1/me returns the caller; the same call with a JWT signed by any other key, an expired Silicon Accounts token, or a Silicon Accounts token issued for another app returns 401 with an error body {error: {code, message, hint}}.

requirements.section: Intro paragraphs, Glossary, and Sign in
requirements.requirement: The service uses the official Silicon Accounts client for everything it does with Silicon Accounts.
requirements.quote: Use the official and latest Silicon Accounts client everywhere.
requirements.acceptance: `cargo tree -p present-service` (with the shared CARGO_TARGET_DIR) shows the official `silicon-accounts-client` crate, and a review of crates/present-service confirms token verification (JWKS fetch and verify) and account lookups go through it, with no hand-rolled JWT/JWKS verification and no direct HTTP calls to Silicon Accounts endpoints the client covers.

requirements.section: Intro paragraphs, Glossary, and Sign in
requirements.requirement: The service uses the latest released version of the official Silicon Accounts client.
requirements.quote: Use the official and latest Silicon Accounts client everywhere.
requirements.acceptance: The `silicon-accounts-client` version Cargo.lock resolves for present-service equals the newest version published on crates.io at test time (`cargo search silicon-accounts-client --limit 1` or the crates.io API).

requirements.section: Intro paragraphs, Glossary, and Sign in
requirements.requirement: The CLI (through the silicon-present-client package) uses the official Silicon Accounts client for signing in, refreshing and signing out.
requirements.quote: Use the official and latest Silicon Accounts client everywhere.
requirements.acceptance: `cargo tree -p present-cli` shows `silicon-accounts-client` (through silicon-present-client), and `present login --slt-stdin`, the Carbon device-code sign-in, token refresh and `present logout` are made with that client's calls, with no hand-written OAuth requests to Silicon Accounts.

requirements.section: Intro paragraphs, Glossary, and Sign in
requirements.requirement: The CLI uses the latest released version of the official Silicon Accounts client.
requirements.quote: Use the official and latest Silicon Accounts client everywhere.
requirements.acceptance: The `silicon-accounts-client` version Cargo.lock resolves for silicon-present-client and present-cli equals the newest version published on crates.io at test time.

requirements.section: Intro paragraphs, Glossary, and Sign in
requirements.requirement: The web signs Carbons in with Silicon Accounts' official client, not a third-party or one-off sign-in implementation.
requirements.quote: Use the official and latest Silicon Accounts client everywhere.
requirements.acceptance: web/package.json and pnpm-lock.yaml contain no third-party sign-in library (e.g. next-auth/Auth.js, openid-client, passport); the /auth/sign-in, /auth/callback, /auth/refresh and /auth/sign-out routes use Silicon Accounts' official client (its official TypeScript package if one is published, otherwise the shared Silicon web kit's Accounts sign-in code at /Users/codanium/Documents/silicon/.migration/web-kit, unmodified) against the Silicon Accounts hosted pages.

requirements.section: Intro paragraphs, Glossary, and Sign in
requirements.requirement: The web uses the latest version of the official Silicon Accounts client.
requirements.quote: Use the official and latest Silicon Accounts client everywhere.
requirements.acceptance: If the web uses an official Silicon Accounts npm package, the version in pnpm-lock.yaml equals the newest one published; if it uses the web kit's sign-in code, web/lib/server/{session,tokens,seal}.ts and web/app/auth/* are identical to the current web kit's.

requirements.section: Intro paragraphs, Glossary, and Sign in
requirements.requirement: Silicon Present stores every Carbon and Silicon by their Silicon Accounts uuid.
requirements.quote: Carbons and Silicons are always stored by their Silicon Accounts uuid
requirements.acceptance: After c:ada and si:designer each create decks and folders, edit, comment, mention, react, share, name a version, transfer and present, every account column in the database (decks/folders owner and creator, access.account and invited_by, deck_updates.author, version_names.named_by, events.actor, threads created_by/resolved_by, comments author and mentions, reactions.account, assets, transfers, presentations.presenter, ting_outbox.recipient) holds the uuid Silicon Accounts gives each of them (the uuid in `present whoami --json`, the token's sub); no c:id, si:id or email is stored as who someone is, apart from pending invites to emails that have no account yet.

requirements.section: Intro paragraphs, Glossary, and Sign in
requirements.requirement: A Carbon or Silicon whose c:id or si:id changes at Silicon Accounts keeps everything in Silicon Present: decks, folders, roles, comments and history stay theirs.
requirements.quote: Carbons and Silicons are always stored by their Silicon Accounts uuid
requirements.acceptance: si:designer owns a deck, is editor on c:ada's deck and has comments and versions there; its id is changed to si:designer2 at Silicon Accounts; after signing in again, `present list` still shows its own deck, `present list --shared` still shows c:ada's deck and it can still edit it, and its earlier comments and versions are still attributed to it.

requirements.section: Intro paragraphs, Glossary, and Sign in
requirements.requirement: Wherever Silicon Present shows a Carbon, it shows their c:id.
requirements.quote: shown by their c:id or si:id
requirements.acceptance: c:ada owns a deck, edits it, comments on it and shares it with si:designer; the web shows her as c:ada wherever she appears (owner on /decks, the share dialog, comment author, her presence on the deck, /decks/<id>/history), and so do `present access <deck>`, `present comments <deck>` and `present versions <deck>`; her uuid and email are never what names her.

requirements.section: Intro paragraphs, Glossary, and Sign in
requirements.requirement: Wherever Silicon Present shows a Silicon, it shows its si:id.
requirements.quote: shown by their c:id or si:id
requirements.acceptance: si:designer edits, comments on and is present in a deck c:ada shared with it; c:ada's web shows it as si:designer wherever it appears (comment author, presence, share dialog, /decks/<id>/history), as do `present whoami`, `present access <deck>`, `present comments <deck>` and `present versions <deck>`; its uuid never names it.

requirements.section: Intro paragraphs, Glossary, and Sign in
requirements.requirement: After a Carbon or Silicon changes their c:id or si:id at Silicon Accounts, Silicon Present shows the new id, not the old one.
requirements.quote: shown by their c:id or si:id
requirements.acceptance: c:ada's id is changed to c:ada2 at Silicon Accounts; once Silicon Present has refreshed her account (at the latest on her next signed-in request), the web (deck owner, comment author, presence, history) and the CLI (`present access <deck>`, `present comments <deck>`, `present versions <deck>`) show c:ada2 and nowhere c:ada.

requirements.section: Intro paragraphs, Glossary, and Sign in
requirements.requirement: A signed-out visitor can view a public deck in the web without being asked to sign in.
requirements.quote: Viewing a public deck never needs signing in.
requirements.acceptance: c:ada makes a deck public with `present public <deck> view` (and in turn with comment and edit); for each mode a fresh browser with no session opens /decks/<id> and /decks/<id>/present, is not redirected to /sign-in or Silicon Accounts, and sees every slide; GET /v1/decks/<id> and GET /v1/decks/<id>/content without an Authorization header return 200.

requirements.section: Intro paragraphs, Glossary, and Sign in
requirements.requirement: A signed-out visitor viewing a public deck also gets all of its assets (images, video, fonts).
requirements.quote: Viewing a public deck never needs signing in.
requirements.acceptance: A public deck holds an uploaded image, a video and a custom font (asset:<id>); in a browser with no session at /decks/<id>, every /api/v1/assets/<id> request returns 200 and the image, video and font show on the slides, with no 401 in the network log.

requirements.section: Intro paragraphs, Glossary, and Sign in
requirements.requirement: The CLI can read a public deck as text without signing in.
requirements.quote: Viewing a public deck never needs signing in.
requirements.acceptance: With a fresh $SILICON_HOME and no sign-in (`present login status --json` gives authenticated false), `present read <public deck link>` prints the deck's slides, elements and notes and exits 0.

requirements.section: Intro paragraphs, Glossary, and Sign in
requirements.requirement: The CLI can render a public deck's slides to images without signing in.
requirements.quote: Viewing a public deck never needs signing in.
requirements.acceptance: With no sign-in saved, `present render <public deck link> 1 -o s1.png` writes a non-blank image of slide 1, and GET /v1/decks/<id>/slides/<slide>/render?format=png with no token returns that image.

requirements.section: Intro paragraphs, Glossary, and Sign in
requirements.requirement: A signed-out visitor can follow a live presentation of a public deck.
requirements.quote: Viewing a public deck never needs signing in.
requirements.acceptance: si:designer runs `present start <public deck>`; a browser with no session opens the printed follow link (/p/<presentation>), is not sent to sign in, sees the current slide, and moves to slide 2 when si:designer runs `present next`.

requirements.section: Intro paragraphs, Glossary, and Sign in
requirements.requirement: Apart from viewing a public deck, using Silicon Present needs signing in.
requirements.quote: Viewing a public deck never needs signing in.
requirements.acceptance: A browser with no session opening /decks, /trash, /transfers or a private deck's /decks/<id> is sent to sign in (/sign-in, then Silicon Accounts) and sees no deck content; without a token, GET /v1/decks?scope=mine, GET /v1/decks/<private id>, POST /v1/decks and POST /v1/decks/<public id>/threads return 401; `present list` with no sign-in saved fails and says to run `present login`.

requirements.requirement: Every deck has exactly one owner at all times, and that owner is a single Carbon or Silicon account.
requirements.quote: Every deck and folder has exactly one owner.
requirements.acceptance: c:ada creates a deck on the web and si:designer creates one with `present new`. For each, `GET /v1/decks/{id}` returns a single `owner` account (uuid, `id` c:... or si:..., `kind` carbon|silicon), and `present list --json` and the /decks row show that one owner. Listing own decks (`GET /v1/decks?scope=mine`, top level and every folder) for c:ada, c:bea, si:designer and si:writer, each deck appears for exactly one of them, including while a transfer of it is pending and after it is accepted.

requirements.requirement: Every folder has exactly one owner at all times, and that owner is a single Carbon or Silicon account.
requirements.quote: Every deck and folder has exactly one owner.
requirements.acceptance: For a folder c:ada makes with "New folder" on /decks and one si:designer makes with `present folder new`, `GET /v1/folders/{id}` returns a single `owner` account. Listing own folders (`GET /v1/folders?scope=mine`, every parent) for c:ada, c:bea, si:designer and si:writer, each folder appears for exactly one of them, including while a transfer of it is pending and after it is accepted.

requirements.requirement: A deck a Carbon creates in their own place belongs to that Carbon.
requirements.quote: Every deck belongs to the Carbon or Silicon who created it.
requirements.acceptance: c:ada signs in on the web, clicks "New deck" on /decks (My decks) and creates "Board update". `GET /v1/decks/{id}` shows `owner.id` = c:ada, `owner.kind` = carbon and `creator.id` = c:ada, and the deck is listed under My decks on /decks.

requirements.requirement: A deck a Silicon creates through the CLI belongs to that Silicon itself, not to any Carbon behind it.
requirements.quote: Every deck belongs to the Carbon or Silicon who created it.
requirements.acceptance: si:designer runs `present new "Q4 review" --json`. The output shows `owner.id` = si:designer, `owner.kind` = silicon and `creator.id` = si:designer, and `present list --json` includes the deck. The deck is in no Carbon's My decks, including the Carbon who runs si:designer (if Silicon Accounts links them).

requirements.requirement: A deck made by opening a file belongs to the Carbon or Silicon who opened it.
requirements.quote: Every deck belongs to the Carbon or Silicon who created it.
requirements.acceptance: si:designer runs `present open board.pptx --json` (`POST /v1/imports`): the new deck's `owner.id` and `creator.id` are si:designer and it is in `present list`. c:ada opens a .pdf as a new deck from /decks: `GET /v1/decks/{id}` shows `owner.id` = c:ada and the deck is listed under My decks.

requirements.requirement: A new deck made from an older version of someone else's deck belongs to whoever made it, not to the source deck's owner.
requirements.quote: Every deck belongs to the Carbon or Silicon who created it.
requirements.acceptance: c:ada owns deck D (several versions) and shares it with si:designer as editor. si:designer runs `present new "Q4 for the client" --from D@3 --json` (`POST /v1/decks {from:{deck,version}}`): the new deck shows `owner.id` = `creator.id` = si:designer, is in `present list` and is not in c:ada's My decks. D's owner is still c:ada.

requirements.requirement: There are no Teams or workspaces: no surface offers creating, joining or switching to a Team or workspace, and no deck or folder ever belongs to one.
requirements.quote: There are no Teams or workspaces.
requirements.acceptance: Service: there are no team or workspace routes (`GET /v1/teams` and `GET /v1/workspaces` return 404), no team or workspace field in deck, folder, access or transfer JSON, and no listing scope beyond mine|shared|trash (`GET /v1/decks?scope=team` is refused). CLI: `present --help` and every subcommand's `--help` have no team or workspace command, flag or wording. Web: /decks, the sidebar and the account menu show no team or workspace switcher, selector or wording (the teamofsilicons.com brand aside).

requirements.requirement: A deck someone else owns appears in neither of your places unless it has been shared with you; nothing gives implicit access (no Team, workspace, or link between a Silicon and its Carbon).
requirements.quote: Decks are personal.
requirements.acceptance: si:designer creates deck D, shares it with no one and leaves public off. c:ada (also when she is the Carbon who runs si:designer) sees D neither in My decks nor in Shared with me on /decks, and `GET /v1/decks?scope=mine` and `?scope=shared` as c:ada exclude it. si:writer's `present list` and `present list --shared` exclude it. `GET /v1/decks/D` as c:ada is refused (403/404).

requirements.requirement: Every Carbon and Silicon has an own-decks place that lists exactly the decks they own.
requirements.quote: Everyone has two places: their own decks, and the decks and folders shared with them.
requirements.acceptance: c:ada and si:designer each create decks, some at the top level, some in their own folders, and someone else creates a deck inside a folder of theirs that is shared with them. c:ada's My decks on /decks (top level plus each folder via /decks?folder=<id>) and si:designer's `present list --json` (plus `present list --folder <id>` for each of its folders) together list every deck whose `owner` is that account and no other deck. `GET /v1/decks?scope=mine` agrees.

requirements.requirement: Every Carbon and Silicon has a shared-with-me place that lists the decks and folders others have shared with them.
requirements.quote: Everyone has two places: their own decks, and the decks and folders shared with them.
requirements.acceptance: c:ada shares deck D1 (sitting inside her unshared folder F) and folder G with si:designer as viewer: `present list --shared --json` shows D1 and G, and `present folder list --shared` shows G. si:designer shares deck E with c:ada as commenter: c:ada's Shared with me (/decks?scope=shared) lists E. `GET /v1/decks?scope=shared` and `GET /v1/folders?scope=shared` return the same.

requirements.requirement: The two places never mix: decks you own never show in your shared-with-me place, and decks someone else owns never show in your own decks.
requirements.quote: Everyone has two places: their own decks, and the decks and folders shared with them.
requirements.acceptance: c:ada owns D1 and shares it with c:bea; si:designer owns D2 and shares it with c:ada as editor. c:ada's My decks lists D1 and not D2, and her Shared with me lists D2 and not D1. si:designer's `present list` includes D2 and `present list --shared` does not.

requirements.requirement: A folder in your shared-with-me place can be opened to reach the decks and folders inside it.
requirements.quote: Everyone has two places: their own decks, and the decks and folders shared with them.
requirements.acceptance: c:ada's folder F holds deck D and folder G (which holds deck H), and F is shared with si:designer and c:bea as viewers. si:designer runs `present list --folder F` and sees D, `present folder list --parent F` and sees G, and `present list --folder G` and sees H. c:bea clicks F under Shared with me, sees D and G with a breadcrumb, then opens G and sees H.

requirements.requirement: An owner can make a folder among their own decks, and the folder belongs to them.
requirements.quote: An owner can sort their decks into folders
requirements.acceptance: c:ada clicks "New folder" on /decks and names it "Clients": it appears in My decks, and `GET /v1/folders/{id}` shows `owner.id` = c:ada and `parent` null. si:designer runs `present folder new "Drafts" --json`: `owner.id` = si:designer, and `present folder list` lists it.

requirements.requirement: An owner can move a deck they own into one of their folders.
requirements.quote: An owner can sort their decks into folders
requirements.acceptance: si:designer runs `present move D F` (both its own): `GET /v1/decks/D` shows `folder` = F, `present list --folder F` lists D, and the top-level `present list` no longer does. c:ada picks More actions, then Move on a deck row and chooses one of her folders: the deck shows on /decks?folder=<id> and is no longer at the top of My decks.

requirements.requirement: An owner can move a deck from one of their folders into another.
requirements.quote: An owner can sort their decks into folders
requirements.acceptance: D is in si:designer's folder F1. si:designer runs `present move D F2`: D is listed by `present list --folder F2` and not by `present list --folder F1`. c:ada moves a deck between two of her folders with Move on the web and sees it only in the new folder.

requirements.requirement: An owner can take a deck out of its folder and back to the top level of their own decks.
requirements.quote: An owner can sort their decks into folders
requirements.acceptance: si:designer runs `present move D root`: `GET /v1/decks/D` shows `folder` null, and D is in the top-level `present list` and not in `present list --folder F`. On the web, Move then "My decks" puts c:ada's deck back at the top of My decks.

requirements.requirement: An owner can make a folder inside one of their folders.
requirements.quote: and folders into other folders
requirements.acceptance: si:designer runs `present folder new "2026" --parent F --json`: `parent` = F, and the folder is listed by `present folder list --parent F` and not at the top level. c:ada opens /decks?folder=F and clicks "New folder": the new folder appears there, with the breadcrumb My decks / F.

requirements.requirement: An owner can move one of their folders into another of their folders.
requirements.quote: and folders into other folders
requirements.acceptance: si:designer runs `present folder move G F`: `GET /v1/folders/G` shows `parent` = F, and G is listed by `present folder list --parent F` and no longer by the top-level `present folder list`. c:ada does the same with Move on a folder row on /decks.

requirements.requirement: An owner can move a nested folder back to the top level of their own decks.
requirements.quote: and folders into other folders
requirements.acceptance: si:designer runs `present folder move G root`: `parent` is null and G is in the top-level `present folder list`. On the web, Move then "My decks" on a nested folder of c:ada's does the same.

requirements.requirement: Folders nest to any depth: a folder inside a folder can itself hold folders and decks.
requirements.quote: and folders into other folders
requirements.acceptance: si:designer makes F1, then F2 with `--parent F1`, F3 with `--parent F2` and F4 with `--parent F3`, then runs `present new "Deep" --folder F4`. At each level `present folder list --parent Fn` shows Fn+1, and `present list --folder F4` shows the deck. c:ada builds the same tree on the web, and /decks?folder=<F4> shows the breadcrumb My decks / F1 / F2 / F3 / F4.

requirements.requirement: Moving a folder moves everything in it along: its decks and folders stay inside it.
requirements.quote: A place to keep decks and other folders together.
requirements.acceptance: si:designer's F1 holds deck D and folder G (which holds deck H). After `present folder move F1 F0`, `present list --folder F1` still lists D, `present folder list --parent F1` still lists G, `present list --folder G` still lists H, and their `folder` and `parent` values are unchanged. On the web, c:ada reaches the same tree through /decks?folder=<F0> and then F1.

requirements.requirement: A folder can't be moved into itself or into a folder inside it, so sorting never cuts folders and decks off from their owner's place.
requirements.quote: and folders into other folders
requirements.acceptance: si:designer's F1 holds F2. `present folder move F1 F1` and `present folder move F1 F2` both fail with a clear error (`PATCH /v1/folders/F1 {parent}` returns 4xx with `{"error":{code,message,hint}}`). Afterwards F1 and F2 keep their parents, and every deck in them is still reachable from `present folder list` and `present list --folder`. The web Move dialog for one of c:ada's folders doesn't offer that folder or anything inside it (or shows the error and changes nothing).

requirements.requirement: Someone who doesn't own a deck can't sort it into a folder of their own.
requirements.quote: An owner can sort their decks into folders
requirements.acceptance: c:ada owns D and shares it with si:designer as editor; si:designer owns folder G. si:designer runs `present move D G` (`PATCH /v1/decks/D {folder: G}`) and it is refused with a clear error. D's `folder` and `owner` are unchanged, and `present list --folder G` does not include D. On the web, c:bea (editor on D) cannot move D into a folder of hers.

requirements.requirement: Someone a folder is shared with as editor can create a deck inside it.
requirements.quote: A deck created inside someone else's shared folder
requirements.acceptance: c:ada shares folder F with si:designer as editor. si:designer runs `present new "Draft" --folder F --json` and it succeeds. The deck is listed by `present list --folder F` and on c:ada's /decks?folder=F.

requirements.requirement: Someone a folder is shared with only as viewer or commenter can't create a deck inside it.
requirements.quote: A deck created inside someone else's shared folder
requirements.acceptance: c:ada shares folder F with si:writer as viewer and with c:bea as commenter. `present new "X" --folder F` run by si:writer is refused with a clear permission error. The web offers c:bea no "New deck" inside F, and `POST /v1/decks {folder: F}` as c:bea is refused. F's contents are unchanged.

requirements.requirement: A deck a Silicon creates inside a Carbon's shared folder belongs to the Carbon who owns the folder, not to the Silicon.
requirements.quote: A deck created inside someone else's shared folder belongs to that folder's owner
requirements.acceptance: c:ada owns folder F (holding her folder G) and shares F with si:designer as editor. `present new "Draft" --folder F --json` prints `owner.id` = c:ada and `creator.id` = si:designer, and `GET /v1/decks/{id}` agrees for both accounts. The same holds for a deck si:designer creates in G, which is shared with it through F.

requirements.requirement: A deck a Carbon creates inside a Silicon's shared folder belongs to the Silicon who owns the folder, not to the Carbon.
requirements.quote: A deck created inside someone else's shared folder belongs to that folder's owner
requirements.acceptance: si:designer owns folder G and runs `present folder share G c:ada --role editor`. c:ada opens G under Shared with me and creates a deck with "New deck". `GET /v1/decks/{id}` shows `owner.id` = si:designer and `creator.id` = c:ada.

requirements.requirement: A deck made by opening a file inside someone else's shared folder belongs to that folder's owner.
requirements.quote: A deck created inside someone else's shared folder belongs to that folder's owner
requirements.acceptance: c:ada owns F and shares it with si:designer as editor. si:designer runs `present open board.pptx --folder F --json` (`POST /v1/imports?folder=F`): the new deck has `owner.id` = c:ada and `creator.id` = si:designer, and it is listed in F. c:bea, also an editor on F, opens a file as a new deck while viewing F on the web, with the same result.

requirements.requirement: A deck created inside someone else's shared folder shows who created it, alongside and distinct from its owner.
requirements.quote: and still shows who created it
requirements.acceptance: After DECK-26, `GET /v1/decks/{id}` and `present list --folder F --json` return `creator.id` = si:designer next to `owner.id` = c:ada, and the plain `present list --folder F` output names si:designer as the creator. On /decks?folder=F the deck row reads "Made by si:designer" for c:ada and for c:bea (if F is shared with her). The creator is shown by si:id, never by uuid.

requirements.requirement: A deck created inside someone else's shared folder is listed among the folder owner's own decks, inside that folder.
requirements.quote: belongs to that folder's owner
requirements.acceptance: After DECK-26, c:ada sees the deck on /decks?folder=F under My decks, and `GET /v1/decks?scope=mine&folder=F` as c:ada includes it.

requirements.requirement: A deck created inside someone else's shared folder is not listed among its creator's own decks; the creator reaches it through the shared folder.
requirements.quote: belongs to that folder's owner
requirements.acceptance: After DECK-26, si:designer's `present list` (top level and each of its own folders) does not include the deck, while `present list --shared` shows F and `present list --folder F` shows the deck. After DECK-27, the deck c:ada created is not in her My decks but is reachable under Shared with me, inside G.

requirements.requirement: A Carbon owner can offer one of their decks to a Silicon from the web.
requirements.quote: The owner can transfer a deck or folder to another Carbon or Silicon
requirements.acceptance: c:ada picks More actions, then "Transfer to someone" on a deck row, enters si:designer and clicks "Offer transfer". Her /transfers page shows the offer under "Offered by you" as waiting. `GET /v1/transfers` as si:designer returns it with `kind` deck, `from.id` c:ada, `to.id` si:designer and `state` pending.

requirements.requirement: A Silicon owner can offer one of its decks to a Carbon from the CLI.
requirements.quote: The owner can transfer a deck or folder to another Carbon or Silicon
requirements.acceptance: si:designer runs `present transfer D c:ada`. `present transfers --json` shows the offer as pending with `to.id` c:ada, and c:ada's /transfers lists it under "Offered to you".

requirements.requirement: An owner can offer one of their folders to another Carbon or Silicon.
requirements.quote: The owner can transfer a deck or folder to another Carbon or Silicon
requirements.acceptance: si:designer runs `present transfer F si:writer --folder`, and si:writer's `present transfers --json` shows a pending offer with `kind` folder. c:ada offers one of her folders to c:bea with "Transfer to someone" on its row, and c:bea sees the offer on /transfers.

requirements.requirement: The Carbon or Silicon a deck or folder is offered to can see the offer, including what it is and who offers it, so they can accept it.
requirements.quote: who has to accept before it moves
requirements.acceptance: After DECK-32, si:designer's `present transfers --json` lists the pending offer with the deck's title, `kind` deck and `from.id` c:ada. After DECK-33, c:ada's /transfers shows under "Offered to you" the deck's title, si:designer as the giver, and Accept and Decline buttons.

requirements.requirement: Until the receiver accepts, nothing moves: the owner stays the owner, and the deck or folder stays in the owner's own decks and is not in the receiver's.
requirements.quote: who has to accept before it moves
requirements.acceptance: While c:ada's offer of D to si:designer is pending, `GET /v1/decks/D` shows `owner.id` c:ada, D is in c:ada's My decks, and si:designer's `present list` does not include D. A pending folder offer behaves the same way (`GET /v1/folders/F`, `present folder list`).

requirements.requirement: When the receiver accepts, the deck moves: the receiver becomes its owner, and it is listed in their own decks and no longer in the previous owner's.
requirements.quote: who has to accept before it moves
requirements.acceptance: si:designer runs `present transfers accept <id>` on c:ada's offer of D. `GET /v1/decks/D` shows `owner.id` si:designer, `present list` includes D, c:ada's My decks no longer lists it, and the transfer shows `state` accepted. In the other direction, c:ada clicks Accept on /transfers for si:designer's offer, and that deck moves into her My decks.

requirements.requirement: Accepting a folder transfer moves the folder, together with everything in it, to the receiver.
requirements.quote: The owner can transfer a deck or folder to another Carbon or Silicon, who has to accept before it moves.
requirements.acceptance: si:designer's folder F holds deck D and folder G (which holds deck H). si:designer runs `present transfer F c:ada --folder` and c:ada accepts on /transfers. `GET` on F, G, D and H all show `owner.id` c:ada, and c:ada's My decks shows F with D and G inside (and H inside G). None of them remain in si:designer's `present list` or `present folder list`.

requirements.requirement: The receiver can decline an offer, and then nothing moves.
requirements.quote: who has to accept before it moves
requirements.acceptance: si:designer offers D to c:ada and c:ada clicks Decline on /transfers. `GET /v1/decks/D` still shows `owner.id` si:designer, D stays in `present list` and never appears in c:ada's My decks, and the transfer shows `state` declined. si:writer declines a folder offer with `present transfers decline <id>`, with the same outcome.

requirements.requirement: Only the owner can offer a deck or folder to someone; anyone else with access, even an editor or the deck's creator, is refused.
requirements.quote: The owner can transfer a deck or folder
requirements.acceptance: c:ada owns deck D and folder F, both shared with si:designer as editor. `present transfer D si:writer` and `present transfer F si:writer --folder` run by si:designer fail with a clear permission error, si:writer's `present transfers` shows nothing, and the owners are unchanged. si:designer also cannot transfer a deck it created inside c:ada's folder. On the web, c:bea (editor on D) is offered no "Transfer to someone" for D, or the service refuses it.

requirements.requirement: Only the Carbon or Silicon an offer is made to can accept it; neither the owner nor anyone else can accept on their behalf.
requirements.quote: who has to accept before it moves
requirements.acceptance: c:ada offers D to si:designer. `POST /v1/transfers/{id}/accept` as c:ada and `present transfers accept <id>` as si:writer are both refused. D's owner is still c:ada, the offer is still pending, and c:ada's /transfers shows no Accept button on her own offer.

requirements.requirement: A deck or folder can only be transferred to another Carbon or Silicon, not to its own owner.
requirements.quote: to another Carbon or Silicon
requirements.acceptance: si:designer, D's owner, runs `present transfer D si:designer`: it fails with a clear error and `present transfers` shows no new offer. The web transfer dialog refuses c:ada's own c:id for her own deck.

requirements.requirement: A transferred deck is the same deck: its id and link, content, comments and full version history move with it unchanged.
requirements.quote: who has to accept before it moves
requirements.acceptance: Before the transfer, record D's id, `present read D --json`, `present comments D --all --json` and `present versions D --json`. After si:designer accepts, the same id opens at /decks/D, the content and threads are identical, and every earlier version is still listed with the same number, author (still c:ada), summary and name. The transfer itself may appear as a new event.

requirements.requirement: The owner of an existing deck or folder never changes except through an accepted transfer; moving, sharing or editing never makes someone else the owner.
requirements.quote: The owner can transfer a deck or folder to another Carbon or Silicon, who has to accept before it moves.
requirements.acceptance: si:designer owns D; c:ada owns folder F, shared with si:designer as editor. `present move D F` is either refused or only offers D to c:ada as a transfer. Either way D's owner stays si:designer and D does not appear in F or in c:ada's My decks until c:ada accepts. Moving one of si:designer's folders into F behaves the same. `PATCH /v1/decks/D` with an `owner` field leaves the owner unchanged, and sharing D with c:ada as editor and her editing it leave `owner.id` si:designer.

requirements.requirement: Deleting a deck puts it in the trash; it is not destroyed.
requirements.quote: Anything deleted goes to the trash
requirements.acceptance: si:designer runs `present trash D`: D is gone from `present list` and listed by `present list --trash` with `trashedAt` set. c:ada uses "Move to trash" on a deck row: the deck leaves My decks and is listed on /trash. `GET /v1/decks?scope=trash` lists both decks for their owners.

requirements.requirement: Deleting a folder puts it in the trash; it is not destroyed.
requirements.quote: Anything deleted goes to the trash
requirements.acceptance: si:designer runs `present folder trash F`: F is in `present folder list --trash` and not in `present folder list`. c:ada's "Move to trash" on a folder row puts the folder on /trash.

requirements.requirement: Deleting a folder takes everything inside it to the trash with it; nothing inside is destroyed or left behind.
requirements.quote: Anything deleted goes to the trash with its full history
requirements.acceptance: F holds D and G (which holds H). After `present folder trash F`, D, G and H can no longer be reached from si:designer's own decks (`present list`, `present folder list` or any `--folder`/`--parent`). They are in the trash with F, not destroyed, and restoring F brings all of them back (DECK-52).

requirements.requirement: The owner can restore a trashed deck; it is back in their own decks and opens again.
requirements.quote: can be restored at any time
requirements.acceptance: si:designer runs `present untrash D`: D is in `present list` and not in `present list --trash`, `trashedAt` is empty, and `present read D` works. c:ada restores a deck on /trash (toast "Restored"): it is back in My decks and opens at /decks/[id].

requirements.requirement: A deck restored from the trash comes back with its full history: every version, its content and its comments as they were.
requirements.quote: goes to the trash with its full history
requirements.acceptance: D has several versions by c:ada and si:designer and two comment threads. Record `present versions D --json`, `present read D --json` and `present comments D --all --json`, then run `present trash D` and `present untrash D`. The content and threads are identical, every earlier version is still listed with the same number, author, summary and name (trash and restore may appear as events), and `present read D --version <oldest>` still works. c:ada sees the same history on /decks/D/history.

requirements.requirement: A restored deck comes back to the folder it was in.
requirements.quote: can be restored at any time
requirements.acceptance: D is in si:designer's folder F. After `present trash D` and `present untrash D`, `GET /v1/decks/D` shows `folder` = F and `present list --folder F` lists D. On the web, a deck c:ada trashed from /decks?folder=<id> and restored on /trash reappears in that folder.

requirements.requirement: The owner can restore a trashed folder; it is back in their own decks.
requirements.quote: can be restored at any time
requirements.acceptance: si:designer runs `present folder untrash F`: F is in `present folder list` and not in `present folder list --trash`. c:ada restores a folder on /trash and it is back in My decks.

requirements.requirement: Restoring a trashed folder brings back everything that was in it, each with its full history.
requirements.quote: Anything deleted goes to the trash with its full history and can be restored at any time.
requirements.acceptance: After DECK-47, si:designer runs `present folder untrash F`. `present list --folder F` lists D, `present folder list --parent F` lists G, `present list --folder G` lists H, and `present versions D` and `present versions H` still list every version they had before the trash. On the web, c:ada restores a trashed folder from /trash and finds its decks and subfolders inside it again.

requirements.requirement: Nothing leaves the trash by itself: trashed decks and folders stay there, restorable, with no expiry or automatic purge.
requirements.quote: can be restored at any time. It stays there until the owner permanently deletes it
requirements.acceptance: Trash deck D and folder F. In the test database, move their `trashed_at` back 400 days, restart the service and let any background job run. Both are still in `present list --trash` / `present folder list --trash` and on /trash, and `present untrash D` and `present folder untrash F` succeed with full history. Neither /trash nor the CLI shows an expiry or "deleted in N days" date.

requirements.requirement: The owner can permanently delete a trashed deck, after which it is truly gone.
requirements.quote: It stays there until the owner permanently deletes it
requirements.acceptance: si:designer runs `present trash D && present delete D --permanent --confirm "<D's title>"`. D is no longer in `present list --trash`, `present read D` and `present untrash D` fail with not found, and `GET /v1/decks/D` returns 404 for everyone it was shared with and without a token (its public link stops working). c:ada uses "Delete forever" on /trash and that deck is gone in the same way.

requirements.requirement: The owner can permanently delete a trashed folder.
requirements.quote: It stays there until the owner permanently deletes it
requirements.acceptance: si:designer runs `present folder trash F && present folder delete F --confirm "<F's name>"`. F is not in `present folder list --trash`, and `GET /v1/folders/F` returns 404. c:ada uses "Delete forever" on a trashed folder on /trash, with the same result.

requirements.requirement: Only the owner can permanently delete a deck or folder; no one else can, not even an editor or the deck's creator.
requirements.quote: until the owner permanently deletes it
requirements.acceptance: c:ada owns D and F, both shared with si:designer as editor, and trashes both. si:designer's `present delete D --permanent --confirm "<title>"`, `present folder delete F --confirm "<name>"` and `DELETE /v1/decks/D?permanent=true&confirm=...` are all refused. A deck si:designer created inside c:ada's folder can only be permanently deleted by c:ada. D and F are still on c:ada's /trash and can be restored.

requirements.requirement: Permanently deleting asks the owner to confirm first; without that confirmation nothing is deleted.
requirements.quote: which asks them to confirm first
requirements.acceptance: Web: "Delete forever" on /trash opens a confirmation that asks for the name; "Keep it" or a wrong name leaves the item in the trash. CLI: `present delete D --permanent` without a terminal and without `--confirm`, or with a wrong `--confirm`, fails and D stays in `present list --trash`; in a terminal it asks for the title first. `present folder delete F` behaves the same. Service: `DELETE /v1/decks/D?permanent=true` without a matching `confirm` is refused and D stays in the trash.

requirements.requirement: Only something already in the trash can be permanently deleted; a live deck or folder can't skip the trash.
requirements.quote: Anything deleted goes to the trash
requirements.acceptance: With D not in the trash, `present delete D --permanent --confirm "<title>"` and `DELETE /v1/decks/D?permanent=true&confirm=<title>` are refused, and D stays in `present list` with its history. `present folder delete F --confirm "<name>"` on a live folder is refused. The web offers "Delete forever" only on /trash.

requirements.requirement: Deleting a slide or an element never makes it truly gone: it can be brought back from the deck's history, along with its assets.
requirements.quote: That is the only way anything in Silicon Present is ever truly gone.
requirements.acceptance: si:designer runs `present add image D 3 photo.png` (an uploaded asset) and notes the version, then runs `present delete D 3 <element>` and `present slide delete D 3`. `present versions D` still lists the earlier versions. `present restore D <version> --slide <id>` brings back the slide with the image, `present render D 3 -o s3.png` shows the image, and `GET /v1/assets/{id}` still serves it. On /decks/D/history, c:ada can bring back a slide she deleted the same way.

requirements.requirement: Deleting a comment never makes it truly gone: it stays in the deck's history.
requirements.quote: That is the only way anything in Silicon Present is ever truly gone.
requirements.acceptance: si:designer runs `present comment D --slide 1 "Check this"` and then `present comment delete <comment>`, and c:ada deletes one of her own comments on the web. The deck's history (`GET /v1/decks/{id}/versions` events and /decks/[id]/history) still records each comment's text and author, and who deleted it and when.

requirements.requirement: The folder's owner can sort a deck someone else created in their folder, like any other deck of theirs, and the deck keeps showing its creator.
requirements.quote: belongs to that folder's owner, and still shows who created it
requirements.acceptance: After DECK-26, c:ada moves the deck si:designer created in F to her folder K with Move on /decks (`PATCH /v1/decks/{id} {folder: K}`). The deck is listed on /decks?folder=K and no longer in F, `owner.id` is still c:ada and `creator.id` is still si:designer, and the row still reads "Made by si:designer".

requirements.requirement: A slide is made of elements: one slide can hold several separate elements of different kinds at the same time.
requirements.quote: A slide is built from elements.
requirements.acceptance: si:designer runs `present add text`, `present add shape` and `present add image` on slide 2 of a deck. `present read <deck> --json` lists three separate elements (kinds text, shape, image) in slide 2's elements; c:ada opens /decks/<id> and can select each of the three on its own; /decks/<id>/present shows all three on slide 2.

requirements.requirement: Any element can be placed (moved) anywhere on its slide, whoever made it.
requirements.quote: Every element can be placed, resized, rotated, layered, grouped, aligned, locked and animated, whoever made it.
requirements.acceptance: One slide holds one element of every kind made by si:designer through `present add ...` (text, shape, image, video, audio, table, chart, html) and one of each kind c:ada can insert in the editor. c:ada drags every Silicon-made element to a new spot in /decks/<id>; si:designer moves every Carbon-made element with `present set <deck> <slide> <element> x=... y=...`. `present read <deck> --json` shows every element at its new x/y, and /decks/<id>/present draws each one there.

requirements.requirement: Any element can be resized, whoever made it.
requirements.quote: Every element can be placed, resized, rotated, layered, grouped, aligned, locked and animated, whoever made it.
requirements.acceptance: On the same mixed slide (every kind, made by si:designer and by c:ada), c:ada drags a resize handle on every Silicon-made element in /decks/<id>; si:designer runs `present set <deck> <slide> <element> w=... h=...` on every Carbon-made element. `present read <deck> --json` shows the new w/h for all of them, and /decks/<id>/present draws each at its new size.

requirements.requirement: Any element can be rotated to any angle, whoever made it.
requirements.quote: Every element can be placed, resized, rotated, layered, grouped, aligned, locked and animated, whoever made it.
requirements.acceptance: On the same mixed slide, c:ada rotates every Silicon-made element with the rotate handle in /decks/<id> (to about 30 degrees); si:designer runs `present set <deck> <slide> <element> rotation=-45` on every Carbon-made element. `present read <deck> --json` shows each rotation, and /decks/<id>/present draws each element turned by its angle.

requirements.requirement: Any element can be layered (brought to the front, sent to the back, or moved one step forward or backward among the elements it overlaps), whoever made it.
requirements.quote: Every element can be placed, resized, rotated, layered, grouped, aligned, locked and animated, whoever made it.
requirements.acceptance: On a slide with three overlapping elements (one made by si:designer, two by c:ada), c:ada brings the Silicon-made one to the front and sends another one step backward with the editor's arrange controls; si:designer runs `present back <deck> <slide> <element>` and `present front <deck> <slide> <element> --step` on Carbon-made ones. After each step the back-to-front order of the slide's elements in `present read <deck> --json` matches, and /decks/<id>/present paints the overlap in that order.

requirements.requirement: Any elements can be grouped together, whoever made them.
requirements.quote: Every element can be placed, resized, rotated, layered, grouped, aligned, locked and animated, whoever made it.
requirements.acceptance: c:ada selects a Silicon-made element and a Carbon-made element in /decks/<id> and groups them; clicking either one then selects both as one unit. si:designer runs `present set <deck> <slide> <element> group=g1` on two Carbon-made elements. `present read <deck> --json` shows each pair sharing one group id.

requirements.requirement: Grouped elements move together: dragging one member of a group in the editor moves every member by the same distance.
requirements.quote: Every element can be placed, resized, rotated, layered, grouped, aligned, locked and animated, whoever made it.
requirements.acceptance: With element A (made by si:designer) and element B (made by c:ada) grouped, c:ada drags A 200 slide px to the right in /decks/<id>. `present read <deck> --json` shows both A and B with x increased by 200 and their y unchanged.

requirements.requirement: A group can be ungrouped, after which its elements move independently again.
requirements.quote: Every element can be placed, resized, rotated, layered, grouped, aligned, locked and animated, whoever made it.
requirements.acceptance: c:ada ungroups a group in /decks/<id> and drags one former member: only that element's x/y change in `present read <deck> --json`. si:designer runs `present set <deck> <slide> <element> group=null` on each member of another group, and the deck JSON shows group null for them.

requirements.requirement: Any elements can be aligned, to each other's edges or centres and to the slide, whoever made them.
requirements.quote: Every element can be placed, resized, rotated, layered, grouped, aligned, locked and animated, whoever made it.
requirements.acceptance: c:ada selects three elements (made by si:designer and by c:ada) in /decks/<id> and aligns their left edges, then their middles: the deck JSON shows equal x, then equal y + h/2.
