With one element selected, aligning it to the centre of the slide gives x = (1920 - w) / 2. si:designer lines up the top edges of two Carbon-made elements through the CLI (`present set ... y=<the other element's y>`), and the deck JSON shows equal y.

requirements.requirement: Any element can be locked and unlocked, whoever made it.
requirements.quote: Every element can be placed, resized, rotated, layered, grouped, aligned, locked and animated, whoever made it.
requirements.acceptance: c:ada locks a Silicon-made element in /decks/<id>; si:designer runs `present set <deck> <slide> <element> locked=true` on a Carbon-made element. `present read <deck> --json` shows locked true for both, and the editor marks both as locked. c:ada then unlocks the first in the editor and si:designer runs `present set ... locked=false` on the second; both read back locked false.

requirements.requirement: A locked element cannot be moved, resized or rotated by dragging in the editor until it is unlocked.
requirements.quote: Every element can be placed, resized, rotated, layered, grouped, aligned, locked and animated, whoever made it.
requirements.acceptance: c:ada tries to drag, resize and rotate a locked element (made by si:designer) in /decks/<id>: its x, y, w, h and rotation in `present read <deck> --json` stay the same. After c:ada unlocks it, the same drag moves it.

requirements.requirement: Any element can be given an animation, whoever made it.
requirements.quote: Every element can be placed, resized, rotated, layered, grouped, aligned, locked and animated, whoever made it.
requirements.acceptance: c:ada gives a Silicon-made element an entrance animation (for example fade, first in order) in /decks/<id>; si:designer runs `present set <deck> <slide> <element> animation=<fly-in on click, order 2, 400 ms>` on a Carbon-made element. `present read <deck> --json` shows both animations. Repeat for one element of every kind, including an html element.

requirements.requirement: A Carbon can add a text box to a slide and type into it directly on the slide.
requirements.quote: Carbons edit text, images, shapes, tables, charts and videos directly on the slide, just like in Google Slides or PowerPoint.
requirements.acceptance: c:ada (editor) adds a text box to slide 1 in /decks/<id> and types 'Quarterly review' on the canvas itself, with no separate form or dialog. GET /v1/decks/{id}/content?format=json shows a text element on slide 1 holding that text.

requirements.requirement: A Carbon can change existing text in place on the slide, including text a Silicon wrote.
requirements.quote: Carbons edit text, images, shapes, tables, charts and videos directly on the slide, just like in Google Slides or PowerPoint.
requirements.acceptance: si:designer adds 'Revnue grew' with `present add text`. c:ada double-clicks it on the canvas in /decks/<id>, corrects it to 'Revenue grew' and clicks away. The deck JSON shows the corrected text in the same element (same id).

requirements.requirement: A Carbon can format text on the slide as in Google Slides or PowerPoint: bold, italic, underline, font, size and colour of selected text, paragraph alignment, and bulleted or numbered lists.
requirements.quote: Carbons edit text, images, shapes, tables, charts and videos directly on the slide, just like in Google Slides or PowerPoint.
requirements.acceptance: c:ada selects one word in a text box on the canvas and applies bold, italic, underline, a font, a size and a colour. Then they centre the paragraph and turn two lines into a bulleted list, then a numbered list. The canvas shows each change. The deck JSON shows a run with bold, italic, underline, font, size and color on that word only, and paragraphs with align center and list bullet, then ordered.

critic.problem: It merges three separate features that can fail independently: character formatting of a selection (bold, italic, underline, font, size, colour), paragraph alignment, and bulleted or numbered lists.
critic.fix: Split it into three items: (a) bold, italic, underline, font, size and colour applied to selected text change only those runs; (b) a paragraph can be aligned left, centre, right or justified; (c) lines can be turned into a bulleted or numbered list and back. Give each its own canvas check and deck-JSON check.

requirements.requirement: A Carbon can add an image to a slide in the editor.
requirements.quote: Carbons edit text, images, shapes, tables, charts and videos directly on the slide, just like in Google Slides or PowerPoint.
requirements.acceptance: c:ada inserts a PNG from their computer into slide 1 in /decks/<id>. It shows on the canvas, and the deck JSON has an image element whose src is asset:<id>, which GET /api/v1/assets/<id> serves.

requirements.requirement: A Carbon can replace the picture of an existing image on the slide, and the image stays where it is.
requirements.quote: Carbons edit text, images, shapes, tables, charts and videos directly on the slide, just like in Google Slides or PowerPoint.
requirements.acceptance: c:ada replaces an image made by si:designer with another file in /decks/<id>. The same element (same id, x and y) now has a new asset src in the deck JSON, and the canvas shows the new picture.

requirements.requirement: A Carbon can add a shape of a chosen type (for example rectangle, ellipse, arrow or star) to a slide in the editor.
requirements.quote: Carbons edit text, images, shapes, tables, charts and videos directly on the slide, just like in Google Slides or PowerPoint.
requirements.acceptance: c:ada inserts an ellipse and a right arrow in /decks/<id>. Both show on the canvas, and the deck JSON has shape elements with shape ellipse and arrow-right.

requirements.requirement: A Carbon can change a shape's fill colour and outline in the editor.
requirements.quote: Carbons edit text, images, shapes, tables, charts and videos directly on the slide, just like in Google Slides or PowerPoint.
requirements.acceptance: c:ada sets a shape's fill to #2f5bea and its outline to #111111 at 4 px in /decks/<id>. The canvas shows them, and the deck JSON shows style.fill, style.stroke and style.strokeWidth with those values.

requirements.requirement: A Carbon can type text inside a shape directly on the slide.
requirements.quote: Carbons edit text, images, shapes, tables, charts and videos directly on the slide, just like in Google Slides or PowerPoint.
requirements.acceptance: c:ada double-clicks a shape on the canvas in /decks/<id> and types 'Step 1'. The shape shows the text, and the deck JSON shows that shape element's text as 'Step 1'.

requirements.requirement: A Carbon can add a table with a chosen number of rows and columns to a slide.
requirements.quote: Carbons edit text, images, shapes, tables, charts and videos directly on the slide, just like in Google Slides or PowerPoint.
requirements.acceptance: c:ada inserts a 3 x 4 table in /decks/<id>. The canvas shows a grid of 3 rows and 4 columns, and the deck JSON has a table element with rows 3 and cols 4.

requirements.requirement: A Carbon can type into a table's cells directly on the slide.
requirements.quote: Carbons edit text, images, shapes, tables, charts and videos directly on the slide, just like in Google Slides or PowerPoint.
requirements.acceptance: c:ada clicks the cell at row 1, column 2 on the canvas in /decks/<id>, types '14', moves to the next cell with Tab and types '21'. The deck JSON shows those texts in cells [1][2] and [1][3].

requirements.requirement: A Carbon can add rows and columns to an existing table.
requirements.quote: Carbons edit text, images, shapes, tables, charts and videos directly on the slide, just like in Google Slides or PowerPoint.
requirements.acceptance: In a filled 2 x 2 table, c:ada inserts a row below row 0 and a column right of column 1 in /decks/<id>. The deck JSON shows rows 3 and cols 3, with the original texts in their (shifted) cells and the new cells empty.

requirements.requirement: A Carbon can delete rows and columns from a table.
requirements.quote: Carbons edit text, images, shapes, tables, charts and videos directly on the slide, just like in Google Slides or PowerPoint.
requirements.acceptance: In a filled 3 x 3 table, c:ada deletes row 1 and column 0 in /decks/<id>. The deck JSON shows rows 2 and cols 2, holding the texts of the remaining cells.

requirements.requirement: A Carbon can add a chart of a chosen type to a slide in the editor.
requirements.quote: Carbons edit text, images, shapes, tables, charts and videos directly on the slide, just like in Google Slides or PowerPoint.
requirements.acceptance: c:ada inserts a column chart in /decks/<id>. A chart shows on the canvas, and the deck JSON has a chart element with chart.type column.

requirements.requirement: A Carbon can edit a chart's data (category labels, series and values) in the editor, and the chart redraws from it.
requirements.quote: Carbons edit text, images, shapes, tables, charts and videos directly on the slide, just like in Google Slides or PowerPoint.
requirements.acceptance: c:ada opens a chart's data in /decks/<id>, renames a label to 'Q4', changes a value from 12 to 30 and adds a second series. The chart on the canvas redraws with the taller bar and two series, and the deck JSON shows the new labels, values and series.

requirements.requirement: A Carbon can change an existing chart's type (for example column to line or pie).
requirements.quote: Carbons edit text, images, shapes, tables, charts and videos directly on the slide, just like in Google Slides or PowerPoint.
requirements.acceptance: c:ada switches a column chart to line, then to pie, in /decks/<id>. The canvas redraws each time, and the deck JSON shows chart.type line, then pie, with the same data.

requirements.requirement: A Carbon can add a video to a slide in the editor, from a file or from a link.
requirements.quote: Carbons edit text, images, shapes, tables, charts and videos directly on the slide, just like in Google Slides or PowerPoint.
requirements.acceptance: c:ada inserts an MP4 file and, separately, a video by URL into slide 3 in /decks/<id>. Both show on the canvas as videos, and the deck JSON has two video elements, one with src asset:<id> and one with the URL.

requirements.requirement: A Carbon can set a video's playback options (start by itself, loop, mute) in the editor.
requirements.quote: Carbons edit text, images, shapes, tables, charts and videos directly on the slide, just like in Google Slides or PowerPoint.
requirements.acceptance: c:ada turns on autoplay, loop and mute for a video in /decks/<id>. The deck JSON shows autoplay true, loop true and muted true for that element.

requirements.requirement: A Carbon can delete any element from a slide in the editor, including one a Silicon made.
requirements.quote: Carbons edit text, images, shapes, tables, charts and videos directly on the slide, just like in Google Slides or PowerPoint.
requirements.acceptance: c:ada selects a chart made by si:designer in /decks/<id> and presses Delete. It disappears from the canvas and from `present read <deck> --json`.

requirements.requirement: A Silicon can make a text element through the CLI.
requirements.quote: Silicons can make and change every kind of element through the CLI.
requirements.acceptance: si:designer runs `present add text <deck> 2 'Revenue grew 40%' --x 140 --y 300 --w 1640 --h 200 --size 72 --bold`, which prints the new element id. `present read <deck> --json` shows a text element with that text, that frame and a bold size-72 run, and c:ada sees it on slide 2 in /decks/<id>.

requirements.requirement: A Silicon can make an image element through the CLI, from a local file or a URL.
requirements.quote: Silicons can make and change every kind of element through the CLI.
requirements.acceptance: si:designer runs `present add image <deck> 2 team.png --alt Team --fit cover` and `present add image <deck> 2 https://<host>/logo.svg`. `present read <deck> --json` shows two image elements: the first with src asset:<id> (GET /v1/assets/<id> returns the file's bytes) and the second with the URL. Both show on slide 2 in /decks/<id>.

requirements.requirement: A Silicon can make a shape element through the CLI.
requirements.quote: Silicons can make and change every kind of element through the CLI.
requirements.acceptance: si:designer runs `present add shape <deck> 2 round-rect --text 'Step 1' --fill '#eef1f5' --stroke '#3a5a80'`. `present read <deck> --json` shows a shape element with shape round-rect, text 'Step 1' and that fill and stroke, and it shows on slide 2 in /decks/<id>.

requirements.requirement: A Silicon can make a table element through the CLI.
requirements.quote: Silicons can make and change every kind of element through the CLI.
requirements.acceptance: si:designer runs `present add table <deck> 3 --rows 2 --cols 2 --cell 0,0=Q3 --cell 0,1=Q4 --cell 1,0=10 --cell 1,1=14` and `present add table <deck> 3 --csv numbers.csv`. `present read <deck> --json` shows a 2 x 2 table with those cell texts and a second table matching the CSV. Both show on slide 3 in /decks/<id>.

requirements.requirement: A Silicon can make a chart element through the CLI.
requirements.quote: Silicons can make and change every kind of element through the CLI.
requirements.acceptance: si:designer runs `present add chart <deck> 3 --type column --labels Q1,Q2,Q3,Q4 --series Revenue=10,12,15,21 --title 2026`. `present read <deck> --json` shows a chart element with that type, labels, series and title, and it shows on slide 3 in /decks/<id>.

requirements.requirement: A Silicon can make a video element through the CLI.
requirements.quote: Silicons can make and change every kind of element through the CLI.
requirements.acceptance: si:designer runs `present add video <deck> 3 demo.mp4 --autoplay --muted --loop`. `present read <deck> --json` shows a video element with src asset:<id> and autoplay, muted and loop all true, and it shows on slide 3 in /decks/<id>.

requirements.requirement: A Silicon can make an audio element through the CLI.
requirements.quote: Silicons can make and change every kind of element through the CLI.
requirements.acceptance: si:designer runs `present add audio <deck> 1 intro.mp3 --autoplay`. `present read <deck> --json` shows an audio element with src asset:<id> and autoplay true, and it shows on slide 1 in /decks/<id>.

requirements.requirement: A Silicon can make an HTML element through the CLI.
requirements.quote: Silicons can make and change every kind of element through the CLI.
requirements.acceptance: si:designer runs `present add html <deck> 4 --html w.html --css w.css --js w.js --x 0 --y 0 --w 1920 --h 1080`. `present read <deck> --json` shows an html element whose html, css and js equal the three files, and it shows running on slide 4 in /decks/<id>.

requirements.requirement: A Silicon can change a text element's content and formatting through the CLI, including one a Carbon made.
requirements.quote: Silicons can make and change every kind of element through the CLI.
requirements.acceptance: On a text element c:ada typed in the editor, si:designer runs `present set <deck> <slide> <element> text='New title'`, then `present replace <deck> <slide> <element> --find New --replace Final`. Then si:designer makes 'Final' bold with `present edit <deck> --ops ops.json` (update_element with rich text). `present read <deck> --json` shows 'Final title' with 'Final' bold, and c:ada's open editor shows it.

requirements.requirement: A Silicon can change an image element (its picture, alt text and fit) through the CLI.
requirements.quote: Silicons can make and change every kind of element through the CLI.
requirements.acceptance: On an image c:ada inserted, si:designer runs `present set <deck> <slide> <element> src=<a URL or asset:<id>> alt='New logo' fit=cover`. `present read <deck> --json` shows the new src, alt and fit, and c:ada's editor shows the new picture.

requirements.requirement: A Silicon can change a shape element (its shape, look and text) through the CLI.
requirements.quote: Silicons can make and change every kind of element through the CLI.
requirements.acceptance: On a shape c:ada inserted, si:designer runs `present set <deck> <slide> <element> shape=star style.fill=#2f5bea text=Go`. `present read <deck> --json` shows shape star, the fill and the text, and c:ada's editor shows a blue star reading 'Go'.

requirements.requirement: A Silicon can change a table element (its size and cell text) through the CLI.
requirements.quote: Silicons can make and change every kind of element through the CLI.
requirements.acceptance: On a 2 x 2 table c:ada made, si:designer runs `present set <deck> <slide> <element> rows=3 cols=3` and `present replace <deck> <slide> <element> --field cell:1:1 --find 14 --replace 16`. `present read <deck> --json` shows a 3 x 3 table with the old texts kept and cell [1][1] reading 16, and c:ada's editor shows the same.

requirements.requirement: A Silicon can change a chart element (its type and data) through the CLI.
requirements.quote: Silicons can make and change every kind of element through the CLI.
requirements.acceptance: On a column chart c:ada made, si:designer runs `present set <deck> <slide> <element> chart=<type line, labels Q1-Q4, one series Revenue 3,5,8,13>`. `present read <deck> --json` shows the new type, labels and values, and c:ada's editor shows a line chart.

requirements.requirement: A Silicon can change a video element (its source and playback options) through the CLI.
requirements.quote: Silicons can make and change every kind of element through the CLI.
requirements.acceptance: On a video c:ada inserted, si:designer runs `present set <deck> <slide> <element> src=<asset:<id> of another upload> autoplay=false loop=true muted=false`. `present read <deck> --json` shows the new src and options, and c:ada's editor shows the new video.

requirements.requirement: A Silicon can change an audio element (its source and playback options) through the CLI.
requirements.quote: Silicons can make and change every kind of element through the CLI.
requirements.acceptance: On audio c:ada inserted, si:designer runs `present set <deck> <slide> <element> src=<asset:<id> of another upload> autoplay=true loop=true`. `present read <deck> --json` shows the new src, autoplay true and loop true.

requirements.requirement: A Silicon can change an HTML element's code (HTML, CSS and JS) through the CLI.
requirements.quote: Silicons can make and change every kind of element through the CLI.
requirements.acceptance: On an HTML element on slide 4, si:designer runs `present set <deck> 4 <element> html=@new.html css=@new.css js=@new.js`, then `present replace <deck> 4 <element> --field js --find 'speed = 1' --replace 'speed = 2'`. `present read <deck> --json` shows the new code, and the element in c:ada's open /decks/<id> runs it.

requirements.requirement: A Silicon can delete an element through the CLI, including one a Carbon made.
requirements.quote: Silicons can make and change every kind of element through the CLI.
requirements.acceptance: si:designer runs `present delete <deck> <slide> <element>` on a shape c:ada made. `present read <deck> --json` no longer lists it, and it disappears from c:ada's editor.

requirements.requirement: An HTML element can be a small part of a slide, alongside other elements.
requirements.quote: An HTML element can be a small part of a slide or cover the whole of it.
requirements.acceptance: si:designer adds a 480 x 270 HTML element at (120,120) with `present add html ... --x 120 --y 120 --w 480 --h 270`, next to a text element at (700,120). In /decks/<id> and /decks/<id>/present the HTML element runs inside exactly that box (its frame maps to 120,120 480 x 270 in slide px), and the text element stays visible beside it.

requirements.requirement: An HTML element can cover the whole slide.
requirements.quote: An HTML element can be a small part of a slide or cover the whole of it.
requirements.acceptance: si:designer adds an HTML element with a full-bleed background using `present add html ... --x 0 --y 0 --w 1920 --h 1080`. In /decks/<id>, /decks/<id>/present and on the public link the element's frame covers the slide edge to edge: its rectangle equals the slide's, and no slide background shows at the corners.

requirements.requirement: In the editor, an HTML element renders live: its real HTML and CSS show, not a placeholder or a picture.
requirements.quote: It renders live, animates, and runs its JS, in the editor, in present mode and on a public link alike.
requirements.acceptance:
si:designer adds an HTML element with

Live

, CSS giving #t background #2f5bea and an infinite @keyframes rotation, and JS that writes an increasing counter into #n every 100 ms. c:ada opens /decks/. Playwright finds the h1 'Live' inside the element's frame, with the computed background rgb(47, 91, 234).

requirements.requirement: In the editor, an HTML element's animations run.
requirements.quote: It renders live, animates, and runs its JS, in the editor, in present mode and on a public link alike.
requirements.acceptance: With the same HTML element (CSS rotates #t forever with @keyframes), c:ada opens /decks/<id>. The computed transform of #t inside the frame differs between two reads 300 ms apart, and two screenshots of the element's box differ.

requirements.requirement: In the editor, an HTML element's JS runs.
requirements.quote: It renders live, animates, and runs its JS, in the editor, in present mode and on a public link alike.
requirements.acceptance: With the same HTML element (JS writes a counter into #n every 100 ms), c:ada opens /decks/<id>. The text of #n inside the frame is a number that increases between two reads 500 ms apart.

requirements.requirement: In present mode, an HTML element renders live: its real HTML and CSS show, not a placeholder or a picture.
requirements.quote: It renders live, animates, and runs its JS, in the editor, in present mode and on a public link alike.
requirements.acceptance: c:ada opens /decks/<id>/present on the slide with the same HTML element. Playwright finds the h1 'Live' inside the element's frame, with the computed background rgb(47, 91, 234).

requirements.requirement: In present mode, an HTML element's animations run.
requirements.quote: It renders live, animates, and runs its JS, in the editor, in present mode and on a public link alike.
requirements.acceptance: In /decks/<id>/present on the same slide, the computed transform of #t inside the element's frame differs between two reads 300 ms apart.

requirements.requirement: In present mode, an HTML element's JS runs.
requirements.quote: It renders live, animates, and runs its JS, in the editor, in present mode and on a public link alike.
requirements.acceptance: In /decks/<id>/present on the same slide, the #n counter inside the element's frame increases between two reads 500 ms apart.

requirements.requirement: On a public link, an HTML element renders live: its real HTML and CSS show, not a placeholder or a picture.
requirements.quote: It renders live, animates, and runs its JS, in the editor, in present mode and on a public link alike.
requirements.acceptance: si:designer runs `present public <deck> view`. A signed-out browser opens /decks/<id> with no sign-in prompt and finds the h1 'Live' inside the element's frame, with the computed background rgb(47, 91, 234).

requirements.requirement: On a public link, an HTML element's animations run.
requirements.quote: It renders live, animates, and runs its JS, in the editor, in present mode and on a public link alike.
requirements.acceptance: In the signed-out browser on the public link /decks/<id>, the computed transform of #t inside the element's frame differs between two reads 300 ms apart.

requirements.requirement: On a public link, an HTML element's JS runs.
requirements.quote: It renders live, animates, and runs its JS, in the editor, in present mode and on a public link alike.
requirements.acceptance: In the signed-out browser on the public link /decks/<id>, the #n counter inside the element's frame increases between two reads 500 ms apart.

requirements.requirement: A Carbon can move an HTML element in the editor like any other element: clicking selects it and dragging moves it.
requirements.quote: Carbons can move and resize an HTML element like any other element.
requirements.acceptance: c:ada clicks a running HTML element made by si:designer in /decks/<id>. It gets selected with handles, the same as a shape (its content does not swallow the click). Dragging it 300 slide px right changes its x by 300 in `present read <deck> --json`, and its JS counter keeps counting after the move.

requirements.requirement: A Carbon can resize an HTML element in the editor like any other element, and its content lays out in the new box.
requirements.quote: Carbons can move and resize an HTML element like any other element.
requirements.acceptance: c:ada drags a corner handle of an 800 x 450 HTML element in /decks/<id> to 1200 x 675. The deck JSON shows w 1200 and h 675. Inside the frame, window.innerWidth and innerHeight are 1200 and 675, and the content fills the larger box.

requirements.requirement: A Carbon can edit an HTML element's code (its HTML, CSS and JS) in the web editor, and the element then runs the new code.
requirements.quote: they edit its code
requirements.acceptance: c:ada opens the code of an HTML element made by si:designer in /decks/<id>, changes the HTML text 'Old' to 'New', a CSS colour and a JS constant, and applies the change. The element's frame shows 'New', the new colour and the new JS behaviour, and `present read <deck> --json` shows the new html, css and js.

requirements.requirement: A Carbon can comment on an HTML element.
requirements.quote: comment on it and mention a Silicon
requirements.acceptance: c:ada (editor) comments on a running HTML element in /decks/<id> with the Comment button, and c:bo (commenter) comments on it by clicking it. GET /v1/decks/{id}/threads shows both threads anchored to that element (anchor kind element with its id).

requirements.requirement: A Carbon can get what's inside an HTML element changed by commenting on it and mentioning a Silicon: the mention reaches that Silicon and identifies the element.
requirements.quote: comment on it and mention a Silicon
requirements.acceptance: c:ada comments '@si:designer make the bars blue' on an HTML element in /decks/<id>. The Ting stand-in records one present.mention.received for si:designer, carrying the deck, the slide, the anchor naming that HTML element, and the comment text. si:designer then runs `present set <deck> <slide> <element> css=@blue.css`, and c:ada's open editor shows the element with blue bars.

requirements.requirement: Every HTML element runs in its own sandbox, cut off from the page that shows it, on every page that shows slides.
requirements.quote: Every HTML element runs sandboxed.
requirements.acceptance: A probe HTML element made by si:designer runs in /decks/<id>, /decks/<id>/present, /decks/<id>/presenter, the follow page /p/<presentation> of a presentation c:ada started, and on the public link. In each, its JS finds that window.parent.document and window.top.document throw, that no variable of the page around it is readable, and that the Present site's cookies, localStorage, sessionStorage and IndexedDB are out of reach. Playwright reads the probe's results through its frame.

requirements.requirement: An HTML element can load and use libraries from the internet.
requirements.quote: It can load anything it needs from the internet, like libraries, fonts, images or live data.
requirements.acceptance: si:designer adds an HTML element that loads d3 from https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/d3@7.9.0 with a script tag and draws an SVG bar chart with it. In /decks/<id>, /decks/<id>/present and on the public link, the element's frame contains the SVG bars d3 drew, and `present render <deck> <slide> --at 3000` shows the bars.

requirements.requirement: An HTML element can load fonts from the internet and show its text in them.
requirements.quote: It can load anything it needs from the internet, like libraries, fonts, images or live data.
requirements.acceptance: An HTML element links https://fonts.googleapis.com/css2?family=Pacifico and sets its heading in Pacifico. In /decks/<id>, /decks/<id>/present and on the public link, document.fonts.check('48px Pacifico') is true inside the frame, and the heading's width differs from the same text in the fallback font. `present render <deck> <slide> --at 3000` shows the heading in Pacifico, not the fallback.

requirements.requirement: An HTML element can load images from the internet.
requirements.quote: It can load anything it needs from the internet, like libraries, fonts, images or live data.
requirements.acceptance: An HTML element shows an img whose src is a public https URL. In /decks/<id>, /decks/<id>/present and on the public link, the img inside the frame is complete with naturalWidth > 0, and `present render <deck> <slide> --at 3000` shows the picture's pixels in the element's box.

requirements.requirement: An HTML element can fetch live data from the internet while it runs.
requirements.quote: It can load anything it needs from the internet, like libraries, fonts, images or live data.
requirements.acceptance: An HTML element's JS fetches https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/d3@7.9.0/package.json when it runs and writes the version field into its DOM, turning green on success and red on failure. In /decks/<id>, /decks/<id>/present and on the public link the frame shows 7.9.0 on green, and `present render <deck> <slide> --at 3000` shows the element green.

requirements.requirement: An HTML element can never find out who is viewing it: no c:id or si:id, name, email, pfp, account uuid, session or token of the viewer is reachable from its code.
requirements.quote: it can never see or act as the Carbon or Silicon viewing it
requirements.acceptance: A probe HTML element collects these into its own DOM: document.cookie, storage, window.name, location, document.referrer, every readable parent or top property, the answers to credentialed fetches of /auth/session and /api/v1/me (relative and absolute to the web origin), and any replies to postMessage requests to its parent. c:ada signs in and opens the slide in /decks/<id> and /decks/<id>/present. Through the probe's frame, Playwright finds none of c:ada's uuid, 'c:ada', display name, email, pfp URL or any token, and the credentialed fetches got no account data.

requirements.requirement: An HTML element can never act as the Carbon or Silicon viewing it: nothing it sends is done with the viewer's identity or rights.
requirements.quote: it can never see or act as the Carbon or Silicon viewing it
requirements.acceptance: c:ada (editor) has the slide open in /decks/<id> and is presenting it at /decks/<id>/present. Meanwhile a probe HTML element sends credentialed requests to create a thread (POST /api/v1/decks/<id>/threads), push a Yjs update (/updates), apply ops (/edits), invite someone (/access) and make the deck public (PUT /public). It sends each one both as JSON and as a CORS-simple request (a text/plain fetch, a form post). It also posts messages to its parent and top that imitate the app's own (such as next slide). Read afterwards as the owner through the service: there is no new thread or comment; the deck version, access list and public mode are unchanged; GET /v1/presentations/{p} shows the same slide and step.

requirements.requirement: An HTML element can never reach the viewer's Silicon Accounts account: it cannot get their tokens, or make requests as them to Silicon Accounts or to the site's sign-in routes.
requirements.quote: never reach their account, their device or the rest of the deck
requirements.acceptance: With c:ada signed in at /decks/<id>, a probe HTML element sends credentialed requests to the Silicon Accounts test stack's session and profile endpoints and to the web's /auth/session, /auth/refresh and /auth/sign-out. Playwright request interception shows that none of the frame's requests carries c:ada's cookies or an Authorization header, and the probe reads no account data. Afterwards c:ada is still signed in (reloading /decks/<id> opens it as c:ada) and their Accounts sessions are unchanged.

requirements.requirement: An HTML element can never reach the viewer's device: camera, microphone, location, clipboard, notifications, local files and hardware are all out of its reach.
requirements.quote: never reach their account, their device or the rest of the deck
requirements.acceptance: A Playwright context grants camera, microphone, geolocation, clipboard-read and notifications to the Present web origin. In it, c:ada opens a slide whose probe HTML element calls getUserMedia (video and audio), geolocation.getCurrentPosition, navigator.clipboard.readText, Notification.requestPermission, the USB, Bluetooth, serial and HID requestDevice calls, and fetch('file:///etc/hosts'). This runs in /decks/<id>, /decks/<id>/present and on the public link. Every call is refused or unavailable, no permission prompt appears, and the probe gets no data.

requirements.requirement: An HTML element can never reach the rest of the deck: it cannot read or change other elements, other slides, speaker notes, comments or other HTML elements.
requirements.quote: never reach their account, their device or the rest of the deck
requirements.acceptance: In a private deck, slide 2 holds probe HTML element A, a second HTML element B (with a secret string in its DOM and in a global), a text element, speaker notes and an open thread; slide 3 holds an image asset. c:ada opens slide 2 in /decks/<id> and /decks/<id>/present. A tries: the parent and top documents; parent.frames[n] documents and globals, to reach B; a BroadcastChannel and storage shared with B; the Present site's IndexedDB, where the editor keeps the deck; credentialed requests to /api/v1/decks/<id>/content, /threads and /live, and to the image's /api/v1/assets/<id>. A's report shows it reached none of the secret, the text, the notes, the comment or the image. B, the text, the notes and the thread are unchanged, and the deck version is the same.

requirements.requirement: An HTML element never draws outside its own box on the slide.
requirements.quote: never run outside its own box on the slide
requirements.acceptance: A 400 x 300 probe HTML element at (200,200) adds position:fixed with inset -2000px and a red background, a 4000 px wide child at negative offsets, and a 2000 px red box-shadow. Screenshots of /decks/<id>, /decks/<id>/present and the public link, and `present render <deck> <slide>`, show red only inside the element's box. Every pixel outside the box, on the slide and in the editor around it, matches the same slide without the probe's overflow CSS.

requirements.requirement: An HTML element can never navigate or reload the page it is shown on.
requirements.quote: never run outside its own box on the slide
requirements.acceptance: In /decks/<id>, /decks/<id>/present and on the public link, a probe HTML element runs top.location = 'https://example.com', window.open('https://example.com', '_top') and parent.location.reload(). After c:ada clicks inside it, it also follows an <a target=_top> link. The page URL stays the same, no reload happens, and the editor or presentation keeps working.

requirements.requirement: An HTML element can never open browser dialogs over the page (alert, confirm, prompt or print).
requirements.quote: never run outside its own box on the slide
requirements.acceptance: A probe HTML element calls alert(), confirm(), prompt() and print() on load and again after a click inside it, in /decks/<id>, /decks/<id>/present and on the public link. Playwright's dialog event never fires, no print dialog opens, and the page keeps responding (in present mode the next-slide key still works).

requirements.requirement: An HTML element can never take the whole screen for itself (fullscreen).
requirements.quote: never run outside its own box on the slide
requirements.acceptance: After c:ada clicks inside a probe HTML element, it calls document.documentElement.requestFullscreen(). In /decks/<id> and on the public link the call is refused and the page's document.fullscreenElement stays null. In /decks/<id>/present, which is already full screen, the page's fullscreen element is still the presentation, not the element's frame.

requirements.requirement: HTML elements stay sandboxed when the converter renders or exports a slide. There too, an element cannot read the rest of the deck, see or act as the Carbon or Silicon who asked, read the host's files, or navigate the render page away.
requirements.quote: Every HTML element runs sandboxed.
requirements.acceptance: Slide 2 of a deck holds a probe HTML element next to other elements and an image. si:designer runs `present render <deck> 2 --at 3000 -o s2.png` and `present export <deck> --format pdf`. The probe turns green only if all of these hold: reading the parent or top document fails; it finds no other element's content, signed asset URL, token or identity; credentialed fetches to the service's /v1/decks/<id>/content and the converter's /render return no deck data; fetch('file:///etc/passwd') fails. It also tries top.location = 'https://example.com'. s2.png and page 2 of the PDF show slide 2 with the probe green.

requirements.requirement: A new slide can be added with a chosen layout (for example title, title and body, or blank), and it comes with that layout's placeholders in place.
requirements.quote: Every deck has what people expect: layouts
requirements.acceptance: c:ada adds a slide with the title-and-body layout in /decks/<id>; it appears with a title box and a body box ready to type into. si:designer runs `present slide add <deck> --layout two-columns --title Plan --body Hire --right Ship`. `present read <deck> --json` shows a slide with layout two-columns holding a title and two column text boxes with those texts, arranged as the layout prescribes.

requirements.requirement: An existing slide's layout can be changed: the slide is rearranged into the new layout and keeps its content.
requirements.quote: Every deck has what people expect: layouts
requirements.acceptance: c:ada switches a filled title-and-body slide to two columns in /decks/<id>; it is rearranged into two columns and all its title and body text is still there. si:designer runs `present slide layout <deck> <slide> title-only` on another filled slide. `present read <deck> --json` shows layout title-only, the slide arranged as title-only, and none of its text lost.

requirements.requirement: A deck's theme (fonts and colours) styles all its slides, and choosing another theme restyles every slide at once.
requirements.quote: themes and masters
requirements.acceptance: On a 3-slide deck, c:ada picks another theme in /decks/<id>: the backgrounds, text colours and fonts of all three slides change at once, in the editor and in /decks/<id>/present. si:designer runs `present theme <deck> Ink`. `present read <deck> --json` shows the new theme, and /decks/<id>/present shows every slide in it.

requirements.requirement: A deck has a master: an element placed on it, such as a logo or footer, appears on every slide.
requirements.quote: themes and masters
requirements.acceptance: c:ada opens the master in /decks/<id> and adds a footer text. It appears on every existing slide and on a slide added afterwards, in the editor and in /decks/<id>/present. si:designer runs `present add image <deck> 1 logo.png --master`, and the logo appears on every slide as well.

requirements.requirement: Changing an element on the master changes it on every slide at once.
requirements.quote: themes and masters
requirements.acceptance: c:ada edits the master footer's text and moves it once in /decks/<id>; every slide shows the new text in the new place. si:designer runs `present set <deck> master <footer element> text=Confidential`, and every slide shows 'Confidential'.

requirements.requirement: A slide can be given a transition (an effect and a duration), and it can be changed or removed.
requirements.quote: slide transitions
requirements.acceptance: c:ada sets a 500 ms fade on slide 2 in /decks/<id>. si:designer runs `present slide transition <deck> 3 push --duration 600 --direction left`, then `present slide transition <deck> 2 none`. `present read <deck> --json` shows slide 3's push transition and no transition on slide 2.

requirements.requirement: When presenting, moving to a slide plays that slide's transition.
requirements.quote: slide transitions
requirements.acceptance: Slide 2 has a 1000 ms fade. In /decks/<id>/present, advancing from slide 1 to slide 2 gives a frame about 500 ms in where slide 2 is partly faded in over slide 1, then slide 2 alone. Advancing to a slide with no transition shows it at once.

requirements.requirement: When presenting, a slide's element animations play in their set order as the presenter advances.
requirements.quote: element animations
requirements.acceptance: Slide 2 has element A (fade, first, on click) and element B (fly-in, second, on click). In /decks/<id>/present, neither A nor B is visible on entering slide 2. The first advance fades A in, the second flies B in, and the third moves to slide 3.

requirements.requirement: Every slide has speaker notes that can be written and changed.
requirements.quote: speaker notes
requirements.acceptance: c:ada types notes under slide 2 in /decks/<id>. si:designer runs `present slide notes <deck> 3 'Pause here'` and `present replace <deck> 2 --field notes --find <a word c:ada typed> --replace <another word>`. `present slide notes <deck> 2` and `present read <deck>` show both slides' notes as changed, and c:ada's editor shows slide 3's notes.

requirements.requirement: The editor has a slide sorter that shows all of a deck's slides at once, as thumbnails in order.
requirements.quote: a slide sorter
requirements.acceptance: c:ada opens the slide sorter for a 12-slide deck in /decks/<id>. Twelve numbered thumbnails show in deck order, each showing its slide's content.

requirements.requirement: Slides can be reordered by dragging them in the slide sorter, and a Silicon can reorder them through the CLI.
requirements.quote: a slide sorter
requirements.acceptance: c:ada drags slide 5 to second place in the sorter; `present read <deck> --json` shows it second. si:designer runs `present slide move <deck> 2 --after 6`, and c:ada's sorter shows the new order.

requirements.requirement: A slide can be marked as skipped and unmarked. A skipped slide stays in the deck and is shown as skipped in the editor.
requirements.quote: skipped slides
requirements.acceptance: c:ada marks slide 3 as skipped in /decks/<id>; it stays in the slide list and the sorter with a visible skipped mark. si:designer runs `present slide skip <deck> 4`, then `present slide skip <deck> 4 --off`. `present read <deck> --json` shows skipped true on slide 3 and false on slide 4.

requirements.requirement: When presenting, skipped slides are passed over.
requirements.quote: skipped slides
requirements.acceptance: With slide 3 skipped, advancing in /decks/<id>/present from slide 2 shows slide 4 next, and going back from slide 4 shows slide 2.

requirements.requirement: A named section can be started at any slide, and the slide list and sorter show slides grouped under their section names.
requirements.quote: sections
requirements.acceptance: c:ada starts a section named Results at slide 4 in /decks/<id>; the slide list and sorter show a Results heading before slide 4. si:designer runs `present slide section <deck> 7 Appendix`. `present read <deck> --json` shows the sections on slides 4 and 7, and c:ada's sorter shows an Appendix heading before slide 7.

requirements.requirement: A section can be renamed.
requirements.quote: sections
requirements.acceptance: c:ada renames Results to Outcomes in /decks/<id>; si:designer renames Appendix with `present slide section <deck> 7 Extras`. `present read <deck> --json` and the sorter show the new names.

requirements.requirement: A section can be removed, leaving its slides where they are.
requirements.quote: sections
requirements.acceptance: c:ada removes the Outcomes section in /decks/<id>, and si:designer runs `present slide section <deck> 7 --clear`. Both headings disappear from the sorter, every slide is still there in the same order, and `present read <deck> --json` shows no section on slides 4 and 7.

requirements.requirement: While an element is dragged in the editor, guides show when it lines up with another element's edge or centre, or with the slide's centre.
requirements.quote: guides and snapping
requirements.acceptance: c:ada drags a shape in /decks/<id> until its left edge is within a few px of another element's left edge; a guide line shows along that edge. Dragging it near the slide's horizontal centre shows a centre guide. Both disappear on release.

requirements.requirement: A dragged element snaps into line with those guides.
requirements.quote: guides and snapping
requirements.acceptance: c:ada drops a shape 3 px off another element's left edge in /decks/<id>; `present read <deck> --json` shows its x exactly equal to that element's x. Dropped 3 px off the slide's centre, it is exactly centred (x = (1920 - w) / 2).

requirements.requirement: A table shows on its slide as a grid of its rows and columns, with each cell's text, in the editor and when presenting.
requirements.quote: tables, charts, video and audio
requirements.acceptance: si:designer adds a 3 x 3 table with a text in every cell through `present add table`. c:ada sees a 3 x 3 grid with each text in its own cell, in /decks/<id> and in /decks/<id>/present.

requirements.requirement: A chart is drawn from its data as its chart type, in the editor and when presenting.
requirements.quote: tables, charts, video and audio
requirements.acceptance: si:designer adds a column chart (labels Q1-Q4, values 10,12,15,21) and a pie chart with `present add chart`. In /decks/<id> and /decks/<id>/present, c:ada sees four labelled columns rising in that order, and a pie with one slice per label.

requirements.requirement: A video on a slide plays, in the editor and when presenting.
requirements.quote: video and audio
requirements.acceptance: c:ada plays a video (added by si:designer with `present add video`) in /decks/<id>; its media currentTime advances. In /decks/<id>/present it plays when clicked.

requirements.requirement: A video's playback options take effect when presenting: autoplay starts it by itself, mute silences it, and loop restarts it at the end.
requirements.quote: video and audio
requirements.acceptance: In /decks/<id>/present, a short video with autoplay, mute and loop set starts as soon as its slide shows (no click), its media element is muted, and after its end it plays again. A video with none of these set waits for a click and stops at its end.

requirements.requirement: A Carbon can add audio to a slide in the editor.
requirements.quote: video and audio
requirements.acceptance: c:ada inserts an MP3 into slide 1 in /decks/<id>. It shows on the slide as audio, and the deck JSON has an audio element whose src is an asset served by /api/v1/assets/<id>.

requirements.requirement: Audio on a slide plays when presenting, on click or by itself when set to autoplay.
requirements.quote: video and audio
requirements.acceptance: In /decks/<id>/present, clicking the audio on slide 1 plays it (its currentTime advances). Audio added by si:designer with `present add audio <deck> 2 intro.mp3 --autoplay` starts by itself when slide 2 shows.

requirements.requirement: Text can be linked to a web address, and clicking it when presenting opens that address.
requirements.quote: links
requirements.acceptance: c:ada selects a word in a text box in /decks/<id> and links it to https://example.com/a. si:designer links a word of another text element to https://example.com/b with `present edit <deck> --ops ops.json` (a text run carrying the link). The deck JSON shows both links on their runs, and clicking each word in /decks/<id>/present opens its address in a new tab.

requirements.requirement: A whole element can be linked to a web address, and clicking it when presenting opens that address.
requirements.quote: links
requirements.acceptance: c:ada links a shape to https://example.com/c in /decks/<id>; si:designer runs `present set <deck> <slide> <image element> link=https://example.com/d`. Clicking each element in /decks/<id>/present opens its address in a new tab.

requirements.requirement: Text or an element can be linked to another slide of the deck, and clicking it when presenting jumps to that slide.
requirements.quote: links
requirements.acceptance: c:ada links a word to slide 5 in /decks/<id> by picking it from the deck's slides; si:designer runs `present set <deck> <slide> <element> link=slide:<slide 6 id>`. In /decks/<id>/present, clicking the word shows slide 5 and clicking the element shows slide 6.

requirements.requirement: A Carbon can find text across the whole deck (text boxes, shapes and table cells), seeing how many matches there are and moving from one match to the next.
requirements.quote: find and replace
requirements.acceptance: In a deck where 'Q3' appears in a text box on slide 1, a shape on slide 2 and a table cell on slide 4, c:ada opens find in /decks/<id> and types Q3. The editor shows 3 matches, and next/previous goes to each in turn, switching slides and highlighting the match.

requirements.requirement: A single match can be replaced on its own.
requirements.quote: find and replace
requirements.acceptance: c:ada replaces only the current Q3 match (in slide 2's shape) with Q4; the deck JSON shows slide 2's text changed and the other two untouched. si:designer runs `present replace <deck> 1 <element> --find Q3 --replace Q4`, and only that passage changes.

requirements.requirement: All matches can be replaced at once.
requirements.quote: find and replace
requirements.acceptance: c:ada uses replace all for Q3 to Q4 in /decks/<id>; every occurrence in the deck (text box, shape, table cell) reads Q4 in the deck JSON. si:designer runs `present replace <deck> <slide> --find 2025 --replace 2026 --all`, and every occurrence on that slide changes.

requirements.requirement: Changes can be undone.
requirements.quote: and undo
requirements.acceptance: In /decks/<id>, c:ada moves a shape, then types a word, then presses Cmd/Ctrl+Z twice (or uses the undo control). First the word is undone, then the move, and the deck JSON matches the state before both. si:designer undoes its own last change through the CLI (`present undo-account <deck> si:designer --since <the version before it>`), and `present read <deck> --json` is back to how it was before that change.

requirements.requirement: An undone change can be redone.
requirements.quote: and undo
requirements.acceptance: After undoing a move in /decks/<id>, c:ada presses Cmd/Ctrl+Shift+Z (or uses the redo control). The deck JSON shows the shape back at the moved position.

requirements.requirement: Undo in the editor takes back only the undoing Carbon's own changes, never changes others made meanwhile.
requirements.quote: and undo
requirements.acceptance: c:ada changes a title in /decks/<id>. Then si:designer changes another element with `present set`, and c:bo changes a third in a second browser. c:ada presses Cmd/Ctrl+Z. The deck JSON shows c:ada's title change undone, while si:designer's and c:bo's changes remain.

requirements.requirement: Opening a PowerPoint .pptx file creates a new deck from it.
requirements.quote: Silicon Present opens every kind of slides and every kind of asset. Opening a file creates a new deck from it
requirements.acceptance: A Silicon runs `present open board.pptx --json` on a 5-slide .pptx saved by PowerPoint (service: POST /v1/imports with X-Filename board.pptx): it exits 0 and prints a deck id that was not in `present list --json` before and is there now, owned by that Silicon, while every existing deck keeps its version; `present read <id>` shows 5 slides in the source order, each with its title text. A Carbon picking the same file with 'Open a file' on /decks lands on /decks/<new id> showing the same 5 slides.

requirements.requirement: Opening a PowerPoint 97-2003 .ppt file creates a new deck from it.
requirements.quote: Silicon Present opens every kind of slides and every kind of asset. Opening a file creates a new deck from it
requirements.acceptance: A Silicon runs `present open legacy.ppt` on a 5-slide binary .ppt (saved as PowerPoint 97-2003): it exits 0, a new deck it owns appears in `present list`, and `present read <id>` shows 5 slides in the source order with their titles. A Carbon picking the same file with 'Open a file' on /decks gets the same deck at /decks/<new id>.

requirements.requirement: Opening a Keynote .key file creates a new deck from it.
requirements.quote: Silicon Present opens every kind of slides and every kind of asset. Opening a file creates a new deck from it
requirements.acceptance: A Silicon runs `present open talk.key` on a 4-slide deck saved by current Keynote: it exits 0, a new deck appears in `present list`, and `present read <id>` shows 4 slides in order with their titles. A Carbon picking the same file with 'Open a file' on /decks (the browser may send it with an empty content type) gets the same deck.

requirements.requirement: Opening an OpenDocument .odp file creates a new deck from it.
requirements.quote: Silicon Present opens every kind of slides and every kind of asset. Opening a file creates a new deck from it
requirements.acceptance: A Silicon runs `present open plan.odp` on a 4-slide .odp saved by LibreOffice Impress: it exits 0, a new deck appears in `present list`, and `present read <id>` shows 4 slides in order with their titles. A Carbon picking the same file with 'Open a file' on /decks gets the same deck.

requirements.requirement: Opening a PDF file creates a new deck from it.
requirements.quote: Silicon Present opens every kind of slides and every kind of asset. Opening a file creates a new deck from it
requirements.acceptance: A Silicon runs `present open report.pdf` on a 6-page PDF: it exits 0 and a new deck with 6 slides appears in `present list`; `present render <id> <n>` of each slide looks like page n rasterised by `pdftoppm` (same content in the same place). A Carbon picking the PDF with 'Open a file' on /decks sees the same 6 slides in the editor.

requirements.requirement: Opening a web page (.html) file creates a new deck from it.
requirements.quote: Silicon Present opens every kind of slides and every kind of asset. Opening a file creates a new deck from it
requirements.acceptance: A Silicon runs `present open page.html` on a standalone page (a styled heading and a script): it exits 0 and a new deck appears in `present list` whose slide shows the page in `present render <id> 1`. A Carbon picking the same file with 'Open a file' on /decks gets the same deck.

requirements.requirement: Opening a .png image creates a new deck from it.
requirements.quote: Silicon Present opens every kind of slides and every kind of asset. Opening a file creates a new deck from it
requirements.acceptance: A Silicon runs `present open photo.png` (3000x2000): it exits 0 and makes a new deck whose slide holds an image element with src asset:<id> (`present read <id> --json`), and `present render <id> 1` shows the whole picture. A Carbon picking photo.png with 'Open a file' on /decks gets the same deck.

requirements.requirement: Opening a .jpg image creates a new deck from it.
requirements.quote: Silicon Present opens every kind of slides and every kind of asset. Opening a file creates a new deck from it
requirements.acceptance: A Silicon runs `present open photo.jpg` (and the same file named photo.jpeg): each exits 0 and makes a new deck whose slide holds an image element with src asset:<id>, and `present render <id> 1` shows the whole picture. A Carbon picking photo.jpg with 'Open a file' on /decks gets the same deck.

requirements.requirement: Slide files of other kinds than those in the table also open as new decks, e.g. PowerPoint shows, templates and macro-enabled decks (.ppsx, .pps, .potx, .pptm) and OpenDocument templates (.otp).
requirements.quote: Silicon Present opens every kind of slides
requirements.acceptance: For fixtures deck.ppsx, deck.pps, deck.potx, deck.pptm and deck.otp (3 titled slides each), a Silicon runs `present open <file>`: each exits 0 with no unsupported-format error and makes a new deck whose `present read` shows the 3 slides in order with their titles. The 'Open a file' picker on /decks accepts each of these files and gives a Carbon the same deck.

requirements.requirement: A Google Slides deck can be opened through its export: opening the file Google Slides exports (e.g. its .pptx download) creates a new deck from it.
requirements.quote: Google Slides decks are opened through their export.
requirements.acceptance: Fixture: a deck made in Google Slides (a title slide, a bulleted slide, a slide with an image and a table, a skipped slide, speaker notes) saved with File > Download > Microsoft PowerPoint (.pptx). A Silicon runs `present open gslides.pptx`: it exits 0 and makes a new deck whose `present read` shows every slide in order with its text, the image, the table cells and the notes, with the skipped slide marked skipped. A Carbon picking the same export with 'Open a file' on /decks gets the same deck.

requirements.requirement: Image files of other kinds than .png and .jpg (e.g. .gif, .webp, .avif, .bmp, .tiff, .heic) open as new decks.
requirements.quote: Silicon Present opens every kind of slides and every kind of asset. Opening a file creates a new deck from it
requirements.acceptance: For photo.gif, photo.webp, photo.avif, photo.bmp, photo.tiff and photo.heic, a Silicon runs `present open <file>`: each exits 0 and makes a new deck whose slide shows the whole picture in `present render <id> 1` and in the editor at /decks/<id> (the image loads with a non-zero natural width). A Carbon picking each file with 'Open a file' on /decks gets the same.

requirements.requirement: Opening a video file creates a new deck from it.
requirements.quote: Silicon Present opens every kind of slides and every kind of asset. Opening a file creates a new deck from it
requirements.acceptance: For clip.mp4 (H.264), clip.webm and clip.mov, a Silicon runs `present open <file>`: each exits 0 and makes a new deck whose slide holds a video element with src asset:<id>; in the editor at /decks/<id> the video plays (currentTime advances after play) and `present render <id> 1` shows a frame of it, not an empty box. A Carbon picking each file with 'Open a file' on /decks gets the same.

requirements.requirement: Opening an audio file creates a new deck from it.
requirements.quote: Silicon Present opens every kind of slides and every kind of asset. Opening a file creates a new deck from it
requirements.acceptance: For sound.mp3, sound.wav, sound.m4a and sound.ogg, a Silicon runs `present open <file>`: each exits 0 and makes a new deck whose slide holds an audio element with src asset:<id> that plays in present mode at /decks/<id>/present (currentTime advances). A Carbon picking each file with 'Open a file' on /decks gets the same.

requirements.requirement: Opening an SVG file creates a new deck from it.
requirements.quote: Silicon Present opens every kind of slides and every kind of asset. Opening a file creates a new deck from it
requirements.acceptance: A Silicon runs `present open logo.svg`: it exits 0 and makes a new deck whose slide shows the drawing; `present render <id> 1` matches the SVG rasterised by Chromium at the same size. A Carbon picking logo.svg with 'Open a file' on /decks gets the same deck.

requirements.requirement: Opening an animation file (e.g. an animated GIF, an animated WebP or APNG, or a Lottie file) creates a new deck from it.
requirements.quote: Silicon Present opens every kind of slides and every kind of asset. Opening a file creates a new deck from it
requirements.acceptance: A Silicon runs `present open spinner.gif` (12 frames), `present open wave.webp` (animated) and `present open loader.json` (Lottie): each exits 0 and makes a new deck in which the animation plays, i.e. two screenshots of its box in the editor at /decks/<id> taken 500 ms apart differ. A Carbon picking each file with 'Open a file' on /decks gets the same.

requirements.requirement: Opening a font file (e.g. .ttf, .otf, .woff, .woff2) creates a new deck from it that holds the font.
requirements.quote: Silicon Present opens every kind of slides and every kind of asset. Opening a file creates a new deck from it
requirements.acceptance: A Silicon runs `present open Fraunces.ttf`, then `present open Fraunces.woff2`: each exits 0 with no unsupported-format error and makes a new deck in `present list` that holds the font, e.g. `present read <id> --json` shows theme.customFonts with family Fraunces and src asset:<id>, and GET /v1/assets/<id> returns the font. A Carbon picking the same file with 'Open a file' on /decks gets the same.

requirements.requirement: Every opened slide shows everything the source slide shows, in the same place, including its background, theme colours and fonts, and master and layout content such as logos, footers and slide numbers.
requirements.quote: Nothing is dropped on the way in.
requirements.acceptance: For .pptx, .ppt, .key and .odp fixtures whose slides use a master logo and footer, slide numbers, theme colours and fonts, and gradient and picture backgrounds, a Silicon runs `present open <file>` and `present render <id> <n>` for every slide. Against LibreOffice's render of the same slide (`soffice --headless --convert-to pdf`, then `pdftoppm`), every object visible in the reference is visible in the same place, and a Carbon sees the same slides in the editor at /decks/<id>.

requirements.requirement: Text comes in as editable text, not as pictures of text.
requirements.quote: Nothing is dropped on the way in.
requirements.acceptance: For .pptx, .ppt, .key and .odp fixtures with a title 'Q4 review' and a body text box, after `present open` a Silicon runs `present replace <id> 1 --find 'Q4' --replace 'Q1'` and it succeeds (the text is text, not a picture), and `present read <id>` shows 'Q1 review'. A Carbon can click into the body box in the editor at /decks/<id> and type.

requirements.requirement: Text keeps its formatting: font, size, colour, bold, italic, underline, alignment, bullets and numbering, indentation and line spacing.
requirements.quote: Nothing is dropped on the way in.
requirements.acceptance: Fixture .pptx: a text box with bold, italic, underlined and red runs in a named font at a set size, a centred paragraph with 1.5 line spacing, a two-level bulleted list and a numbered list. After `present open`, `present read <id> --json` shows a text element whose runs carry bold, italic, underline, color, size and font as in the source, and whose paragraphs carry align center, lineHeight 1.5, list bullet (indent 1 on the second level) and list ordered.

requirements.requirement: Pictures come in as picture elements of their own.
requirements.quote: Nothing is dropped on the way in.
requirements.acceptance: Fixture .pptx: slide 1 has a text box and two pictures. After `present open`, `present read <id> --json` shows two image elements (src asset:<id>) besides the text element, and `present set <id> 1 <picture id> x=100` moves only that picture.

requirements.requirement: Pictures keep their alt text.
requirements.quote: Nothing is dropped on the way in.
requirements.acceptance: Fixture .pptx with a picture whose alt text is 'Launch day photo'. After `present open`, `present read <id> --json` shows that image element with alt 'Launch day photo'.

requirements.requirement: Shapes come in as shape elements of their own, of the same shape.
requirements.quote: Nothing is dropped on the way in.
requirements.acceptance: Fixture .pptx: a rounded rectangle (fill #2F5BEA, 4 px dark outline, text 'Step 1'), a right arrow and a star. After `present open`, `present read <id> --json` shows three shape elements with shape round-rect, arrow-right and star, the rectangle's style.fill, stroke and strokeWidth as in the source and its text 'Step 1' editable; `present render <id> 1` shows the same shapes as the source.

requirements.requirement: Tables come in as tables, with every cell's text and fill.
requirements.quote: Nothing is dropped on the way in.
requirements.acceptance: Fixture .pptx: a 4 x 3 table with a header row, a filled cell, a bold cell and two merged cells. After `present open`, `present read <id> --json` shows a table element with rows 4, cols 3, headerRow true, every cell's text (the merged cells' text kept) and the filled cell's fill, and `present replace <id> <slide> <table id> --field cell:1:2 --find <old> --replace <new>` edits that one cell.

requirements.requirement: Charts come in as charts, keeping their type, labels and series values.
requirements.quote: Nothing is dropped on the way in.
requirements.acceptance: Fixture .pptx: a native column chart (labels Q1-Q4, series Revenue 10,12,15,21 and Cost 8,9,9,10) and a pie chart. After `present open`, `present read <id> --json` shows chart elements of type column and pie with exactly those labels, series names and values, and `present render` draws both.

requirements.requirement: Video embedded in a slide file comes in and plays.
requirements.quote: Nothing is dropped on the way in.
requirements.acceptance: Fixture .pptx with an embedded 30 s .mp4 on slide 2. After `present open`, `present read <id> --json` shows a video element on slide 2 whose asset (GET /v1/assets/<id>) is that video at its full 30 s, and it plays in present mode at /decks/<id>/present.

requirements.requirement: Audio embedded in a slide file comes in and plays.
requirements.quote: Nothing is dropped on the way in.
requirements.acceptance: Fixture .pptx with an embedded 20 s .mp3 on slide 3. After `present open`, `present read <id> --json` shows an audio element on slide 3 whose asset is that audio at its full 20 s, and it plays in present mode at /decks/<id>/present.

requirements.requirement: Speaker notes come in.
requirements.quote: Nothing is dropped on the way in.
requirements.acceptance: Fixtures .pptx, .ppt, .key and .odp whose slide 1 has the notes 'Pause here' and slide 2 two lines of notes. After `present open`, `present read <id>` shows those notes on those slides word for word, and the presenter view at /decks/<id>/presenter shows them.

requirements.requirement: Hidden slides come in as skipped slides.
requirements.quote: Nothing is dropped on the way in.
requirements.acceptance: Fixture .pptx with slide 3 hidden, and a .key with a skipped slide. After `present open`, `present read <id> --json` still has that slide, with skipped true.

requirements.requirement: Sections come in.
requirements.quote: Nothing is dropped on the way in.
requirements.acceptance: Fixture .pptx with sections 'Intro' (slides 1-2) and 'Results' (slides 3-5). After `present open`, `present read <id> --json` shows section 'Intro' on slide 1 and section 'Results' on slide 3.

requirements.requirement: Slide transitions come in, none lost, even one with no exact equivalent.
requirements.quote: Nothing is dropped on the way in.
requirements.acceptance: Fixture .pptx: slide 2 fades over 500 ms, slide 3 pushes from the left, slide 4 uses Vortex. After `present open`, `present read <id> --json` shows a fade of 500 ms on slide 2, a push from the left on slide 3 and a non-null transition on slide 4, and present mode plays them.

requirements.requirement: Element animations come in, none lost, even one with no exact equivalent.
requirements.quote: Nothing is dropped on the way in.
requirements.acceptance: Fixture .pptx: the title fades in on click, a picture flies in from the left after the previous one, a shape uses a Bounce entrance. After `present open`, `present read <id> --json` shows animation effect fade with trigger click on the title, fly-in with trigger after-previous and direction left on the picture, and a non-null animation on the shape, in that order; present mode plays them.

requirements.requirement: Links come in, both to web addresses and to other slides.
requirements.quote: Nothing is dropped on the way in.
requirements.acceptance: Fixture .pptx: a text run linked to https://example.com and a shape linked to slide 4. After `present open`, `present read <id> --json` shows the run with link https://example.com and the shape with link slide:<slide 4 id>, and clicking the shape in present mode goes to slide 4.

requirements.requirement: Grouped objects come in still grouped, so they move together.
requirements.quote: Nothing is dropped on the way in.
requirements.acceptance: Fixture .pptx: an icon and a label grouped together. After `present open`, `present read <id> --json` shows both elements with the same non-null group id, and dragging one in the editor at /decks/<id> moves both.

requirements.requirement: Every element keeps its position, size, rotation and front-to-back order.
requirements.quote: Nothing is dropped on the way in.
requirements.acceptance: Fixture .pptx: three overlapping shapes, the middle one rotated 30 degrees. After `present open`, `present read <id> --json` lists them back to front in the source order, with x, y, w and h equal to the source converted to slide px (within 1 px), and rotation 30 on the middle one.

requirements.requirement: The new deck keeps the source's slide size and aspect ratio (a 4:3 deck stays 4:3).
requirements.quote: Nothing is dropped on the way in.
requirements.acceptance: A 4:3 .pptx and a 4:3 PDF. After `present open`, `present read <id> --json` shows a size whose width/height is 4/3, and `present render <id> 1` gives a 4:3 image with nothing cut off.

requirements.requirement: Fonts embedded in the source file come in, so text keeps its typeface.
requirements.quote: Nothing is dropped on the way in.
requirements.acceptance: A .pptx whose title uses a font embedded in the file and not installed on the machine. After `present open`, the deck holds that font (e.g. an entry in theme.customFonts with an asset) and `present render <id> 1` shows the title in that typeface, matching a reference render made with the font installed rather than a fallback font.

requirements.requirement: Comments in the source file come in as comments on the same slides, keeping their text and their original author's name.
requirements.quote: Nothing is dropped on the way in.
requirements.acceptance: A .pptx with two review comments on slide 2, one by 'Ada' reading 'Needs a source'. After `present open`, `present comments <id>` (GET /v1/decks/<id>/threads) lists threads on slide 2 including 'Needs a source', with 'Ada' kept as its original author's name.

critic.problem: It doesn't say which Carbon or Silicon an imported comment belongs to. 'every change and every comment always has a Carbon or Silicon behind it', and SHR-76's 'no comment lacks an author', mean an imported comment can't be left without an author or credited only to the name in the file.
critic.fix: Require each imported comment to be authored by the account that opened the file, shown by its c:id or si:id in the web, in `present comments` and in the API. The author name from the file ('Ada') is kept as text on the comment. No comment may have a null author.

requirements.requirement: Anything the deck can't hold as one of its own element kinds (e.g. SmartArt, 3D models, ink, WordArt effects, equations, embedded objects) still comes in, looking the same in the same place, for example as a picture of it.
requirements.quote: Nothing is dropped on the way in.
requirements.acceptance: A .pptx with a SmartArt diagram, an ink drawing, a 3D model and an equation. After `present open`, `present read <id> --json` shows an element covering each one's original frame, and `present render <id> <n>` shows each part as LibreOffice's render of that slide does; no area that shows content in the reference is empty.

requirements.requirement: Opening a PDF keeps each page's text as text that can be read and searched, not only as a picture.
requirements.quote: Nothing is dropped on the way in.
requirements.acceptance: A 3-page PDF whose page 2 says 'Quarterly revenue grew 40%'. After `present open report.pdf`, `present read <id>` shows that sentence on slide 2 (in an element or its notes), and `present search 'Quarterly revenue grew'` (GET /v1/search) returns the new deck.

critic.problem: Its check relies on `present search` and GET /v1/search, which UNDERSTANDING.md doesn't include. It also passes when the page text is only in the speaker notes, which leaves a deck made from a PDF where a Silicon can't change any visible text, against 'every deck has to be a comfortable place for a Silicon to work' (INTRO-23).
critic.fix: Check with the web's find (SLD-106), `present read` and a `present replace` on that slide. Require the page text to be on the slide as text, in its original place. If it is only in the notes, record that as an open question for a Carbon, not as a pass.

requirements.requirement: A web page opened as a deck keeps all its HTML, CSS and JS, so it renders and runs live as it does in a browser.
requirements.quote: Nothing is dropped on the way in.
requirements.acceptance: A Silicon runs `present open page.html` on a page with a heading styled by an inline <style> and a <script> that writes a counter into the page every 500 ms. In the editor at /decks/<id> and in present mode the heading has its styling and the counter keeps rising, and `present render <id> 1 --at 3000` shows the styled heading with a counter of at least 5.

requirements.requirement: A file opened as a deck is kept whole: an image at full resolution and uncropped, a video or audio file at full length, an animation with every frame, an SVG as SVG.
requirements.quote: Nothing is dropped on the way in.
requirements.acceptance: A Silicon runs `present open` on a 4000x3000 PNG, a 30 s .mp4, a 60 s .mp3, a 24-frame GIF and an SVG: each new deck's asset (GET /v1/assets/<id>) has the source's pixel size, duration or frame count, the SVG is still served as image/svg+xml, and `present render <id> 1` shows the whole image with nothing cropped.

requirements.requirement: Any image can be added to a slide.
requirements.quote: Any image, video, audio, font, SVG or animation can be added to a slide.
requirements.acceptance: A Silicon editor runs `present add image <deck> 2 photo.<ext> --x 100 --y 100 --w 800 --h 600` for .png, .jpg, .gif, .webp, .avif, .bmp, .tiff and .heic: each prints an element id, `present read <deck> --json` shows an image element with src asset:<id>, and the picture shows in its box in `present render <deck> 2` and in the editor at /decks/<deck>. A Carbon editor inserting the same files in the editor sees each one on the slide.

requirements.requirement: Any video can be added to a slide.
requirements.quote: Any image, video, audio, font, SVG or animation can be added to a slide.
requirements.acceptance: A Silicon editor runs `present add video <deck> 3 clip.<ext>` for .mp4, .webm, .mov and .m4v: each adds a video element with src asset:<id> that plays in the editor at /decks/<deck> and in present mode (currentTime advances), and `present render <deck> 3` shows a frame rather than an empty box. A Carbon editor inserting the same files in the editor gets videos that play.

requirements.requirement: Any audio can be added to a slide.
requirements.quote: Any image, video, audio, font, SVG or animation can be added to a slide.
requirements.acceptance: A Silicon editor runs `present add audio <deck> 1 sound.<ext>` for .mp3, .wav, .m4a, .ogg and .flac: each adds an audio element with src asset:<id> that plays in present mode at /decks/<deck>/present (currentTime advances). A Carbon editor inserting the same files in the editor gets the same.

requirements.requirement: Any font can be added and used for text on a slide.
requirements.quote: Any image, video, audio, font, SVG or animation can be added to a slide.
requirements.acceptance: A Silicon editor, using only the present CLI, adds Fraunces.woff2 (then a .ttf and an .otf) to the deck and sets slide 1's title in it: `present read <deck> --json` shows the font in the deck (theme.customFonts with src asset:<id>) and the title runs with font Fraunces, and `present render <deck> 1` shows the title in Fraunces (it differs from the render without the font and matches a reference). A Carbon editor adds the same file in the editor at /decks/<deck>, picks it for a text box and sees that text in Fraunces in the editor and in present mode.

requirements.requirement: Any SVG can be added to a slide.
requirements.quote: Any image, video, audio, font, SVG or animation can be added to a slide.
requirements.acceptance: A Silicon editor runs `present add image <deck> 2 logo.svg` (and again with an https URL of an SVG): each adds an image element whose drawing shows in its box in `present render <deck> 2` and in the editor at /decks/<deck>. A Carbon editor inserting logo.svg in the editor sees it on the slide.

requirements.requirement: Any animation (e.g. an animated GIF, an animated WebP or APNG, or a Lottie file) can be added to a slide and plays there.
requirements.quote: Any image, video, audio, font, SVG or animation can be added to a slide.
requirements.acceptance: A Silicon editor, using only the present CLI (e.g. `present add image <deck> 2 spinner.gif`), adds an animated GIF, an animated WebP or APNG, and a Lottie file to slide 2: in the editor at /decks/<deck> and in present mode, two screenshots of each one's box taken 500 ms apart differ. A Carbon editor inserting the same files in the editor sees them animate.

requirements.requirement: An asset added to a slide is kept whole: images at full resolution, video and audio at full length, animations with every frame, SVGs as SVG, fonts complete.
requirements.quote: Nothing is dropped on the way in.
requirements.acceptance: After a Silicon adds a 4000x3000 JPEG, a 30 s video, a 60 s audio file, a 24-frame GIF, an SVG and a .woff2 with the CLI, and a Carbon adds the same files in the editor, GET /v1/assets/<id> for each returns the original (same sha256) or, where a conversion was needed to show it, a file with the same pixel size, duration or frame count; the SVG is still served as image/svg+xml.

requirements.requirement: Any deck can be downloaded as a PowerPoint .pptx file.
requirements.quote: | PowerPoint      | `.pptx`                        |
requirements.acceptance: The Silicon owning a 3-slide deck (titles, body text, a picture, notes) runs `present export <deck> --format pptx -o d.pptx` (GET /v1/decks/<id>/export?format=pptx): it exits 0, d.pptx is a zip with [Content_Types].xml and ppt/presentation.xml holding 3 slides, and `soffice --headless --convert-to pdf d.pptx` gives 3 pages in slide order. A Carbon choosing Download > PowerPoint (.pptx) in the editor at /decks/<id> gets a .pptx of the same deck.

requirements.requirement: A deck cannot be downloaded as a PowerPoint 97-2003 .ppt file; .ppt only opens.
requirements.quote: Any deck can be downloaded in exactly these formats, and no others:
requirements.acceptance: `present export <deck> --format ppt` is refused by the CLI with the list of formats it takes, and GET /v1/decks/<id>/export?format=ppt answers 400 invalid_format whose hint lists pptx, odp, pdf, txt, png, jpg, svg.
