The Download menu in /decks/<id> has no PowerPoint 97-2003 item. `present open legacy.ppt` still makes a deck.

requirements.requirement: A deck cannot be downloaded as a Keynote .key file; .key only opens.
requirements.quote: For Keynote, download `.pptx` and open it in Keynote.
requirements.acceptance: `present export <deck> --format key` is refused by the CLI with the list of formats it takes, and GET /v1/decks/<id>/export?format=key answers 400 invalid_format. The Download menu in /decks/<id> has no Keynote item; `present docs export` tells a Keynote user to export .pptx and open it in Keynote. `present open d.key` still makes a deck.

requirements.requirement: Any deck can be downloaded as an OpenDocument .odp file.
requirements.quote: | OpenDocument    | `.odp`                         |
requirements.acceptance: The Silicon runs `present export <deck> --format odp -o d.odp`: it exits 0, d.odp is a zip whose mimetype entry is application/vnd.oasis.opendocument.presentation, and LibreOffice converts it to 3 pages in slide order with their text. A Carbon choosing Download > OpenDocument (.odp) in /decks/<id> gets the same.

requirements.requirement: Any deck can be downloaded as a PDF.
requirements.quote: | PDF             | `.pdf`                         |
requirements.acceptance: The Silicon runs `present export <deck> --format pdf -o d.pdf`: it exits 0, d.pdf starts with %PDF and has 3 pages in slide order, each at the deck's aspect ratio (16:9 by default) and looking like `present render <deck> <n>`. A Carbon choosing Download > PDF (.pdf) in /decks/<id> gets the same.

requirements.requirement: A deck cannot be downloaded as a web page (.html); .html only opens.
requirements.quote: Any deck can be downloaded in exactly these formats, and no others:
requirements.acceptance: `present export <deck> --format html` is refused by the CLI with the list of formats it takes, and GET /v1/decks/<id>/export?format=html answers 400 invalid_format. The Download menu in /decks/<id> has no web page item. Opening an .html file still makes a deck.

requirements.requirement: Any deck can be downloaded as .png images (one slide, or a .zip of every slide).
requirements.quote: | Images          | `.png`, `.jpg`, `.svg` (one slide) |
requirements.acceptance: The Silicon runs `present export <deck> --format png -o d.zip` on the 3-slide deck: it exits 0 with a .zip of 3 PNG images in slide order, each decoding as PNG at the deck's aspect ratio (1920x1080 by default) and looking like `present render <deck> <n>`. A Carbon choosing Download > Images (PNG) in /decks/<id> gets the same.

requirements.requirement: Any deck can be downloaded as .jpg images (one slide, or a .zip of every slide).
requirements.quote: | Images          | `.png`, `.jpg`, `.svg` (one slide) |
requirements.acceptance: The Silicon runs `present export <deck> --format jpg -o d.zip` on the 3-slide deck: it exits 0 with a .zip of 3 JPEG images in slide order at the deck's aspect ratio, each looking like `present render <deck> <n>`. A Carbon choosing Download > Images (JPG) in /decks/<id> gets the same.

requirements.requirement: Any deck can be downloaded as plain text (.txt).
requirements.quote: | Plain text      | `.txt`                         |
requirements.acceptance: `present export <deck> --format txt -o d.txt` exits 0 and d.txt holds the text of every slide in order. A Carbon choosing Download > Plain text (.txt) in /decks/<id> gets the same.

requirements.requirement: Any slide can be downloaded as an .svg image.
requirements.quote: | Images          | `.png`, `.jpg`, `.svg` (one slide) |
requirements.acceptance: `present export <deck> --format svg --slide 2 -o s2.svg` exits 0 with one SVG of slide 2; without --slide the converter refuses with slide_required. A Carbon choosing Download > Scalable Vector Graphics (.svg, current slide) in /decks/<id> gets the slide on screen.

requirements.requirement: Every deck can be downloaded in every listed format whatever it holds; no format refuses a deck because of its content.
requirements.quote: any deck can be downloaded in any of these formats
requirements.acceptance: A Silicon builds a deck holding every element kind (text, shapes, images, an SVG, an animated GIF, video, audio, a table, a chart, a full-slide HTML element), a custom font, a skipped slide, sections, transitions, animations, master elements and notes (like fixtures/contract/every-element.json with real assets). For each of pptx, ppt, key, odp, pdf, html, png and jpg, `present export <deck> --format <f>` exits 0 with a valid file of that format (GET /v1/decks/<id>/export answers 200, never an error about unsupported content). The same holds for a deck made with `present open` from a .pptx.

requirements.requirement: Every downloaded slide looks like that slide does in Silicon Present.
requirements.quote: any deck can be downloaded in any of these formats
requirements.acceptance: For a deck holding text, shapes, pictures, a table, a chart, a video, an HTML element and master elements, compare `present render <deck> <n>` with slide n of each download: .pdf, .png and .jpg directly (pdftoppm for the PDF), .pptx, .ppt, .key and .odp through LibreOffice's render, .html through a Chromium screenshot of that slide. Every object visible in Silicon Present is visible in the same place in each.

requirements.requirement: Text is exported as real text wherever the format can hold text: editable text in .pptx and .odp, selectable text in .pdf, and all of it in .txt.
requirements.quote: it's exported as the closest thing that format allows
requirements.acceptance: On a deck whose slide 1 says 'Revenue grew 40%': d.pptx's slide XML holds it as text runs (a:t) that LibreOffice opens as an editable text box; LibreOffice's text export of d.ppt and d.odp and `present open d.key` contain it; `pdftotext d.pdf` contains 'Revenue grew 40%'; in d.html document.body.innerText contains it.

requirements.requirement: Speaker notes are exported into the formats that hold notes: .pptx and .odp.
requirements.quote: it's exported as the closest thing that format allows
requirements.acceptance: Slide 2's notes say 'Pause here': d.pptx has a notes slide for slide 2 containing 'Pause here'; LibreOffice shows it as slide 2's notes in d.ppt and d.odp; `present open d.key` gives slide 2 the notes 'Pause here'.

requirements.requirement: Pictures are exported as picture objects of their own in .pptx, .ppt, .key and .odp, not merged into a whole-slide image.
requirements.quote: it's exported as the closest thing that format allows
requirements.acceptance: A slide with a text box and two pictures: d.pptx's slide has two p:pic elements at the pictures' places plus a text shape; LibreOffice shows two separately selectable pictures in d.ppt and d.odp, and `present open d.key` gives two image elements.

requirements.requirement: Shapes are exported as shapes, with their geometry, fill, outline and text, in .pptx, .ppt, .key and .odp.
requirements.quote: it's exported as the closest thing that format allows
requirements.acceptance: A slide with a round-rect reading 'Step 1' (fill #2F5BEA) and an ellipse: d.pptx has two p:sp with preset geometry roundRect and ellipse, a 2F5BEA fill and the text 'Step 1'; LibreOffice opens them as editable shapes in d.ppt and d.odp, and `present open d.key` gives two shape elements.

requirements.requirement: Tables are exported as tables in .pptx, .ppt, .key and .odp.
requirements.quote: it's exported as the closest thing that format allows
requirements.acceptance: A slide with a 3 x 3 table: d.pptx has an a:tbl with 3 rows, 3 columns and the cell texts; LibreOffice shows it as a table in d.ppt and d.odp, and `present open d.key` gives a table element with the same cells.

requirements.requirement: Charts are exported as charts with their data in .pptx, .ppt, .key and .odp.
requirements.quote: it's exported as the closest thing that format allows
requirements.acceptance: A column chart (labels Q1-Q4, series Revenue 10,12,15,21): d.pptx has a chart part with a column chart holding those categories and values; LibreOffice opens it as a chart with that data in d.ppt and d.odp, and `present open d.key` gives a chart element with the same data.

requirements.requirement: Video and audio are exported as playable media wherever the format can hold media (e.g. .pptx and .html).
requirements.quote: it's exported as the closest thing that format allows
requirements.acceptance: A slide with demo.mp4 and intro.mp3: d.pptx contains both files under ppt/media, attached to that slide as a video and an audio that LibreOffice or PowerPoint plays; in d.html opened from disk with the Present service stopped, the video and the audio play (currentTime advances).

requirements.requirement: Slide transitions are exported in the formats that hold transitions (.pptx, .ppt, .key, .odp and .html).
requirements.quote: it's exported as the closest thing that format allows
requirements.acceptance: Slide 2 fades over 500 ms and slide 3 pushes from the left: d.pptx's slide 2 has a 500 ms fade transition and slide 3 a push; LibreOffice reports those transitions for d.ppt and d.odp; `present open d.key` gives them back; in d.html, moving to slide 2 fades.

requirements.requirement: Element animations are exported in the formats that hold animations (.pptx, .ppt, .key, .odp and .html).
requirements.quote: it's exported as the closest thing that format allows
requirements.acceptance: The title on slide 2 fades in on click: d.pptx's slide 2 has a click-triggered fade entrance on the title's shape; LibreOffice lists that effect for d.ppt and d.odp; `present open d.key` gives it back; in d.html the title appears on the first click or arrow key on slide 2.

requirements.requirement: Skipped slides are exported as hidden slides in the formats that can mark them (.pptx, .ppt, .key, .odp).
requirements.quote: it's exported as the closest thing that format allows
requirements.acceptance: Slide 3 is skipped: d.pptx's slide 3 has its show attribute set to 0; LibreOffice reports slide 3 as hidden in d.ppt and d.odp; `present open d.key` gives slide 3 back skipped.

requirements.requirement: Sections are exported in the formats that hold sections (e.g. .pptx).
requirements.quote: it's exported as the closest thing that format allows
requirements.acceptance: Sections 'Intro' (from slide 1) and 'Results' (from slide 3): d.pptx's presentation.xml has a section list with those two names over those slides, and `present open d.pptx` gives back the same sections.

requirements.requirement: Links to web addresses and to other slides are exported in the formats that hold links (.pptx, .ppt, .key, .odp, .pdf and .html).
requirements.quote: it's exported as the closest thing that format allows
requirements.acceptance: A text run linked to https://example.com and a shape linked to slide 4: d.pptx has a click hyperlink to the URL and a jump to slide 4; d.pdf has a URI link annotation and a link to page 4; in d.html clicking the run opens the URL and clicking the shape shows slide 4; d.ppt, d.odp and d.key (checked through LibreOffice or `present open`) keep both.

requirements.requirement: Text in a custom font keeps that font in every download: drawn in it in .pdf, .png, .jpg and .html, and set in it in .pptx, .ppt, .key and .odp.
requirements.quote: it's exported as the closest thing that format allows
requirements.acceptance: A deck whose title uses the custom font Fraunces (in theme.customFonts): `pdffonts d.pdf` lists Fraunces as embedded; the d.png and d.jpg images and d.html (Present service stopped) show the title in Fraunces, matching `present render`; the title runs in d.pptx, d.ppt, d.odp and d.key name the typeface Fraunces.

requirements.requirement: HTML elements stay live in the web page (.html) download: they render, animate and run their JS.
requirements.quote: it's exported as the closest thing that format allows
requirements.acceptance: A slide with an HTML element whose JS raises a counter every 500 ms and whose CSS animates a box: d.html, opened from disk with the Present service stopped, shows on that slide the counter rising and the box moving.

requirements.requirement: An HTML element in a PDF download comes out as the closest thing a PDF allows (a picture of it as it looks running, in its place on the slide), never left out.
requirements.quote: When a format can't hold something on the way out, like an HTML element in a PDF, it's exported as the closest thing that format allows
requirements.acceptance: A slide with an 800x600 HTML element whose JS draws a red circle and the word LIVE on a canvas 500 ms after load: after `present export <deck> --format pdf -o d.pdf`, that page rasterised with pdftoppm shows the red circle and LIVE at the element's position and size, matching `present render <deck> <n>`, not an empty box or the blank state before the script ran.

requirements.requirement: Anything else a download format can't hold is exported as the closest thing that format allows instead of being left out.
requirements.quote: When a format can't hold something on the way out, like an HTML element in a PDF, it's exported as the closest thing that format allows
requirements.acceptance: An HTML element that draws a red circle and the word LIVE with JS, exported to .pptx, .ppt, .key, .odp, .png and .jpg, shows the circle and LIVE in its place (in .pptx a picture at its frame, or something closer such as a video of it); a video exported to .pdf, .png and .jpg shows a still of it (its poster or a frame) in its box rather than an empty area.

requirements.requirement: Elements that animate in still appear in downloads that can't animate (.pdf, .png, .jpg), as on the fully built slide.
requirements.quote: When a format can't hold something on the way out, like an HTML element in a PDF, it's exported as the closest thing that format allows
requirements.acceptance: A slide whose title and picture both fly in on click: in d.pdf and in the d.png and d.jpg images, that slide shows the title and the picture, not just its background.

requirements.requirement: No slide ever comes out blank, in any download format.
requirements.quote: so no slide ever comes out blank
requirements.acceptance: A deck whose slide 1 is only a full-slide HTML element drawing a chart with JS, slide 2 only a video, and slide 3 only elements that animate in on click is exported in all eight formats: every slide in every file (pdf pages and png/jpg images directly; pptx, ppt, key and odp through LibreOffice's render; html through a Chromium screenshot) shows content where Silicon Present shows content, never only the background.

requirements.requirement: A folder can be shared with Carbons and Silicons the same way a deck is shared.
requirements.quote: Decks and folders are shared the same way.
requirements.acceptance: Carbon A creates folder F and, from the Share dialog on F in /decks, invites c:b as commenter; Silicon S creates folder G (`present folder new "G"`) and runs `present share G c:b --role viewer --folder`. GET /v1/folders/{F}/access and `present access G --folder --json` list Carbon B (shown as c:b) as commenter and viewer respectively, through the same /access request and response shape used for decks (POST/GET /v1/decks/{id}/access), and Carbon B sees F and G in Shared with me on /decks.

requirements.requirement: The owner of a deck or folder can invite a Carbon by their c:id.
requirements.quote: The owner, and anyone who can edit, can invite Carbons and Silicons by their c:id, si:id or email.
requirements.acceptance: Carbon A owns deck D and folder F. In the Share dialog at /decks/{D}, A enters c:b, picks Viewer and invites; for F, A runs `present share F c:b --role viewer --folder`. GET /v1/decks/{D}/access and GET /v1/folders/{F}/access list Carbon B as c:b with role viewer, and with no accept step Carbon B, signed in, sees D and F in Shared with me and can open /decks/{D}.

requirements.requirement: The owner of a deck or folder can invite a Silicon by its si:id.
requirements.quote: The owner, and anyone who can edit, can invite Carbons and Silicons by their c:id, si:id or email.
requirements.acceptance: Carbon A invites si:s to deck D as commenter from the Share dialog at /decks/{D}, and to folder F with POST /v1/folders/{F}/access {"to":"si:s","role":"viewer"}. `present access D --json` lists si:s as commenter; with no accept step Silicon S sees D in `present list --shared --json` and F in `present folder list --shared`, and `present read D` succeeds.

requirements.requirement: The owner of a deck or folder can invite someone by the email of their existing Silicon Accounts account, and that account then has the chosen role.
requirements.quote: The owner, and anyone who can edit, can invite Carbons and Silicons by their c:id, si:id or email.
requirements.acceptance: Carbon B already has a Silicon Accounts account with email b@example.test. Carbon A runs `present share D b@example.test --role commenter` and invites the same address to folder F from the Share dialog. Once B is signed in to the web, D and F are in B's Shared with me, B can comment on D (POST /v1/decks/{D}/threads → 201) but not edit it (POST /v1/decks/{D}/edits → 403), and GET /v1/decks/{D}/access lists B once, as c:b, with role commenter.

requirements.requirement: Inviting an email address that has no Silicon Accounts account sends that address an invite to join.
requirements.quote: Inviting an email that isn't on Silicon Accounts yet sends them an invite to join.
requirements.acceptance: Carbon A invites new-<random>@example.test (no account on the Accounts test stack) to deck D as viewer from the Share dialog at /decks/{D}, and to folder F with `present share F new-<random>@example.test --role viewer --folder`. Both succeed; GET /v1/decks/{D}/access lists a pending member email:new-<random>@example.test with role viewer; and an invite to join addressed to that email is recorded (its row in the service's email_outbox, or a message to it in the Accounts mock mailbox at http://127.0.0.1:9743/_messages).

critic.problem: The check passes on a row in email_outbox, which means Present mailed the invite itself. 'Silicon Present never sends its own' may forbid that, as MEN-14 points out, so SHR-05 can pass on behaviour another line rules out.
critic.fix: Record which path delivered the invite: Silicon Accounts, Ting, or Present's own mailer. Tie SHR-05 to the same Carbon ruling as MEN-14, and until that ruling, report an invite sent by Present's own mailer as an open question, not a pass.

requirements.requirement: Someone invited by an email that was not yet on Silicon Accounts gets the role they were invited with once they join with that email.
requirements.quote: Inviting an email that isn't on Silicon Accounts yet sends them an invite to join. … Everyone invited gets one of three roles
requirements.acceptance: Continuing SHR-05, a new Carbon signs up on the Accounts test stack with new-<random>@example.test (code read from the mock mailbox) and signs in to the web. With nothing more done by A, D and F are in their Shared with me; at /decks/{D} they see every slide but cannot comment (POST /v1/decks/{D}/threads → 403) or edit (POST /v1/decks/{D}/edits → 403); GET /v1/decks/{D}/access lists them once, by their c:id, with role viewer.

requirements.requirement: An Editor of a deck or folder who is not its owner can invite other Carbons and Silicons to it.
requirements.quote: `Editor` - can edit, comment and invite others.
requirements.acceptance: Owner A makes Carbon B an editor on deck D and on folder F. From the Share dialog at /decks/{D}, B invites si:s as editor and c:c as commenter; B runs `present share F c:e --role viewer --folder`. All succeed: GET /v1/decks/{D}/access lists si:s (editor) and c:c (commenter), GET /v1/folders/{F}/access lists c:e (viewer), and each invitee can open the deck or folder with that role.

requirements.requirement: Someone who can edit a deck only through a shared folder can invite others to that deck.
requirements.quote: The owner, and anyone who can edit, can invite Carbons and Silicons by their c:id, si:id or email.
requirements.acceptance: Owner A shares folder F, which holds deck D, with Carbon B as editor; B has no direct entry on D. B invites c:c to D as viewer from the Share dialog at /decks/{D} (POST /v1/decks/{D}/access → 2xx); c:c appears in GET /v1/decks/{D}/access and Carbon C can open /decks/{D}.

requirements.requirement: A Commenter cannot invite anyone to the deck or folder.
requirements.quote: `Commenter` - can view and comment. … The owner, and anyone who can edit, can invite Carbons and Silicons by their c:id, si:id or email.
requirements.acceptance: Carbon B is a commenter on deck D and on folder F. The web gives B no way to invite at /decks/{D}; POST /v1/decks/{D}/access and POST /v1/folders/{F}/access {"to":"c:c","role":"viewer"} with B's token return 403 with the standard {"error":{code,message,hint}} body; both access lists are unchanged.

requirements.requirement: A Viewer cannot invite anyone to the deck or folder.
requirements.quote: `Viewer` - can only view. … The owner, and anyone who can edit, can invite Carbons and Silicons by their c:id, si:id or email.
requirements.acceptance: Carbon B is a viewer on deck D and on folder F. The web gives B no way to invite at /decks/{D}; POST /v1/decks/{D}/access and POST /v1/folders/{F}/access {"to":"c:c","role":"viewer"} with B's token return 403; both access lists are unchanged.

requirements.requirement: The only roles an invitation can give are Editor, Commenter and Viewer; any other role is refused.
requirements.quote: Everyone invited gets one of three roles
requirements.acceptance: The Share dialog offers exactly Editor, Commenter and Viewer. `present share D c:b --role owner` is rejected by the CLI and changes nothing. POST /v1/decks/{D}/access and POST /v1/folders/{F}/access with role "owner" or "admin" return a 4xx validation error in the standard error body, and GET .../access shows no new member.

requirements.requirement: Each invited Carbon or Silicon holds exactly one role on a given deck or folder; inviting them again never leaves them with two roles there.
requirements.quote: Everyone invited gets one of three roles
requirements.acceptance: Carbon A invites si:s to deck D as viewer and then again as editor (`present share D si:s --role editor`), and invites c:b to folder F as commenter twice. GET /v1/decks/{D}/access and `present access D --json` list si:s exactly once with a single role, GET /v1/folders/{F}/access lists c:b exactly once, and S's rights match the role shown (if editor, `present add text D 1 "x"` succeeds; if viewer, it fails with 403).

requirements.requirement: An Editor can edit the deck.
requirements.quote: `Editor` - can edit, comment and invite others.
requirements.acceptance: Carbon B, invited to deck D as editor, opens /decks/{D}, changes the text of a text element and adds a slide. Carbon A, with /decks/{D} open, sees both changes without reloading; after reload GET /v1/decks/{D}/content?format=json contains them and GET /v1/decks/{D}/versions lists them by c:b.

requirements.requirement: An Editor can comment on the deck.
requirements.quote: `Editor` - can edit, comment and invite others.
requirements.acceptance: Carbon B (editor on D) comments on slide 1 in /decks/{D} and replies to A's existing thread; both appear in GET /v1/decks/{D}/threads with author c:b (POST /v1/decks/{D}/threads and POST /v1/threads/{t}/replies with B's token return 2xx).

requirements.requirement: A Commenter can view the deck.
requirements.quote: `Commenter` - can view and comment.
requirements.acceptance: Carbon B, invited to deck D as commenter, opens /decks/{D} and sees every slide; GET /v1/decks/{D}/content with B's token returns 200 with the deck.

requirements.requirement: A Commenter can comment on the deck.
requirements.quote: `Commenter` - can view and comment.
requirements.acceptance: Carbon B (commenter on D) clicks a point on slide 2 in /decks/{D}, writes a comment and posts it, then replies to A's thread; both appear in GET /v1/decks/{D}/threads with author c:b.

requirements.requirement: A Commenter cannot edit the deck.
requirements.quote: `Commenter` - can view and comment.
requirements.acceptance: Carbon B (commenter on D) cannot change slide content in /decks/{D}: typing or dragging leaves the deck unchanged after reload. With B's token POST /v1/decks/{D}/updates and POST /v1/decks/{D}/edits return 403, and the deck's version in GET /v1/decks/{D}/content does not advance.

requirements.requirement: A Viewer can view the deck.
requirements.quote: `Viewer` - can only view.
requirements.acceptance: Carbon B, invited to deck D as viewer, opens /decks/{D} and sees every slide; GET /v1/decks/{D}/content with B's token returns 200.

requirements.requirement: A Viewer cannot comment.
requirements.quote: `Viewer` - can only view.
requirements.acceptance: Carbon B (viewer on D) cannot get any comment posted from /decks/{D}; with B's token POST /v1/decks/{D}/threads and POST /v1/threads/{t}/replies return 403, and GET /v1/decks/{D}/threads is unchanged.

requirements.requirement: A Viewer cannot edit.
requirements.quote: `Viewer` - can only view.
requirements.acceptance: Carbon B (viewer on D) cannot change slide content in /decks/{D} (unchanged after reload); with B's token POST /v1/decks/{D}/updates and POST /v1/decks/{D}/edits return 403 and the deck's version does not advance.

requirements.requirement: A Commenter or Viewer cannot make the deck public or change its public mode.
requirements.quote: `Commenter` - can view and comment. … `Viewer` - can only view.
requirements.acceptance: Deck D is private. Carbon B (commenter) tries the public switch in the Share dialog at /decks/{D}, and Silicon S (viewer) runs `present public D view`; both are refused (PUT /v1/decks/{D}/public → 403) and a tokenless GET /v1/decks/{D}/content still fails. With D public (view), B and S likewise cannot set it to comment, edit or off.

requirements.requirement: A Silicon can be given any of the three roles (Editor, Commenter, Viewer) on a deck or folder, exactly as a Carbon can.
requirements.quote: Carbons and Silicons get exactly the same roles and the same rights.
requirements.acceptance: From the Share dialog at /decks/{D}, Carbon A invites si:s1 as editor, si:s2 as commenter and si:s3 as viewer, and invites si:s1 to folder F as viewer. The dialog offers Silicons the same three roles as Carbons; GET /v1/decks/{D}/access and `present access D --json` show each Silicon with exactly the chosen role, and GET /v1/folders/{F}/access shows si:s1 as viewer.

requirements.requirement: A Silicon Editor can edit the deck directly through the CLI: its change goes straight into the live deck, as a Carbon editor's does.
requirements.quote: Carbons and Silicons get exactly the same roles and the same rights. … `Editor` - can edit, comment and invite others.
requirements.acceptance: Silicon S, invited to deck D as editor (not owner), runs `present add text D 1 "From S"` and `present edit D --ops ops.json` with an update_element op. Both succeed with no approval step; `present read D` and GET /v1/decks/{D}/content show the changes; Carbon A, with /decks/{D} open, sees them appear live; GET /v1/decks/{D}/versions attributes them to si:s.

requirements.requirement: A Silicon Editor can comment on the deck through the CLI.
requirements.quote: Carbons and Silicons get exactly the same roles and the same rights. … `Editor` - can edit, comment and invite others.
requirements.acceptance: Silicon S (editor on D) runs `present comment D --slide 1 "Check the numbers"` and `present reply <thread> "Done"`; both succeed and appear in `present comments D` and GET /v1/decks/{D}/threads with author si:s.

requirements.requirement: A Silicon Editor can invite others through the CLI.
requirements.quote: Carbons and Silicons get exactly the same roles and the same rights. … `Editor` - can edit, comment and invite others.
requirements.acceptance: Silicon S (editor on D, not owner) runs `present share D c:c --role viewer` and `present share D si:t --role commenter`; both succeed, `present access D --json` lists c:c (viewer) and si:t (commenter), and Carbon C can open /decks/{D}.

requirements.requirement: A Silicon Commenter can view the deck through the CLI.
requirements.quote: Carbons and Silicons get exactly the same roles and the same rights. … `Commenter` - can view and comment.
requirements.acceptance: Silicon S (commenter on D) runs `present read D` and `present render D 1 -o s1.png`; the first prints the deck's slides as text, the second writes a PNG of slide 1; both exit 0.

requirements.requirement: A Silicon Commenter can comment on the deck through the CLI.
requirements.quote: Carbons and Silicons get exactly the same roles and the same rights. … `Commenter` - can view and comment.
requirements.acceptance: Silicon S (commenter on D) runs `present comment D --slide 2 "Typo here"` and `present reply <thread> "Agreed"`; both succeed and appear in GET /v1/decks/{D}/threads with author si:s.

requirements.requirement: A Silicon Commenter cannot edit the deck.
requirements.quote: Carbons and Silicons get exactly the same roles and the same rights. … `Commenter` - can view and comment.
requirements.acceptance: Silicon S (commenter on D) runs `present add text D 1 "x"` and `present edit D --ops ops.json`; both exit non-zero with a clear no-edit-access error (POST /v1/decks/{D}/edits → 403), and `present read D --json` shows the same version and content as before.

requirements.requirement: A Silicon Commenter cannot invite anyone.
requirements.quote: Carbons and Silicons get exactly the same roles and the same rights. … `Commenter` - can view and comment.
requirements.acceptance: Silicon S (commenter on D) runs `present share D c:c --role viewer`; it exits non-zero (POST /v1/decks/{D}/access → 403) and GET /v1/decks/{D}/access read by owner A is unchanged.

requirements.requirement: A Silicon Viewer can view the deck through the CLI.
requirements.quote: Carbons and Silicons get exactly the same roles and the same rights. … `Viewer` - can only view.
requirements.acceptance: Silicon S (viewer on D) runs `present read D` and `present render D 1 -o s1.png`; both exit 0, printing the deck's slides and writing a PNG of slide 1.

requirements.requirement: A Silicon Viewer cannot comment.
requirements.quote: Carbons and Silicons get exactly the same roles and the same rights. … `Viewer` - can only view.
requirements.acceptance: Silicon S (viewer on D) runs `present comment D --slide 1 "x"` and `present reply <thread> "x"`; both exit non-zero (403) and GET /v1/decks/{D}/threads is unchanged.

requirements.requirement: A Silicon Viewer cannot edit.
requirements.quote: Carbons and Silicons get exactly the same roles and the same rights. … `Viewer` - can only view.
requirements.acceptance: Silicon S (viewer on D) runs `present add text D 1 "x"` and `present edit D --ops ops.json`; both exit non-zero (POST /v1/decks/{D}/edits → 403) and the deck's version does not advance.

requirements.requirement: A Silicon Viewer cannot invite anyone.
requirements.quote: Carbons and Silicons get exactly the same roles and the same rights. … `Viewer` - can only view.
requirements.acceptance: Silicon S (viewer on D) runs `present share D c:c --role viewer`; it exits non-zero (403) and the access list is unchanged.

requirements.requirement: A Silicon that owns a deck or folder can invite others to it through the CLI.
requirements.quote: Carbons and Silicons get exactly the same roles and the same rights. … The owner, and anyone who can edit, can invite Carbons and Silicons by their c:id, si:id or email.
requirements.acceptance: Silicon S creates deck D (`present new "S deck"`) and folder F (`present folder new "S folder"`), then runs `present share D c:a --role commenter`, `present share D new-<random>@example.test --role viewer` and `present folder share F si:t --role editor`. Carbon A sees D in Shared with me and can comment on it; an invite to join is recorded for the new email (email_outbox or the mock mailbox); Silicon T sees F in `present folder list --shared`.

critic.problem: Same issue as SHR-05: the check accepts an invite to join recorded in email_outbox, which is Present sending its own email, against 'Silicon Present never sends its own' (MEN-14).
critic.fix: Record the delivery path and apply the same Carbon ruling as SHR-05 and MEN-14. Until that ruling, don't count Present's own mailer as a pass.

requirements.requirement: Whether the caller is a Carbon or a Silicon never changes what a role allows: a Carbon and a Silicon with the same role get identical results for every action.
requirements.quote: Carbons and Silicons get exactly the same roles and the same rights.
requirements.acceptance: For each role (editor, commenter, viewer), granted directly on deck D and, separately, only through folder F, give Carbon B and Silicon S that role. With each one's token call GET /v1/decks/{D}/content, GET /v1/decks/{D}/slides/{s}/render, POST /v1/decks/{D}/threads, POST /v1/threads/{t}/replies, POST /v1/decks/{D}/edits, POST /v1/decks/{D}/updates, POST /v1/decks/{D}/access and PUT /v1/decks/{D}/public. Every call returns the same status for B as for S.

requirements.requirement: Sharing a folder gives the invitee the folder's role on every deck in it.
requirements.quote: Sharing a folder shares everything in it, including anything added later.
requirements.acceptance: Folder F (owner A) holds decks D1 and D2. A shares F with Carbon B as commenter and with Silicon S as editor; neither has direct access to D1 or D2. B opens F from Shared with me, sees D1 and D2, and can comment on D1 (POST /v1/decks/{D1}/threads → 201) but not edit it (POST /v1/decks/{D1}/edits → 403); S sees both in `present list --folder F --json` and `present add text D2 1 "x"` succeeds.

requirements.requirement: Sharing a folder also shares every folder inside it, at any depth, and everything in those.
requirements.quote: Sharing a folder shares everything in it, including anything added later.
requirements.acceptance: Folder F holds folder G, which holds folder H with deck D3. A shares only F with Carbon B as viewer. B navigates F → G → H from Shared with me on /decks, opens /decks/{D3} and sees its slides (GET /v1/decks/{D3}/content → 200), and cannot comment on it (POST /v1/decks/{D3}/threads → 403).

requirements.requirement: A deck added to a shared folder after it was shared, whether created in it or moved into it, is shared with everyone the folder is shared with.
requirements.quote: Sharing a folder shares everything in it, including anything added later.
requirements.acceptance: After A shares folder F with Carbon B (viewer) and Silicon S (editor), A creates deck D4 in F (`present new "D4" --folder F`, or POST /v1/decks {"folder": F}) and moves existing deck D5 into F (`present move D5 F`, or PATCH /v1/decks/{D5} {"folder": F}). With no new invitation, B sees D4 and D5 in F and can open /decks/{D4} and /decks/{D5}; S's `present add text D4 1 "x"` and `present add text D5 1 "x"` succeed.

requirements.requirement: A folder added to a shared folder after it was shared, whether created in it or moved into it, is shared too, with everything in it.
requirements.quote: Sharing a folder shares everything in it, including anything added later.
requirements.acceptance: After A shares folder F with Carbon B as commenter, A creates folder K inside F (`present folder new "K" --parent F`) holding a new deck D6, and moves existing folder L, holding deck D7, into F (`present folder move L F`). With no new invitation, B sees K and L inside F and can comment on D6 and D7 (POST /v1/decks/{D6}/threads and POST /v1/decks/{D7}/threads → 201).

requirements.requirement: A deck moved out of a shared folder is no longer shared through that folder.
requirements.quote: Sharing a folder shares everything in it, including anything added later.
requirements.acceptance: Carbon B can reach deck D1 only through folder F (viewer). A moves D1 to the root (`present move D1 root`). B no longer sees D1 in F or in Shared with me, GET /v1/decks/{D1}/content with B's token returns 403 or 404, and /decks/{D1} shows B no deck; B's access to the decks still in F is unchanged.

requirements.requirement: Someone with a lower role directly on a deck and a higher role through a folder gets the higher role.
requirements.quote: If someone has access both directly and through a folder, they get whichever role gives them more.
requirements.acceptance: Carbon B is a direct viewer on deck D and an editor on folder F, which holds D. B can edit D at /decks/{D} (POST /v1/decks/{D}/edits → 2xx) and invite others to it (POST /v1/decks/{D}/access → 2xx). Likewise, with subfolder G inside F shared with B directly as viewer, B can edit the decks in G.

requirements.requirement: Someone with a higher role directly on a deck keeps it even when a folder gives them a lower one.
requirements.quote: If someone has access both directly and through a folder, they get whichever role gives them more.
requirements.acceptance: Silicon S is a direct editor on deck D and a viewer on folder F, which holds D. `present add text D 1 "x"` and `present share D c:c --role viewer` both succeed.

requirements.requirement: Someone who reaches a deck through more than one enclosing folder gets the highest of those roles.
requirements.quote: If someone has access both directly and through a folder, they get whichever role gives them more.
requirements.acceptance: Folder F holds folder G, which holds deck D. Carbon B is an editor on F and a viewer on G: B can edit D (POST /v1/decks/{D}/edits → 2xx). With the roles swapped (viewer on F, editor on G), B can still edit D.

requirements.requirement: A deck is private until it is made public: its link shows nothing to anyone who is signed out or has no access.
requirements.quote: Any deck can be made public at any time with one switch. … Making it private again stops the link working.
requirements.acceptance: Carbon A creates deck D in the web and another with `present open board.pptx`. For both, the Share dialog shows the public switch off; a signed-out browser at /decks/{D} sees no slide content; a tokenless GET /v1/decks/{D}/content returns 401 or 404; signed-in Carbon C (never invited) gets no deck at /decks/{D} (403 or 404 from the API); and Silicon T's `present read <link>` (link = http://localhost:4320/decks/{D}) fails.

requirements.requirement: The owner can make a deck public with a single switch.
requirements.quote: Any deck can be made public at any time with one switch.
requirements.acceptance: Carbon A opens the Share dialog at /decks/{D} and turns on the public switch; nothing else is needed (PUT /v1/decks/{D}/public {"mode":"view"} is sent). A fresh signed-out browser then opens /decks/{D} and sees the slides.

requirements.requirement: A deck can be made public at any time, including again after it was made private.
requirements.quote: Any deck can be made public at any time with one switch.
requirements.acceptance: Carbon A makes D public in the Share dialog, private with `present public D off`, then public again with `present public D view`. After each step a tokenless GET /v1/decks/{D}/content succeeds when public and fails when private. The same sequence works on a deck inside a folder and on a deck already shared with invitees.

requirements.requirement: Anyone signed in who has a public deck's link can view it without being invited.
requirements.quote: Anyone with the link can then view it, or, if the owner chooses, comment on it or edit it.
requirements.acceptance: D is public (view). Carbon C, signed in, never invited and with no folder access, opens /decks/{D} from the link and sees every slide; GET /v1/decks/{D}/content with C's token returns 200.

requirements.requirement: A Silicon that was never invited can view a public deck through its link with the CLI.
requirements.quote: Anyone with the link can then view it, or, if the owner chooses, comment on it or edit it. … Carbons and Silicons get exactly the same roles and the same rights.
requirements.acceptance: D is public (view). Silicon T, signed in and never invited, runs `present read http://localhost:4320/decks/{D}` and `present render http://localhost:4320/decks/{D} 1 -o s1.png`; both exit 0.

requirements.requirement: When the owner turns on the public switch without choosing more, people reaching the deck by its link can view it but cannot comment.
requirements.quote: Anyone with the link can then view it, or, if the owner chooses, comment on it or edit it.
requirements.acceptance: Carbon A turns on only the public switch (mode view). Carbon C (signed in, never invited) cannot get a comment posted at /decks/{D} (POST /v1/decks/{D}/threads with C's token → 403), Silicon T's `present comment <link> --slide 1 "x"` exits non-zero, and GET /v1/decks/{D}/threads is unchanged.

requirements.requirement: When the owner turns on the public switch without choosing more, people reaching the deck by its link cannot edit it.
requirements.quote: Anyone with the link can then view it, or, if the owner chooses, comment on it or edit it.
requirements.acceptance: With only the public switch on, Carbon C (signed in, never invited) cannot change anything at /decks/{D}; POST /v1/decks/{D}/updates and POST /v1/decks/{D}/edits with C's token return 403; Silicon T's `present add text <link> 1 "x"` exits non-zero; the deck's version does not advance.

requirements.requirement: The owner can choose to let anyone with the link comment on a public deck.
requirements.quote: Anyone with the link can then view it, or, if the owner chooses, comment on it or edit it.
requirements.acceptance: Carbon A sets Anyone with the link to Comment in the Share dialog (PUT /v1/decks/{D}/public {"mode":"comment"}). Carbon C (signed in, never invited) clicks slide 1 at /decks/{D}, posts a comment and replies to A's thread; both appear in GET /v1/decks/{D}/threads with author c:c.

requirements.requirement: When the owner lets people with the link comment, they still cannot edit.
requirements.quote: Anyone with the link can then view it, or, if the owner chooses, comment on it or edit it.
requirements.acceptance: With mode comment, Carbon C (signed in, never invited) cannot change slide content at /decks/{D}; POST /v1/decks/{D}/updates and POST /v1/decks/{D}/edits with C's token return 403; Silicon T's `present add text <link> 1 "x"` exits non-zero.

requirements.requirement: The owner can choose to let anyone with the link edit a public deck.
requirements.quote: Anyone with the link can then view it, or, if the owner chooses, comment on it or edit it.
requirements.acceptance: Carbon A sets Anyone with the link to Edit (PUT /v1/decks/{D}/public {"mode":"edit"}). Carbon C (signed in, never invited) changes a text element at /decks/{D}; A, with the deck open, sees it live; GET /v1/decks/{D}/content contains it.

requirements.requirement: When the owner lets people with the link edit, they can also comment.
requirements.quote: Anyone with the link can then view it, or, if the owner chooses, comment on it or edit it.
requirements.acceptance: With mode edit, Carbon C (signed in, never invited) posts a comment on slide 1 at /decks/{D} (POST /v1/decks/{D}/threads → 201).

requirements.requirement: Someone who can edit a deck through its public link can invite others, like anyone else who can edit.
requirements.quote: The owner, and anyone who can edit, can invite Carbons and Silicons by their c:id, si:id or email. … Anyone with the link can then view it, or, if the owner chooses, comment on it or edit it.
requirements.acceptance: With mode edit, Carbon C (signed in, never invited) invites c:e as viewer from the Share dialog at /decks/{D} (POST /v1/decks/{D}/access → 2xx); c:e appears in GET /v1/decks/{D}/access and Carbon E can open the deck.

requirements.requirement: Lowering the public level takes the higher rights away from people using the link.
requirements.quote: Anyone with the link can then view it, or, if the owner chooses, comment on it or edit it.
requirements.acceptance: With mode edit, Carbon C (signed in, never invited) edits D through the link. A switches the level to Comment: C's next POST /v1/decks/{D}/edits returns 403 while commenting still works. A switches to view only: C's POST /v1/decks/{D}/threads returns 403 while /decks/{D} still shows the slides.

requirements.requirement: A Silicon that owns a deck can make it public through the CLI.
requirements.quote: Any deck can be made public at any time with one switch. … Carbons and Silicons get exactly the same roles and the same rights.
requirements.acceptance: Silicon S creates deck D (`present new "S deck"`) and runs `present public D view`; a fresh signed-out browser opens /decks/{D} and sees the slides.

requirements.requirement: A Silicon that owns a public deck can let anyone with the link comment, through the CLI.
requirements.quote: Anyone with the link can then view it, or, if the owner chooses, comment on it or edit it. … Carbons and Silicons get exactly the same roles and the same rights.
requirements.acceptance: Silicon S (owner of public deck D) runs `present public D comment`; Carbon C (signed in, never invited) can then comment at /decks/{D} (POST /v1/decks/{D}/threads → 201) but not edit (POST /v1/decks/{D}/edits → 403).

requirements.requirement: A Silicon that owns a public deck can let anyone with the link edit, through the CLI.
requirements.quote: Anyone with the link can then view it, or, if the owner chooses, comment on it or edit it. … Carbons and Silicons get exactly the same roles and the same rights.
requirements.acceptance: Silicon S (owner of public deck D) runs `present public D edit`; Carbon C (signed in, never invited) can then change a slide at /decks/{D} (POST /v1/decks/{D}/edits → 2xx).

requirements.requirement: A signed-in Silicon that was never invited can comment on a public deck through its link when the owner allows commenting.
requirements.quote: Anyone with the link can then view it, or, if the owner chooses, comment on it or edit it. … Carbons and Silicons get exactly the same roles and the same rights.
requirements.acceptance: D is public with mode comment. Silicon T (signed in, never invited) runs `present comment <link> --slide 1 "Looks off"` (link = http://localhost:4320/decks/{D}); it exits 0 and the thread appears in GET /v1/decks/{D}/threads with author si:t.

requirements.requirement: A signed-in Silicon that was never invited can edit a public deck through its link when the owner allows editing.
requirements.quote: Anyone with the link can then view it, or, if the owner chooses, comment on it or edit it. … Carbons and Silicons get exactly the same roles and the same rights.
requirements.acceptance: D is public with mode edit. Silicon T (signed in, never invited) runs `present add text <link> 1 "From T"`; it exits 0, `present read <link>` shows the new text and GET /v1/decks/{D}/versions attributes it to si:t.

requirements.requirement: A public deck is never listed for people who have no other access to it: it does not appear in their decks or in Shared with me, even after they open its link.
requirements.quote: Nothing is listed anywhere: the deck is just reachable by its link.
requirements.acceptance: D is public (tried with view, comment and edit). Carbon C and Silicon T, never invited, check /decks (My decks and Shared with me), GET /v1/decks?scope=mine and ?scope=shared, `present list` and `present list --shared --json`: D is absent. Each then opens D by its link (and C comments on it in comment mode); re-checking, D is still absent everywhere.

requirements.requirement: A public deck never appears in search results for people who have no other access to it.
requirements.quote: Nothing is listed anywhere: the deck is just reachable by its link.
requirements.acceptance: Public deck D has a unique title word (for example "zebrafjord"). Carbon C (never invited) calls GET /v1/search?q=zebrafjord and uses any search in the web; Silicon T (never invited) runs `present search zebrafjord --json`. Neither gets D, before or after opening its link, while owner A's GET /v1/search?q=zebrafjord does return D.

requirements.requirement: Silicon Present has no place that lists public decks: no gallery, directory or index, and no deck links in the site's sitemap.xml or llms.txt.
requirements.quote: Nothing is listed anywhere: the deck is just reachable by its link.
requirements.acceptance: With several public decks owned by different accounts, a signed-out client fetches /, /sitemap.xml, /llms.txt and /robots.txt, and a never-invited Carbon looks through every page under /decks and the GET /v1/decks listings: nothing enumerates other accounts' public decks, and no /decks/{id} URL appears in sitemap.xml or llms.txt.

requirements.requirement: A public deck's page asks search engines not to index it, so the deck stays reachable only by its link.
requirements.quote: Nothing is listed anywhere: the deck is just reachable by its link.
requirements.acceptance: A signed-out GET of /decks/{D} for public deck D returns a page with <meta name="robots" content="noindex"> (or an X-Robots-Tag: noindex response header).

requirements.requirement: Making a public deck private again stops its link working for signed-out visitors, including the slide images, assets and exports reached through it.
requirements.quote: Making it private again stops the link working.
requirements.acceptance: D was public (view) and a signed-out browser had loaded /decks/{D}. A turns the switch off (Share dialog, or `present public D off`). A fresh signed-out load of /decks/{D} shows no slide content (a sign-in or no-access page instead); tokenless GET /v1/decks/{D}/content, GET /v1/decks/{D}/slides/{s}/render, GET /v1/decks/{D}/export?format=pdf and GET /v1/assets/{id} for an image in D return 401, 403 or 404; a logged-out `present read <link>` fails.

requirements.requirement: Making a public deck private again stops its link working for signed-in people who were never invited.
requirements.quote: Making it private again stops the link working.
requirements.acceptance: D was public (edit) and Carbon C and Silicon T, never invited, had viewed and edited it through the link. After A turns the switch off, C at /decks/{D} sees no slide content; GET /v1/decks/{D}/content, POST /v1/decks/{D}/threads and POST /v1/decks/{D}/edits with C's token return 403 (or 404); T's `present read <link>` fails with a no-access error.

requirements.requirement: Making a deck private also cuts off link-only visitors who already have it open: they get no further changes and cannot act on it.
requirements.quote: Making it private again stops the link working.
requirements.acceptance: A signed-out browser and never-invited Carbon C have /decks/{D} open while D is public (edit), each with its live stream (GET /v1/decks/{D}/live) connected. A turns the switch off, then changes slide 1. Neither page receives the change (the stream ends or delivers no further update), C's next comment or edit is refused with 403, and reloading shows no deck.

requirements.requirement: Making a deck private again does not affect the people it is shared with: they keep their roles.
requirements.quote: Making it private again stops the link working. … Everyone invited gets one of three roles
requirements.acceptance: D is shared directly with Carbon B (commenter) and, through folder F, with Silicon S (editor). A makes D public (edit) and then private again. B can still open /decks/{D} and comment (POST /v1/decks/{D}/threads → 201); S's `present add text D 1 "x"` still succeeds; GET /v1/decks/{D}/access is unchanged.

requirements.requirement: Making a deck public never lowers the role of anyone it is shared with.
requirements.quote: Anyone with the link can then view it, or, if the owner chooses, comment on it or edit it. … Everyone invited gets one of three roles
requirements.acceptance: Carbon B is an invited editor on D. A makes D public with mode view. B can still edit at /decks/{D} (POST /v1/decks/{D}/edits → 2xx) and invite others (POST /v1/decks/{D}/access → 2xx).

requirements.requirement: An invited person whose role is lower than the public link's level gets the link's level while signed in.
requirements.quote: Anyone with the link can then view it, or, if the owner chooses, comment on it or edit it.
requirements.acceptance: Carbon B is an invited viewer on D. A sets the public level to Edit: B, signed in, can edit at /decks/{D} (POST /v1/decks/{D}/edits → 2xx). A sets Comment: B can comment but POST /v1/decks/{D}/edits → 403. A turns the switch off: B can only view again.

requirements.requirement: Viewing a public deck never needs signing in, at any public level (view, comment or edit).
requirements.quote: Viewing a public deck never needs signing in.
requirements.acceptance: For D public with each level in turn (view, comment, edit), a fresh browser context with no session opens /decks/{D}: the slides show, including an image element, with no sign-in page or prompt in the way; GET /v1/decks/{D}/content and GET /v1/assets/{id} for that image without an Authorization header return 200.

requirements.requirement: The CLI can read a public deck by its link without being signed in.
requirements.quote: Viewing a public deck never needs signing in.
requirements.acceptance: After `present logout` (`present login status --json` → {"authenticated": false}), `present read <link>` for public deck D prints its slides and `present render <link> 1 -o s1.png` writes the image; both exit 0.

requirements.requirement: Commenting through a public deck's link needs signing in: a signed-out visitor cannot post a comment and is asked to sign in instead.
requirements.quote: Commenting or editing through the link does, so every change and every comment always has a Carbon or Silicon behind it.
requirements.acceptance: D is public with mode comment. In a signed-out browser at /decks/{D}, trying to comment leads to sign-in instead of posting, and no thread is created; tokenless POST /v1/decks/{D}/threads, POST /v1/threads/{t}/replies and PUT /v1/comments/{c}/reactions/👍 return 401; a logged-out `present comment <link> --slide 1 "x"` fails and says to sign in. After signing in as a never-invited Carbon, the same comment posts.

requirements.requirement: Editing through a public deck's link needs signing in: a signed-out visitor cannot change the deck and is asked to sign in instead.
requirements.quote: Commenting or editing through the link does, so every change and every comment always has a Carbon or Silicon behind it.
requirements.acceptance: D is public with mode edit. In a signed-out browser at /decks/{D}, trying to change a slide leads to sign-in and the deck is unchanged after reload; tokenless POST /v1/decks/{D}/updates and POST /v1/decks/{D}/edits return 401 and the version does not advance; a logged-out `present add text <link> 1 "x"` fails and says to sign in. After signing in, the same edit goes through.

requirements.requirement: Every comment made through a public link is attributed to the signed-in Carbon or Silicon who wrote it.
requirements.quote: Commenting or editing through the link does, so every change and every comment always has a Carbon or Silicon behind it.
requirements.acceptance: D is public with mode comment. Never-invited Carbon C (in the web) and Silicon T (`present comment <link> --slide 1 "…"`) each comment through the link. GET /v1/decks/{D}/threads, `present comments D` and the deck's thread list in the web show each comment with its author, c:c and si:t; no comment on D lacks an author.

requirements.requirement: Every change made through a public link is attributed to the signed-in Carbon or Silicon who made it.
requirements.quote: Commenting or editing through the link does, so every change and every comment always has a Carbon or Silicon behind it.
requirements.acceptance: D is public with mode edit. Never-invited Carbon C (in the web) and Silicon T (`present add text <link> 1 "…"`) each change a slide through the link. /decks/{D}/history and GET /v1/decks/{D}/versions list the changes under c:c and si:t; every update in D's history has an author.

requirements.requirement: Two or more Carbons who can edit a deck can edit it at the same time in the web editor, even on the same slide. Nobody is locked out, blocked or made read-only because someone else is editing.
requirements.quote: Everyone edits the same deck at the same time
requirements.acceptance: Carbons A (c:ada) and B (c:bob), both Editors of deck D, open /decks/D in two browsers on slide 2. In the same few seconds A drags a shape and B types into a text box on that slide. Neither editor shows a lock, a 'being edited by' block or a read-only state, and every POST /v1/decks/D/updates sent by either tab gets a 2xx.

requirements.requirement: A Silicon that can edit a deck changes that same live deck directly through the CLI. Its change lands in the deck everyone has open, with no copy, branch, draft or approval step in between.
requirements.quote: Everyone edits the same deck at the same time
requirements.acceptance: Silicon S (si:designer, Editor of D) runs `present add text D 2 "From S" --x 100 --y 100`. It exits 0. Right away, `present read D`, GET /v1/decks/D/content?format=json and a fresh load of /decks/D by Carbon A all contain the new text box. Nobody has to accept or approve anything, and no new deck or pending suggestion appears (`present list` shows the same decks as before).

requirements.requirement: A Silicon can change a deck through the CLI while Carbons are editing it in the web editor at that moment. Its change is accepted, with no lock, conflict or busy error.
requirements.quote: Everyone edits the same deck at the same time
requirements.acceptance: Carbon A is typing continuously in a text box on slide 2 of /decks/D. Meanwhile Silicon S runs `present set D 2 <another element on slide 2> x=400 y=300` and `present slide add D --title "Added by S"`. Both commands exit 0 with no lock, conflict or busy error, and both changes are in `present read D`.

requirements.requirement: When different people change different parts of a deck at the same moment, every change is kept. None overwrites another.
requirements.quote: Everyone edits the same deck at the same time
requirements.acceptance: Within the same second: Carbon A changes the title text on slide 1 in /decks/D, Carbon B changes a shape's fill on slide 1, and Silicon S runs `present slide notes D 1 "Pause here"`. Once all three have settled, both browsers and `present read D` show all three changes.

requirements.requirement: When two Carbons type in the same text at the same time, both keep what they typed.
requirements.quote: Everyone edits the same deck at the same time
requirements.acceptance: A text box on slide 2 says "Revenue". Carbon A puts her caret at the end and Carbon B puts his at the start. At the same moment A types " grew" and B types "Q4 ". Within 2 s both browsers show "Q4 Revenue grew", and so does `present read D`.

requirements.requirement: When a Silicon changes a text through the CLI while a Carbon is typing in that same text, both changes are kept. The Silicon's change does not wipe the Carbon's typing, and the typing does not undo the Silicon's change.
requirements.quote: Everyone edits the same deck at the same time
requirements.acceptance: A text box on slide 2 says "Q3 revenue". Carbon A is typing " grew 40%" at its end in /decks/D. At that moment Silicon S runs `present replace D 2 <that element> --find "Q3" --replace "Q4"`. Afterwards A's editor and `present read D` both show "Q4 revenue grew 40%".

requirements.requirement: Other people's changes never interrupt a Carbon's own editing. The Carbon stays in the text they are typing in, their caret keeps its place in the text, and their selection stays.
requirements.quote: Everyone edits the same deck at the same time
requirements.acceptance: Carbon A is typing steadily in text box T on slide 2 of /decks/D. Meanwhile Carbon B moves a shape on slide 2, Silicon S runs `present set D 2 <another text> text="Changed by S"`, and B types a word at the start of T. A never leaves T and never loses focus. Each character she types lands right after the one before, even when B's word is inserted in front of her caret, and none of her keystrokes are dropped.

requirements.requirement: A change one Carbon makes in the web editor appears in every other open editor of that deck as it happens, with no reload.
requirements.quote: sees every change as it happens
requirements.acceptance: Carbons A and B both have /decks/D open on slide 2. A drags a shape to a new spot. Within 2 s, with no reload, B's canvas shows the shape in its new position, and B's GET /v1/decks/D/live stream has delivered an `update` event whose author is c:ada.

requirements.requirement: Others see text while it is being typed, not only when the typist finishes or leaves the text box.
requirements.quote: sees every change as it happens
requirements.acceptance: Carbon A types "Hello world" into a text box on slide 2, one character every 300 ms, and stays in the box. Carbon B is watching slide 2. B sees the text grow while A is still typing ("Hello" is visible before A types the "w"), with each character showing up within about 1 s of A typing it.

requirements.requirement: Everyone in the deck sees changes to slides as they happen: adding, duplicating, deleting and reordering slides, and changing a slide's layout, background, transition, skipped state, section or whether it shows the master.
requirements.quote: sees every change as it happens
requirements.acceptance: Carbon B has /decks/D open. Carbon A (in her editor) and Silicon S (with `present slide add|duplicate|move|delete|skip|section|layout|background|transition|master`) take turns making one of these slide changes each. After each one, within 2 s and with no reload, B's slide list and canvas show it: the new, copied or moved slide in its place, the deleted slide gone, the skipped mark, the section name, the new background and so on.

requirements.requirement: Everyone in the deck sees changes to elements as they happen: adding and deleting, moving, resizing, rotating, restyling, layering, locking, grouping, links, animations, table cells, chart data, and an HTML element's HTML, CSS and JS.
requirements.quote: sees every change as it happens
requirements.acceptance: Carbon B has /decks/D open on slide 3. Carbon A (in her editor) and Silicon S (with `present add|set|front|back|replace|delete`) take turns: add an image, move and rotate a shape, set style.fill, bring an element to the front, lock two elements and group them, change a table cell, change a chart's series, and change an HTML element's js. After each change, within 2 s and with no reload, B's canvas shows it. After the js change, the HTML element runs its new code.

requirements.requirement: Everyone in the deck sees changes to speaker notes as they happen.
requirements.quote: sees every change as it happens
requirements.acceptance: Carbon B has slide 2's speaker notes open in /decks/D. Carbon A types in slide 2's notes, and then Silicon S runs `present slide notes D 2 "Pause here"`. Each change shows in B's notes within 2 s, with no reload.

requirements.requirement: Everyone in the deck sees changes to the whole deck as they happen: the theme, the master elements and the slide size.
requirements.quote: sees every change as it happens
requirements.acceptance: Carbon B has /decks/D open. Silicon S runs, in turn, `present theme D Ink`, `present add text D 1 "Footer" --master`, and `present edit D --ops` with an `update_deck` op that sets size to 1080x1080. Within 2 s of each one, with no reload, B's canvas and slide list show it: the new theme's colours and fonts, the footer on every slide that doesn't hide the master, and the new slide shape.

requirements.requirement: Everyone who has a deck open sees it renamed as soon as it is renamed.
requirements.quote: sees every change as it happens
requirements.acceptance: Carbon B has /decks/D open. Silicon S runs `present rename D "Q4 review (final)"`. Within 2 s, with no reload, B's editor shows the new title, and B's live stream has delivered a `deck` event carrying it.

requirements.requirement: Everyone who has a deck open sees a restore as it happens, whether a whole version, one slide or one element was restored.
requirements.quote: sees every change as it happens
requirements.acceptance: Carbon B has /decks/D open at the latest version. Silicon S runs `present restore D 12`, and later `present restore D 12 --slide <slide> --element <element>`. After each one, within 2 s and with no reload, B's editor shows the deck (or that one element) as it was at version 12.

requirements.requirement: Everyone who has a deck open sees it happen when everything one Carbon or Silicon changed since a version is undone.
requirements.quote: sees every change as it happens
requirements.acceptance: Silicon S made several changes after version 40, and Carbon B has /decks/D open. Carbon A undoes S's changes since version 40, either from /decks/D/history or with `present undo-account D si:designer --since 40`. Within 2 s, with no reload, B's editor no longer shows any of S's changes.

requirements.requirement: Everyone who has a deck open sees it happen when a file is opened on top of the deck as its next version.
requirements.quote: sees every change as it happens
requirements.acceptance: Carbon B has /decks/D open. Silicon S runs `present open v2.pptx --into D`. Within 2 s of the command finishing, with no reload, B's slide list and canvas show the content from v2.pptx.

critic.problem: It requires opening a file on top of an existing deck as that deck's next version (`present open v2.pptx --into D`, POST /v1/decks/{id}/imports). UNDERSTANDING.md has no such feature, and its own sentence says the opposite: 'Opening a file creates a new deck from it'. The item makes an extra feature the build added into a contract requirement.
critic.fix: Drop EDIT-17 from the contract matrix: FMT-01 already checks that opening a file makes a new deck and leaves existing decks unchanged. If the Carbon wants opening a file into an existing deck, UNDERSTANDING.md needs a line for it first. Until then, a test may only check that, where the feature exists, it adds a new version and loses nothing.

requirements.requirement: A change a Silicon makes through the CLI appears in every open web editor of that deck as it happens, with no reload.
requirements.quote: sees every change as it happens
requirements.acceptance: Carbon A has /decks/D open on slide 3. Silicon S runs `present add shape D 3 ellipse --fill "#2f5bea" --x 100 --y 100 --w 300 --h 300`. Within 2 s of the command returning, with no reload, the ellipse is on A's canvas.

requirements.requirement: A Silicon can follow a deck's changes through the CLI as they happen.
requirements.quote: sees every change as it happens
requirements.acceptance: Silicon S runs `present watch D --json`. Carbon A moves a shape on slide 2 in /decks/D. Within 2 s, watch prints an `update` line whose author is c:ada and whose touched slides include slide 2's id.

requirements.requirement: A Silicon reading a deck through the CLI gets everyone's latest changes, including ones made in the web editor a moment earlier.
requirements.quote: sees every change as it happens
requirements.acceptance: Carbon A types "Hello from A" into a text box on slide 2 in /decks/D. Two seconds later Silicon S runs `present read D` and `present slide D 2 --json`. Both outputs contain "Hello from A".

requirements.requirement: A Silicon rendering a slide through the CLI sees everyone's latest changes in the image, including ones made a moment earlier.
requirements.quote: sees every change as it happens
requirements.acceptance: Carbon A changes a shape's fill on slide 2 from white to #ff0000 in /decks/D. Two seconds later Silicon S runs `present render D 2 -o s2.png`. The shape is red in s2.png.

requirements.requirement: Commenters and Viewers who have a deck open see every change as it happens, just as editors do.
requirements.quote: Everyone edits the same deck at the same time and sees every change as it happens.
requirements.acceptance: Carbon V (Viewer of D) and Carbon M (Commenter of D) have /decks/D open. Carbon A changes a text on slide 1, and Silicon S runs `present slide add D --title "New"`. Within 2 s, with no reload, both V's page and M's page show the changed text and the new slide.

requirements.requirement: Someone viewing a public deck through its link, without signing in, sees every change as it happens.
requirements.quote: Everyone edits the same deck at the same time and sees every change as it happens.
requirements.acceptance: Carbon A, the owner, runs `present public D view`. A browser that is not signed in opens D's link. A changes a text on slide 1 in /decks/D. Within 2 s, with no reload, the signed-out page shows the change.

requirements.requirement: Each Carbon who has a deck open shows up to everyone else in that deck.
requirements.quote: Each Carbon and Silicon in the deck shows up
requirements.acceptance: Carbons A and B open /decks/D. Within 2 s, each editor shows the other Carbon in its list of people in the deck, and each GET /v1/decks/D/live stream has delivered a `presence` event for the other's session.

requirements.requirement: A Carbon in a deck shows up with their name.
requirements.quote: Each Carbon and Silicon in the deck shows up with their name, pfp, cursor and the slide they're on.
requirements.acceptance: While A and B are both in /decks/D, B's editor shows an entry for A with A's name as Silicon Accounts holds it (her display name or c:ada).

critic.problem: The check passes if A's presence entry shows only her display name ('her display name or c:ada'). The Sign in section says Carbons are 'shown by their c:id or si:id', and SIGN-15 requires her presence to show c:ada, so the two items contradict each other.
critic.fix: Require A's presence entry to show c:ada; her display name may appear next to it. An entry that names her only by display name fails.

requirements.requirement: A Carbon in a deck shows up with their pfp.
requirements.quote: Each Carbon and Silicon in the deck shows up with their name, pfp, cursor and the slide they're on.
requirements.acceptance: A's Silicon Accounts account has a profile picture. While A is in /decks/D, B's editor shows that picture on A's entry.

requirements.requirement: A Carbon in a deck shows up with their cursor, which moves live as they move it over the slide.
requirements.quote: Each Carbon and Silicon in the deck shows up with their name, pfp, cursor and the slide they're on.
requirements.acceptance: A and B are both on slide 2 of /decks/D, with different window sizes and zoom. A moves her pointer to the slide's top-left corner and then to its bottom-right corner. Within about 1 s of each move, B sees A's cursor at that same spot on the slide.

requirements.requirement: A Carbon in a deck shows up with the slide they're on, and that updates when they move to another slide.
requirements.quote: Each Carbon and Silicon in the deck shows up with their name, pfp, cursor and the slide they're on.
requirements.acceptance: B is on slide 1 of /decks/D. A opens slide 3, and B's editor marks slide 3 as where A is (for example, A's picture on slide 3 in the slide list). A moves to slide 5, and within 2 s the mark moves to slide 5.

requirements.requirement: Everyone in a deck shows up, whatever their role. Commenters and Viewers who have it open appear just as editors do.
requirements.quote: Each Carbon and Silicon in the deck shows up
requirements.acceptance: Carbon V (Viewer of D) opens /decks/D on slide 2. Within 2 s, Carbon A's editor shows V's name and picture in its list of people in the deck, with V on slide 2. The same holds for Carbon M (Commenter).

requirements.requirement: Someone who leaves a deck, by closing it or losing their connection, stops showing up in it.
requirements.quote: Each Carbon and Silicon in the deck shows up
requirements.acceptance: A and B are in /decks/D, and B closes his tab. Within about 30 s (the presence expiry), B's entry, cursor and slide mark disappear from A's editor, and A's live stream delivers `presence_left` for B's session. Taking B's browser offline instead gives the same result, and so does Silicon S stopping `present watch D --here 2`.

requirements.requirement: The name and pfp someone shows up with always belong to the account they are signed in as. Nobody can show up as someone else.
requirements.quote: Each Carbon and Silicon in the deck shows up with their name, pfp, cursor and the slide they're on.
requirements.acceptance: Carbon B sends POST /v1/decks/D/presence with his own token and a body that also claims Carbon A's account (her uuid, c:ada, her name and pfp). A's editor and A's live stream show that session as B, with B's name and pfp, and never as A.

requirements.requirement: A Silicon following a deck through the CLI shows up in that deck, in the same list as the Carbons, for as long as it follows.
requirements.quote: Silicons show up exactly like Carbons do.
requirements.acceptance: Silicon S runs `present watch D --here 2 --json`. Within 2 s, Carbon A's open /decks/D lists S among the people in the deck, alongside the Carbons. S is still listed 90 s later while watch keeps running, well past the 30 s presence expiry.

requirements.requirement: While a Silicon is changing a deck through the CLI, it shows up in the deck on the slide it is changing, just as a Carbon editing that slide does.
requirements.quote: Silicons show up exactly like Carbons do.
requirements.acceptance: Without running `present watch`, Silicon S runs `present set D 3 <element> x=200`, and a few seconds later `present add text D 3 "Note"`. Within 2 s of the first command, Carbon A's open /decks/D shows S among the people in the deck, on slide 3.

requirements.requirement: A Silicon in a deck shows up with its name.
requirements.quote: Each Carbon and Silicon in the deck shows up with their name, pfp, cursor and the slide they're on. Silicons show up exactly like Carbons do.
requirements.acceptance: While Silicon S is in D (`present watch D --here 2`), Carbon A's editor shows an entry for S with S's name as Silicon Accounts holds it (its display name or si:designer).

critic.problem: The check passes if S's presence entry shows only a display name ('its display name or si:designer'), which contradicts 'shown by their c:id or si:id' and SIGN-16.
critic.fix: Require the entry to show si:designer; a display name may appear next to it. An entry with only a display name fails.

requirements.requirement: A Silicon in a deck shows up with its pfp.
requirements.quote: Each Carbon and Silicon in the deck shows up with their name, pfp, cursor and the slide they're on. Silicons show up exactly like Carbons do.
requirements.acceptance: Silicon S's Silicon Accounts account has a profile picture. While S is in D (`present watch D --here 2`), Carbon A's editor shows that picture on S's entry.

requirements.requirement: A Silicon in a deck shows up with a cursor, as a Carbon does.
requirements.quote: Each Carbon and Silicon in the deck shows up with their name, pfp, cursor and the slide they're on. Silicons show up exactly like Carbons do.
requirements.acceptance: Silicon S is in D on slide 2 (`present watch D --here 2`) and changes an element there with `present set D 2 <element> x=600`. Carbon A, also on slide 2, sees a cursor for S on the slide, drawn the same way as Carbon cursors.

requirements.requirement: A Silicon in a deck shows up with the slide it's on, and that updates when it moves to another slide.
requirements.quote: Each Carbon and Silicon in the deck shows up with their name, pfp, cursor and the slide they're on. Silicons show up exactly like Carbons do.
requirements.acceptance: Silicon S runs `present watch D --here 2`, and Carbon A's editor marks slide 2 as where S is. S then switches to slide 5 (`present watch D --here 5`, or starts changing slide 5 through the CLI). Within 2 s the mark moves to slide 5.

requirements.requirement: A Silicon in a deck is shown exactly as a Carbon is: in the same list, with the same name, picture, cursor and slide mark, not in a separate list and not in a different or lesser form.
requirements.quote: Silicons show up exactly like Carbons do.
requirements.acceptance: Carbon B is on slide 2 of D in the editor, and Silicon S is on slide 2 through `present watch D --here 2`. In Carbon A's editor, B and S appear in the same list with the same parts (picture and name). Both have a cursor on slide 2 and both are marked on slide 2 in the slide list. Apart from its own name and picture, nothing about S's entry differs from B's.

requirements.requirement: A Silicon following a deck through the CLI can see who else is in it, with each person's name, pfp, cursor and the slide they're on.
requirements.quote: Each Carbon and Silicon in the deck shows up with their name, pfp, cursor and the slide they're on.
requirements.acceptance: Silicon S runs `present watch D --json`. Carbon A opens /decks/D on slide 2 and moves her pointer. Within 2 s, watch prints `presence` lines for A carrying c:ada, her name, her pfp URL, slide 2's id, and cursor x,y values that change as she moves. When A closes her tab, watch prints `presence_left` for her session within about 30 s.

requirements.requirement: Everyone sees a Silicon's change appear all at once: every part of one change shows up at the same moment, never piece by piece.
requirements.quote: When a Silicon makes a change, the whole change appears at once
requirements.acceptance: Carbon A has /decks/D open. Silicon S runs `present edit D --ops ops.json`, where the one ops file adds a slide with three elements, rewrites a text on slide 2 and deletes a shape on slide 3. A's GET /v1/decks/D/live stream delivers exactly one `update` event for it, and A's editor never shows only some of those changes (for example, the new slide without its elements). The same holds for a single `present slide add D --layout title-body --title "Plan" --body $'One\nTwo'`.

requirements.requirement: If a Silicon's change can't be applied in full, none of it is applied and no part of it appears.
requirements.quote: the whole change appears at once
requirements.acceptance: Silicon S runs `present edit D --ops ops.json`, where the first op adds a slide and the second is a `replace_text` for a passage that isn't in the deck. The CLI exits non-zero with `text_not_found`. The deck's version stays the same, `present read D` has no new slide, and Carbon A's live stream delivers no `update` for it.

requirements.requirement: Pushing a pulled folder counts as one Silicon change, so everything in the push appears to others at once.
requirements.quote: When a Silicon makes a change, the whole change appears at once
requirements.acceptance: Silicon S runs `present pull D q4/`, edits slide.json for slides 2 and 4 and one HTML element's .html file, then runs `present push q4/`. Carbon A's live stream delivers one `update` event holding all of it, and A's editor shows every one of the changes at the same moment.

requirements.requirement: When a Silicon's change appears, it is briefly highlighted so the people watching can see what changed.
requirements.quote: briefly highlighted with its name
requirements.acceptance: Carbon A is on slide 2 of /decks/D. Silicon S runs `present edit D --ops ops.json`, which restyles one element and adds another on slide 2.
