As they appear, both elements are visibly highlighted on A's canvas (for example, outlined). Elements S didn't touch are not highlighted.

requirements.requirement: The highlight on a Silicon's change shows the name of the Silicon that made it.
requirements.quote: briefly highlighted with its name
requirements.acceptance: In the EDIT-43 run, the highlight on A's canvas carries S's name as Silicon Accounts holds it (display name or si:designer), the account that made the change.

critic.problem: It reads 'briefly highlighted with its name' as either the display name or the si:id. Read together with 'shown by their c:id or si:id', the highlight has to name si:designer.
critic.fix: Require the highlight to show si:designer; a display name may be added. A highlight showing only a display name fails.

requirements.requirement: The highlight is brief: it goes away by itself after a short time, and the change stays.
requirements.quote: briefly highlighted with its name
requirements.acceptance: In the EDIT-43 run, A touches nothing. Within a few seconds (at most about 10 s) of the change appearing, the highlight and S's name are gone from A's canvas, and the restyled and added elements remain as S left them.

requirements.requirement: A Carbon whose connection drops can keep editing in the web editor, and everything they do meanwhile stays.
requirements.quote: If a connection drops, nothing is lost.
requirements.acceptance: Carbon A has /decks/D open, and her browser goes offline (Playwright `context.setOffline(true)`). She adds a slide, types "Offline edit" in a text box and moves a shape. The editor keeps taking her edits and shows all three. It never turns read-only and never drops what she typed.

requirements.requirement: Changes a Carbon made while their connection was down merge into the live deck on their own as soon as it returns, without the Carbon doing anything.
requirements.quote: Changes made meanwhile merge back in once it returns.
requirements.acceptance: Continuing from EDIT-46, A's browser goes back online. Within 5 s, without A reloading or clicking anything, Carbon B's open /decks/D and `present read D` both show A's new slide, "Offline edit" and the moved shape.

requirements.requirement: When a Carbon's connection returns, they get every change others made while it was down.
requirements.quote: Changes made meanwhile merge back in once it returns.
requirements.acceptance: While Carbon A is offline, Carbon B edits a text on slide 3 and Silicon S runs `present slide add D --title "Added by S"`. When A comes back online, within 5 s and with no reload, A's editor shows both. It also holds when the proxy routinely ends A's live stream after 5 minutes while B and S keep editing: nothing they did in the gap is missing.

requirements.requirement: If someone changes a text while offline and someone else changes the same text in the meantime, both changes are kept once the connection returns.
requirements.quote: Changes made meanwhile merge back in once it returns.
requirements.acceptance: Slide 1's title is "Plan". Carbon A goes offline and adds " (draft)" to its end. Meanwhile Carbon B, still online, adds "Q4 " to its start. When A is back online, within 5 s A's editor, B's editor and `present read D` all show "Q4 Plan (draft)".

requirements.requirement: Changes made offline survive closing the tab before the connection returns, and they merge in when the deck is next opened online in that browser.
requirements.quote: If a connection drops, nothing is lost.
requirements.acceptance: Carbon A goes offline in /decks/D, types "Typed offline" into a text box, and closes the tab while still offline. Her connection comes back, and she opens /decks/D again in the same browser. Within 5 s, "Typed offline" is in her editor, in Carbon B's editor and in `present read D`.

requirements.requirement: A Silicon working on a pulled folder while its connection is down loses nothing. Once the connection returns, `present push` merges its changes in alongside whatever others did meanwhile.
requirements.quote: Changes made meanwhile merge back in once it returns.
requirements.acceptance: Silicon S runs `present pull D q4/`. Its connection is then cut (for example, the CLI's PRESENT_API_URL points at an address that drops traffic), and it edits q4/slides/02-*/slide.json. Meanwhile Carbon A changes slide 3 in the web editor. When the connection is back, S runs `present push q4/`. It exits 0, and both `present read D` and A's editor show S's change to slide 2 and A's change to slide 3.

requirements.requirement: A CLI change tried while the Silicon's connection is down is never lost without a word. The CLI says it didn't go in, and the pulled folder keeps the edits so they can be pushed later.
requirements.quote: If a connection drops, nothing is lost.
requirements.acceptance: With S's connection cut, `present push q4/` and `present set D 2 <element> x=10` both exit non-zero, with an error saying the service could not be reached and nothing was changed. `present status q4/` still lists every local edit. Once the connection is back, the deck shows nothing from the failed attempts until S pushes again, and then it shows the folder's edits.

requirements.requirement: A Silicon following a deck through the CLI gets every change made while its connection was down, once the connection returns, without restarting.
requirements.quote: If a connection drops, nothing is lost.
requirements.acceptance: Silicon S runs `present watch D --json`. Its connection is cut for 20 s, and during that time Carbon A adds a slide. Without S restarting anything, watch reconnects on its own once the connection is back and prints an event that brings in A's new slide. Nothing A did during the cut is missing from what watch reports.

requirements.requirement: A signed-in Carbon who can comment but can't edit the deck (Commenter role, or comment access through a public link) gets the comment box with one click anywhere on a slide in the web. It opens right at that spot, ready to type, with no button, menu or mode switch first.
requirements.quote: Commenting has to be as easy as pointing. For anyone who can't edit, or who is just viewing, clicking on a slide opens the comment box right there, with no button or menu in between.
requirements.acceptance: c:ada (owner) runs `present share <deck> c:bea --role commenter`. c:bea opens /decks/{id} and clicks once on empty background of slide 1 at slide point (400,300). Observe: a comment box opens at or right beside that point with its text field focused, and nothing was pressed before the click (no Comment button, menu or mode switch). Clicking on a text box instead does the same and doesn't start text editing. c:bea types and posts, and GET /v1/decks/{id}/threads shows a new open thread by c:bea on slide 1. Repeat with c:cy, who has no share, after c:ada runs `present public <deck> comment`: once signed in, the same single click opens the box, and the thread is authored by c:cy.

requirements.requirement: Someone just viewing the deck, such as a visitor who isn't signed in on a public link that allows commenting, also gets the comment box right where they click on a slide, with no button or menu first. Posting from it asks them to sign in first. (Interpretation of 'just viewing'; see the note.)
requirements.quote: For anyone who can't edit, or who is just viewing, clicking on a slide opens the comment box right there, with no button or menu in between. … Viewing a public deck never needs signing in. Commenting or editing through the link does, so every change and every comment always has a Carbon or Silicon behind it.
requirements.acceptance: c:ada (owner) runs `present public <deck> comment`. In a browser with no session, open /decks/{id}: the deck shows without signing in. Click once on slide 1 at (500,400): the comment box (or its sign-in prompt) opens at that spot, with nothing pressed before. Trying to post leads through Silicon Accounts sign-in. Signed in as c:dee, they can post at that point, and GET /v1/decks/{id}/threads shows the thread authored by c:dee. POST /v1/decks/{id}/threads with no token is refused (401). Note: UNDERSTANDING.md doesn't define 'just viewing'. Sharing says a Viewer 'can only view', so the box must never let a Viewer-role member post (POST with their token returns 403). If the Carbon meant an Editor who is viewing rather than editing, the web needs that viewing state, so confirm this reading with the Carbon.

requirements.requirement: For an Editor who is editing, a plain click on a slide selects or edits as in Google Slides and doesn't open the comment box. Editors start a comment with the Comment button or the shortcut. (implied)
requirements.quote: Editors get a small `Comment` button and a keyboard shortcut. … Carbons edit text, images, shapes, tables, charts and videos directly on the slide, just like in Google Slides or PowerPoint.
requirements.acceptance: c:ada (Editor) opens /decks/{id} and clicks a text box on slide 1: it gets selected (resize handles show) and no comment box opens. Clicking empty background clears the selection and also opens no comment box. GET /v1/decks/{id}/threads is unchanged.

requirements.requirement: The web editor shows Editors a small 'Comment' button. Pressing it lets them put a comment on the slide by pointing at it (clicking a point or dragging over an area).
requirements.quote: Editors get a small `Comment` button and a keyboard shortcut.
requirements.acceptance: c:ada (Editor) sees a compact 'Comment' button in the editor at /decks/{id}. She presses it and clicks slide 2 at (600,500): the comment box opens there. Posting creates a point thread at about (600,500) on slide 2 (GET /v1/decks/{id}/threads). With the button pressed, dragging over (100,100)–(500,400) instead creates an area thread.

requirements.requirement: The web editor gives Editors a keyboard shortcut that starts a comment, the same as pressing the Comment button.
requirements.quote: Editors get a small `Comment` button and a keyboard shortcut.
requirements.acceptance: c:ada (Editor), with the canvas focused and no text field active, presses the editor's comment shortcut (the key named on the Comment button or in the editor's shortcut list) without touching the button. She then clicks slide 2 at (700,400): the comment box opens there, and posting creates a point thread at about (700,400) (GET /v1/decks/{id}/threads).

requirements.requirement: A comment can be put on a point on a slide by clicking it. The thread is tied to that point in slide coordinates, and everyone who opens the deck sees it there.
requirements.quote: A comment can be on: … a point on a slide, by clicking it
requirements.acceptance: c:bea (Commenter) clicks empty background on slide 2 at (400,300) in /decks/{id} and posts. GET /v1/decks/{id}/threads shows anchor kind 'point' on slide 2's id at x≈400, y≈300 (±2 slide px). c:ada (owner) opens the deck at a different window size or zoom and sees the thread's marker at that same spot on slide 2. `present comments <deck> --json` reports it on slide 2 at 400,300. The other way: si:designer (Editor) runs `present comment <deck> --slide 2 --point 1500,800 'Nudge left'`, and c:ada sees a marker at (1500,800) on slide 2 that opens that thread.

requirements.requirement: A comment can be put on an area of a slide by dragging over it. The thread is tied to that rectangle, which is shown when the thread is opened.
requirements.quote: A comment can be on: … an area of a slide, by dragging over it
requirements.acceptance: c:bea (Commenter) drags over empty background of slide 2 from (200,150) to (900,600) in /decks/{id}. The comment box opens by the area and c:bea posts. The API anchor is kind 'area' on slide 2 with x≈200, y≈150, w≈700, h≈450. When c:ada (owner) opens the thread, that rectangle is outlined on slide 2. si:designer (Editor) runs `present comment <deck> --slide 2 --area 100,100,600,400 'Simplify'`, and the web outlines (100,100, 600×400) for that thread. `present comments <deck>` lists both as areas with their rectangles.

requirements.requirement: A comment can be on an element itself (any kind), not just on a point or area of the slide. Opening the thread shows which element it's on.
requirements.quote: A comment can be on: … an element, including an HTML element while it's running
requirements.acceptance: Slide 2 holds chart e_chart and image e_img. c:bea (Commenter) comments on the chart itself in /decks/{id}, using the web's way of commenting on a whole element, and posts. GET /v1/decks/{id}/threads shows anchor kind 'element' with element e_chart, and opening the thread highlights the chart. si:designer (Editor) runs `present comment <deck> --slide 2 --element e_img 'Crop tighter'`. c:ada (owner) sees that thread on the image, and `present read <deck> --comments` prints it next to e_img.

requirements.requirement: A comment can be put on an HTML element while it is running, without the element being stopped or reloaded.
requirements.quote: A comment can be on: … an element, including an HTML element while it's running
requirements.acceptance: si:designer (Editor) adds an HTML element to slide 3 whose JS shows a counter rising every 100 ms (`present add html <deck> 3 --html counter.html --js counter.js --x 200 --y 200 --w 800 --h 400`). c:bea (Commenter) opens slide 3 in /decks/{id}, waits until the counter passes 20, comments on that HTML element and posts. Observe: the counter keeps rising the whole time and never drops back to 0, so the element wasn't reloaded. The API anchor names the HTML element's id (kind 'element'). `present comment <deck> --slide 3 --element <html id> 'Slower please'` also succeeds, and c:ada (owner) sees that thread on the running element.

requirements.requirement: For anyone who can comment, clicking on a running HTML element, even one covering the whole slide, opens the comment box at that spot and the comment lands on that point. The element doesn't swallow the click and keeps running. (implied)
requirements.quote: clicking on a slide opens the comment box right there … an element, including an HTML element while it's running … An HTML element can be a small part of a slide or cover the whole of it.
requirements.acceptance: Slide 4 holds one HTML element at 0,0, 1920×1080 that animates and listens for clicks in its JS (`present add html <deck> 4 --html full.html --js anim.js --x 0 --y 0 --w 1920 --h 1080`). c:bea (Commenter) clicks slide 4 at (960,540) in /decks/{id}. The comment box opens at that spot and the animation keeps going. The posted thread's anchor is a point at about (960,540) on slide 4 (GET /v1/decks/{id}/threads). The same works for c:ada (Editor) after pressing the Comment button.

requirements.requirement: For anyone who can comment, dragging over part of a running HTML element makes an area comment over that part. The element doesn't take the drag and keeps running. (implied)
requirements.quote: an area of a slide, by dragging over it … an element, including an HTML element while it's running … An HTML element can be a small part of a slide or cover the whole of it.
requirements.acceptance: On slide 4's full-slide running HTML element, c:bea (Commenter) drags from (300,200) to (800,600) in /decks/{id}. The area is drawn, the comment box opens, and the animation keeps running. The posted thread is an area of about (300,200, 500×400) on slide 4 (GET /v1/decks/{id}/threads).

requirements.requirement: A comment can be on some text inside an element, such as a passage of a text box or of a shape's text. The thread is tied to that passage, which is highlighted when the thread is opened.
requirements.quote: A comment can be on: … some text inside an element
requirements.acceptance: si:designer (Editor) runs `present add text <deck> 3 'Revenue grew 40% in Q3'`. c:bea (Commenter, can't edit) picks the passage '40% in Q3' in /decks/{id}, using the web's way of commenting on text, and posts 'Is this Q4?'. The API anchor is kind 'text' with that element, field 'text' and quote '40% in Q3', and opening the thread highlights exactly that passage. si:designer runs `present comment <deck> --slide 3 --element <id> --text 'Revenue grew' 'Say by how much'`, and the web highlights 'Revenue grew' for that thread. A shape's text works the same way. `present comments <deck>` shows each quote next to its element.

requirements.requirement: Text inside a table cell can be commented on, with the thread tied to that passage in that cell. (implied: a table is an element)
requirements.quote: some text inside an element … `Element` - Anything placed on a slide: text, an image, a shape, a table, a chart, a video, or an HTML element.
requirements.acceptance: si:designer (Editor) runs `present add table <deck> 5 --rows 3 --cols 3 --cell '1,2=12 units'`. c:bea (Commenter) comments on 'units' in that cell from /decks/{id}. The API anchor is kind 'text' with field 'cell:1:2' and quote 'units', and opening the thread highlights it in that cell. `present comment <deck> --slide 5 --element <table id> --text 12 --field cell:1:2 'Check this'` succeeds, and the web shows that thread on the same cell.

requirements.requirement: A comment can be on a whole slide.
requirements.quote: A comment can be on: … a whole slide
requirements.acceptance: On slide 4, c:bea (Commenter) starts a whole-slide comment in /decks/{id} (e.g. the comments list's 'On this slide') and posts. The API anchor is kind 'slide' with slide 4's id and no point, area or element. The web shows the thread under slide 4 as on the whole slide. si:designer (Editor) runs `present comment <deck> --slide 4 'Too dense'`, and c:ada (owner) sees it under slide 4 as a whole-slide comment.

requirements.requirement: A comment can be on the whole deck.
requirements.quote: A comment can be on: … the whole deck
requirements.acceptance: c:bea (Commenter) starts a comment on the whole deck in /decks/{id} (e.g. 'On the whole deck') and posts. The API anchor is kind 'deck'. The web shows the thread as on the whole deck, not under any slide. si:designer (Editor) runs `present comment <deck> --deck 'Looks great overall'`, and c:ada (owner) sees it with the deck-wide threads. `present comments <deck>` lists both as on the whole deck.

requirements.requirement: A Silicon with only the Commenter role (no edit rights) can make every kind of comment through the CLI, as a Carbon Commenter can in the web. (implied)
requirements.quote: A comment can be on: … Carbons and Silicons get exactly the same roles and the same rights. … a Silicon can read, write, reply to, react to and resolve comments, exactly like a Carbon.
requirements.acceptance: c:ada (owner) runs `present share <deck> si:reviewer --role commenter`. si:reviewer runs `present comment <deck>` six times, with --deck, --slide 1, --slide 1 --point 100,100, --slide 1 --area 0,0,500,300, --slide 1 --element <id>, and --slide 1 --element <id> --text '<passage>'. Each one succeeds. In /decks/{id}, c:ada sees all six threads authored by si:reviewer and shown by its si:id. Sanity check: `present set <deck> 1 <id> x=0` by si:reviewer is refused, so it really can't edit.

requirements.requirement: Anyone who can comment can reply to a comment, and the reply joins that comment's thread.
requirements.quote: Comments can be replied to, reacted to, edited and resolved. … A comment and its replies are a `thread`. … a Silicon can read, write, reply to, react to and resolve comments, exactly like a Carbon.
requirements.acceptance: c:bea (Commenter) starts a thread on slide 2. si:designer (Editor) runs `present reply <thread> 'Done in the latest version'`. In /decks/{id}, c:ada (owner) opens the thread and sees c:bea's comment followed by si:designer's reply in the same thread, the reply shown by its si:id. c:ada replies 'Thanks' in the web. `present comments <deck> --json` and GET /v1/decks/{id}/threads show one thread holding the three comments in order.

requirements.requirement: Anyone who can comment can react to a comment with an emoji, and everyone who opens the thread sees the reaction on that comment.
requirements.quote: Comments can be replied to, reacted to, edited and resolved. … a Silicon can read, write, reply to, react to and resolve comments, exactly like a Carbon.
requirements.acceptance: si:designer (Editor) runs `present react <comment id> 👍` on c:bea's comment. In /decks/{id}, c:ada (owner) sees 👍 with a count of 1 on that comment and adds 🎉 in the web. `present comments <deck> --json` shows both reactions on that comment. Reacting to a reply works the same way.

requirements.requirement: The author of a comment can edit its text, and everyone then sees the new text in place of the old, in the same thread.
requirements.quote: Comments can be replied to, reacted to, edited and resolved. … The `present` CLI is how Silicons use Silicon Present, and it can do everything the web editor can.
requirements.acceptance: c:bea (Commenter) edits her comment from 'Too close to the edge' to 'Too close to the left edge' in /decks/{id}. c:ada (owner) and `present comments <deck>` see the new text in the same thread, at the same anchor. si:designer (Editor) edits its own reply with `present comment edit <comment> 'Fixed wording'`, and the web shows 'Fixed wording'.

requirements.requirement: Only a comment's author can change its text; no one else can, not even an Editor or the owner. (implied)
requirements.quote: Comments can be replied to, reacted to, edited and resolved. … so every change and every comment always has a Carbon or Silicon behind it.
requirements.acceptance: c:ada (owner) opens c:bea's comment in /decks/{id} and finds no way to edit it. PATCH /v1/comments/{id} with c:ada's token is refused with 403. si:designer (Editor) running `present comment edit <c:bea's comment id> 'x'` fails with a permission error. The text stays unchanged in the web, in `present comments` and in the API.

requirements.requirement: A thread can be resolved, and it then shows as resolved to everyone.
requirements.quote: Comments can be replied to, reacted to, edited and resolved. … a Silicon can read, write, reply to, react to and resolve comments, exactly like a Carbon.
requirements.acceptance: c:bea's thread is open. si:designer (Editor) runs `present resolve <thread>`. GET /v1/decks/{id}/threads?state=open no longer includes it, and ?state=resolved does. In /decks/{id}, c:ada and c:bea see it marked resolved wherever it's listed. c:ada (owner) resolves a second thread from the web, and `present comments <deck> --resolved` lists it.

requirements.requirement: A resolved thread can be reopened, and it is then open again for everyone.
requirements.quote: Resolved threads can be reopened. … it can do everything the web editor can.
requirements.acceptance: With her thread resolved, c:bea (Commenter) finds it in /decks/{id} (e.g. with 'Show resolved' on) and reopens it. GET /v1/decks/{id}/threads?state=open includes it again, and c:ada sees it as open. si:designer (Editor) reopens another resolved thread with `present reopen <thread>`, and `present comments <deck>` lists it as open.

requirements.requirement: A comment on an element follows that element when it is moved or resized, whoever makes the change (a Silicon through the CLI included).
requirements.quote: A comment follows its element as the slide changes.
requirements.acceptance: An element comment is on image e_img at 200,200, 400×300 on slide 2. si:designer (Editor) runs `present set <deck> 2 e_img x=1100 y=600 w=600 h=450`. In /decks/{id}, c:ada (owner) sees the thread's marker or highlight on the image at its new place, with nothing left at the old spot. `present read <deck> --comments` prints the thread next to e_img at its new position. c:ada then drags the image elsewhere in the web, and after the drop the marker is on the image again.

requirements.requirement: A point comment made by clicking on an element stays on the same spot of that element when the element is moved or resized. (implied)
requirements.quote: a point on a slide, by clicking it … A comment follows its element as the slide changes.
requirements.acceptance: Image e_img is at 200,200, 400×300 on slide 2. c:bea (Commenter) clicks it at (300,350), a quarter in from its left edge and halfway down, and posts. si:designer (Editor) also runs `present comment <deck> --slide 2 --point 250,250 --element e_img 'Sharper'`. Then si:designer runs `present set <deck> 2 e_img x=1000 y=400 w=800 h=600`. In /decks/{id}, c:bea's marker is now at about (1200,700) and the CLI one at about (1100,500), the same spots of the moved and scaled image, not the old coordinates. GET /v1/decks/{id}/threads shows both anchors still tied to e_img.

requirements.requirement: An area comment dragged over an element keeps covering the same part of that element when the element is moved or resized. (implied)
requirements.quote: an area of a slide, by dragging over it … A comment follows its element as the slide changes.
requirements.acceptance: Chart e_chart is at 100,100, 800×400 on slide 2. c:bea (Commenter) drags over its right half, from (500,100) to (900,500), and posts. si:designer (Editor) also runs `present comment <deck> --slide 2 --area 500,100,400,400 --element e_chart 'Too busy'`. si:designer then runs `present set <deck> 2 e_chart x=900 y=500`, and in /decks/{id} both outlined areas become about (1300,500, 400×400). Then `present set <deck> 2 e_chart w=400 h=200` makes them about (1100,500, 200×200). Each time they still cover the chart's right half.

requirements.requirement: A comment on some text stays on the same passage when the element's text is edited around it. (implied)
requirements.quote: some text inside an element … A comment follows its element as the slide changes.
requirements.acceptance: A text comment made in the web is on '40% in Q3' in 'Revenue grew 40% in Q3' on slide 3, and another, made with `present comment <deck> --slide 3 --element <id> --text 'in Q3' 'Which year?'`, is on 'in Q3'. si:designer (Editor) runs `present replace <deck> 3 <id> --find 'Revenue grew' --replace 'Total revenue grew'`, and c:ada (owner) types 'Note: ' at the very start of the text box in /decks/{id}. Opening each thread still highlights exactly its own passage, not a shifted range, and `present comments <deck>` still quotes them on that element.

requirements.requirement: Comments on a slide, or on anything on it, stay with that slide when the slides are reordered. (implied)
requirements.quote: a whole slide … A comment follows its element as the slide changes.
requirements.acceptance: Slide 4 ('Pricing') has a whole-slide comment, a point comment and an element comment. si:designer (Editor) runs `present slide move <deck> 4 --first`. In /decks/{id}, all three threads now show on slide 1 'Pricing' and are listed under it. `present comments <deck>` lists them under slide 1, and none of them appears on the slide that is now slide 4.

requirements.requirement: Deleting an element doesn't delete the comments on it: its threads, replies included, stay in the deck.
requirements.quote: If the element is deleted, the comment stays, showing what it was on.
requirements.acceptance: A thread with one reply is on chart e_chart on slide 2. si:designer (Editor) runs `present delete <deck> 2 e_chart`. GET /v1/decks/{id}/threads?state=all still returns the thread, still open, with both comments. It stays in the web list at /decks/{id} for c:ada and c:bea and in `present comments <deck>`, and it can still be opened, replied to and resolved.

requirements.requirement: A comment whose element was deleted shows what it was on: the kind of element and its slide, and for a text comment, the quoted text.
requirements.quote: If the element is deleted, the comment stays, showing what it was on.
requirements.acceptance: After `present delete <deck> 2 e_chart`, the web at /decks/{id} shows the orphaned thread as having been on a chart on slide 2, and `present comments <deck>` and `present read <deck> --comments` say the same. A text comment on '40% in Q3' whose text box was deleted still shows '40% in Q3' and its slide. A thread made with `present comment --element` shows the same kind of description after its element is deleted as one made in the web.

requirements.requirement: Deleting a slide doesn't delete the comments on its elements: they stay, showing what they were on. (implied: deleting a slide deletes its elements)
requirements.quote: If the element is deleted, the comment stays, showing what it was on.
requirements.acceptance: Slide 3 has an element comment on its title text box and a text comment on its body. si:designer (Editor) runs `present slide delete <deck> 3`. Both threads are still returned by GET /v1/decks/{id}/threads?state=all and are still listed in the web at /decks/{id} and in `present comments <deck>`. Each still shows what it was on: a text box on slide 3, and the quoted passage.

requirements.requirement: Deleting a slide doesn't delete the comments on the slide itself (whole-slide, point and area): they stay, showing which slide they were on. (implied)
requirements.quote: If the element is deleted, the comment stays, showing what it was on. … Everything in Silicon Present is versioned, and nothing is ever lost.
requirements.acceptance: Slide 3 has a whole-slide, a point and an area comment. si:designer (Editor) runs `present slide delete <deck> 3`. All three threads stay in GET /v1/decks/{id}/threads?state=all, in the web list at /decks/{id} and in `present comments <deck>`, each showing that it was on slide 3.

requirements.requirement: All of a deck's threads can be seen together in one list, from every slide and including deck-wide ones, without going slide by slide.
requirements.quote: All of a deck's threads can be seen in one list
requirements.acceptance: The deck has threads on the deck and on slides 1–3 (point, area, element and text), one resolved, and one whose element was deleted. With slide 1 showing, c:ada (owner) opens the comments list in /decks/{id}. Every open thread from every slide is in that one list, the deck-wide and deleted-element ones included, and asking for resolved threads (e.g. 'Show resolved') adds the resolved one. `present comments <deck> --all` lists every thread, and GET /v1/decks/{id}/threads?state=all returns them all in one response.

requirements.requirement: The deck's list of threads is grouped by slide.
requirements.quote: All of a deck's threads can be seen in one list, grouped by slide
requirements.acceptance: In that same deck, the web list at /decks/{id} shows one group per slide that has threads, headed by that slide and holding every thread on it whatever the kind, with the groups in the deck's slide order. Deck-wide threads sit outside every slide's group. `present comments <deck>` prints the same grouping. After `present slide move <deck> 3 --first`, the groups follow the new order.

requirements.requirement: The threads in the list can be moved through one by one with the keyboard.
requirements.quote: moved through one by one with the keyboard
requirements.acceptance: c:bea (Commenter) focuses the comments list in /decks/{id} and uses only the keyboard. The next-thread key (e.g. ↓ or j) opens the first thread, then each following thread one at a time in list order, crossing from one slide's group into the next. The previous-thread key (e.g. ↑ or k) steps back one at a time. Every thread can be reached without the mouse.

requirements.requirement: Writing a Carbon's c:id as a mention in a comment (`@c:<handle>`, the form the contract's own example uses) sends that Carbon a `present.mention.received` ting.
requirements.quote: Anyone can mention a Carbon or Silicon in a comment with their c:id or si:id.
requirements.acceptance: si:designer (editor) runs `present comment <deck> --slide 2 "@c:ada can you check these numbers"`. Within a few seconds (delivery is queued), the Ting stand-in (port 4323 in the final e2e lane) has exactly one `present.mention.received` for this comment, with `for` = c:ada's Silicon Accounts uuid (the one `GET /v1/accounts/resolve?q=c:ada` returns). Then c:bob (editor) opens /decks/[id] in the web, uses the Comment button on slide 3, types `@c:ada please look` in the comment box and posts it. A second `present.mention.received` for c:ada appears, for that comment.

requirements.requirement: Writing a Silicon's si:id as a mention in a comment (`@si:<handle>`) sends that Silicon a `present.mention.received` ting.
requirements.quote: Anyone can mention a Carbon or Silicon in a comment with their c:id or si:id.
requirements.acceptance: c:ada (editor) opens /decks/[id] in the web, uses the Comment button on slide 2, types `@si:designer make the title shorter` and posts it. The Ting stand-in has exactly one `present.mention.received` for that comment, with `for` = si:designer's Silicon Accounts uuid. Then si:writer runs `present comment <deck> --deck "@si:designer please check the theme"`, so a Silicon mentions a Silicon, and a second `present.mention.received` for si:designer appears.

requirements.requirement: Anyone who can comment can mention, not only the owner or editors. A Carbon or Silicon with only the commenter role can mention, and the mention is delivered.
requirements.quote: Anyone can mention a Carbon or Silicon in a comment with their c:id or si:id.
requirements.acceptance: c:ada owns the deck and shares it with si:writer and c:bob as commenter only (`present share <deck> si:writer --role commenter`, same for c:bob). si:writer runs `present comment <deck> --slide 1 "@c:ada the intro is long"`. c:bob opens /decks/[id], clicks on slide 1 (the comment box opens right there, no button), types `@si:designer simplify this` and posts it. The Ting stand-in has a `present.mention.received` for c:ada (from si:writer's comment) and one for si:designer (from c:bob's comment).

requirements.requirement: A signed-in Carbon or Silicon who was never invited can mention when commenting through the deck's public link (public mode `comment` or `edit`). The mentioned account gets `present.mention.received`.
requirements.quote: Anyone can mention a Carbon or Silicon in a comment with their c:id or si:id.
requirements.acceptance: c:ada runs `present public <deck> comment`. c:bob has no invite. He signs in, opens the deck's link in the web, clicks on slide 2 and posts `@si:designer fix the typo`. si:writer also has no invite and runs `present comment <deck> --slide 2 "@c:ada wrong date"`. The Ting stand-in has a `present.mention.received` for si:designer whose comment is by c:bob, and one for c:ada whose comment is by si:writer.

requirements.requirement: A mention in a reply sends the mentioned account `present.mention.received`, the same as a mention in a thread's first comment.
requirements.quote: | `present.mention.received` | Someone mentions you in a comment | The one mentioned |
requirements.acceptance: c:ada starts a thread on slide 2 in the web, with no mention. si:designer runs `present reply <thread> "Done. @c:bob can you double-check?"`. The Ting stand-in has a `present.mention.received` for c:bob that carries this reply. c:ada then replies in the web with `@si:writer please proofread`, and si:writer gets one too. Neither c:bob nor si:writer had written in the thread before, so this checks the mention itself, not `present.comment.replied`.

requirements.requirement: A mention is recognised wherever it appears in the comment: at the start, mid-sentence, at the end, on a later line, and directly followed by punctuation.
requirements.quote: Anyone can mention a Carbon or Silicon in a comment with their c:id or si:id.
requirements.acceptance: si:writer posts five separate comments with `present comment <deck> --deck ...`: `@si:designer, make this simpler`, `Thanks @c:ada.`, `Can you look (@c:bob)?`, `Ping @si:designer: shorten it`, and a two-line body whose second line is `over to you @c:ada`. For each comment, the Ting stand-in has `present.mention.received` for exactly the intended account (si:designer, c:ada, c:bob, si:designer, c:ada) and for no other. Accounts handles are 3 to 30 characters of a-z, 0-9, `-` and `_`, so none of this punctuation can be part of the id.

requirements.requirement: A comment that mentions several Carbons and Silicons sends one `present.mention.received` to each of them and to no one else.
requirements.quote: | `present.mention.received` | Someone mentions you in a comment | The one mentioned |
requirements.acceptance: The deck is shared with c:bob, si:designer, si:writer and c:carol. c:ada (owner) drags over part of slide 3 in the web and posts `@c:bob @si:designer @si:writer please review`. The Ting stand-in has exactly three `present.mention.received` for this comment, one each for c:bob, si:designer and si:writer, and none for c:carol or anyone else.

requirements.requirement: Mentioning the same account more than once in one comment sends it a single `present.mention.received` for that comment.
requirements.quote: | `present.mention.received` | Someone mentions you in a comment | The one mentioned |
requirements.acceptance: si:writer runs `present comment <deck> --slide 2 "@si:designer simplify this, and @si:designer also fix the colours"`. The Ting stand-in has exactly one `present.mention.received` for si:designer for this comment.

requirements.requirement: Editing a comment so that it mentions someone it didn't before sends the newly mentioned account `present.mention.received`. Accounts the comment already mentioned don't get a second one. (Implied: after the edit, someone has mentioned them in a comment.)
requirements.quote: | `present.mention.received` | Someone mentions you in a comment | The one mentioned |
requirements.acceptance: c:ada posts `@si:designer simplify this` on slide 2 in the web, and si:designer gets one ting. She edits that comment in the web (`PATCH /v1/comments/{c}`) to `@si:designer simplify this, @si:writer check the copy`. The Ting stand-in gains exactly one new `present.mention.received`, for si:writer, and no second one for si:designer. A Silicon editing its own comment with `present comment edit <comment> "... @c:bob"` sends c:bob one the same way.

requirements.requirement: An `@c:...` or `@si:...` written anywhere other than a comment is not a mention and sends no ting. This covers slide text, speaker notes, table cells and HTML/CSS/JS.
requirements.quote: Anyone can mention a Carbon or Silicon in a comment with their c:id or si:id.
requirements.acceptance: si:designer (editor) uses the CLI to put `Questions to @c:ada` into a text element (`present set <deck> 2 text:1 text="Questions to @c:ada"`), into slide 2's speaker notes, into a table cell and into an HTML element's `html`. c:bob (editor) types `ask @si:writer` into a text box in the web editor. The Ting stand-in records no ting of any type for c:ada or si:writer.

requirements.requirement: The text puts no access condition on who can be mentioned. A comment can mention any Carbon or Silicon by c:id or si:id, even one the deck isn't shared with, and that account is still 'the one mentioned' who gets `present.mention.received`. This is the literal reading and needs a Carbon's ruling.
requirements.quote: Anyone can mention a Carbon or Silicon in a comment with their c:id or si:id.
requirements.acceptance: si:outsider exists on Silicon Accounts but has no access to c:ada's private deck. c:ada posts `@si:outsider can you take this on?` on slide 1 in the web. The comment is posted, not rejected, and the Ting stand-in has a `present.mention.received` for si:outsider. Open question for a Carbon: the current service skips accounts without access and returns them as `mentionedWithoutAccess`. The text neither grants nor withholds access through a mention, so this check asserts only the ting and must not assume the deck gets shared.

requirements.requirement: Mentioning yourself sends you no ting. (Implied: 'Someone mentions you' describes another account doing it.)
requirements.quote: | `present.mention.received` | Someone mentions you in a comment | The one mentioned |
requirements.acceptance: si:designer runs `present comment <deck> --slide 2 "@si:designer remember to redo this"`, and c:ada posts `@c:ada note to self` in the web. The Ting stand-in has no `present.mention.received` for si:designer or for c:ada from these comments.

requirements.requirement: Every notification Silicon Present produces is delivered as a Silicon Ting, posted to Ting (`PRESENT_TING_URL`) for the recipient's Silicon Accounts account.
requirements.quote: All notifications go through Silicon Ting
requirements.acceptance: With `PRESENT_TING_URL` pointing at the Ting stand-in, cause one of each event: a mention, a new comment on someone else's deck, a reply, a resolve and a deck share. For each expected recipient, the stand-in receives a ting (`POST /v1/tings`). Each is accepted with the `present` app's proof, typed with the matching `present.*` name, with `for` = the recipient's uuid. Poll for a few seconds, since delivery is queued.

requirements.requirement: Silicon Present sends no notification of its own, by email or any other channel, for any of the five events.
requirements.quote: Silicon Present never sends its own.
requirements.acceptance: Run the five events (mention, new comment, reply, resolve, share with an existing account) while the stand-in records. Present's own mail outbox (`email_outbox`) gets no row for any of them, and the Accounts test stack's mock mailbox (`http://127.0.0.1:9743/_messages`) gets no message. The stand-in is the only place a notification arrives. Open question for a Carbon: the service currently emails invites to addresses not yet on Silicon Accounts through its own mailer (`mail::send_invite`, Postmark; that invite comes from the Sharing section). The text doesn't settle whether such an invite to join counts as a notification under this line.

requirements.requirement: Present has no notification inbox of its own in any surface: no notification feed in the service API, no notification bell, inbox or browser notifications in the web, and no notification or inbox command in the CLI. Carbons and Silicons hear about mentions and the rest only through Silicon Ting.
requirements.quote: All notifications go through Silicon Ting; Silicon Present never sends its own.
requirements.acceptance: While c:ada is mentioned, replied to and shared a deck, the web at /decks and /decks/[id] shows no notification bell, inbox or unread-notification badge, and never asks for browser notification permission. `present --help` and `present docs` list no notification or inbox command. The service API has no notifications endpoint. Comment threads and live comment updates (in the editor and through `present watch`) are collaboration, not notifications, and are allowed.

requirements.requirement: When a Carbon or Silicon starts a new comment on a deck, the deck's owner (a Carbon or a Silicon) gets a `present.comment.created` ting, and no one else gets one.
requirements.quote: | `present.comment.created` | Someone comments on your deck | The owner |
requirements.acceptance: si:designer creates a deck (`present new "Pitch"`) and shares it with c:ada as commenter and c:bob as editor. c:ada clicks on slide 2 at /decks/[id] and posts `Tighten this`. The Ting stand-in has exactly one `present.comment.created` for this comment, `for` = si:designer, and none for c:ada or c:bob. On a deck owned by c:ada, si:writer (commenter) runs `present comment <deck> --deck "Love the theme"`, and c:ada gets one. After `present public <deck> comment`, a signed-in c:carol with no invite comments through the link, and c:ada gets one for that too. Not settled by the text: whether a reply in a thread the owner isn't in also counts as 'comments on your deck'. The current service sends the owner `present.comment.created` for replies as well, so a Carbon should rule before either is tested.

requirements.requirement: An owner commenting on their own deck gets no `present.comment.created`. (Implied: 'Someone comments on your deck' describes another account.)
requirements.quote: | `present.comment.created` | Someone comments on your deck | The owner |
requirements.acceptance: si:designer (owner) runs `present comment <deck> --slide 1 "redo the chart"`, and c:ada comments in the web on a deck she owns. The Ting stand-in has no `present.comment.created` for si:designer or c:ada from these comments.

requirements.requirement: For a deck created inside someone else's shared folder, `present.comment.created` goes to the deck's owner, who is the folder's owner, not to the account that created the deck.
requirements.quote: | `present.comment.created` | Someone comments on your deck | The owner |
requirements.acceptance: c:ada owns folder F and runs `present folder share F si:designer --role editor` and `present folder share F c:bob --role commenter`. si:designer runs `present new "Draft" --folder F`, so si:designer is the creator and c:ada the owner. c:bob comments on slide 1 in the web. The Ting stand-in has a `present.comment.created` for c:ada and none for si:designer.

requirements.requirement: `present.comment.created` goes to whoever owns the deck when the comment is made: the current owner while a transfer is still waiting, and the new owner once the transfer is accepted.
requirements.quote: | `present.comment.created` | Someone comments on your deck | The owner |
requirements.acceptance: c:ada owns the deck, c:bob is a commenter, and c:ada runs `present transfer <deck> si:designer`. c:bob comments, and the Ting stand-in has `present.comment.created` for c:ada. si:designer runs `present transfers accept <id>`. c:bob comments again, and this comment's `present.comment.created` goes to si:designer, with none to c:ada.

requirements.requirement: When someone replies in a thread, every Carbon and Silicon in that thread (whoever started it and everyone who has replied in it) gets a `present.comment.replied` ting, and no one outside the thread does.
requirements.quote: | `present.comment.replied` | Someone replies in a thread you're in | Everyone in the thread |
requirements.acceptance: On a deck owned by c:olga, c:ada starts a thread on slide 2 in the web. si:designer runs `present reply <thread> "Simplified"`, and the Ting stand-in has a `present.comment.replied` for c:ada. c:bob replies in the web, and one each arrives for c:ada and si:designer. si:writer runs `present reply <thread> "Copy fixed"`, and one each arrives for c:ada, si:designer and c:bob. c:olga and members who never wrote in the thread get no `present.comment.replied`. Not settled by the text: whether an account that was only mentioned, or only reacted, is 'in the thread'. This check covers only accounts that wrote in it.

requirements.requirement: The one replying gets no `present.comment.replied` for their own reply, even though they're in the thread. (Implied: 'Someone replies in a thread you're in' describes another account replying.)
requirements.quote: | `present.comment.replied` | Someone replies in a thread you're in | Everyone in the thread |
requirements.acceptance: In the MEN-20 thread, si:writer's reply produces no `present.comment.replied` for si:writer. c:ada, the starter, then replies in the web. She gets no `present.comment.replied` for her own reply, while si:designer, c:bob and si:writer each get one.

requirements.requirement: When a thread is resolved, the Carbon or Silicon who started it gets a `present.thread.resolved` ting. No one else does, neither the others in the thread nor the owner.
requirements.quote: | `present.thread.resolved` | A thread you started is resolved | Who started it |
requirements.acceptance: On a deck owned by c:olga, c:ada starts a thread on slide 4 in the web: `@si:designer make this simpler`. si:designer replies, then runs `present resolve <thread>`. The Ting stand-in has exactly one `present.thread.resolved` for this thread, `for` = c:ada, and none for si:designer, c:olga or anyone else. Then si:writer starts a thread with `present comment <deck> --slide 1 "Typo in the title"`, and c:bob resolves it from the deck's thread list in the web. One `present.thread.resolved` arrives, for si:writer.

requirements.requirement: A starter who resolves their own thread gets no `present.thread.resolved`. (Implied because a ting tells you what someone else did. The row is passive, so this rests on that reading more than MEN-12, MEN-17 and MEN-21 do.)
requirements.quote: | `present.thread.resolved` | A thread you started is resolved | Who started it |
requirements.acceptance: si:writer runs `present comment <deck> --slide 1 "check the date"`, then `present resolve <thread>`. c:ada resolves a thread she started, in the web. The Ting stand-in has no `present.thread.resolved` for si:writer or c:ada from these.

requirements.requirement: Each resolution counts. A thread that is reopened and then resolved again sends its starter another `present.thread.resolved`.
requirements.quote: | `present.thread.resolved` | A thread you started is resolved | Who started it |
requirements.acceptance: c:ada starts a thread. si:designer runs `present resolve <thread>`, and c:ada gets one ting. si:designer then runs `present reopen <thread>` and `present resolve <thread>` again. The Ting stand-in has a second `present.thread.resolved` for c:ada, and it isn't swallowed as a duplicate of the first.

requirements.requirement: When a deck is shared with a Carbon (by c:id) or a Silicon (by si:id), that account gets a `present.deck.shared` ting. No one else gets one: not the owner, not whoever shared it, and not other members.
requirements.quote: | `present.deck.shared` | A deck or folder is shared with you | The one invited |
requirements.acceptance: c:ada (owner) shares the deck with si:designer as editor from the share dialog in the web editor (/decks/[id]). The Ting stand-in has exactly one `present.deck.shared`, for si:designer. si:designer, now an editor, runs `present share <deck> c:bob --role commenter`. Exactly one arrives for c:bob, and nothing for c:ada or si:designer.

requirements.requirement: When a folder is shared with a Carbon or Silicon, that account gets a `present.deck.shared` ting for the folder.
requirements.quote: | `present.deck.shared` | A deck or folder is shared with you | The one invited |
requirements.acceptance: c:ada owns folder F, which holds two decks, and runs `present folder share F si:writer --role viewer`. The Ting stand-in has a `present.deck.shared` for si:writer that identifies folder F. Sharing F with c:bob from the folder's share dialog at /decks produces one for c:bob. Not settled by the text: whether each deck inside, or a deck added to F later, also sends one. Don't assert either way.

requirements.requirement: Inviting by email sends `present.deck.shared` to the Silicon Accounts account that has that email, if there is one, because that account is 'the one invited'.
requirements.quote: | `present.deck.shared` | A deck or folder is shared with you | The one invited |
requirements.acceptance: c:bob exists on Silicon Accounts with the email bob@example.test and has never opened Present. c:ada runs `present share <deck> bob@example.test --role viewer`. Without c:bob signing in to Present, the Ting stand-in has a `present.deck.shared` with `for` = c:bob's uuid. Not settled by the text: whether someone invited by an email that had no account yet gets one when they later join.

critic.problem: It requires the ting to arrive 'without c:bob signing in to Present'. The table says the person invited gets present.deck.shared, but not when. Silicon Accounts gives apps no way to turn an email into an account (docs/accounts-and-ting.md), so the item asks for something the text doesn't require and the platform can't do.
critic.fix: Require exactly one present.deck.shared for c:bob's uuid, sent no later than the moment Present can tell the address is his (at the latest, his first sign-in to Present), and none to anyone else.

requirements.requirement: Sharing a deck again with someone who was removed from it sends `present.deck.shared` again.
requirements.quote: | `present.deck.shared` | A deck or folder is shared with you | The one invited |
requirements.acceptance: c:ada runs `present share <deck> si:designer --role editor`, and one ting arrives. She runs `present unshare <deck> si:designer`, then shares again. The Ting stand-in has a second `present.deck.shared` for si:designer. The text doesn't cover a role change for someone who already has access, so that isn't tested.

requirements.requirement: Each row of the table applies on its own. When one comment meets several rows for the same account, that account gets every matching ting: a new comment on its deck that mentions it brings both `present.comment.created` and `present.mention.received`, and a reply that mentions someone already in the thread brings them both `present.comment.replied` and `present.mention.received`. This is the literal reading, since no merging is stated, and needs a Carbon's ruling.
requirements.quote:
| `present.mention.received` | Someone mentions you in a comment | The one mentioned |
| `present.comment.created` | Someone comments on your deck | The owner |
| `present.comment.replied` | Someone replies in a thread you're in | Everyone in the thread |
requirements.acceptance: si:designer owns the deck. c:ada posts `@si:designer make this simpler` on slide 4 in the web. The Ting stand-in has both a `present.comment.created` and a `present.mention.received` for si:designer for that comment. c:bob starts a thread and c:ada replies in it, then si:writer runs `present reply <thread> "@c:bob see the new version"`. The stand-in has both a `present.comment.replied` and a `present.mention.received` for c:bob. Open question: the current service sends each account at most one ting per comment, preferring the mention.

requirements.requirement: Every comment ting (`present.mention.received`, `present.comment.created`, `present.comment.replied`, `present.thread.resolved`) identifies the deck, so the recipient can open it directly.
requirements.quote: A ting carries enough for a Silicon to act straight away: the deck, the slide, what the comment is on, and the comment itself.
requirements.acceptance: Cause one ting of each of the four types for si:designer: it is mentioned, it owns the deck, it is in a thread that gets a reply, and it started a thread that gets resolved. Each recorded ting's `data` holds the deck's id. si:designer's `present read <that id>` prints that deck without first running `present list` or `present search`.

requirements.requirement: For a comment on a slide or any part of one, every comment ting identifies that slide, so the recipient can open or render exactly that slide.
requirements.quote: A ting carries enough for a Silicon to act straight away: the deck, the slide, what the comment is on, and the comment itself.
requirements.acceptance: In the web, c:ada comments on an element on the third slide and mentions si:designer. The recorded `present.mention.received` names that slide, and `present slide <deck> <slide from the ting>` and `present render <deck> <slide from the ting> -o s.png` both show the third slide. The `present.comment.created`, `present.comment.replied` and `present.thread.resolved` tings for that thread name the same slide.

requirements.requirement: For a comment on a point, the ting gives the slide and the point clicked, plus the element at that point when there is one.
requirements.quote: A ting carries enough for a Silicon to act straight away: the deck, the slide, what the comment is on, and the comment itself.
requirements.acceptance: c:ada (commenter) clicks an image on slide 2 at /decks/[id] and posts `@si:designer swap this photo`. The recorded ting says the comment is on a point and gives slide 2, the clicked position in slide px, and the image element's id. si:designer runs `present comment <deck> --slide 2 --point 960,540 "@c:ada here?"` on an empty spot. That ting gives slide 2 and the point (960, 540), with no element.

requirements.requirement: For a comment on an area, the ting gives the slide and the rectangle that was dragged over.
requirements.quote: A ting carries enough for a Silicon to act straight away: the deck, the slide, what the comment is on, and the comment itself.
requirements.acceptance: si:writer runs `present comment <deck> --slide 2 --area 100,100,600,400 "@si:designer this corner is empty"`. The recorded ting gives slide 2 and the area (x 100, y 100, w 600, h 400 in slide px). In the web, c:ada drags over an empty part of slide 2 and mentions si:designer, and that ting gives the rectangle she dragged.

requirements.requirement: For an area dragged over an element, as in the contract's example of dragging over a chart, the ting also identifies that element, so a request like 'make this simpler' points at the chart without guessing.
requirements.quote: Mentioning a Silicon is how a Carbon asks it for something, for example dragging over a chart and writing "@si:designer make this simpler".
requirements.acceptance: Slide 4 has a chart element. c:ada (commenter) drags over the chart at /decks/[id] and posts `@si:designer make this simpler`. The Ting stand-in has one `present.mention.received` for si:designer. It carries the deck, slide 4, the dragged area, the chart element's id and kind (`chart`), and the body `@si:designer make this simpler`.

requirements.requirement: For a comment on an element, the ting identifies that element by id and kind.
requirements.quote: A ting carries enough for a Silicon to act straight away: the deck, the slide, what the comment is on, and the comment itself.
requirements.acceptance: si:writer runs `present comment <deck> --slide 2 --element e_ab12cd "@si:designer align this with the title"`. The recorded ting names element e_ab12cd and its kind. In the web, c:ada comments on a table element on slide 2 and mentions si:designer. That ting names the table element and kind `table`.

requirements.requirement: For a comment on an HTML element, made while it is running, the ting identifies that HTML element (its id and kind `html`), so the Silicon can change its code straight away.
requirements.quote: A ting carries enough for a Silicon to act straight away: the deck, the slide, what the comment is on, and the comment itself.
requirements.acceptance: Slide 3 has an animated HTML element. c:ada clicks on it in the web editor while it runs and posts `@si:designer slow the animation down`. The recorded ting names that element's id with kind `html`. Using only that id, si:designer runs `present replace <deck> 3 <element> --field js --find "speed = 1" --replace "speed = 0.5"`, and it succeeds.

requirements.requirement: For a comment on some text inside an element, the ting identifies the element and quotes the commented text.
requirements.quote: A ting carries enough for a Silicon to act straight away: the deck, the slide, what the comment is on, and the comment itself.
requirements.acceptance: si:writer runs `present comment <deck> --slide 3 --element e_ab12cd --text "Q3 numbers" "@si:designer these are Q4"`. The recorded ting names element e_ab12cd and carries the quoted text `Q3 numbers`. In the web, c:ada selects the words `Q3 numbers` in that text box, comments, and mentions si:designer. Her ting carries the same element and quote.

requirements.requirement: For a comment on a whole slide, the ting says it is on that whole slide, not on a point, area or element.
requirements.quote: A ting carries enough for a Silicon to act straight away: the deck, the slide, what the comment is on, and the comment itself.
requirements.acceptance: si:writer runs `present comment <deck> --slide 5 "@si:designer this slide drags"`. The recorded ting says the comment is on all of slide 5. A whole-slide comment made in the web that mentions si:designer gives the same.

requirements.requirement: For a comment on the whole deck, the ting says it is on the whole deck and names no slide.
requirements.quote: A ting carries enough for a Silicon to act straight away: the deck, the slide, what the comment is on, and the comment itself.
requirements.acceptance: si:writer runs `present comment <deck> --deck "@c:ada the theme is too dark"`. The recorded ting names the deck, says the comment is on the whole deck, and carries no slide. A deck-wide comment made in the web gives the same.

requirements.requirement: Every comment ting carries the comment itself: its full text, exactly as written, mentions included. For `present.mention.received` and `present.comment.created` that is the new comment, for `present.comment.replied` the new reply, and for `present.thread.resolved` the thread's opening comment.
requirements.quote: A ting carries enough for a Silicon to act straight away: the deck, the slide, what the comment is on, and the comment itself.
requirements.acceptance: c:ada posts a two-line comment on si:designer's deck: `@si:designer make this simpler`, then `keep the colours`. Its `present.mention.received` and `present.comment.created` both carry exactly that text. When c:bob replies `also the legend`, the `present.comment.replied` tings carry `also the legend`, not the opening comment. When the thread is resolved, c:ada's `present.thread.resolved` carries the opening comment's text.

requirements.requirement: Every comment ting says who wrote the comment, shown by their c:id or si:id, so the recipient knows who is asking.
requirements.quote: A ting carries enough for a Silicon to act straight away: the deck, the slide, what the comment is on, and the comment itself.
requirements.acceptance: c:ada's `@si:designer make this simpler` produces a ting for si:designer that names c:ada as the comment's author. When si:designer replies, c:ada's `present.comment.replied` names si:designer as the author. The author is shown as a c:id or si:id, not only as a uuid or a display name.

requirements.requirement: Every comment ting carries the ids the recipient needs to answer it: the thread id (to reply or resolve) and the comment id (to react).
requirements.quote: A ting carries enough for a Silicon to act straight away: the deck, the slide, what the comment is on, and the comment itself.
requirements.acceptance: si:designer takes the thread id and the comment id from its recorded `present.mention.received`. `present reply <thread> "On it"` and `present react <comment>` (with an emoji) both succeed without first running `present comments` or `present read --comments`.

requirements.requirement: A mentioned Silicon can act on the request using only what its ting carries. With no listing, searching or guessing, it can look at the slide, render it, change the element, reply and resolve.
requirements.quote: A ting carries enough for a Silicon to act straight away: the deck, the slide, what the comment is on, and the comment itself.
requirements.acceptance: c:ada drags over the chart on slide 4 in the web and posts `@si:designer make this simpler`. si:designer reads the deck id, slide, chart element id, thread id and text from the recorded ting, then runs `present slide <deck> <slide>`, `present render <deck> <slide> -o before.png`, `present set <deck> <slide> <element> 'chart={...one series...}'`, `present reply <thread> "Simplified: one series"` and `present resolve <thread>`. Each succeeds on its first try, and it never runs `present list`, `present search`, `present comments` or `present read --comments`. c:ada then receives `present.comment.replied` and `present.thread.resolved`.

requirements.requirement: A `present.deck.shared` ting identifies what was shared, the deck or the folder, so the invitee can open it straight away.
requirements.quote: A ting carries enough for a Silicon to act straight away: the deck, the slide, what the comment is on, and the comment itself.
requirements.acceptance: After c:ada runs `present share <deck> si:designer --role editor`, the recorded `present.deck.shared` holds the deck's id, and si:designer's `present read <id>` works at once. After `present folder share <folder> si:designer --role viewer`, the ting holds the folder's id, and `present list --folder <id>` lists the decks in it.

requirements.requirement: A Carbon can present any deck full screen from the web: the slide being presented fills the screen, with no editor UI or speaker notes on it.
requirements.quote: Any deck can be presented full screen
requirements.acceptance: c:ada opens her 3-slide deck at /decks/{id}, clicks Present in the top bar, lands on /decks/{id}/present and turns on full screen (F or the full-screen button). Observe: document.fullscreenElement is set; slide 1 fills the screen at the deck's aspect ratio (letterboxed, not cropped); no editor toolbar, slide list, comment UI or speaker notes are visible.

requirements.requirement: Every deck can be presented whatever it contains: every element on a slide (text, image, shape, table, chart, video, audio and HTML) is shown in present mode.
requirements.quote: Any deck can be presented full screen
requirements.acceptance: si:designer uses the CLI to build a deck with one slide per element kind (present add text / image / shape / table / chart / video / audio / html). c:ada presents it at /decks/{id}/present and moves through every slide. Observe: on each slide every element is visible at its x/y/w/h, scaled to the screen, and matches `present render <deck> <n>` for that slide; no slide is empty or shows an error.

requirements.requirement: A Carbon presenting can move forward to the next slide.
requirements.quote: Any deck can be presented full screen
requirements.acceptance: In /decks/{id}/present, on a slide 1 with no animations, c:ada presses the right arrow. Observe: the stage (data-testid=present-stage) shows slide 2, and its data-slide is slide 2's id.

requirements.requirement: A Carbon presenting can move back to the previous slide.
requirements.quote: Any deck can be presented full screen
requirements.acceptance: On slide 2 in /decks/{id}/present, c:ada presses the left arrow. Observe: the stage shows slide 1 again (data-slide = slide 1's id).

requirements.requirement: Slides marked skipped are never shown while presenting: moving forward or back passes over them, a presentation never starts on one, and the presenter view never shows one as the next slide (read with 'skipped slides' in Slides and elements > Everything else).
requirements.quote: Any deck can be presented full screen
requirements.acceptance: A 4-slide deck has slide 3 marked skipped (present edit <deck> --ops with update_slide skipped=true). c:ada presents: from slide 2 the right arrow lands on slide 4, and from slide 4 the left arrow lands on slide 2; on slide 2 the presenter view shows slide 4 as the next slide. si:designer runs `present start <deck>`, `present goto 2`, `present next`: `present show status --json` reports slide 4, and a follower never sees slide 3. If slide 1 is the skipped one instead, present mode opened from the deck list and `present start <deck>` both begin on slide 2.

requirements.requirement: A slide's transition plays when the presentation moves to that slide (read with 'slide transitions' in Slides and elements > Everything else).
requirements.quote: Any deck can be presented full screen
requirements.acceptance: Slide 2 has transition {type: 'fade', duration: 1000}. c:ada presents and presses the right arrow on slide 1. Observe: a frame captured about 300 ms after the key press shows slide 2 part-way through fading in over slide 1, different from both the slide 1 frame and the finished slide 2 frame; after about a second only slide 2 is shown. Moving to a slide whose transition is null switches at once.

requirements.requirement: Click-triggered element animations play one click at a time while presenting: moving forward first reveals the slide's next animation step, and moves to the next slide only after the last step (read with 'element animations' in Slides and elements > Everything else).
requirements.quote: Any deck can be presented full screen
requirements.acceptance: On slide 1, element B has animation {effect: 'fade', trigger: 'click', order: 1, duration: 400, delay: 0}, set with present set <deck> 1 <B> 'animation=...'. c:ada presents: B is not visible at first; the right arrow reveals B and the stage stays on slide 1 (data-step=1); the next right arrow goes to slide 2. si:designer, after `present start <deck>`: one `present next` makes `present show status --json` report slide 1, step 1, and a second `present next` reports slide 2, step 0.

requirements.requirement: The presenter view shows the speaker notes of the slide being presented.
requirements.quote: a presenter view showing speaker notes
requirements.acceptance: Slide 1's notes are 'Say hello' (present slide notes <deck> 1 'Say hello'). c:ada starts presenting and opens the presenter view (the Presenter view button, /decks/{id}/presenter). Observe: the notes panel (data-testid=speaker-notes) reads 'Say hello'; on a slide without notes it does not show another slide's notes.

requirements.requirement: The presenter view shows the next slide.
requirements.quote: the next slide
requirements.acceptance: c:ada's presenter view is on slide 1 of a 3-slide deck whose slide 2 is titled 'Plan'. Observe: a separate next-slide panel shows a picture of slide 2 with 'Plan' visible in it.

requirements.requirement: The presenter view shows a timer that keeps running while presenting.
requirements.quote: and a timer
requirements.acceptance: c:ada opens the presenter view. Observe: a timer (role=timer) first reads 0:00 or 0:01, reads at least 0:04 after she waits 5 seconds, and keeps counting while she moves between slides.

requirements.requirement: The presenter view stays on the slide being presented: when the presentation moves, its speaker notes and next slide change to match the new slide.
requirements.quote: with a presenter view showing speaker notes, the next slide and a timer
requirements.acceptance: c:ada has /decks/{id}/present and /decks/{id}/presenter open in the same browser; slides 1-3 have the notes 'one', 'two' and 'three'. She presses the right arrow in the full-screen window. Observe within 1 s: the presenter view's notes read 'two' and its next-slide panel shows slide 3.

requirements.requirement: The presenter can move the presentation from the presenter view, and the full-screen slide moves with it.
requirements.quote: with a presenter view showing speaker notes, the next slide and a timer
requirements.acceptance: With both windows open on slide 1, c:ada clicks Next (or presses the right arrow) in the presenter view. Observe within 1 s: the full-screen window's stage shows slide 2; clicking Previous in the presenter view brings the full-screen window back to slide 1.

requirements.requirement: HTML elements run live in present mode: their JS runs and their content keeps changing, rather than showing a still picture.
requirements.quote: HTML elements run live while presenting.
requirements.acceptance: si:designer adds an HTML element to slide 2 (present add html <deck> 2 --html w.html --css w.css --js w.js). Its JS writes a counter into the element every 200 ms, and its CSS runs an endless animation. c:ada presents and moves to slide 2. Observe: the element shows the counter its JS writes, the value read 1 s later is higher, and the animated part has moved between two screenshots.

requirements.requirement: HTML elements run live for everyone following a presentation, not only on the presenter's screen.
requirements.quote: HTML elements run live while presenting.
requirements.acceptance: c:ada presents the PRES-13 deck with a follow link and moves to slide 2. c:bob (Viewer) opens the follow link /p/{presentation}. Observe: on c:bob's page the element's counter is running, and a read 1 s later is higher.

requirements.requirement: HTML elements stay sandboxed while presenting and while following: an element on a presented slide can never act as the presenter or a follower, for example by calling the API with their sign-in to move the presentation or read their account (read with 'Every HTML element runs sandboxed.' in HTML elements).
requirements.quote: HTML elements run live while presenting.
requirements.acceptance:
An HTML element on slide 2 tries each of the following and writes each outcome into itself: fetch('/api/v1/me', {credentials: 'include'}); a PUT to /api/v1/presentations/

that moves the running presentation to slide 3 (the test writes

into its JS); reading window.top.document and document.cookie; setting window.top.location. Run it in c:ada's present mode while her follow link is running, and in c:bob's follow view. Observe on both: every attempt fails (no account data, no session cookie, no access to the surrounding page, no navigation), GET /v1/presentations/

still reports slide 2, and nothing the element draws appears outside its box.

requirements.requirement: A Carbon presenting in the web can get a link that others open to follow the presentation.
requirements.quote: A presentation can be followed live through a link
requirements.acceptance: Signed-in c:ada clicks Share a follow link in /decks/{id}/present or in the presenter view. Observe: POST /v1/decks/{id}/presentations answers 201 with {id, followUrl, slide, step}; the page shows the link /p/{id} with a copy button; c:bob, who has access, opens it in another browser and gets the follow page for that presentation.

requirements.requirement: Opening a follow link shows the slide being presented at that moment, not the first slide.
requirements.quote: so everyone watching stays on the slide being shown
requirements.acceptance: c:ada starts a follow link and moves to slide 3. c:bob (Viewer) then opens the follow link. Observe: the follow page's slide (data-testid=follow-stage) has data-slide = slide 3's id and shows slide 3's content.

requirements.requirement: When the presenter moves, everyone following moves to the same slide live, without reloading.
requirements.quote: A presentation can be followed live through a link, so everyone watching stays on the slide being shown.
requirements.acceptance: c:bob (Viewer) and c:carol (Commenter) both have /p/{presentation} open. c:ada presses the right arrow twice in present mode. Observe: within 3 s of each key press, both follow pages show her new slide (slide 2, then slide 3), and neither page navigates or reloads.

requirements.requirement: Followers see the same animation step as the presenter, not just the same slide.
requirements.quote: and everyone following sees it live
requirements.acceptance: Element B on slide 1 has a click-triggered animation. With c:bob following, c:ada presses the right arrow once (B appears; still slide 1). Observe within 3 s: c:bob's follow page shows B on slide 1 (follow-stage data-step=1). When c:ada presses the left arrow, B disappears on c:bob's page too.

requirements.requirement: A follower cannot move away from the slide being shown: their own keys, clicks and swipes do not change the slide they see.
requirements.quote: so everyone watching stays on the slide being shown
requirements.acceptance: c:bob follows c:ada's presentation, which is on slide 2. He presses the right arrow, the left arrow and Space, and clicks the slide. Observe: c:bob's follow page stays on slide 2, and GET /v1/presentations/{p} still reports slide 2.

requirements.requirement: Only the presenter can move a presentation: no follower, not even the deck's owner or an editor, can change the slide everyone is shown.
requirements.quote: a Silicon can start a presentation and move through it, and everyone following sees it live
requirements.acceptance:
si:designer starts a presentation of c:ada's deck (present start ). c:ada, the owner, sends PUT /v1/presentations/{p} {slide: }, and si:scout, an Editor, runs `present goto 3 --presentation

`. Observe: both are refused with 403 not_the_presenter; GET /v1/presentations/{p} still reports si:designer's slide, and followers do not move.

requirements.requirement: Each presentation has its own follow link: when two presentations of the same deck run at once, the followers of one are not moved by the other.
requirements.quote: A presentation can be followed live through a link
requirements.acceptance: c:ada (in the web) and si:designer (present start <deck>) each present the same deck and get two different follow links. c:bob follows c:ada's link and c:carol follows si:designer's. si:designer runs `present goto 4`. Observe: c:carol's follow page shows slide 4 within 3 s, and c:bob's stays on c:ada's slide.

requirements.requirement: Followers stay on the slide being shown after their connection drops and comes back.
requirements.quote: so everyone watching stays on the slide being shown
requirements.acceptance: c:bob follows on /p/{presentation}. His browser context goes offline; c:ada moves from slide 1 to slide 4; the context comes back online. Observe: within 5 s, without a manual reload, c:bob's page shows slide 4 and keeps following later moves. A follower left on the page for more than 5 minutes (past the proxy's stream cut) is still moved by the next move, and `present follow` likewise keeps printing moves after its stream is cut.

requirements.requirement: A follow link does not show a private deck to anyone it isn't shared with: following needs view access to the deck unless the deck is public (read with Sharing and Public decks, where only the owner, the Carbons and Silicons it is shared with, and anyone with the link of a public deck can see a deck).
requirements.quote: A presentation can be followed live through a link
requirements.acceptance: c:ada presents her private deck, shared with no one, and passes on the follow link. c:bob, signed in but without access, opens /p/{presentation}: he sees only an access error and no slide content. GET /v1/presentations/{p} and GET /v1/presentations/{p}/live as c:bob answer 403 (or 404). A signed-out browser sees no slide and is asked to sign in. si:scout gets an access error from `present follow <followUrl>`. After `present share <deck> c:bob --role viewer`, the same link shows c:bob the current slide.

requirements.requirement: A presentation of a public deck can be followed through its link without signing in (read with 'Viewing a public deck never needs signing in.').
requirements.quote: A presentation can be followed live through a link
requirements.acceptance: c:ada makes the deck public (present public <deck> view). si:designer runs `present start <deck>` and shares the follow URL, which a signed-out browser opens. Observe: no redirect to sign in; the current slide is shown; after si:designer runs `present next`, the signed-out page moves to the new slide within 3 s.

requirements.requirement: A Silicon can start a presentation of a deck through the CLI.
requirements.quote: a Silicon can start a presentation
requirements.acceptance: si:designer, the deck's owner, runs `present start <deck>`. Observe: exit code 0, and `present show status --json` reports a presentation that has not ended, on the deck's first slide that isn't skipped, at step 0.

requirements.requirement: Starting a presentation through the CLI gives the Silicon the follow link to share.
requirements.quote: A presentation can be followed live through a link
requirements.acceptance: si:designer runs `present start <deck> --json`. Observe: the output includes followUrl in the form <web>/p/<presentation id> (the text output prints it after 'Follow along:'); c:ada, who has access, opens it and sees the presentation's current slide.

requirements.requirement: A Silicon can move its presentation forward through the CLI.
requirements.quote: a Silicon can start a presentation and move through it
