requirements.acceptance: On a deck without animations, si:designer runs `present start <deck>` and then `present next`. Observe: exit 0, the output names slide 2, and `present show status --json` reports slide 2 (slideNumber 2).

requirements.requirement: A Silicon can move its presentation back through the CLI.
requirements.quote: a Silicon can start a presentation and move through it
requirements.acceptance: With its presentation on slide 2, si:designer runs `present prev`. Observe: `present show status --json` reports slide 1.

requirements.requirement: A Silicon can take its presentation straight to any slide through the CLI.
requirements.quote: a Silicon can start a presentation and move through it
requirements.acceptance: si:designer runs `present goto 4`, then `present goto <slide 2's id>`. Observe: `present show status --json` reports slide 4, then slide 2.

requirements.requirement: Everyone following a Silicon's presentation sees each of its moves live.
requirements.quote: and everyone following sees it live
requirements.acceptance: si:designer runs `present start <deck>`, and c:ada and c:bob open the follow URL in their browsers. si:designer runs `present next`, then `present goto 4`. Observe: within 3 s of each command, both follow pages show the new slide (slide 2, then slide 4) without reloading.

requirements.requirement: A Silicon that is only a Viewer of a deck can present it through the CLI, just as a Carbon Viewer can (read with 'Carbons and Silicons get exactly the same roles and the same rights.').
requirements.quote: Silicons can present too
requirements.acceptance: c:ada shares her deck with si:scout as Viewer (present share <deck> si:scout --role viewer). si:scout runs `present start <deck>` and then `present next`. Observe: both succeed, a follow URL is printed, and c:ada sees slide 2 when she follows that URL.

requirements.requirement: A Silicon can follow a presentation live through the CLI and gets each slide change as it happens (read with 'it can do everything the web editor can' in Silicons).
requirements.quote: and everyone following sees it live
requirements.acceptance: c:ada presents her deck, which is shared with si:scout as Viewer, with a follow link. si:scout runs `present follow <followUrl> --json --count 3`, and c:ada presses the right arrow twice. Observe: the CLI first prints the current slide, then one line per move naming slide 2 and then slide 3, each within 3 s of the key press, and exits after the third event.

requirements.requirement: The presenter can end a presentation they started, after which it can no longer be moved and stops being live for its followers.
requirements.quote: a Silicon can start a presentation
requirements.acceptance:
si:designer runs `present stop`. Observe: `present show status --json` reports the presentation as ended (endedAt set); a later `present next --presentation

` is refused; c:ada's open follow page says the presentation has ended. In the web, c:ada ending her follow link (End the follow link) has the same effect on her followers.

requirements.requirement: Presenting needs only view access: a Carbon who is a Viewer of a deck can present it full screen (Carbons present the decks Silicons make: 'Carbons will mostly review and present them').
requirements.quote: Any deck can be presented full screen
requirements.acceptance: si:designer makes a deck and shares it with c:ada as Viewer (present share <deck> c:ada --role viewer). c:ada opens /decks/{id}/present from the deck list or the editor's Present button. Observe: slide 1 is shown, full screen works, the arrow keys move through the slides, and no permission error appears.

requirements.requirement: A Carbon who is only a Viewer can start a presentation that others follow through a link.
requirements.quote: A presentation can be followed live through a link
requirements.acceptance: c:ada, a Viewer of si:designer's deck, clicks Share a follow link in /decks/{id}/present. Observe: POST /v1/decks/{id}/presentations answers 201 with a followUrl, and the link /p/{presentation} is shown. c:bob, also a Viewer, opens it, sees c:ada's current slide, and moves when she presses the right arrow.

requirements.requirement: Anyone with the link to a public deck can present it full screen without signing in (read with 'Viewing a public deck never needs signing in.').
requirements.quote: Any deck can be presented full screen
requirements.acceptance: c:ada makes the deck public (present public <deck> view). A signed-out browser opens /decks/{id}/present. Observe: no redirect to sign in; slide 1 is shown, the arrow keys move through the slides, and full screen works.

requirements.requirement: The presenter view of a public deck opens without signing in (read with 'Viewing a public deck never needs signing in.').
requirements.quote: with a presenter view showing speaker notes, the next slide and a timer
requirements.acceptance: With the deck public (view), a signed-out browser opens the presenter view (/decks/{id}/presenter, or its button in present mode). Observe: no redirect to sign in; the page shows the current slide's speaker notes, the next slide and a running timer.

requirements.requirement: Every kind of change to a deck's content is recorded in its version history: slide text, element position, size and style, adding, deleting and reordering slides and elements, speaker notes and the theme.
requirements.quote: Everything in Silicon Present is versioned
requirements.acceptance: On a new deck, c:ada (owner) edits a text box on slide 1 in the web editor at /decks/{id}, drags an element, edits the speaker notes and changes the theme. si:designer (editor) runs `present slide add`, `present set <deck> 2 <el> style.fill=#ff0000`, `present slide move <deck> 3 --first` and `present delete` on an element. `present versions <deck>` and /decks/{id}/history then account for every one of these changes: for each history entry, `present compare <deck> <before> <after>` shows exactly that entry's changes, and none of the changes is missing from the history.

requirements.requirement: Changes to a deck that are not slide content, such as renaming it, are versioned too. Each rename appears in the deck's history with who made it and when, and the earlier title can still be seen.
requirements.quote: Everything in Silicon Present is versioned
requirements.acceptance: c:ada renames the deck from 'Q4' to 'Q4 review' in the web, then si:designer (editor) runs `present rename <deck> 'Q4 final'`. /decks/{id}/history and `present versions <deck>` show both renames, credited to c:ada and si:designer with their times, and the earlier titles 'Q4' and 'Q4 review' are still visible there.

requirements.requirement: Content that was deleted or overwritten (a slide, an element, replaced text) is never lost: it can always be found again in the deck's history.
requirements.quote: nothing is ever lost
requirements.acceptance: si:designer uses the CLI to add a slide with a chart and a text box reading 'Draft A' (version N). c:ada then changes the text to 'Draft B' in the web editor, deletes the chart, and finally deletes the slide. Opening version N, either from /decks/{id}/history or with `present read <deck> --version N`, shows the slide with its chart and 'Draft A' exactly as they were.

requirements.requirement: Editing a comment does not lose its earlier wording: the previous text is kept and can still be found.
requirements.quote: nothing is ever lost
requirements.acceptance: c:ada comments 'Make the chart blue' on slide 2 in the web, then edits it to 'Make the chart green'. si:designer writes a comment and changes it with `present comment edit <comment> 'Fixed wording'`. Afterwards both earlier wordings ('Make the chart blue' and si:designer's original text) can still be retrieved rather than having been overwritten, for example from the comment's edit history in the web, from `present comments <deck> --all --json`, or from the deck's history.

requirements.requirement: The web editor has no save button or save step, and never warns about unsaved changes.
requirements.quote: There is no save button
requirements.acceptance: c:ada opens /decks/{id} in the web editor and edits a text box. No Save button, save menu item or 'unsaved changes' indicator appears anywhere, and reloading or closing the tab right after the edit raises no 'leave without saving' prompt.

requirements.requirement: Every change is saved the moment it is made with no further action, whether it is made in the web editor or by a CLI command.
requirements.quote: every change is saved the moment it's made
requirements.acceptance: c:ada types 'Revenue up 12%' into a text box on slide 2 at /decks/{id} and does nothing else. Within about a second, si:designer's `present read <deck>` shows the text, and when c:ada reloads the page the text is still there. Then si:designer runs `present set <deck> 2 <element> style.fill=#ff0000`. As soon as the command returns, a fresh `present read <deck> --json` from another session and a newly opened editor tab both show the new fill. No save, commit or sync step was needed: `present --help` lists none, and `present push` only applies to a pulled folder.

requirements.requirement: Every change stays in the deck's history for as long as the deck exists. Old changes are never pruned, squashed or expired, however old they are or however many changes come after them.
requirements.quote: Every change to a deck is kept for as long as the deck exists
requirements.acceptance: si:designer makes a first change (adds a slide titled 'First') and notes its version number N1. It then makes 250 or more further changes through the CLI, for example a loop of `present set` and `present replace` on other slides. `present versions <deck>` still lists that first change with its author and time, `present read <deck> --version N1 --json` returns the deck exactly as it was right after that change, and the earliest version still opens from /decks/{id}/history.

requirements.requirement: Grouping changes into versions never discards the individual changes inside a version: the deck as it was after each single change is kept.
requirements.quote: Every change to a deck is kept
requirements.acceptance: Within one minute, si:designer runs three separate commands: `present set <deck> 1 <el> x=100`, then `present set <deck> 1 <el> style.fill=#0000ff`, then a change to slide 1's notes. The history shows these as one version. Take the update numbers between the previous version and this one from `present versions <deck> --json` (GET /v1/decks/{id}/versions). Reading the deck at those numbers with `present read <deck> --version N --json` (GET /v1/decks/{id}/content?version=N&format=json) shows the deck after the first change only, then after the first two, then after all three.

requirements.requirement: A deck's whole history, including every version and its author, time and name, survives the deck being put in the trash and brought back.
requirements.quote: Every change to a deck is kept for as long as the deck exists
requirements.acceptance: Take a deck with versions by c:ada and si:designer and one version named 'Sent to the client'. Its owner trashes it (`present trash <deck>`, or from /decks) and brings it back (`present untrash <deck>`). Afterwards `present versions <deck>` lists the same versions with the same authors, times and names as before, and `present read <deck> --version N --json` for an older N returns the same content as before.

requirements.requirement: A deck's history survives transferring the deck to a new owner, and earlier changes stay credited to whoever made them.
requirements.quote: Every change to a deck is kept for as long as the deck exists, with who made it
requirements.acceptance: c:ada transfers her deck to si:designer (`present transfer <deck> si:designer`), and si:designer accepts with `present transfers accept <id>`. Run as si:designer, `present versions <deck>` still lists every earlier version with c:ada's changes credited to c:ada, and those earlier versions still open with `present read <deck> --version N`.

requirements.requirement: Every change is recorded with the Carbon or Silicon who made it, shown by their c:id or si:id.
requirements.quote: with who made it
requirements.acceptance: c:ada edits slide 2 in the web editor. si:designer edits slide 4 with `present set`, and changes slide 6 by running `present pull <deck> q4/`, editing the folder and then running `present push q4/`. c:ada then runs `present public <deck> edit`, and c:bob, who was never invited but is signed in, edits slide 5 through the deck's public link. /decks/{id}/history and `present versions <deck>` credit the slide 2 change to c:ada, the slide 4 and slide 6 changes to si:designer, and the slide 5 change to c:bob. No change is ever shown as anonymous, as 'system' or as made by the wrong account.

critic.problem: The check covers edits, a pull and push, and an edit through a public link. It doesn't cover changes that create a deck's content in one step: a deck made by opening a file, and a deck made from an older version. Those must also be credited to whoever made them.
critic.fix: Add two checks: the first version of a deck made with `present open board.pptx` is credited to si:designer, and the first version of a deck c:ada makes from an older version is credited to c:ada. No entry in either history lacks an author or shows 'system'.

requirements.requirement: Every change is recorded with when it was made, and the history shows that time.
requirements.quote: with who made it and when
requirements.acceptance: si:designer notes the time, runs `present set <deck> 3 <element> x=200`, and notes the time again. c:ada does the same around an edit in the web editor. `present versions <deck> --json` and /decks/{id}/history show each change at a time between its two noted times (allowing a few seconds of clock difference), with the earlier change listed before the later one.

requirements.requirement: The history shows, for every change, whether a Carbon or a Silicon made it.
requirements.quote: whether it was a Carbon or a Silicon
requirements.acceptance: c:ada edits in the web editor and si:designer edits through the CLI. /decks/{id}/history and `present versions <deck>` (including its --json output) show c:ada's change as a Carbon's, by its c:id, and si:designer's change as a Silicon's, by its si:id, so the two can be told apart at a glance.

requirements.requirement: Versions are formed automatically as changes are made. Nobody has to create, commit or checkpoint a version for it to appear in the history.
requirements.quote: Changes are grouped into versions automatically
requirements.acceptance: si:designer makes a few CLI edits to slide 4 and c:ada edits slide 2 in the web editor, and neither does anything else. `present versions <deck>` and /decks/{id}/history list new versions for both, without anyone taking a 'create version' or 'save version' action.

requirements.requirement: A run of many small changes by one Carbon or Silicon in one sitting shows in the history as a single version, not as one entry per change or keystroke.
requirements.quote: Changes are grouped into versions
requirements.acceptance: Within one minute, c:ada types a 40-character sentence into a text box on slide 2 in the web editor (dozens of separate updates) and nudges an element twice. /decks/{id}/history and `present versions <deck>` show one new version by c:ada for all of it, not dozens of entries.

requirements.requirement: Each version in the history reads as a short statement of who did what: it names the Carbon or Silicon and what they changed, including which slides, for example "si:designer rebuilt slide 4".
requirements.quote: so the history reads as a list of who did what, for example "si:designer rebuilt slide 4"
requirements.acceptance: si:designer changes only slide 4, using several `present set` and `present add` commands. Later, c:ada adds two slides in the web editor. In /decks/{id}/history and `present versions <deck>`, the two entries read in plain words, for example 'si:designer changed slide 4' and 'c:ada added 2 slides'. Each entry names the account and says what changed by slide number, not with raw ids, update counts or ops.

requirements.requirement: When Carbons and Silicons change a deck at the same time, the history still credits each change to whoever made it. One account's changes are never folded into a version credited to someone else.
requirements.quote: the history reads as a list of who did what
requirements.acceptance: Within the same two minutes, c:ada edits slide 2 in the web editor and si:designer edits slide 4 through the CLI, taking turns several times. /decks/{id}/history and `present versions <deck>` show c:ada's versions changing slide 2 and si:designer's changing slide 4. No entry credits a slide 4 change to c:ada or a slide 2 change to si:designer.

requirements.requirement: Anyone who can edit can give a version a name, and the name is shown with that version in the history.
requirements.quote: Anyone who can edit can also name a version, like `Sent to the client`.
requirements.acceptance: c:ada (owner) names the newest version 'Sent to the client' on /decks/{id}/history. si:designer (editor, not the owner) runs `present version name <deck> <N> 'First draft'` for an older version N. Both the history page and `present versions <deck>` show 'Sent to the client' and 'First draft' next to the right versions, and still do after further edits.

requirements.requirement: A named version keeps meaning the deck exactly as it was when it was named. Changes made afterwards, even by the same person moments later, are not folded into it.
requirements.quote: name a version, like `Sent to the client`
requirements.acceptance: c:ada sets slide 1's title to 'v1', names the current version 'Sent to the client', and within a minute changes the title to 'v2'. Opening 'Sent to the client' from /decks/{id}/history, or running `present read <deck> --version <its number>`, shows 'v1'. In `present versions <deck>` the name stays on that state and is not attached to a version that contains 'v2'.

requirements.requirement: Carbons and Silicons who can only comment or view cannot name a version.
requirements.quote: Anyone who can edit can also name a version
requirements.acceptance: c:carol and si:critic (commenters) and si:reader and c:dan (viewers) each run `present version name <deck> <N> 'x'`. Each is refused with a clear error about their role, and no name appears in `present versions <deck>`. In the web, c:carol and c:dan are offered no way to name a version.

requirements.requirement: Anyone who can edit can open the deck exactly as it was at any version, including the very first: every slide, element, position, text and speaker note, and the theme, as they were then.
requirements.quote: Anyone who can edit can open a deck exactly as it was at any version
requirements.acceptance: At version N, si:designer saves the output of `present read <deck> --json`. Then c:ada and si:designer change text, move an element, delete slide 3, edit notes and change the theme. `present read <deck> --version N --json` equals the saved JSON apart from the version number. When c:ada opens version N from /decks/{id}/history she sees slide 3 again, with the old text, positions, notes and theme, drawn the same as the editor showed them at the time. Opening the deck's first version works the same way.

requirements.requirement: Opening a deck as it was at an older version is read-only: it neither changes the live deck nor adds anything to its history.
requirements.quote: open a deck exactly as it was at any version
requirements.acceptance: Save the live deck JSON and the output of `present versions <deck> --json`. c:ada opens version N on /decks/{id}/history and looks through its slides. si:designer runs `present read <deck> --version N` and `present pull <deck> old/ --version N`. Afterwards the live deck JSON and the version list are exactly as saved.

requirements.requirement: Carbons and Silicons who can only comment or view, including anyone viewing through a public link, cannot open a deck as it was at an older version.
requirements.quote: Anyone who can edit can open a deck exactly as it was at any version
requirements.acceptance: c:ada puts the text 'secret figure' on slide 2 and then deletes it. She shares the deck with c:carol and si:critic as commenters and si:reader and c:dan as viewers, then runs `present public <deck> view`. Acting as each of them, these commands are refused or return only the current deck: `present read <deck> --version <N before the delete>`, `present pull <deck> old/ --version N`, `present render <deck> 2 --version N` and `present export <deck> --format pdf --version N`. The same service calls made without a token (content?version=N, export?version=N, render?version=N) behave the same. 'secret figure' is never returned, and the web gives these accounts and an anonymous visitor no way to open an older version.

requirements.requirement: Anyone who can edit can compare any two versions slide by slide, seeing for each slide whether it was added, removed, changed or left alone between them, and what changed on it.
requirements.quote: compare two versions slide by slide
requirements.acceptance: At version A the deck has slides 1 to 3. c:ada then changes slide 2's title, and later si:designer deletes slide 3 and adds a new slide, giving version B. `present compare <deck> A B` (with and without --json) reports slide 1 unchanged, slide 2 changed (showing the old and new title), slide 3 removed and the new slide added. The compare view on /decks/{id}/history shows the same thing slide by slide, with each slide as it looked in A and in B. Comparing two versions that are both older than the current one, and not next to each other, works the same way.

requirements.requirement: Carbons and Silicons who can only comment or view cannot compare versions.
requirements.quote: Anyone who can edit can open a deck exactly as it was at any version, compare two versions slide by slide
requirements.acceptance: c:carol and si:critic (commenters) and si:reader and c:dan (viewers) each run `present compare <deck> A B`. Each is refused with a clear error and gets no diff. On a public deck, GET /v1/decks/{id}/compare?from=A&to=B without a token is refused too.

requirements.requirement: Anyone who can edit can restore a whole version: the live deck becomes exactly what it was at that version, with the same slides in the same order and the same elements, text, notes and theme.
requirements.quote: restore a whole version
requirements.acceptance: Save the output of `present read <deck> --json` at version N. Then add a slide, delete slide 2, edit slide 1's text and change the theme. c:ada restores version N from /decks/{id}/history, and `present read <deck> --json` now equals the saved JSON apart from the version number. After more edits, si:designer (editor) runs `present restore <deck> N`, with the same result.

requirements.requirement: Carbons and Silicons who can only comment or view cannot restore a version.
requirements.quote: Anyone who can edit can open a deck exactly as it was at any version, compare two versions slide by slide, restore a whole version
requirements.acceptance: c:carol and si:critic (commenters) and si:reader and c:dan (viewers) each run `present restore <deck> N`. Each is refused, and the live deck and `present versions <deck>` are unchanged. The history page offers c:carol and c:dan no restore action.

requirements.requirement: Anyone who can edit can bring back a single slide from an older version. That slide becomes as it was at that version, and reappears if it was deleted since, while every other slide keeps its current content.
requirements.quote: bring back a single slide or element
requirements.acceptance: At version N, slide 3 is titled 'Plan' and holds a chart. Later si:designer deletes slide 3 and edits slide 4, and c:ada edits slide 2. c:ada brings back slide 3 from version N on /decks/{id}/history: it reappears with 'Plan' and its chart exactly as at N, while slides 2 and 4 keep the later edits. Then si:designer changes slide 2 again and runs `present restore <deck> N --slide <slide 2's id>`: slide 2 returns to its version-N content and the other slides are untouched.

requirements.requirement: Anyone who can edit can bring back a single element from an older version. That element becomes as it was at that version, and reappears if it was deleted since, while every other element keeps its current state.
requirements.quote: bring back a single slide or element
requirements.acceptance: At version N, slide 4 has a chart e_chart with 3 bars, a title e_title at x=100 and an image e_img. Later si:designer changes the chart data and moves e_title to x=600, and c:ada deletes e_img. si:designer runs `present restore <deck> N --slide 4 --element e_chart`: e_chart has its 3 bars again, while e_title stays at x=600 and e_img stays deleted. c:ada then brings back e_img from version N on /decks/{id}/history: it reappears exactly as at N, and e_chart and e_title are unchanged.

requirements.requirement: Carbons and Silicons who can only comment or view cannot bring back a slide or an element from an older version.
requirements.quote: Anyone who can edit can open a deck exactly as it was at any version, compare two versions slide by slide, restore a whole version, bring back a single slide or element
requirements.acceptance: c:carol and si:critic (commenters) and si:reader and c:dan (viewers) each run `present restore <deck> N --slide <id>` and `present restore <deck> N --slide <id> --element <id>`. Every call is refused, and the live deck and history are unchanged. The web offers c:carol and c:dan no way to bring back a slide or element.

requirements.requirement: Anyone who can edit can undo everything one chosen Carbon or Silicon changed since a given version, while every change anyone else made in that time is kept.
requirements.quote: undo everything one Carbon or Silicon changed since a given version
requirements.acceptance: Starting from version N, si:intern makes several CLI edits on slides 2 and 4 while c:ada edits slide 3's text in the web editor, the edits interleaved. c:ada undoes si:intern's changes since N from /decks/{id}/history: slides 2 and 4 are back to their version-N content and slide 3 keeps c:ada's text. Then, with a Carbon as the target, c:bob and si:designer both make changes after version M, and si:designer runs `present undo-account <deck> c:bob --since M`: c:bob's changes since M are gone and si:designer's are kept.

requirements.requirement: Undoing one account's changes since a given version leaves in place the changes that account made up to that version.
requirements.quote: since a given version
requirements.acceptance: si:intern sets slide 2's title to 'A' (version N1) and later sets slide 5's title to 'B'. si:designer runs `present undo-account <deck> si:intern --since N1`. Slide 5's title is back to what it was before 'B', and slide 2 still reads 'A'.

requirements.requirement: Undoing one account's changes is recorded as a new version made by whoever did the undo. It is not credited to the account whose changes were undone.
requirements.quote: with who made it
requirements.acceptance: si:designer runs `present undo-account <deck> si:intern --since N`. The newest entry in `present versions <deck>` and on /decks/{id}/history is by si:designer and says it undid si:intern's changes. The deck's version number has gone up, and no new entry is credited to si:intern.

requirements.requirement: Carbons and Silicons who can only comment or view cannot undo an account's changes.
requirements.quote: Anyone who can edit can open a deck exactly as it was at any version, compare two versions slide by slide, restore a whole version, bring back a single slide or element, undo everything one Carbon or Silicon changed since a given version
requirements.acceptance: c:carol and si:critic (commenters) and si:reader and c:dan (viewers) each run `present undo-account <deck> si:intern --since N`. Each is refused, and the live deck and history are unchanged. The web offers c:carol and c:dan no such action.

requirements.requirement: Anyone who can edit can make a new deck from any older version, and the new deck starts exactly as the original was at that version.
requirements.quote: make a new deck from any older version
requirements.acceptance: si:designer, an editor of c:ada's deck, runs `present new 'Q4 for the client' --from <deck>@N` for an older version N. `present read <new> --json` has the same slides, elements, text, positions, notes and theme as `present read <deck> --version N --json`. c:ada does the same from version M on /decks/{id}/history and gets a new deck that matches version M.

requirements.requirement: Making a new deck from an older version leaves the original deck and its history unchanged.
requirements.quote: make a new deck from any older version
requirements.acceptance: Save the original deck's live JSON and the output of `present versions <deck> --json`. Make a new deck with `present new 'Copy' --from <deck>@N`, and another from /decks/{id}/history. Afterwards both saved outputs are exactly as before.

requirements.requirement: A deck made from an older version belongs to the Carbon or Silicon who made it, not to the original deck's owner, because every deck belongs to whoever created it.
requirements.quote: make a new deck from any older version
requirements.acceptance: si:designer, an editor on c:ada's deck, runs `present new 'Mine' --from <deck>@N` without a folder. `present list --json` for si:designer shows the new deck owned by si:designer. The new deck is not among c:ada's own decks (`present list` run as c:ada, or /decks).

requirements.requirement: Carbons and Silicons who can only comment or view cannot make a new deck from an older version of the deck.
requirements.quote: Anyone who can edit can open a deck exactly as it was at any version, compare two versions slide by slide, restore a whole version, bring back a single slide or element, undo everything one Carbon or Silicon changed since a given version, or make a new deck from any older version.
requirements.acceptance: c:carol and si:critic (commenters) and si:reader and c:dan (viewers) each run `present new 'Copy' --from <deck>@N`. Each is refused, and no new deck appears in their `present list`.

requirements.requirement: A signed-in Carbon or Silicon who can edit only because the deck is public in edit mode can use the version features just like an invited editor.
requirements.quote: Anyone who can edit
requirements.acceptance: c:ada runs `present public <deck> edit`. si:outsider, who was never invited, uses the deck's link to run `present version name <link> <N> 'Checked'` and `present restore <link> <N> --slide <id>`. Both succeed and appear in `present versions <deck>`. c:bob, also never invited, signs in on the web through the link and can open an older version on /decks/{id}/history.

requirements.requirement: Going back (restoring a whole version, bringing back a slide or element, or undoing an account's changes) never removes anything from the history. Every version that existed before is still listed and opens exactly as it did, including the state just before going back.
requirements.quote: Going back never deletes anything.
requirements.acceptance: With versions N < M < L, where L is current, save the output of `present versions <deck> --json` and `present read <deck> --version M --json`. Run `present restore <deck> N`, then `present restore <deck> M --slide <id>`, then `present undo-account <deck> c:ada --since N`. After each step, every previously listed version is still listed with the same number, author and name, `present read <deck> --version M --json` is identical to before, and /decks/{id}/history still shows those versions. Finally, `present restore <deck> L` brings the deck back exactly to L's content.

requirements.requirement: Restoring, whether a whole version or a single slide or element, is added to the history as a new version made by whoever restored. The history is never rewound.
requirements.quote: Restoring is itself a new version.
requirements.acceptance: With the live deck at version L, c:ada restores version N from /decks/{id}/history. The newest history entry is by c:ada and says it restored version N, and the deck's version number is now greater than L (not N). si:designer then runs `present restore <deck> N --slide <id>`, and a newer entry by si:designer about that slide appears on top.

requirements.requirement: A restore is a change like any other, so everyone who has the deck open sees it as it happens, without reloading.
requirements.quote: Restoring is itself a new version.
requirements.acceptance: c:ada has /decks/{id} open in the web editor on slide 2 when si:designer runs `present restore <deck> N`. Within a couple of seconds, and without a reload, c:ada's editor shows the deck as it was at version N.

requirements.requirement: When two changes to a deck meet, both are kept and merged, including when two people type in the same text at once.
requirements.quote: when two changes meet, both are kept and merged
requirements.acceptance: While c:ada types 'Hello ' at the start of a text box on slide 2 in the web editor, si:designer at the same moment runs `present replace <deck> 2 <same element> --find 'world' --replace 'there'` and `present set <deck> 2 <another element> x=500`. Afterwards the web editor and `present read <deck>` show c:ada's 'Hello ', the replaced 'there' and the moved element together, and `present versions <deck>` lists both changes with their authors.

requirements.requirement: A change made on top of an older copy of the deck, such as a pulled folder or edits sent against an older version, is merged with everything that happened since and never silently replaces it.
requirements.quote: No change ever silently replaces another
requirements.acceptance: si:designer runs `present pull <deck> q4/` at version N. c:ada then edits slide 2's text and slide 4's notes in the web editor. si:designer changes an element in q4/slides/04-*/slide.json and runs `present push q4/`. `present read <deck>` shows c:ada's slide 2 text and slide 4 notes together with si:designer's slide 4 change. The same holds when si:designer sends the change with `present edit <deck> --ops ops.json --base N`.

requirements.requirement: When two changes meet that cannot both be kept as they are, the conflict is shown rather than one side silently winning. Examples are two people setting the same property to different values at once, or one person deleting an element while another edits it.
requirements.quote: anything that can't be merged is shown
requirements.acceptance: Case 1: from the same version N, c:ada drags element e_logo on slide 3 to x=100 in the web editor while si:designer runs `present edit <deck> --ops ops.json --base N` setting e_logo's x to 900. Case 2: si:designer deletes e_note while c:ada, offline in the web editor, edits its text and then reconnects. In both cases the conflict is flagged where both sides can see it, naming both sides: in the web for Carbons (the editor or /decks/{id}/history), and through the CLI for Silicons (the edit or push output, or `present versions <deck>`). Neither change disappears without notice.

requirements.requirement: Both sides of a change that could not be merged are kept in the history, and each side can be found and brought back.
requirements.quote: with both sides kept in the history
requirements.acceptance: After the e_logo conflict in VER-45, `present versions <deck>` lists c:ada's and si:designer's changes with their authors. Opening the deck at the matching versions (`present read <deck> --version N1` and `--version N2`, or `present compare`) shows e_logo at x=100 in one and at x=900 in the other, and e_note's edited text can also be found in one of them. `present restore <deck> <that version> --slide 3 --element e_logo` brings back whichever side lost.

requirements.requirement: A Silicon can sign in to the present CLI as itself, with its own Silicon Accounts identity and without any Carbon's session.
requirements.quote: The `present` CLI is how Silicons use Silicon Present
requirements.acceptance: At the Accounts test stack, mint a short-lived token for si:designer and pipe it to `present login --slt-stdin` under si:designer's own SILICON_HOME. `present login status --json` reports authenticated as si:designer. `present new "Silicon deck"` then succeeds, and `GET /v1/decks/{id}` shows si:designer (its Accounts uuid, shown as si:designer) as owner and creator. No Carbon signs in at any point.

requirements.requirement: Through the CLI, a Silicon can read as plain text any deck it can view, including one a Carbon built in the web editor.
requirements.quote: any deck can be read as text
requirements.acceptance: c:ada builds a 3-slide deck titled "Q4 review" in the web editor (`/decks/[id]`) and shares it with si:designer as Editor. si:designer runs `present read <deck>`. It exits 0, and stdout is readable plain text (not JSON or binary) that names the deck and each of its slides.

requirements.requirement: The text read of a deck includes every slide, in deck order, including skipped slides.
requirements.quote: any deck can be read as text: every slide
requirements.acceptance: A deck has four slides titled One, Two, Three and Four, and c:ada marks slide 3 skipped in the web editor. `present read <deck>` shows all four slides in the order One, Two, Three, Four, with the skipped slide 3 still included.

requirements.requirement: The text read lists every element on each slide, with its kind and its content.
requirements.quote: every slide, its elements
requirements.acceptance: In the web editor, c:ada puts one element of each kind on slide 2: text "Revenue up", a shape with text "Step 1", an image with alt text "Logo", a table with a cell "Q1", a chart labelled Q1,Q2, a video, an audio clip and an HTML element. Under slide 2, `present read <deck>` lists all eight with their id and kind, and shows "Revenue up", "Step 1", "Logo", "Q1" and the chart's labels and values.

requirements.requirement: The text read gives the position of every element on its slide.
requirements.quote: its elements, their positions
requirements.acceptance: c:ada drags a text box to x=140, y=900 in the web editor, and `GET /v1/decks/{id}/content?format=json` confirms it. In `present read <deck>`, that element's entry shows its position as 140, 900 in slide pixels.

requirements.requirement: The text read includes each slide's speaker notes, shown with the slide they belong to.
requirements.quote: the speaker notes
requirements.acceptance: c:ada types "Pause after Hire" into slide 2's speaker notes in the web editor. In `present read <deck>`, "Pause after Hire" appears within slide 2's part of the output and nowhere else.

requirements.requirement: In the text read, a comment on an element (including an HTML element) appears next to that element.
requirements.quote: the comments next to what they're on
requirements.acceptance: In the web editor, c:ada comments "Make this simpler" on the chart on slide 4 and "Slower please" on the HTML element on slide 5. In the text read with comments (`present read <deck> --comments`), each comment appears inside the entry of the element it is on, before the next element, and not only in a list at the end.

requirements.requirement: In the text read, a comment on some text inside an element appears next to that element, together with the quoted text.
requirements.quote: the comments next to what they're on
requirements.acceptance: c:ada selects "Q3 numbers" in a text box on slide 2 and comments "These are Q4". The text read shows "These are Q4" at that text box, together with the quoted passage "Q3 numbers".

requirements.requirement: In the text read, a comment on a point of a slide appears with that slide and shows where the point is.
requirements.quote: the comments next to what they're on
requirements.acceptance: c:ada clicks the point (960, 540) on slide 3 and comments "This spot". The text read shows "This spot" under slide 3 with its location (960, 540), and with the element it sits on if there is one.

requirements.requirement: In the text read, a comment on an area of a slide appears with that slide and shows the area.
requirements.quote: the comments next to what they're on
requirements.acceptance: c:ada drags over the rectangle from (100, 100) to (700, 500) on slide 3 and comments "Tidy this area". The text read shows "Tidy this area" under slide 3 with that rectangle's position and size.

requirements.requirement: In the text read, a comment on a whole slide appears with that slide.
requirements.quote: the comments next to what they're on
requirements.acceptance: c:ada comments "Tighten this slide" on the whole of slide 2. The text read shows it with slide 2 itself, not under an element and not under another slide.

requirements.requirement: In the text read, a comment on the whole deck appears at deck level, outside every slide.
requirements.quote: the comments next to what they're on
requirements.acceptance: c:ada comments "Looks great overall" on the whole deck. The text read shows it at deck level, outside every slide's section.

requirements.requirement: In the text read, the replies in a thread appear with that thread, in order, each with its author.
requirements.quote: the comments next to what they're on
requirements.acceptance: c:ben replies "Agreed" and then si:intern replies "Done" to c:ada's comment on the chart. The text read shows both replies in that order with the thread at the chart, marked c:ben and si:intern.

requirements.requirement: In the text read, a comment whose element has been deleted still appears and shows what it was on.
requirements.quote: the comments next to what they're on
requirements.acceptance: c:ada comments on an image on slide 3 and then deletes the image in the web editor. The text read still shows the comment on slide 3 with what it was on (for example the image's kind and label from when the comment was made) instead of dropping it.

requirements.requirement: A Silicon with only the Viewer role can read the deck as text through the CLI.
requirements.quote: any deck can be read as text
requirements.acceptance: c:ada shares a deck with si:intern as Viewer. si:intern runs `present read <deck>` and gets the full text read: slides, elements, positions and notes.

requirements.requirement: Through the CLI, a public deck can be read as text from its link without signing in.
requirements.quote: any deck can be read as text
requirements.acceptance: c:ada switches a deck to public (view) in the web editor. From a SILICON_HOME with no sign-in, `present read <deck link>` prints the deck as text.

requirements.requirement: Through the CLI, a Silicon can render any single slide of a deck to an image file, skipped slides included.
requirements.quote: any slide can be rendered to an image
requirements.acceptance: A deck has five slides, each with its own background colour, and slide 4 is skipped. si:designer runs `present render <deck> 3 -o s3.png` and `present render <deck> 4 -o s4.png`. Each writes a valid PNG at the deck's size (1920x1080), filled with that slide's own background colour.

requirements.requirement: A slide rendered through the CLI looks the same as that slide does to a Carbon in the web editor and present mode.
requirements.quote: the same way a Carbon would see it
requirements.acceptance: Slide 2 has a theme, a master footer, an uploaded image, a shape, a table and a chart. si:designer runs `present render <deck> 2 -o cli.png`. Playwright, signed in as c:ada, screenshots slide 2 full screen at 1920x1080 in `/decks/[id]/present`. The two images match within a small tolerance (for example, under 1% of pixels differ noticeably), and the footer and the image are both visible in the CLI render.

requirements.requirement: In a slide rendered through the CLI, HTML elements look as they do while running: their JS has run and their CSS animations have moved on.
requirements.quote: so a Silicon can look at what it made, the same way a Carbon would see it
requirements.acceptance: Slide 5 has an HTML element whose CSS paints its box black and whose JS, after load, repaints it #12a594 and writes "Live 42". It also has a bar with a 1-second CSS width animation. `present render <deck> 5 --at 2000 -o s5.png` shows pixels inside the box as #12a594 (not black, and not the source code), with the bar at its final width.

requirements.requirement: A slide rendered right after a change shows that change.
requirements.quote: so a Silicon can look at what it made
requirements.acceptance: si:designer runs `present set <deck> 2 <box> style.fill=#ff0000` and then, straight away, `present render <deck> 2 -o after.png`. The pixel at the box's centre is #ff0000, where a render taken before the change showed the old fill.

requirements.requirement: A Silicon with only the Viewer role can render a deck's slides to images through the CLI.
requirements.quote: any slide can be rendered to an image
requirements.acceptance: si:intern is a Viewer of c:ada's deck. It runs `present render <deck> 1 -o v.png` and gets a valid PNG that matches the owner's render of slide 1.

requirements.requirement: A Silicon's CLI change to one element changes only that element. Every other element and slide stays exactly as it was.
requirements.quote: a Silicon changes exactly the slide or element it means to, not the whole deck
requirements.acceptance: si:designer saves `GET /v1/decks/{id}/content?format=json` at version N, runs `present set <deck> 2 <box> x=300`, then reads the content again. The only difference is that box's x. The matching `update` event on `GET /v1/decks/{id}/live` lists only slide 2 in `touched`.

requirements.requirement: A Silicon's CLI change to a slide's own properties changes only that slide.
requirements.quote: a Silicon changes exactly the slide or element it means to, not the whole deck
requirements.acceptance: si:designer runs `present slide notes <deck> 3 "New notes"`. The content before and after differs only in slide 3's notes, and the update's `touched` lists slide 3 alone.

requirements.requirement: When a Silicon sets some properties of an element through the CLI, the element's other properties stay as they were.
requirements.quote: a Silicon changes exactly the slide or element it means to
requirements.acceptance: A shape has fill #eef1f5, stroke #3a5a80, text "Step 1" and x=1300. si:designer runs `present set <deck> 2 <shape> style.fill=#fff8f5 x=1280`. Afterwards the fill is #fff8f5 and x is 1280, while stroke, text, y, w, h and rotation are unchanged.

requirements.requirement: When a Carbon changes one element in the web editor while a Silicon changes another element on the same slide through the CLI, both changes are kept.
requirements.quote: so its change merges cleanly with whatever anyone else is doing
requirements.acceptance: c:ada has `/decks/[id]` open on slide 2 and drags element A to x=600. In the same second, si:designer runs `present set <deck> 2 <B> style.fill=#ff0000`. Afterwards the content has A at x=600 and B red. c:ada's open editor shows B red without a reload, and `present read <deck>` shows A at 600.

requirements.requirement: When a Carbon and a Silicon change different properties of the same element at the same time, both changes are kept.
requirements.quote: so its change merges cleanly with whatever anyone else is doing
requirements.acceptance: c:ada changes element E's fill to #00aa00 in the web editor while si:designer runs `present set <deck> 2 <E> x=500 y=200`. The final content, and c:ada's editor, show E with fill #00aa00 at x=500, y=200.

requirements.requirement: A Silicon's CLI text change merges with a Carbon's typing in the same text element at the same time.
requirements.quote: so its change merges cleanly with whatever anyone else is doing
requirements.acceptance: A text box reads "Hello world". c:ada types " today" at its end in the web editor while si:designer runs `present replace <deck> 2 <box> --find "Hello" --replace "Hi"`. The content and c:ada's editor both end with "Hi world today", and the untouched words keep their formatting.

requirements.requirement: A Silicon's CLI edit never reverts changes that others made after the Silicon last read the deck.
requirements.quote: so its change merges cleanly with whatever anyone else is doing
requirements.acceptance: si:designer runs `present read <deck> --json` at version N. Then, in the web editor, c:ada retitles slide 1 "Carbon title" and deletes element X on slide 3. Then si:designer runs `present set <deck> 2 <B> y=400`. The deck still has "Carbon title" and no element X, and B's y is 400.

requirements.requirement: `present pull` writes the whole deck into a local folder.
requirements.quote: `present pull` brings a deck down as a folder
requirements.acceptance: In the web editor, c:ada builds a deck with a theme, a master footer, and five slides holding every element kind and speaker notes. si:designer runs `present pull <deck> q4/`. Together, the folder's files hold the theme, the master, every slide in order with all its elements and fields, and every slide's notes, all matching `GET /v1/decks/{id}/content?format=json` at the pulled version.

requirements.requirement: In a pulled folder, each HTML element's code is in its own files, not inside the slide data.
requirements.quote: with HTML elements as their own files
requirements.acceptance: Slide 5 has an HTML element e_w. After `present pull <deck> q4/`, its HTML, CSS and JS are separate files beside that slide (for example `slides/05-<id>/e_w.html`, `.css`, `.js`). Their bytes equal the element's code, and the slide file points to them instead of holding the code.

requirements.requirement: A pulled folder holds a copy of every asset the deck uses, alongside the slides.
requirements.quote: and assets alongside
requirements.acceptance: The deck uses an uploaded image, a video and an audio file. After `present pull`, the folder has one file per asset (for example under `assets/`). Each file's sha256 equals the bytes from `GET /v1/assets/{id}`, and the slide files refer to those files.

requirements.requirement: A pulled folder is plain files that a Silicon can change with ordinary tools, without the present CLI.
requirements.quote: A Silicon can work on it with any tools it likes
requirements.acceptance: After `present pull <deck> q4/`, si:designer changes the folder using only ordinary tools: `sed` on a title in a slide file, `jq` on an element's x, and a shell redirect that rewrites an HTML element's .js file. It runs no present command until `present push q4/`. Each of those changes is then in the live deck.

requirements.requirement: `present push` applies element fields changed in the folder to the live deck.
requirements.quote: `present push` merges its changes back
requirements.acceptance: In the pulled folder, si:designer changes slide 1's title text to "Pushed title" and a box's x to 222, then runs `present push q4/ --summary "Folder edits"`. `GET /v1/decks/{id}/content` shows both changes, and c:ada's open editor shows them live.

requirements.requirement: `present push` applies slide properties changed in the folder, such as speaker notes and layout.
requirements.quote: `present push` merges its changes back
requirements.acceptance: In the folder, si:designer sets slide 1's notes to "Notes from the folder" and its layout to title-only, then pushes. The content shows both on slide 1.

requirements.requirement: `present push` applies edits made to an HTML element's files back to that element.
requirements.quote: `present push` merges its changes back
requirements.acceptance: si:designer rewrites `e_w.js` in the folder so it writes "Pushed widget", then pushes. The element's js in the content equals the file, and both `present render <deck> 5` and c:ada's editor show "Pushed widget" running.

requirements.requirement: `present push` creates a slide that was added in the folder.
requirements.quote: `present push` merges its changes back
requirements.acceptance: si:designer adds a new slide directory (for example `slides/06-new/slide.json`) holding a text element "Slide made in a folder", then pushes. The deck gains a sixth slide, at the end, holding that text.

requirements.requirement: `present push` creates an element that was added in the folder.
requirements.quote: `present push` merges its changes back
requirements.acceptance: si:designer adds a text element with no id to the end of slide 2's elements in the folder, then pushes. Slide 2 now has that element, with a new id, at the front of the stacking order.

requirements.requirement: `present push` deletes an element that was removed in the folder.
requirements.quote: `present push` merges its changes back
requirements.acceptance: si:designer removes a shape from slide 2's elements in the folder, then pushes. The shape is gone from slide 2 in the content and in c:ada's editor, and nothing else on slide 2 changes.

requirements.requirement: `present push` deletes a slide that was removed in the folder.
requirements.quote: `present push` merges its changes back
requirements.acceptance: si:designer deletes slide 4's directory in the folder, then pushes. The deck no longer has that slide, and the other slides keep their order and content.

requirements.requirement: `present push` applies a slide order changed in the folder.
requirements.quote: `present push` merges its changes back
requirements.acceptance: si:designer changes the slide order in the folder (for example, renaming the slide directories so slide 4 sorts first), then pushes. The deck's `order` in the content, and the web editor's slide list, now start with that slide. The other slides keep their order relative to each other.

requirements.requirement: `present push` applies deck-wide changes made in the folder, such as the theme.
requirements.quote: `present push` merges its changes back
requirements.acceptance: si:designer changes the theme's accent colour in the folder's deck file, then pushes. The deck's theme in the content has the new accent, and `present render` shows it.

requirements.requirement: `present push` uploads a new media file placed in the folder and uses it wherever the folder refers to it.
requirements.quote: `present push` merges its changes back
requirements.acceptance: si:designer copies `photo2.png` into the folder and points an image element's src at it, then pushes. The content shows that element's src as `asset:<new id>`, `GET /v1/assets/<new id>` returns photo2.png's bytes, and the render shows the new picture.

requirements.requirement: `present push` keeps every change others made to the deck after the pull.
requirements.quote: `present push` merges its changes back
requirements.acceptance: si:designer pulls at version N. Then c:ada changes slide 2's title in the web editor, and si:intern runs `present set <deck> 1 <A> y=500`. si:designer changes a different element, B, on slide 1 in the folder and pushes. Afterwards c:ada's title, A at y=500, and si:designer's change to B are all in the deck.

requirements.requirement: `present push` merges a text change made in the folder with changes others made to the same text after the pull.
requirements.quote: `present push` merges its changes back
requirements.acceptance: A text box reads "Alpha beta gamma". After si:designer pulls, c:ada changes "Alpha" to "ALPHA" in the web editor. si:designer changes "gamma" to "delta" in the folder and pushes. The text reads "ALPHA beta delta".

requirements.requirement: Pushing a folder with no changes in it changes nothing in the deck.
requirements.quote: `present push` merges its changes back
requirements.acceptance: si:designer runs `present pull <deck> q4/` and then `present push q4/` without editing anything. The deck's version is unchanged, and `GET /v1/decks/{id}/versions` shows no new change by si:designer.

requirements.requirement: Through the CLI, a Silicon can read a deck's comment threads, each with what it is on, each comment's author and text, and the replies.
requirements.quote: a Silicon can read, write, reply to, react to and resolve comments, exactly like a Carbon
requirements.acceptance: In the web editor, c:ada comments on the deck, on slide 2, on a point, on the chart and on a quoted passage, and c:ben replies to one of them. si:designer runs `present comments <deck>`. Every thread is listed with what it is on (slide number, element, quoted text), its author's c:id, its text, and c:ben's reply.

requirements.requirement: Through the CLI, a Silicon can see all of a deck's threads, open and resolved, in one list grouped by slide.
requirements.quote: a Silicon can read, write, reply to, react to and resolve comments, exactly like a Carbon
requirements.acceptance: There are threads on the deck, on slide 1 and on slide 3, and one of them is resolved. `present comments <deck> --all` prints them as one list grouped as deck, slide 1 and slide 3, with the resolved thread included.

requirements.requirement: A Silicon can comment on a whole deck through the CLI.
requirements.quote: a Silicon can read, write, reply to, react to and resolve comments, exactly like a Carbon
requirements.acceptance: si:designer runs `present comment <deck> --deck "Looks great"`. `GET /v1/decks/{id}/threads` has a new thread by si:designer anchored to the deck, and c:ada sees it in the web editor as a comment on the whole deck.

requirements.requirement: A Silicon can comment on a whole slide through the CLI.
requirements.quote: a Silicon can read, write, reply to, react to and resolve comments, exactly like a Carbon
requirements.acceptance: si:designer runs `present comment <deck> --slide 2 "Tighten this slide"`. The new thread is anchored to the whole of slide 2, and c:ada sees it on slide 2 in the web editor.

requirements.requirement: A Silicon can comment on a point of a slide through the CLI.
requirements.quote: a Silicon can read, write, reply to, react to and resolve comments, exactly like a Carbon
requirements.acceptance: si:designer runs `present comment <deck> --slide 2 --point 960,540 "This spot"`. The new thread is anchored to a point at (960, 540) on slide 2, and c:ada's editor shows its pin at that spot.

requirements.requirement: A Silicon can comment on an area of a slide through the CLI.
requirements.quote: a Silicon can read, write, reply to, react to and resolve comments, exactly like a Carbon
requirements.acceptance: si:designer runs `present comment <deck> --slide 4 --area 1150,200,300,200 "Make this simpler"`. The new thread is anchored to an area with that rectangle, and c:ada's editor marks that area.

requirements.requirement: A Silicon can comment on an element, including an HTML element, through the CLI.
requirements.quote: a Silicon can read, write, reply to, react to and resolve comments, exactly like a Carbon
requirements.acceptance: si:designer runs `present comment <deck> --slide 5 --element <html element> "Slower please"`, and the same on a chart. Each new thread is anchored to its element. In c:ada's editor the comments are attached to those elements, including the HTML element while it runs.

requirements.requirement: A Silicon can comment on some text inside an element through the CLI.
requirements.quote: a Silicon can read, write, reply to, react to and resolve comments, exactly like a Carbon
requirements.acceptance: si:designer runs `present comment <deck> --slide 1 --element <title box> --text "Zebra" "Is Zebra right?"`. The new thread is anchored to text in that box with the quote "Zebra", and c:ada's editor highlights "Zebra" in the box.

requirements.requirement: A Silicon can reply to a thread through the CLI.
requirements.quote: a Silicon can read, write, reply to, react to and resolve comments, exactly like a Carbon
requirements.acceptance: c:ada starts a thread in the web editor. si:designer runs `present reply <thread> "Done in v43"`. The thread in `GET /v1/decks/{id}/threads` and in c:ada's editor shows si:designer's reply after c:ada's comment.

requirements.requirement: A Silicon can react to a comment through the CLI.
requirements.quote: a Silicon can read, write, reply to, react to and resolve comments, exactly like a Carbon
requirements.acceptance: si:designer runs `present react <comment>` with a thumbs-up emoji on c:ada's comment. The API and c:ada's editor show that reaction from si:designer on it.

requirements.requirement: A Silicon can resolve a thread through the CLI.
requirements.quote: a Silicon can read, write, reply to, react to and resolve comments, exactly like a Carbon
requirements.acceptance: si:designer runs `present resolve <thread>` on c:ada's thread. `GET /v1/decks/{id}/threads?state=resolved` lists it as resolved by si:designer, and it leaves the open threads in c:ada's editor.

requirements.requirement: A Silicon can reopen a resolved thread through the CLI, as a Carbon can.
requirements.quote: a Silicon can read, write, reply to, react to and resolve comments, exactly like a Carbon
requirements.acceptance: After a thread has been resolved, si:designer runs `present reopen <thread>`. The thread is open again in `GET /v1/decks/{id}/threads?state=open` and in c:ada's editor.

requirements.requirement: A Silicon can edit its own comment through the CLI, as a Carbon can.
requirements.quote: a Silicon can read, write, reply to, react to and resolve comments, exactly like a Carbon
requirements.acceptance: si:designer comments "Teh numbers", then runs `present comment edit <comment> "The numbers"`. The comment now reads "The numbers" and is marked edited, in the API and in c:ada's editor.

requirements.requirement: A Silicon can mention a Carbon or a Silicon by c:id or si:id in a comment it writes through the CLI, and the one mentioned gets the mention ting.
requirements.quote: a Silicon can read, write, reply to, react to and resolve comments, exactly like a Carbon
requirements.acceptance: si:designer runs `present comment <deck> --slide 2 "@c:ada @si:intern can you check this?"`. The Ting stand-in (`GET /_tings?type=present.mention.received`) records one ting for c:ada's uuid and one for si:intern's. Each carries the deck, slide 2, what the comment is on, and the comment text.

requirements.requirement: When a Silicon comments through the CLI on a deck someone else owns, the owner gets `present.comment.created`.
requirements.quote: a Silicon can read, write, reply to, react to and resolve comments, exactly like a Carbon
requirements.acceptance: On c:ada's deck, si:designer runs `present comment <deck> --slide 1 "Hello"`. The Ting stand-in records `present.comment.created` for c:ada's uuid.

requirements.requirement: When a Silicon replies through the CLI, everyone else in the thread gets `present.comment.replied`.
requirements.quote: a Silicon can read, write, reply to, react to and resolve comments, exactly like a Carbon
requirements.acceptance: c:ada started a thread and c:ben replied in it. si:designer runs `present reply <thread> "Done"`. The Ting stand-in records `present.comment.replied` for both c:ada and c:ben.

requirements.requirement: When a Silicon resolves a thread through the CLI, whoever started it gets `present.thread.resolved`.
requirements.quote: a Silicon can read, write, reply to, react to and resolve comments, exactly like a Carbon
requirements.acceptance: c:ada started a thread. si:designer runs `present resolve <thread>`. The Ting stand-in records `present.thread.resolved` for c:ada.

requirements.requirement: A comment that a Silicon writes through the CLI shows up for Carbons exactly the way a Carbon's comment does.
requirements.quote: a Silicon can read, write, reply to, react to and resolve comments, exactly like a Carbon
requirements.acceptance: With `/decks/[id]` open as c:ada, si:designer runs `present comment <deck> --slide 2 --element <chart> "Simplified"`. Without a reload, c:ada sees the comment on the chart and in the thread list, with si:designer's si:id, name and pfp, shown the same way as a Carbon's comment.

requirements.requirement: A Silicon with the Commenter role can write comments and replies through the CLI.
requirements.quote: a Silicon can read, write, reply to, react to and resolve comments, exactly like a Carbon
requirements.acceptance: c:ada shares her deck with si:intern as Commenter. si:intern runs `present comment <deck> --slide 1 "Commenter note"` and `present reply <thread> "Me too"`. Both succeed and appear in `present comments <deck>`.

requirements.requirement: A Silicon with only the Viewer role cannot write comments or replies through the CLI, just as a Carbon viewer can't.
requirements.quote: a Silicon can read, write, reply to, react to and resolve comments, exactly like a Carbon
requirements.acceptance: c:ada shares her deck with si:intern as Viewer. `present comments <deck>` works for si:intern, but `present comment <deck> --slide 1 "x"` and `present reply <thread> "x"` are refused with 403, and no thread or comment is created.

requirements.requirement: When a deck's public link allows commenting, a signed-in Silicon that was never invited can comment on it through the CLI.
requirements.quote: a Silicon can read, write, reply to, react to and resolve comments, exactly like a Carbon
requirements.acceptance: c:ada makes the deck public with commenting allowed. si:intern, signed in but never invited, runs `present comment <deck> --slide 1 "From the link"`. The comment is created and attributed to si:intern.

requirements.requirement: A Silicon can start a presentation of a deck through the CLI and gets the link to follow it.
requirements.quote: a Silicon can start a presentation
requirements.acceptance: si:designer runs `present start <deck>`. It prints a presentation id and a follow link (`/p/<presentation>`), and `GET /v1/presentations/{p}` shows the presentation on the first slide.

requirements.requirement: A Silicon can move its presentation forward to the next slide through the CLI.
requirements.quote: a Silicon can start a presentation and move through its slides
requirements.acceptance: On a deck with no click animations, during si:designer's presentation, `present next` moves the presentation to slide 2 (`GET /v1/presentations/{p}` shows slide 2's id). Running it again moves to slide 3.

requirements.requirement: A Silicon can move its presentation back to the previous slide through the CLI.
requirements.quote: a Silicon can start a presentation and move through its slides
requirements.acceptance: From slide 3 of si:designer's presentation, `present prev` moves it back to slide 2, as `GET /v1/presentations/{p}` shows.

requirements.requirement: Everyone following a Silicon's presentation sees each of its moves live.
requirements.quote: a Silicon can start a presentation and move through its slides
requirements.acceptance: c:ada opens the follow link `/p/<presentation>` in a browser, and si:intern runs `present follow <presentation> --json`. Each time si:designer runs `present next` or `present prev`, both followers move to the same slide within about a second, without reloading.

requirements.requirement: A Silicon can stop its presentation through the CLI, as a Carbon can leave present mode.
requirements.quote: The `present` CLI is how Silicons use Silicon Present, and it can do everything the web editor can.
requirements.acceptance: si:designer runs `present stop`. `GET /v1/presentations/{p}` reports the presentation ended, c:ada's `/p/<presentation>` page shows it ended, and `present next` is refused afterwards.

requirements.requirement: While presenting through the CLI, a Silicon can see what the presenter view shows: the current slide's speaker notes, the next slide and the elapsed time.
requirements.quote: The `present` CLI is how Silicons use Silicon Present, and it can do everything the web editor can.
requirements.acceptance: si:designer presents a deck whose slide 2 has the notes "Breathe" and moves to slide 2. Through the CLI it can then get slide 2's notes ("Breathe"), which slide comes next, and how long the presentation has been running.

requirements.requirement: A Silicon can follow a live presentation through the CLI and stay on the slide being shown.
requirements.quote: The `present` CLI is how Silicons use Silicon Present, and it can do everything the web editor can.
requirements.acceptance: c:ada starts presenting from `/decks/[id]/present`. si:designer runs `present follow <presentation> --json`. When c:ada moves to slide 3, the CLI prints a state line for slide 3, and when she stops, it prints an ended line.

requirements.requirement: Through the CLI, a Silicon can list a deck's versions, each with who made it (Carbon or Silicon), when, and a summary of what they did.
requirements.quote: a Silicon can list, read, compare, name and restore versions
requirements.acceptance: c:ada edits slide 1 in the web editor, then si:designer changes slide 4 through the CLI. `present versions <deck>` lists both versions, each with who made it (c:ada, si:designer), when, and a summary of what they did (for example "si:designer changed slide 4").

requirements.requirement: Through the CLI, a Silicon can read a deck as text exactly as it was at any version.
requirements.quote: a Silicon can list, read, compare, name and restore versions
requirements.acceptance: si:designer changes slide 2's title from "Plan" to "Plan B". `present read <deck> --version N`, where N is the version before the change, prints the deck as text with "Plan". `present read <deck>` prints "Plan B".

requirements.requirement: Through the CLI, a Silicon can compare two versions of a deck slide by slide.
requirements.quote: a Silicon can list, read, compare, name and restore versions
requirements.acceptance: Between versions A and B, c:ada added a slide and si:designer changed the chart on slide 2. `present compare <deck> A B` reports, slide by slide, the added slide and the changed chart on slide 2.

requirements.requirement: Through the CLI, a Silicon can name a version.
requirements.quote: a Silicon can list, read, compare, name and restore versions
requirements.acceptance: si:designer runs `present version name <deck> <N> "Sent to the client"`. `present versions <deck>` and c:ada's `/decks/[id]/history` show version N named "Sent to the client".

requirements.requirement: Through the CLI, a Silicon can restore a deck to a whole earlier version.
requirements.quote: a Silicon can list, read, compare, name and restore versions
requirements.acceptance: The deck is at version 20 after changes since version 12. si:designer runs `present restore <deck> 12`. The content now equals version 12's content, the restore appears in `present versions` as a new version by si:designer, and versions 13 to 20 are still listed and readable with `present read --version`.

requirements.requirement: Through the CLI, a Silicon can bring back a single slide from an earlier version and leave the rest of the deck as it is.
requirements.quote: The `present` CLI is how Silicons use Silicon Present, and it can do everything the web editor can.
requirements.acceptance: si:designer runs `present restore <deck> 12 --slide <s2>`. Slide 2 matches version 12, every other slide keeps its current content, and the restore shows as a new version.

requirements.requirement: Through the CLI, a Silicon can bring back a single element from an earlier version.
requirements.quote: The `present` CLI is how Silicons use Silicon Present, and it can do everything the web editor can.
requirements.acceptance: si:designer runs `present restore <deck> 12 --slide <s2> --element <chart>`. Only that chart returns to its version-12 state, and the rest of slide 2 is unchanged.

requirements.requirement: Through the CLI, a Silicon can undo everything one Carbon or Silicon changed since a given version and keep everyone else's changes.
requirements.quote: The `present` CLI is how Silicons use Silicon Present, and it can do everything the web editor can.
requirements.acceptance: Since version 30, si:intern changed slide 2 and c:ada changed slide 3. si:designer runs `present undo-account <deck> si:intern --since 30`. si:intern's changes are gone, c:ada's remain, and the undo shows in the history as a new version.

requirements.requirement: Through the CLI, a Silicon can make a new deck from any older version of a deck.
requirements.quote: The `present` CLI is how Silicons use Silicon Present, and it can do everything the web editor can.
requirements.acceptance: si:designer runs `present new "Q4 (as sent)" --from <deck>@12`. The new deck is owned by si:designer and has exactly version 12's slides and content, and the original deck is unchanged.

requirements.section: Silicons > Everything the web editor can do
requirements.requirement: A Silicon can create a new deck with a title through the CLI, and the deck belongs to that Silicon.
requirements.quote: The `present` CLI is how Silicons use Silicon Present, and it can do everything the web editor can.
requirements.acceptance: si:designer runs `present new "Q4 review"`, which prints a deck id. `GET /v1/decks/{id}` shows the title "Q4 review" with si:designer as owner and creator, and `present list` shows the deck.

requirements.section: Silicons > Everything the web editor can do
requirements.requirement: A Silicon can list its own decks through the CLI.
requirements.quote: The `present` CLI is how Silicons use Silicon Present, and it can do everything the web editor can.
requirements.acceptance: si:designer owns two decks, and c:ada has shared a third with it. `present list` shows exactly the two decks si:designer owns.

requirements.section: Silicons > Everything the web editor can do
requirements.requirement: A Silicon can list the decks and folders shared with it through the CLI.
requirements.quote: The `present` CLI is how Silicons use Silicon Present, and it can do everything the web editor can.
requirements.acceptance: c:ada shares a deck and a folder with si:designer in the web. `present list --shared` shows the deck, and `present folder list --shared` shows the folder. Neither appears among si:designer's own decks.

requirements.section: Silicons > Everything the web editor can do
requirements.requirement: A Silicon can create a folder through the CLI.
requirements.quote: The `present` CLI is how Silicons use Silicon Present, and it can do everything the web editor can.
requirements.acceptance: si:designer runs `present folder new "Clients"`, which prints a folder id. `GET /v1/folders/{id}` shows the name "Clients" with si:designer as owner.

requirements.section: Silicons > Everything the web editor can do
requirements.requirement: A Silicon can move one of its decks into one of its folders through the CLI.
requirements.quote: The `present` CLI is how Silicons use Silicon Present, and it can do everything the web editor can.
requirements.acceptance: si:designer runs `present move <deck> <folder>`. `GET /v1/decks?scope=mine&folder=<folder>` lists the deck, and `present list --folder <folder>` shows it.

requirements.section: Silicons > Everything the web editor can do
requirements.requirement: A Silicon can put one of its folders inside another of its folders through the CLI.
requirements.quote: The `present` CLI is how Silicons use Silicon Present, and it can do everything the web editor can.
requirements.acceptance: si:designer runs `present folder move <child> <parent>`. `GET /v1/folders/{child}` shows the parent, and `present folder list --parent <parent>` lists the child.

requirements.section: Silicons > Everything the web editor can do
requirements.requirement: A deck that a Silicon creates through the CLI inside a Carbon's shared folder belongs to that folder's owner and still shows the Silicon as its creator.
requirements.quote: The `present` CLI is how Silicons use Silicon Present, and it can do everything the web editor can.
requirements.acceptance: c:ada shares folder F with si:designer as Editor. si:designer runs `present new "Draft" --folder F`. `GET /v1/decks/{id}` shows owner c:ada and creator si:designer, and c:ada sees "Draft" among her decks at `/decks`, shown as created by si:designer.

requirements.section: Silicons > Everything the web editor can do
requirements.requirement: A Silicon can transfer a deck it owns to a Carbon or Silicon through the CLI, and the deck moves only once they accept.
requirements.quote: The `present` CLI is how Silicons use Silicon Present, and it can do everything the web editor can.
requirements.acceptance: si:designer runs `present transfer <deck> c:ada`. `GET /v1/decks/{id}` still shows si:designer as owner until c:ada accepts the transfer at `/decks`. After she accepts, the owner is c:ada.

requirements.section: Silicons > Everything the web editor can do
requirements.requirement: A Silicon can transfer a folder it owns to a Carbon or Silicon through the CLI, and the folder moves only once they accept.
requirements.quote: The `present` CLI is how Silicons use Silicon Present, and it can do everything the web editor can.
requirements.acceptance: si:designer runs `present transfer <folder> c:ada --folder`. The folder stays si:designer's until c:ada accepts. After she accepts, `GET /v1/folders/{id}` shows c:ada as owner.

requirements.section: Silicons > Everything the web editor can do
requirements.requirement: A Silicon can accept a deck or folder transferred to it through the CLI.
requirements.quote: The `present` CLI is how Silicons use Silicon Present, and it can do everything the web editor can.
requirements.acceptance: c:ada offers a deck to si:designer from `/decks`. `present transfers` lists it as incoming, and `present transfers accept <id>` makes si:designer the owner. The deck then appears in `present list`.

requirements.section: Silicons > Everything the web editor can do
requirements.requirement: A Silicon can delete a deck through the CLI, which moves it to the trash with its full history.
requirements.quote: The `present` CLI is how Silicons use Silicon Present, and it can do everything the web editor can.
requirements.acceptance: si:designer runs `present trash <deck>`. The deck leaves `present list` and shows in `present list --trash`, and `GET /v1/decks/{id}/versions` still lists every version.

requirements.section: Silicons > Everything the web editor can do
requirements.requirement: A Silicon can restore a deck from the trash through the CLI.
requirements.quote: The `present` CLI is how Silicons use Silicon Present, and it can do everything the web editor can.
requirements.acceptance: si:designer runs `present untrash <deck>` on a trashed deck. It is back in `present list` with the same content and its full history.

requirements.section: Silicons > Everything the web editor can do
requirements.requirement: A Silicon can permanently delete a deck from the trash through the CLI, which asks it to confirm first.
requirements.quote: The `present` CLI is how Silicons use Silicon Present, and it can do everything the web editor can.
requirements.acceptance: A trashed deck is titled "Old draft". `present delete <deck> --permanent` with no confirmation, or with a wrong title, is refused and the deck stays. With `--confirm "Old draft"` the deck is gone, and `present read <deck>` reports it not found.

requirements.section: Silicons > Everything the web editor can do
requirements.requirement: A Silicon can delete a folder through the CLI, which moves it to the trash.
requirements.quote: The `present` CLI is how Silicons use Silicon Present, and it can do everything the web editor can.
