requirements.acceptance: si:designer runs `present folder trash <id>`. The folder shows in `present folder list --trash` and no longer in `present folder list`.

requirements.section: Silicons > Everything the web editor can do
requirements.requirement: A Silicon can restore a folder from the trash through the CLI.
requirements.quote: The `present` CLI is how Silicons use Silicon Present, and it can do everything the web editor can.
requirements.acceptance: si:designer runs `present folder untrash <id>` on a trashed folder. It is back in `present folder list` with its decks.

requirements.section: Silicons > Everything the web editor can do
requirements.requirement: A Silicon can add a slide to a deck through the CLI.
requirements.quote: The `present` CLI is how Silicons use Silicon Present, and it can do everything the web editor can.
requirements.acceptance: si:designer runs `present slide add <deck> --layout title-body --title "Plan" --body "Hire"`. The deck gains a title-body slide holding "Plan" and "Hire", and c:ada's editor shows it live.

requirements.section: Silicons > Everything the web editor can do
requirements.requirement: A Silicon can delete a slide through the CLI.
requirements.quote: The `present` CLI is how Silicons use Silicon Present, and it can do everything the web editor can.
requirements.acceptance: si:designer runs `present slide delete <deck> 3`. That slide is gone from the deck's `order` and from c:ada's editor, and the other slides are unchanged.

requirements.section: Silicons > Everything the web editor can do
requirements.requirement: A Silicon can reorder slides through the CLI, as the slide sorter does.
requirements.quote: The `present` CLI is how Silicons use Silicon Present, and it can do everything the web editor can.
requirements.acceptance: si:designer runs `present slide move <deck> 4 --first`. The deck's `order` starts with that slide, and c:ada's slide sorter shows the new order.

requirements.section: Silicons > Everything the web editor can do
requirements.requirement: A Silicon can change a slide's layout through the CLI.
requirements.quote: The `present` CLI is how Silicons use Silicon Present, and it can do everything the web editor can.
requirements.acceptance: si:designer runs `present slide layout <deck> 2 two-columns`. Slide 2's layout is two-columns in the content and in the web editor.

requirements.section: Silicons > Everything the web editor can do
requirements.requirement: A Silicon can change a deck's theme through the CLI.
requirements.quote: The `present` CLI is how Silicons use Silicon Present, and it can do everything the web editor can.
requirements.acceptance: si:designer runs `present theme <deck> Ivory --color accent=#b4532a`. The content's theme has that name and accent colour, and both `present render` and c:ada's editor show the new theme.

requirements.section: Silicons > Everything the web editor can do
requirements.requirement: A Silicon can put elements on the deck's master through the CLI, so that they appear under every slide.
requirements.quote: The `present` CLI is how Silicons use Silicon Present, and it can do everything the web editor can.
requirements.acceptance: si:designer runs `present add text <deck> 1 "Acme footer" --master`. The master holds the footer, and a render of every slide that does not hide the master shows it.

requirements.section: Silicons > Everything the web editor can do
requirements.requirement: A Silicon can set a slide's transition through the CLI.
requirements.quote: The `present` CLI is how Silicons use Silicon Present, and it can do everything the web editor can.
requirements.acceptance: si:designer runs `present slide transition <deck> 2 push --duration 500 --direction left`. Slide 2's transition in the content is push, 500 ms, left, and it plays in c:ada's present mode.

requirements.section: Silicons > Everything the web editor can do
requirements.requirement: A Silicon can write a slide's speaker notes through the CLI.
requirements.quote: The `present` CLI is how Silicons use Silicon Present, and it can do everything the web editor can.
requirements.acceptance: si:designer runs `present slide notes <deck> 2 "Pause after Hire"`. Slide 2's notes are that text in the content and in c:ada's presenter view (`/decks/[id]/presenter`).

requirements.section: Silicons > Everything the web editor can do
requirements.requirement: A Silicon can mark a slide as skipped, and unmark it, through the CLI.
requirements.quote: The `present` CLI is how Silicons use Silicon Present, and it can do everything the web editor can.
requirements.acceptance: si:designer runs `present slide skip <deck> 4`. Slide 4 is skipped in the content, and c:ada's present mode goes from slide 3 straight to slide 5. `present slide skip <deck> 4 --off` makes it a normal slide again.

requirements.section: Silicons > Everything the web editor can do
requirements.requirement: A Silicon can start a named section at a slide through the CLI.
requirements.quote: The `present` CLI is how Silicons use Silicon Present, and it can do everything the web editor can.
requirements.acceptance: si:designer runs `present slide section <deck> 2 "Results"`. A section named "Results" starts at slide 2 in the content and in the web editor's slide list.

requirements.section: Silicons > Everything the web editor can do
requirements.requirement: A Silicon can make a text element and change its text and formatting through the CLI.
requirements.quote: The `present` CLI is how Silicons use Silicon Present, and it can do everything the web editor can.
requirements.acceptance: si:designer runs `present add text <deck> 1 "Q4" --size 48 --bold --color "#b4532a"`, then `present replace <deck> 1 <id> --find "Q4" --replace "Q4 2026"`. The content holds a text element reading "Q4 2026" in bold, size 48, colour #b4532a, and c:ada's editor shows it.

requirements.section: Silicons > Everything the web editor can do
requirements.requirement: A Silicon can add an image from a local file to a slide, and change it, through the CLI.
requirements.quote: The `present` CLI is how Silicons use Silicon Present, and it can do everything the web editor can.
requirements.acceptance: si:designer runs `present add image <deck> 3 photo.png --alt "Gradient"`, then `present set <deck> 3 <id> fit=cover`. The image's src is `asset:<id>`, `GET /v1/assets/{id}` returns photo.png's bytes, alt is "Gradient" and fit is cover. `present render` shows the picture.

requirements.section: Silicons > Everything the web editor can do
requirements.requirement: A Silicon can make a shape and change it through the CLI.
requirements.quote: The `present` CLI is how Silicons use Silicon Present, and it can do everything the web editor can.
requirements.acceptance: si:designer runs `present add shape <deck> 2 star --text "Hi" --fill "#ffcc00"`, then `present set <deck> 2 <id> shape=hexagon`. The content holds a hexagon with the text "Hi" and fill #ffcc00.

requirements.section: Silicons > Everything the web editor can do
requirements.requirement: A Silicon can make a table and change its cells through the CLI.
requirements.quote: The `present` CLI is how Silicons use Silicon Present, and it can do everything the web editor can.
requirements.acceptance: si:designer runs `present add table <deck> 4 --rows 3 --cols 2 --cell 0,0=Name`, then changes cell 1,1 to "42" with a fill through the CLI. The content's table is 3x2, with "Name" at 0,0 and "42" with that fill at 1,1.

requirements.section: Silicons > Everything the web editor can do
requirements.requirement: A Silicon can make a chart and change its type and data through the CLI.
requirements.quote: The `present` CLI is how Silicons use Silicon Present, and it can do everything the web editor can.
requirements.acceptance: si:designer runs `present add chart <deck> 4 --type column --labels Q1,Q2,Q3 --series "Revenue=10,12,15"`, then uses `present set` to make it a line chart with Q3 at 18. The content's chart is a line chart with Revenue 10, 12, 18, and `present render` shows a line chart.

requirements.section: Silicons > Everything the web editor can do
requirements.requirement: A Silicon can add a video from a local file to a slide, and change its settings, through the CLI.
requirements.quote: The `present` CLI is how Silicons use Silicon Present, and it can do everything the web editor can.
requirements.acceptance: si:designer runs `present add video <deck> 3 demo.mp4 --muted --loop`, then `present set <deck> 3 <id> autoplay=true`. The video's src is an asset holding demo.mp4's bytes, set to muted, loop and autoplay, and it plays in c:ada's editor.

requirements.section: Silicons > Everything the web editor can do
requirements.requirement: A Silicon can add audio from a local file to a slide, and change its settings, through the CLI.
requirements.quote: The `present` CLI is how Silicons use Silicon Present, and it can do everything the web editor can.
requirements.acceptance: si:designer runs `present add audio <deck> 3 tone.mp3`, then `present set <deck> 3 <id> loop=true`. The audio's src is an asset holding tone.mp3's bytes, set to loop, and it plays in c:ada's editor.

requirements.section: Silicons > Everything the web editor can do
requirements.requirement: A Silicon can make an HTML element and change its HTML, CSS and JS through the CLI.
requirements.quote: The `present` CLI is how Silicons use Silicon Present, and it can do everything the web editor can.
requirements.acceptance: si:designer runs `present add html <deck> 5 --html w.html --css w.css --js w.js`, then `present set <deck> 5 <id> js=@w2.js`. The element's code in the content is w.html, w.css and w2.js, and c:ada's editor runs the new JS.

requirements.section: Silicons > Everything the web editor can do
requirements.requirement: A Silicon can move any element through the CLI, including one a Carbon made.
requirements.quote: The `present` CLI is how Silicons use Silicon Present, and it can do everything the web editor can.
requirements.acceptance: c:ada draws a shape in the web editor. si:designer runs `present set <deck> 2 <shape> x=100 y=200`. The shape is at 100, 200 in the content and in c:ada's editor.

requirements.section: Silicons > Everything the web editor can do
requirements.requirement: A Silicon can resize any element through the CLI, including one a Carbon made.
requirements.quote: The `present` CLI is how Silicons use Silicon Present, and it can do everything the web editor can.
requirements.acceptance: si:designer runs `present set <deck> 2 <shape> w=800 h=300` on c:ada's shape. Its size is 800x300 in the content and in c:ada's editor.

requirements.section: Silicons > Everything the web editor can do
requirements.requirement: A Silicon can rotate any element through the CLI, including one a Carbon made.
requirements.quote: The `present` CLI is how Silicons use Silicon Present, and it can do everything the web editor can.
requirements.acceptance: si:designer runs `present set <deck> 2 <shape> rotation=15` on c:ada's shape. Its rotation is 15 in the content, and `present render` shows it turned.

requirements.section: Silicons > Everything the web editor can do
requirements.requirement: A Silicon can change an element's layer through the CLI, bringing it forward or sending it back.
requirements.quote: The `present` CLI is how Silicons use Silicon Present, and it can do everything the web editor can.
requirements.acceptance: On slide 3, an image overlaps a shape. After `present front <deck> 3 <image>`, the image is last in the slide's back-to-front order and drawn over the shape. After `present back <deck> 3 <image>`, it is first and drawn under the shape.

requirements.section: Silicons > Everything the web editor can do
requirements.requirement: A Silicon can group elements through the CLI, including ones a Carbon made.
requirements.quote: The `present` CLI is how Silicons use Silicon Present, and it can do everything the web editor can.
requirements.acceptance: si:designer groups two of c:ada's elements (for example `present set ... group=g1` on both). The content shows the same group id on both, and in c:ada's editor dragging one moves both.

requirements.section: Silicons > Everything the web editor can do
requirements.requirement: A Silicon can align elements through the CLI.
requirements.quote: The `present` CLI is how Silicons use Silicon Present, and it can do everything the web editor can.
requirements.acceptance: Three boxes sit at x=100, 140 and 180. si:designer aligns their left edges through the CLI. All three have the same x in the content, and nothing else about them changes.

requirements.section: Silicons > Everything the web editor can do
requirements.requirement: A Silicon can lock an element through the CLI.
requirements.quote: The `present` CLI is how Silicons use Silicon Present, and it can do everything the web editor can.
requirements.acceptance: si:designer runs `present set <deck> 2 <shape> locked=true`. The content shows the shape as locked, and c:ada's editor treats it as locked: dragging it does not move it.

requirements.section: Silicons > Everything the web editor can do
requirements.requirement: A Silicon can animate an element through the CLI.
requirements.quote: The `present` CLI is how Silicons use Silicon Present, and it can do everything the web editor can.
requirements.acceptance: si:designer runs `present set <deck> 2 <box> 'animation={"effect":"fly-in","trigger":"click","order":1,"duration":500,"delay":0,"direction":"left"}'`. The content holds that animation, and in present mode the box flies in on the first click or `present next`.

requirements.section: Silicons > Everything the web editor can do
requirements.requirement: A Silicon can delete an element through the CLI.
requirements.quote: The `present` CLI is how Silicons use Silicon Present, and it can do everything the web editor can.
requirements.acceptance: si:designer runs `present delete <deck> 2 <shape>`. The shape is gone from slide 2 in the content and in c:ada's editor, and the other elements are unchanged.

requirements.section: Silicons > Everything the web editor can do
requirements.requirement: A Silicon can add a link to an element through the CLI, pointing to a web address or to another slide.
requirements.quote: The `present` CLI is how Silicons use Silicon Present, and it can do everything the web editor can.
requirements.acceptance: si:designer runs `present set <deck> 2 <a> link=https://example.com` and `present set <deck> 2 <b> link=slide:<s5>`. The content holds both links, and in c:ada's present mode clicking b goes to slide 5.

requirements.section: Silicons > Everything the web editor can do
requirements.requirement: A Silicon can find and replace text across a whole deck through the CLI.
requirements.quote: The `present` CLI is how Silicons use Silicon Present, and it can do everything the web editor can.
requirements.acceptance: "Acme" appears in text on slides 1 and 3 and in a table cell on slide 4. si:designer replaces every "Acme" with "Zenith" through the CLI. `present read <deck>` then shows "Zenith" in all three places and no "Acme".

requirements.section: Silicons > Everything the web editor can do
requirements.requirement: A Silicon can undo its own last change through the CLI without undoing anyone else's.
requirements.quote: The `present` CLI is how Silicons use Silicon Present, and it can do everything the web editor can.
requirements.acceptance: si:designer sets a box's fill to #ff0000 through the CLI, then c:ada edits slide 3 in the web editor. si:designer undoes its own change through the CLI. The box has its old fill again, c:ada's edit to slide 3 is still there, and the undo shows as a new version in `present versions`.

requirements.section: Silicons > Everything the web editor can do
requirements.requirement: A Silicon can open a file of any supported format as a new deck through the CLI.
requirements.quote: The `present` CLI is how Silicons use Silicon Present, and it can do everything the web editor can.
requirements.acceptance: For each of a .pptx, .ppt, .key, .odp, .pdf, .html, .png and .jpg file, si:designer runs `present open <file>`. Each makes a new deck owned by si:designer, and `present read` shows the file's content (for example, the pptx's slide titles).

requirements.section: Silicons > Everything the web editor can do
requirements.requirement: A Silicon can download a deck in any supported format through the CLI.
requirements.quote: The `present` CLI is how Silicons use Silicon Present, and it can do everything the web editor can.
requirements.acceptance: For each of pptx, ppt, key, odp, pdf, html, png and jpg, si:designer runs `present export <deck> --format <f> -o out.<f>`. Each produces a valid file of that format, checked by its signature bytes and by opening it.

requirements.section: Silicons > Everything the web editor can do
requirements.requirement: A Silicon can add an SVG file to a slide through the CLI.
requirements.quote: The `present` CLI is how Silicons use Silicon Present, and it can do everything the web editor can.
requirements.acceptance: si:designer runs `present add image <deck> 2 logo.svg`. The SVG is stored as an asset with the same bytes, and it shows on slide 2 in `present render` and in c:ada's editor.

requirements.section: Silicons > Everything the web editor can do
requirements.requirement: A Silicon can add an animation file, such as an animated GIF, to a slide through the CLI.
requirements.quote: The `present` CLI is how Silicons use Silicon Present, and it can do everything the web editor can.
requirements.acceptance: si:designer adds spinner.gif to slide 2 through the CLI. `GET /v1/assets/{id}` returns the same bytes, and the GIF animates in c:ada's editor.

requirements.section: Silicons > Everything the web editor can do
requirements.requirement: A Silicon can add a font file to a deck through the CLI and use it for text.
requirements.quote: The `present` CLI is how Silicons use Silicon Present, and it can do everything the web editor can.
requirements.acceptance: si:designer adds a .woff2 font to the deck through the CLI and sets a text box to use that font family. The deck's theme lists the font as an asset, and `present render` shows the text in that font rather than a fallback.

requirements.section: Silicons > Everything the web editor can do
requirements.requirement: A Silicon can invite a Carbon to a deck by c:id, with a role, through the CLI.
requirements.quote: The `present` CLI is how Silicons use Silicon Present, and it can do everything the web editor can.
requirements.acceptance: si:designer runs `present share <deck> c:ada --role commenter`. `GET /v1/decks/{id}/access` lists c:ada as commenter, the deck shows in c:ada's shared decks at `/decks`, and the Ting stand-in records `present.deck.shared` for c:ada.

requirements.section: Silicons > Everything the web editor can do
requirements.requirement: A Silicon can invite another Silicon to a deck by si:id, with a role, through the CLI.
requirements.quote: The `present` CLI is how Silicons use Silicon Present, and it can do everything the web editor can.
requirements.acceptance: si:designer runs `present share <deck> si:intern --role editor`. `GET /v1/decks/{id}/access` lists si:intern as editor, and `present list --shared` run as si:intern shows the deck.

requirements.section: Silicons > Everything the web editor can do
requirements.requirement: A Silicon can invite someone by email through the CLI, including an email that is not on Silicon Accounts yet.
requirements.quote: The `present` CLI is how Silicons use Silicon Present, and it can do everything the web editor can.
requirements.acceptance: si:designer runs `present share <deck> newcomer@example.test --role viewer`. `GET /v1/decks/{id}/access` shows a pending invite for that address. Once an account with that verified email is made at the Accounts test stack and signs in, it can view the deck.

requirements.section: Silicons > Everything the web editor can do
requirements.requirement: A Silicon can share a folder through the CLI, which shares everything in it, including anything added later.
requirements.quote: The `present` CLI is how Silicons use Silicon Present, and it can do everything the web editor can.
requirements.acceptance: si:designer runs `present folder share <folder> c:ben --role viewer`. c:ben can view every deck in the folder, including a deck si:designer adds to it afterwards.

requirements.section: Silicons > Everything the web editor can do
requirements.requirement: A Silicon with the Editor role on someone else's deck can invite others to it through the CLI.
requirements.quote: The `present` CLI is how Silicons use Silicon Present, and it can do everything the web editor can.
requirements.acceptance: c:ada shares her deck with si:designer as Editor. si:designer runs `present share <deck> c:ben --role viewer`, and c:ben gets view access, as `GET /v1/decks/{id}/access` shows.

requirements.section: Silicons > Everything the web editor can do
requirements.requirement: A Silicon can make its deck public through the CLI with one switch, choosing whether the link lets people view, comment or edit.
requirements.quote: The `present` CLI is how Silicons use Silicon Present, and it can do everything the web editor can.
requirements.acceptance: si:designer runs `present public <deck> view`, and the link opens the deck in a signed-out browser. After `present public <deck> comment`, a signed-in Carbon who was never invited can comment through the link. After `present public <deck> edit`, they can also edit.

requirements.section: Silicons > Everything the web editor can do
requirements.requirement: A Silicon can make its public deck private again through the CLI, which stops the link working.
requirements.quote: The `present` CLI is how Silicons use Silicon Present, and it can do everything the web editor can.
requirements.acceptance: After `present public <deck> off`, the link no longer opens the deck, either in a signed-out browser or for an account that was never invited.

requirements.section: Silicons > Everything the web editor can do
requirements.requirement: A Silicon given the Editor role on a Carbon's deck can edit it directly through the CLI.
requirements.quote: The `present` CLI is how Silicons use Silicon Present, and it can do everything the web editor can.
requirements.acceptance: c:ada shares her deck with si:intern as Editor. si:intern runs `present set <deck> 2 <box> x=300` and `present slide add <deck>`. Both changes land, and both show in c:ada's editor.

requirements.section: Silicons > Everything the web editor can do
requirements.requirement: When a deck's public link allows editing, a signed-in Silicon that was never invited can edit it through the CLI.
requirements.quote: The `present` CLI is how Silicons use Silicon Present, and it can do everything the web editor can.
requirements.acceptance: c:ada makes the deck public with editing allowed. si:intern, signed in but never invited, runs `present set <deck> 1 <box> y=905`. The change lands, and `present versions` shows it as si:intern's.

requirements.section: Silicons > Everything the web editor can do
requirements.requirement: Through the CLI, a Silicon can see other people's changes to a deck as they happen.
requirements.quote: The `present` CLI is how Silicons use Silicon Present, and it can do everything the web editor can.
requirements.acceptance: si:designer runs `present watch <deck> --json`. When c:ada edits slide 2 in the web editor, a line appears within about a second naming c:ada as author, with slide 2 in `touched`. When c:ben comments, a comments line appears.

requirements.section: Silicons > Everything the web editor can do
requirements.requirement: Through the CLI, a Silicon can see who is in a deck and which slide each person is on.
requirements.quote: The `present` CLI is how Silicons use Silicon Present, and it can do everything the web editor can.
requirements.acceptance: While `present watch <deck> --json` runs, c:ada opens slide 3 in the web editor, and a presence line names c:ada on slide 3. When she leaves, a presence_left line appears.

requirements.section: Silicons > Everything the web editor can do
requirements.requirement: A Silicon working in a deck through the CLI shows up in the deck the same way a Carbon does, with its name, pfp and the slide it is on.
requirements.quote: The `present` CLI is how Silicons use Silicon Present, and it can do everything the web editor can.
requirements.acceptance: si:designer runs `present watch <deck> --here 3`. c:ada's editor shows si:designer in the deck with its name and pfp on slide 3, the same way it shows a Carbon.

requirements.requirement: The web editor's public address is present.teamofsilicons.com.
requirements.quote: The web editor at `present.teamofsilicons.com`
requirements.acceptance: Against the deployed stack, a signed-out browser opens https://present.teamofsilicons.com/ and gets HTTP 200 with the Silicon Present landing page on that same host, with no redirect to another host. The production web's PUBLIC_URL is https://present.teamofsilicons.com. c:ada signs in from there and lands on https://present.teamofsilicons.com/decks showing her decks, and https://present.teamofsilicons.com/decks/<id> opens one of them in the editor.

requirements.requirement: Every link Silicon Present hands out to open a deck or follow a presentation points at the web editor's address (present.teamofsilicons.com in production), never at the service, the converter or any other host.
requirements.quote: The web editor at `present.teamofsilicons.com`
requirements.acceptance: Local e2e lane (web PUBLIC_URL http://localhost:4320, service 4321, converter 4322, Ting stand-in 4323). si:designer runs `present start <deck>`: both the printed follow link and `followUrl` from POST /v1/decks/{id}/presentations start with http://localhost:4320/p/. c:bob comments on c:ada's deck: the Ting stand-in records a `present.comment.created` whose deck link starts with http://localhost:4320/decks/<id>. After `present public <deck> view`, the link c:ada copies from the web share dialog starts with http://localhost:4320/decks/. No link contains :4321 or :4322. Against the deployed stack, the same links start with https://present.teamofsilicons.com/.

requirements.requirement: Every control on every page of the website that Silicon UI has a component for is that Silicon UI component, whoever is looking (editor, commenter, viewer, or signed-out visitor of a public deck).
requirements.quote: is built entirely with Silicon UI
requirements.acceptance: Static check over web/app and web/components outside the Silicon UI component folder: no raw <button>, <input>, <select>, <textarea> or <dialog>, and no direct @radix-ui/* import, builds a control that https://ui.teamofsilicons.com/r/registry.json provides. Exempt: slide content, and canvas-only parts with no Silicon UI counterpart such as selection handles and guides. Then Playwright, as c:ada (editor), c:bob (commenter), c:cy (viewer) and a signed-out visitor of a public deck, walks /, /sign-in, /decks, /trash, /transfers, /decks/<id>, /decks/<id>/present, /decks/<id>/presenter, /decks/<id>/history, /p/<presentation> and a not-found page. It opens every dialog and menu: new deck, open a file, share, export, transfer, comment box, threads list, name a version. Each control must be the Silicon UI one and match it in look and behaviour, e.g. presence -> avatar/avatar-group, comment box and threads -> mention-input/comment-thread, colour choices -> color-picker, right-click -> context-menu, opening a file -> file-dropzone/file-upload.

requirements.requirement: The website uses no UI component library or design system other than Silicon UI.
requirements.quote: is built entirely with Silicon UI
requirements.acceptance: A reviewer checks web/package.json, pnpm-lock.yaml and the built client bundle. There is no other component library or design system (MUI, Chakra, Ant Design, Mantine, Bootstrap, Bulma, Semantic UI, a stock shadcn theme or similar), and no page loads another design system's stylesheet. Every remaining UI dependency (e.g. @radix-ui/*, lucide-react) appears in the `dependencies` of a Silicon UI item the site installs (https://ui.teamofsilicons.com/r/<name>.json). A library used only as an engine (e.g. quill for rich text) shows none of its own themes, toolbars or CSS on any page (no quill snow/bubble styles); the controls around it are Silicon UI.

requirements.requirement: The Silicon UI components the website uses are installed from Silicon UI's own registry at ui.teamofsilicons.com.
requirements.quote: built entirely with Silicon UI (`ui.teamofsilicons.com`)
requirements.acceptance: A reviewer checks web/components.json: the registry the components are added from is https://ui.teamofsilicons.com/r/{name}.json, and no other registry host is configured. Every component in the website's Silicon UI set has an item of the same name in https://ui.teamofsilicons.com/r/registry.json. At the time of writing, web/components.json registers only @uiarc -> https://uiarc.dev/r/{name}.json, which fails this check.

requirements.requirement: Silicon UI components are used as Silicon UI publishes them, not restyled into a different look.
requirements.quote: Silicon UI (`ui.teamofsilicons.com`), our design system for every Silicon website
requirements.acceptance: For every Silicon UI component in the website, a reviewer fetches https://ui.teamofsilicons.com/r/<name>.json and diffs its files against the site's copy. Apart from import-path rewrites, nothing changes in class names, CSS, tokens, sizes or variants. Playwright then compares a button, text field, dropdown menu and dialog on /decks with the same components on ui.teamofsilicons.com and finds the same computed font, colours, radius, height and shadow.

requirements.requirement: The website's colours, type, radii, shadows and motion come from Silicon UI's foundation tokens, with no palette, typeface or values of its own.
requirements.quote: our design system for every Silicon website
requirements.acceptance: A scan of the website's own CSS (web/styles and every *.module.css) and inline style props covers the site's own chrome only, not slide content or the deck-font lists. Every colour, font family, radius, shadow and duration/easing must be written as a token defined by https://ui.teamofsilicons.com/r/silicon-foundation.json or silicon-motion-tokens (var(--background), var(--foreground), var(--primary), var(--radius-control), var(--shadow-floating), var(--font-body) and so on). There are no hard-coded hex/rgb/hsl colours and no extra font family. At runtime on /decks and /decks/<id>: the computed body background equals silicon-foundation's light --background, body text equals --foreground, the primary button's fill equals --primary, and text uses --font-body or --font-display.

requirements.section: Carbon's standing instruction for this build (not in UNDERSTANDING.md): light mode only
requirements.requirement: Every page of the website shows its light look even when the viewer's device or browser prefers dark; for now there is no dark look.
requirements.quote: light mode only for now
requirements.acceptance: Playwright opens /, /sign-in, /decks, /trash, /transfers, /decks/<id> (as editor, as commenter and as a signed-out visitor of a public deck), /decks/<id>/present, /decks/<id>/presenter, /decks/<id>/history, /p/<presentation> and a not-found page. It opens each once with colorScheme 'light' and once with 'dark'. In both runs: <html> keeps data-theme='light' (never 'dark'), computed color-scheme is 'light', and body background equals silicon-foundation's light --background. Full-page screenshots of the two runs are identical, native fields and scrollbars included (animations disabled; cursors, presence and timestamps masked).

requirements.section: Carbon's standing instruction for this build (not in UNDERSTANDING.md): light mode only
requirements.requirement: The website has no theme, appearance or dark-mode switch anywhere.
requirements.quote: light mode only for now
requirements.acceptance: c:ada walks every page, the account menu, the command palette, every settings surface and the keyboard-shortcut list. No control labelled theme, appearance, dark, light or system exists. None of Silicon UI's theme-switch components (theme-switch, theme-switch-eclipse, theme-switch-split, theme-switch-rise) is imported anywhere in web/ or rendered. With localStorage 'present.theme' set to 'dark' (a stale saved choice), reloading /decks and /decks/<id> still shows the light look.

requirements.section: Carbon's standing instruction for this build (not in UNDERSTANDING.md): light mode only
requirements.requirement: Slides shown on the website look the same whatever the viewer's dark preference; only the deck's own theme decides a slide's colours.
requirements.quote: light mode only for now
requirements.acceptance: si:designer builds a deck with text, a shape, a table, a chart and an HTML element with static content (`present add text|shape|table|chart|html ...`). It also makes a copy with a dark theme (`present theme <copy> Paper --color background=#111111 --color text=#FFFFFF`). Playwright screenshots the slide canvas of both decks in the editor, present mode and the signed-out public view, once with colorScheme 'dark' and once with 'light'. Each pair is pixel-identical. The first deck's slides stay light and the dark-theme copy's slides stay dark in both runs.

critic.problem: The check uses an HTML element with static content only, so it can't catch slide content that follows the viewer's dark preference. An HTML element with @media (prefers-color-scheme: dark) would look different to a Carbon whose device is set to dark, to a follower in light mode, and in `present render`.
critic.fix: Add an HTML element whose CSS changes colours under prefers-color-scheme: dark. Require it to look the same, showing its light styling, with colorScheme 'dark' and with 'light', in the editor, present mode, the follow page and the public view, and to match `present render`.

requirements.section: Carbon's standing instruction for this build (not in UNDERSTANDING.md): minimal
requirements.requirement: The website's own interface has nothing purely decorative: no illustrations, ornamental images, decorative gradients or washes, background patterns or decorative motion.
requirements.quote: the website is minimal
requirements.acceptance: A reviewer audits full-page screenshots at 1440x900 and 390x844 of /, /decks, /trash, /transfers, the editor with the comment box and threads list open, history, present, presenter, /p/<presentation> and a not-found page. Checked against that list (slide content excluded), none is found. A scan of web/ finds no CSS gradient, background pattern image or looping decorative @keyframes in the website's own styles. No Silicon UI decorative-motion component (e.g. text-shimmer, text-reveal, text-morph, in-view-title, slot-text) is in use.

requirements.section: Carbon's standing instruction for this build (not in UNDERSTANDING.md): minimal
requirements.requirement: The website uses few boxes: page content sits directly on the page, never in a box inside another box.
requirements.quote: the website is minimal
requirements.acceptance: On every page listed in MIN-01, at 1440x900 and 390x844, a Playwright DOM check looks for layout containers with a visible border, a shadow, or a fill different from their parent's background. None of them contains another such container. Exempt: form fields, floating menus, popovers, dialogs, toasts, the slide canvas and slide thumbnails. A reviewer confirms the decks list, trash, transfers, threads list and history read as rows on the page, not as boxed panels.

requirements.section: Carbon's standing instruction for this build (not in UNDERSTANDING.md): minimal
requirements.requirement: The website's copy is minimal: each page carries only the words it needs, and the signed-out landing page is a short statement of what Silicon Present is with a way to sign in, not a long marketing page.
requirements.quote: the website is minimal
requirements.acceptance: A signed-out visit to / at 1440x900 and 390x844 shows a headline, a short lede, a sign-in action and at most a brief list of what Present does. It shows none of: testimonials, logo walls, pricing or plan tables, stats counters, FAQs, newsletter sign-up, announcement bars, or repeated calls to action. None of Silicon UI's logo-marquee, announcement-bar, animated-counter, plan-comparison or billing-toggle is in use. On /decks, /trash, /transfers, the editor and history, a reviewer finds no text beyond titles, labels, short empty states and errors.

requirements.requirement: The only kind of document in Silicon Present is a deck of slides: creating, copying or opening anything always produces a deck of slides.
requirements.quote: Silicon Present is just normal slides.
requirements.acceptance: si:designer runs `present new 'Blank'`, `present new 'Copy' --from <deck>@<version>`, `present open page.html` (an ordinary web page that links to other pages) and `present open clip.mp4`. Each returns a deck id, and `present read <id> --json` shows deck JSON with a `slides` array. The web page arrives as one slide holding one full-slide HTML element; the video arrives as one slide holding a video element. c:ada finds that every create or open-a-file action in the web leads to /decks/<id> showing slides. POST /v1/docs, /v1/sites and /v1/pages return 404.

critic.problem: Overstated: it requires an opened web page to become exactly one slide holding one full-slide HTML element, and an opened video to become exactly one slide. The text only says Silicon Present is 'just normal slides' and that opening a file creates a new deck.
critic.fix: Check only that every create, copy and open produces a deck of slides (deck JSON with a slides array, opening at /decks/<id>) and that no other kind of document exists. Leave how a page or video is laid out to FMT-06, FMT-12 and FMT-40.

requirements.requirement: Silicon Present has no docs editor: there is no document type and no document-style editing where text flows from page to page; writing in a deck happens inside elements on slides and in speaker notes.
requirements.quote: It is not a docs editor
requirements.acceptance: c:ada finds no way in the web to create or switch to a document: no 'new document' option, and no page-flow writing view with page breaks, footnotes or a table of contents. `present --help` and `present docs` list no document commands. c:ada types on a slide in the web, and si:designer runs `present add text`, `present replace --field notes`, and `present set` on a table cell. `present read <deck> --json` then shows every piece of that text under an element's `text`, a table's `cells` or a slide's `notes`, and nowhere else.

requirements.requirement: Silicon Present has no website builder: a deck can't be turned into, configured as or hosted as a website.
requirements.quote: a website builder
requirements.acceptance: c:ada opens every deck menu, the share dialog and the deck settings in the web. She finds no custom domain, vanity URL or slug, SEO/meta settings, site navigation menu, page or route management, forms, or hosting option. The deck is reachable only at its own /decks/<id> link on the web editor's address (and at /p/<presentation> while it is presented). `present --help` lists no site, domain or hosting command. `present export <deck> --format pdf` and every web download return a file (Content-Disposition: attachment), not a hosted address.

requirements.requirement: Silicon Present has no video editor: a video is only placed and played as an element on a slide, with no tools to edit the video itself.
requirements.quote: a video editor
requirements.acceptance: c:ada adds a video to a slide in the web, and si:designer adds one with `present add video <deck> <slide> clip.mp4`. The element gets the normal element tools (place, resize, rotate, layer, group, align, lock, animate) and playback settings, and nothing else. There is no timeline, no cutting or joining of clips, no video effects or filters, and no composing a new video from clips. `present --help` lists no command that edits a video's content.

requirements.requirement: Silicon Present has no publishing: there is no publish action or destination for decks, and beyond invites the only way to open a deck to others is the public switch, which just makes it reachable by its link.
requirements.quote: a place to publish or list decks
requirements.acceptance: c:ada opens every editor menu, the share dialog and the /decks row menu: no 'Publish', 'Publish to the web', 'Post' or 'Submit to gallery' action exists. The share dialog offers only invites (c:id, si:id or email, with a role) and the public switch (off, view, comment, edit). Turning the switch on gives the deck's own link and nothing else. si:designer's `present publish <deck>` fails as an unknown command, and `present --help` lists no publish command. POST /v1/decks/{id}/publish returns 404.

requirements.requirement: Silicon Present has no place that lists decks for others to discover: no gallery, explore, featured or popular page, no public profile listing someone's decks, and no 'more decks' suggestions on a deck.
requirements.quote: a place to publish or list decks
requirements.acceptance: c:ada owns a public deck (`present public <deck> view`) and is presenting it. A signed-out visitor and c:bob (no access to anything of ada's) follow every link from /, /decks, ada's public deck page and /p/<presentation>. No page shows any of ada's decks except the one opened by its link. The public deck page shows no 'more from c:ada', related or recommended decks. Clicking ada's c:id or pfp opens no page listing her decks. On the web, GET /explore, /gallery and /discover return 404. GET /v1/decks?scope=public returns a validation error with no decks. `present --help` lists no browse or explore command.

requirements.requirement: Making a deck public never puts it in anyone else's deck lists or search results; it stays reachable only by its link.
requirements.quote: a place to publish or list decks
requirements.acceptance: c:ada makes a deck titled 'zebracorn 7f3', with that word on a slide, and runs `present public <deck> view`; the test then repeats with comment and edit. c:bob has never been invited and has never opened the link. He runs `present list`, `present list --shared` and `present search zebracorn`, calls GET /v1/decks?scope=mine, GET /v1/decks?scope=shared and GET /v1/search?q=zebracorn, and checks the web /decks (his own and shared with him) and its search. In every mode, the deck appears in none of them. Unauthenticated GET /v1/decks and GET /v1/search?q=zebracorn return 401 with no decks. bob opening the deck's link still shows the deck.

requirements.requirement: Public decks and follow-along pages aren't offered to search or answer engines: their pages ask not to be indexed, and no sitemap, robots.txt or llms.txt names a deck or presentation.
requirements.quote: a place to publish or list decks
requirements.acceptance: Signed-out fetches of a public deck's /decks/<id> and of a live /p/<presentation> return HTML carrying <meta name='robots' content='noindex...'> or an X-Robots-Tag: noindex header. GET /sitemap.xml lists no /decks/ or /p/ URL. GET /llms.txt and GET /robots.txt name no deck or presentation. The landing page may stay indexable.

requirements.requirement: There are no teams, workspaces or organizations in Silicon Present: none can be created, joined, switched to or managed, in the web, the CLI or the API.
requirements.quote: There are no Teams.
requirements.acceptance: c:ada walks every web page and menu (header, account menu, /decks, share dialog, /transfers). No team, workspace or organization switcher, creation, membership or settings appears. No string a Carbon or Silicon reads offers a team, workspace or organization as a place decks live, an owner, or a group to join; the Team of Silicons name and domain are the only exception. `present --help` and every subcommand's --help show no team, org or workspace command or flag; `present teams` and `present list --team x` fail as unknown. GET /v1/teams, /v1/orgs and /v1/workspaces return 404.

requirements.requirement: No deck or folder is ever owned by, or transferable to, a team: its owner and any transfer target is always exactly one Carbon or Silicon.
requirements.quote: There are no Teams.
requirements.acceptance: c:ada runs `present transfer <deck> team:design` and `present transfer <folder> team:design --folder`, and POSTs a body with to set to team:design to /v1/decks/{id}/transfer and /v1/folders/{id}/transfer. Each is refused with a 4xx whose hint says only a c:id or si:id can receive it. GET /v1/decks/{id}, `present read <deck> --json` and the web each show owner and creator as a single c:id or si:id with name and pfp. That includes a deck c:bob created inside ada's shared folder (owner c:ada, creator c:bob).

requirements.requirement: Invites only reach individual Carbons and Silicons (by c:id, si:id or email); a deck or folder can't be shared with a team, group, organization or email domain.
requirements.quote: There are no Teams.
requirements.acceptance: c:ada runs `present share <deck> team:design --role viewer`, `present share <deck> @example.com --role viewer` and `present share <folder> example.com --role viewer --folder`. She also POSTs the same `to` values to /v1/decks/{id}/access and /v1/folders/{id}/access. Each is refused with a 4xx naming the accepted forms: c:id, si:id or an email address. The web share dialog's invite field accepts only a c:id, si:id or email and offers no group, team or domain option. GET /v1/decks/{id}/access lists only accounts and pending emails.

requirements.requirement: The public switch has no team-, organization- or domain-restricted option: a public deck is open to anyone with its link.
requirements.quote: There are no Teams.
requirements.acceptance: c:ada sends PUT /v1/decks/{id}/public with mode 'team', 'org' and 'domain'. Each returns a 400 validation error listing off, view, comment and edit. `present public <deck> team` is refused with the same choices. The web share dialog's public switch offers only those modes, each worded for anyone with the link.

requirements.section: Intro paragraphs, Glossary, and Sign in
requirements.requirement: Opening a deck link, a comment link from a ting or a follow link while signed out goes through Silicon Accounts sign-in and then back to that same page, not to the deck list.
requirements.quote: Signing in and signing up are handled entirely by Silicon Accounts.
requirements.acceptance: c:ada shares a private deck with c:bea as commenter, starts a follow link and mentions c:bea, so the Ting stand-in records a thread link. A browser with no session opens /decks/<id>, the ting's thread link and /p/<presentation>. Each one goes to the Silicon Accounts hosted sign-in. After c:bea signs in, the browser lands on the address it started from: the deck opens (with that thread open, for the ting link) and the follow page shows the current slide. It never lands on /decks.

requirements.requirement: If a Carbon's Silicon Accounts session runs out while they edit, nothing is lost. The editor keeps saving through a token refresh. If they have to sign in again, the changes they made in the meantime still reach the deck afterwards.
requirements.quote: If a connection drops, nothing is lost. Changes made meanwhile merge back in once it returns.
requirements.acceptance: c:ada edits /decks/<id> while the test makes her access token expire (short token lifetime on the Accounts test stack). She types 'After expiry', and within 5 s it is in GET /v1/decks/<id>/content with no sign-in prompt. Then her session is revoked at Silicon Accounts. She types 'Before sign-in', is asked to sign in, signs in through Silicon Accounts and lands back in the deck. Both texts are in the deck JSON and in c:bea's open editor.

requirements.requirement: A folder made inside someone else's shared folder belongs to that folder's owner and still shows who made it, the same as a deck made there. The text says this only for decks, so a Carbon should confirm the folder case.
requirements.quote: A deck created inside someone else's shared folder belongs to that folder's owner, and still shows who created it.
requirements.acceptance: c:ada shares folder F with si:designer as editor and with si:writer as viewer. si:designer runs `present folder new 'Drafts' --parent F --json`. GET /v1/folders/<new> shows owner c:ada and creator si:designer. c:ada sees the folder inside F on /decks?folder=F, marked as made by si:designer. The folder is not in si:designer's own `present folder list`, but si:designer can still reach it through F. The same command run by si:writer is refused.

requirements.requirement: Permanently deleting a trashed folder also permanently deletes everything that went to the trash with it, and nothing else.
requirements.quote: It stays there until the owner permanently deletes it, which asks them to confirm first. That is the only way anything in Silicon Present is ever truly gone.
requirements.acceptance: si:designer's folder F holds deck D (shared with c:ada) and folder G, which holds deck H (public). Deck K was moved out of F earlier. si:designer runs `present folder trash F`, then `present folder delete F --confirm '<F's name>'`. GET /v1/decks/D, /v1/folders/G and /v1/decks/H return 404 for si:designer, for c:ada and with no token. `present untrash D` fails with not found. H's public link no longer opens. K is unchanged and still in `present list`.

requirements.requirement: Permanently deleting a deck removes all of it, not just its entry in the list: its assets, threads, older versions and running presentations can no longer be reached.
requirements.quote: That is the only way anything in Silicon Present is ever truly gone.
requirements.acceptance:
Public deck D has an uploaded image, two threads, several versions and a running presentation that someone follows at /p/

. Its owner trashes D and runs `present delete D --permanent --confirm ''`. With the owner's token and with no token, all of these return 404: GET /v1/assets/<image id>, GET /v1/decks/D/threads, GET /v1/decks/D/versions, GET /v1/decks/D/content?version=1 and GET /v1/presentations/<p>. The open follow page says the presentation is gone.

requirements.requirement: In the web editor, a Carbon can copy, cut, paste and duplicate elements, on the same slide or onto another slide. Copies keep their look and get new ids.
requirements.quote: It has everything people expect from Google Slides or PowerPoint.
requirements.acceptance: In /decks/<id>, c:ada selects a shape and a text box on slide 1, presses Cmd/Ctrl+C, opens slide 3 and presses Cmd/Ctrl+V. Both appear on slide 3 with the same position, style and text, and with new ids (`present read <deck> --json`). Cmd/Ctrl+X on slide 3 removes them, and Cmd/Ctrl+V on slide 2 puts them there. Cmd/Ctrl+D on a selected image adds a copy next to it.

requirements.requirement: A slide can be duplicated, or copied and pasted elsewhere in the deck, with all its elements, notes and settings. A Silicon can duplicate a slide through the CLI.
requirements.quote: It has everything people expect from Google Slides or PowerPoint.
requirements.acceptance: c:ada duplicates slide 2 from the slide list. A copy appears right after it with every element, the notes, background, transition and animations, all with new ids. She copies slide 4 and pastes it after slide 6, with the same result. si:designer runs `present slide duplicate <deck> 3`, and `present read <deck> --json` shows an identical slide right after slide 3, with new slide and element ids.

requirements.requirement: Elements and slides can be pasted into another deck. Their images, video, audio and fonts keep working there for everyone who can see that deck.
requirements.quote: It has everything people expect from Google Slides or PowerPoint.
requirements.acceptance: c:ada copies a slide holding an uploaded image and a video from her private deck A. She pastes it into deck B and shares B with c:bea, who has no access to A. In B, c:bea sees the image and can play the video. GET /v1/assets/<id> for B's elements returns 200 for c:bea, and `present render B <n>` shows the picture. After c:ada permanently deletes A, the image and video in B still work.

requirements.requirement: An image can be put on a slide by pasting it from the clipboard (for example a screenshot) or by dropping an image file onto the slide.
requirements.quote: Any image, video, audio, font, SVG or animation can be added to a slide.
requirements.acceptance: With slide 2 of /decks/<id> focused, Playwright puts a PNG on the clipboard and presses Cmd/Ctrl+V. An image element with src asset:<id> appears on slide 2 and shows that picture. Dropping photo.jpg from the file system onto slide 3 adds an image element there in the same way.

requirements.requirement: A slide's background can be set to a colour or an image, or reset to the theme's, both in the web and through the CLI. It shows everywhere the slide is drawn.
requirements.quote: It has everything people expect from Google Slides or PowerPoint.
requirements.acceptance: c:ada sets slide 2's background to #111214 in /decks/<id>. si:designer runs `present slide background <deck> 3 cover.jpg --fit cover` and `present slide background <deck> 4 none`. `present read <deck> --json` shows each change. The editor, present mode, `present render` and the PDF download all show slide 2 dark, slide 3 filled with the picture and slide 4 with the theme background.

requirements.requirement: A Carbon can crop an image on the slide and reset the crop. The original picture is kept whole.
requirements.quote: Carbons edit text, images, shapes, tables, charts and videos directly on the slide, just like in Google Slides or PowerPoint.
requirements.acceptance: In /decks/<id>, c:ada crops an image to its left half (Crop, then drag the handles). The editor, present mode, `present render` and the .pptx download (as a cropped picture) show only the left half. GET /v1/assets/<id> still returns the whole original file. Resetting the crop shows the whole image again.

requirements.requirement: The deck's slide size can be changed (16:9, 4:3 or a custom size), and every slide, render and download follows the new size.
requirements.quote: It has everything people expect from Google Slides or PowerPoint.
requirements.acceptance: c:ada switches a 16:9 deck to 4:3 in /decks/<id>. The canvas, slide list, present mode, `present render <deck> 1` (a 4:3 image) and the PDF download are all 4:3, and every element is still on its slide. si:designer sets the size to 1080 x 1080 through the CLI (`present edit <deck> --ops` with update_deck size), with the same result.

requirements.requirement: A slide can hide the master's elements, like PowerPoint's 'Hide background graphics', and show them again, both in the web and through the CLI. Other items already assume this exists (EDIT-10, EDIT-13, SIL-103).
requirements.quote: themes and masters
requirements.acceptance: The master holds a footer. c:ada hides the master on slide 1 in /decks/<id>. The footer disappears from slide 1 in the editor, present mode, `present render` and the PDF, and stays on the other slides. si:designer runs `present slide master <deck> 2 --hide`, then `present slide master <deck> 2`. `present read <deck> --json` shows hideMaster true and then false, and the footer disappears and then comes back.

requirements.requirement: A layout can be edited on the master. Moving its placeholders or changing their text style changes every slide that uses that layout.
requirements.quote: layouts, themes and masters
requirements.acceptance: c:ada opens the master view in /decks/<id>. She moves the title placeholder of the title-body layout 100 px down and sets its text to 60 px. Every title-body slide whose title she hasn't moved by hand follows, new title-body slides use the new placement, and slides with other layouts don't change (checked in the editor, present mode and `present render`). si:designer can make the same change through the CLI, and `present read` shows it.

requirements.requirement: In the web editor, a Carbon can change the theme's colours and fonts, and every slide that uses them changes at once.
requirements.quote: themes and masters
requirements.acceptance: In /decks/<id>, c:ada sets the theme's accent colour to #b4532a and its heading font to Fraunces. Every slide's themed accents and headings change at once in the editor and in present mode. `present read <deck> --json` shows theme.colors.accent and theme.fonts.heading. An element with its own explicit colour keeps that colour.

requirements.requirement: An animation can start on click, with the previous animation or after the previous animation, and the order of a slide's animations can be changed. Present mode plays them that way. SLD-86 only tests on-click animations.
requirements.quote: element animations
requirements.acceptance: On slide 2, c:ada sets A to fade on click, B to fly in with the previous and C to appear after the previous, then moves C before B in the animation list. In /decks/<id>/present, one advance plays A and B together, then C right after them with no further click, and the next advance goes to slide 3. On slide 4, si:designer sets the same triggers with `present set <deck> 4 <element> 'animation=...'`, and present mode plays them the same way. `present read <deck> --json` shows the triggers and the order.

requirements.requirement: Elements can have exit animations, such as fade out or fly out, as well as entrance animations.
requirements.quote: element animations
requirements.acceptance: In /decks/<id>, c:ada gives a shape on slide 2 a fade-out exit on click. In present mode the shape is visible when slide 2 opens and disappears on the first advance. si:designer gives another element an exit animation through the CLI, with the same result. The .pptx download keeps it as an exit effect.

requirements.requirement: A Carbon can add their own guides to a slide, and elements snap to them. Guides never show when presenting or in downloads. SLD-95 and SLD-96 only cover automatic alignment guides.
requirements.quote: guides and snapping
requirements.acceptance: In /decks/<id>, c:ada adds a vertical guide at x=480 (for example from the ruler or the View menu). She drops a shape with its left edge 4 px from the guide, and `present read <deck> --json` shows x=480. The guide is still there after a reload. It doesn't appear in present mode, in `present render` or in the PDF download.

requirements.requirement: A Carbon can style table cells: their fill, their borders and the formatting of the text inside them.
requirements.quote: Carbons edit text, images, shapes, tables, charts and videos directly on the slide, just like in Google Slides or PowerPoint.
requirements.acceptance: In /decks/<id>, c:ada selects a table's header row, sets its fill to #2f5bea and its text to bold white, and sets the table's borders to 2 px #111111. The editor, present mode, `present render` and the .pptx download show this. `present read <deck> --json` shows the fills and the bold white runs on those cells only.

requirements.requirement: Table cells can be merged and unmerged.
requirements.quote: Carbons edit text, images, shapes, tables, charts and videos directly on the slide, just like in Google Slides or PowerPoint.
requirements.acceptance: In /decks/<id>, c:ada merges cells (0,0) and (0,1). In the editor, present mode and `present render`, one cell spans both columns and keeps the text, and the .pptx download has the merge (gridSpan). Unmerging gives two cells again. si:designer merges two cells of another table through the CLI, with the same result.

requirements.requirement: A table's column widths and row heights can be changed by dragging the lines between them.
requirements.quote: Carbons edit text, images, shapes, tables, charts and videos directly on the slide, just like in Google Slides or PowerPoint.
requirements.acceptance: In /decks/<id>, c:ada drags the line between columns 0 and 1 of a 3-column table 100 px to the right. `present read <deck> --json` shows column 0 wider and column 1 narrower by 100 slide px, with the table's width unchanged, and `present render` shows the same. Dragging a row line changes rowHeights in the same way.

requirements.requirement: Selected text can be struck through, highlighted in a colour, or set as superscript or subscript.
requirements.quote: Carbons edit text, images, shapes, tables, charts and videos directly on the slide, just like in Google Slides or PowerPoint.
requirements.acceptance: In /decks/<id>, c:ada strikes through one word, highlights another in yellow, sets the 2 in 'm2' as superscript and sets the 2 in 'H2O' as subscript. The editor, present mode, `present render` and the .pptx download show each one. `present read <deck> --json` shows those attributes on those runs only.

requirements.requirement: Line spacing and indentation can be set on paragraphs, and list items can be nested by indenting them.
requirements.quote: Carbons edit text, images, shapes, tables, charts and videos directly on the slide, just like in Google Slides or PowerPoint.
requirements.acceptance: In /decks/<id>, c:ada sets 1.5 line spacing on a paragraph and presses Tab on the second bullet of a list (Shift+Tab takes it back). The editor and `present render` show the spacing and the nested bullet. `present read <deck> --json` shows lineHeight 1.5 and indent 1 on those paragraphs.

requirements.requirement: An element can be flipped horizontally or vertically.
requirements.quote: It has everything people expect from Google Slides or PowerPoint.
requirements.acceptance: In /decks/<id>, c:ada flips an arrow shape and an image horizontally and flips another shape vertically. The editor, present mode, `present render` and the .pptx download show them mirrored, and `present read <deck> --json` records each flip. si:designer flips an element through the CLI, with the same result.

requirements.requirement: Three or more selected elements can be spaced evenly, horizontally or vertically.
requirements.quote: Every element can be placed, resized, rotated, layered, grouped, aligned, locked and animated, whoever made it.
requirements.acceptance: Three shapes, each 100 px wide, sit at x=100, 300 and 900 on a slide in /decks/<id>. c:ada selects them and picks Distribute horizontally. `present read <deck> --json` shows the two outer shapes unchanged and the middle one at x=500.

requirements.requirement: In the web editor, a Carbon can set and change the alt text of images and videos. SLD-32 and SLD-40 cover the CLI only.
requirements.quote: Carbons edit text, images, shapes, tables, charts and videos directly on the slide, just like in Google Slides or PowerPoint.
requirements.acceptance: In /decks/<id>, c:ada sets alt text 'Team photo' on an image and 'Product demo' on a video. `present read <deck> --json` shows both. The .pptx download carries 'Team photo' as the picture's description, and in the .html download the image has alt 'Team photo'.

requirements.requirement: The editor's canvas can be zoomed in and out and fitted to the window, without changing the deck.
requirements.quote: It has everything people expect from Google Slides or PowerPoint.
requirements.acceptance: c:ada zooms /decks/<id> to 200%. The slide is drawn twice as large and can be scrolled, and dragging an element 100 screen px moves it 50 slide px. Fit shows the whole slide again. GET /v1/decks/<id> shows the same version before and after zooming.

requirements.requirement: Slide numbers can be shown on slides. Each slide shows its own number, and the numbers update when slides are added, removed or moved.
requirements.quote: It has everything people expect from Google Slides or PowerPoint.
requirements.acceptance: c:ada turns on slide numbers in /decks/<id> (for example a slide-number field on the master). Each slide shows its own number in the editor, present mode, `present render` and the PDF. After `present slide move <deck> 5 --first`, the moved slide shows 1 and the other slides renumber. The .pptx download uses PowerPoint's slide-number field. si:designer can turn slide numbers on through the CLI.

requirements.requirement: A Carbon can draw lines and arrows and set their colour, weight, dash style and arrowheads.
requirements.quote: Carbons edit text, images, shapes, tables, charts and videos directly on the slide, just like in Google Slides or PowerPoint.
requirements.acceptance: In /decks/<id>, c:ada draws a line from (200,200) to (800,500), adds an arrowhead at its end, and makes it 4 px, dashed and #e5484d. The editor, present mode, `present render` and the .pptx download (a line with an arrowhead) show it. When she drags the end to (900,500), the start point stays where it was. si:designer draws the same arrow through the CLI.

requirements.requirement: Elements can be made partly transparent and given a drop shadow.
requirements.quote: It has everything people expect from Google Slides or PowerPoint.
requirements.acceptance: In /decks/<id>, c:ada sets an image to 50% transparency and gives a shape a drop shadow. The editor, present mode and `present render` show the image see-through over what's behind it, and show the shadow. `present read <deck> --json` shows both settings. si:designer sets both on other elements with `present set`, with the same result.

requirements.requirement: Someone who can edit a deck can make a copy of it as it is now. The copy is a new deck of their own. VER-35 only covers older versions.
requirements.quote: It has everything people expect from Google Slides or PowerPoint.
requirements.acceptance: c:ada uses Make a copy in /decks/<id>, and si:designer (an editor) runs `present new 'Copy' --from <deck>` with no version. Each new deck matches `present read <deck> --json` at that moment and is owned by whoever made it. The original's content and versions don't change. Not settled: whether a Viewer may make a copy, as Google Slides allows.

requirements.requirement: An empty layout placeholder shows its prompt (such as 'Click to add title') only while editing. The prompt never appears when presenting, following, rendering or downloading.
requirements.quote: layouts
requirements.acceptance: c:ada adds a title-body slide and types only a title. In /decks/<id> the empty body shows its prompt. In /decks/<id>/present, /p/<presentation>, `present render <deck> <n>` and the PDF and PNG downloads, the body area is empty. `present read <deck>` doesn't list the prompt as text.

requirements.requirement: Text in any script stays intact when it is typed, read, replaced, rendered and downloaded. This includes emoji, Chinese and Japanese, and right-to-left Arabic and Hebrew.
requirements.quote: It has everything people expect from Google Slides or PowerPoint.
requirements.acceptance: c:ada types 'Hello 👋🏽 世界 مرحبا שלום' into a text box in /decks/<id>. si:designer's `present read <deck>` shows it exactly. `present replace <deck> 1 <element> --find '👋🏽' --replace '🎉'` changes only the emoji. The editor, present mode, `present render` and the PDF and .pptx downloads show every character in order, with Arabic and Hebrew right to left and no boxes or question marks.

requirements.requirement: Arrow keys move the selected elements by a small step, and by a bigger step with Shift held.
requirements.quote: Every element can be placed, resized, rotated, layered, grouped, aligned, locked and animated, whoever made it.
requirements.acceptance: In /decks/<id>, c:ada selects a shape at x=500, y=300 and presses → twice and Shift+↓ once. `present read <deck> --json` shows x moved by two small steps and y by one big step (for example 1 px and 10 px), and nothing else changed.

requirements.requirement: Changes made to a deck while it is being presented show up as they happen in present mode, in the presenter view and on every follow page, without moving the presentation.
requirements.quote: Everyone edits the same deck at the same time and sees every change as it happens.
requirements.acceptance:
c:ada presents slide 2 at /decks//present, with the presenter view open and a follow link that c:bob follows at /p/

. si:designer runs `present replace 2 --find Q3 --replace Q4` and `present slide notes 2 'New note'`. Within 2 s and with no reload, the present stage and c:bob's follow page show Q4 on slide 2, and the presenter view shows 'New note'. All of them stay on slide 2 at the same step.

requirements.requirement: A Carbon can start presenting from the slide they are on or from the beginning.
requirements.quote: Any deck can be presented full screen … It has everything people expect from Google Slides or PowerPoint.
requirements.acceptance: With slide 4 selected in /decks/<id>, c:ada picks Present from current slide, and present mode opens on slide 4. Present from beginning opens on the first slide that isn't skipped. si:designer's `present start <deck> --slide 4` starts on slide 4, as `present show status --json` shows.

requirements.requirement: Esc leaves present mode and returns the Carbon to the deck, on the slide they were showing.
requirements.quote: Any deck can be presented full screen … It has everything people expect from Google Slides or PowerPoint.
requirements.acceptance: c:ada is on slide 3 in /decks/<id>/present and presses Esc. Full screen ends and she is back in /decks/<id> with slide 3 showing.

requirements.requirement: An invitee's role can be changed after they are invited, including lowered, and the new role takes effect at once, even on pages they already have open. SHR-12 only covers raising a role by inviting again. The text doesn't say who besides the owner may change roles.
requirements.quote: Everyone invited gets one of three roles
requirements.acceptance: c:ada (the owner) shares deck D with c:bea as editor and with si:designer as viewer. While c:bea has /decks/D open, c:ada changes her to commenter in the share dialog. Within 2 s c:bea can no longer edit (her next POST /v1/decks/D/updates returns 403), but she can still comment. c:ada runs `present share D si:designer --role editor`, and `present add text D 1 'x'` run by si:designer then succeeds. GET /v1/decks/D/access lists each of them once, with the new role. The same works on a folder.

requirements.requirement: Someone's access to a deck or folder can be removed, and a pending email invite can be withdrawn. They lose access everywhere at once, and everything they did stays in the deck under their c:id or si:id. The text doesn't mention removing access, but Google Slides has it, and GLOS-18 and MEN-28 already use `present unshare`. Not settled: who besides the owner may remove others.
requirements.quote: It has everything people expect from Google Slides or PowerPoint.
requirements.acceptance: c:ada shares deck D with c:bea (editor), si:designer (commenter) and the pending address new-<random>@example.test, and shares folder F (which holds deck E) with c:bea as viewer. c:bea has /decks/D open and has edited and commented on it. c:ada removes c:bea from D in the share dialog, runs `present unshare D si:designer`, withdraws the email invite and removes c:bea from F. Within a few seconds c:bea's open editor shows she no longer has access and receives no further updates. D and E leave her Shared with me, and GET /v1/decks/D/content and /v1/decks/E/content return 403 or 404 for her token. `present read D` fails for si:designer. Signing up with the withdrawn email gives no access. c:bea's earlier changes and comments are still in D's history and threads, attributed to c:bea.

requirements.requirement: Only the owner chooses whether people with the link can comment or edit. Someone who can edit but isn't the owner can't raise the public level to comment or edit. Not settled: whether a non-owner editor may turn on view-only.
requirements.quote: Anyone with the link can then view it, or, if the owner chooses, comment on it or edit it.
requirements.acceptance: c:ada owns D and shares it with si:designer and c:bea as editors. si:designer runs `present public D comment` and `present public D edit`, and c:bea tries the same in the share dialog (PUT /v1/decks/D/public {mode: 'comment' or 'edit'} with her token). Each attempt is refused with a clear error, and GET /v1/decks/D still shows the public mode c:ada set. c:ada can still set comment and edit herself (SHR-51, SHR-53).

requirements.requirement: Making a deck private again also cuts off people who reached it only through its public link while it was being presented: their present-mode pages, follow pages and CLI follows stop showing it.
requirements.quote: Making it private again stops the link working.
requirements.acceptance:
D is public (view). c:ada presents it with a follow link. One signed-out browser has /p/ open, another has /decks/D/present open, and si:writer, who was never invited, runs `present follow `. c:ada turns the public switch off and moves to the next slide. None of the three receives the move: their streams end or deliver nothing more, and reloading shows no slide. GET /v1/presentations/

with no token returns 401, 403 or 404, and `present follow` exits with a no-access error. c:bea, invited as a viewer, keeps following.

requirements.requirement: A Viewer, or someone viewing a public deck, can read its speaker notes in the web, just as a Silicon Viewer can through the CLI.
requirements.quote: Carbons and Silicons get exactly the same roles and the same rights. … any deck can be read as text: every slide, its elements, their positions, the speaker notes, and the comments next to what they're on.
requirements.acceptance: c:ada writes notes on slide 2, shares the deck with c:cy and si:reader as viewers, and runs `present public <deck> view`. c:cy at /decks/<id>, and a signed-out browser on the link, can each open slide 2's notes and read them but can't change them. si:reader's `present read <deck>` shows the same notes (SIL-015, SIGN-20). A Carbon should confirm that link visitors are meant to see the notes.

requirements.requirement: Anyone a deck is shared with, including a Viewer or Commenter, can download it in every listed format: a Carbon from the web, a Silicon through the CLI. FMT-49 to FMT-56 only test the owner, or a Carbon in the editor with no role given.
requirements.quote: any deck can be downloaded in any of these formats
requirements.acceptance: c:ada shares a 3-slide deck with c:bea as viewer and with si:designer as commenter. c:bea uses Download in /decks/<id> for .pptx, .pdf, .html and .png, and si:designer runs `present export <deck> --format <f>` for all eight formats. Each one succeeds with a valid file of that format holding the 3 slides, passing the same checks as FMT-49 to FMT-56.

requirements.requirement: Someone viewing a public deck without signing in can download it in every listed format. This reads 'any deck can be downloaded' together with 'Viewing a public deck never needs signing in'; a Carbon should confirm it.
requirements.quote: Viewing a public deck never needs signing in.
requirements.acceptance: c:ada runs `present public <deck> view`. A browser with no session at /decks/<id> downloads .pdf and .pptx, and GET /v1/decks/<id>/export?format=... with no token returns 200 with the file. `present export <link> --format png` with no sign-in saved writes the images. After `present public <deck> off`, the same downloads are refused (SHR-66).

requirements.requirement: New comments, replies, reactions, edits, resolves and reopens appear for everyone who has the deck open as they happen, without a reload, both in the web and in `present watch`. SIL-063 only covers a Silicon's new comment appearing for a Carbon.
requirements.quote: Everyone edits the same deck at the same time and sees every change as it happens.
requirements.acceptance: c:ada and c:bea have /decks/<id> open, and si:designer runs `present watch <deck> --json`. c:bea posts a comment on slide 2. Within 2 s it shows in c:ada's thread list and on slide 2, and watch prints a comments event. Then si:designer replies with `present reply`, c:ada reacts with 👍, c:bea edits her comment, si:designer resolves the thread and c:ada reopens it. After each step, the other two see the change within 2 s with no reload, and watch prints a comments event.

requirements.requirement: A Commenter can resolve a thread. A Viewer can neither resolve nor reopen one. The matrix shows only Editors and the owner resolving (CMT-21), and Commenters only reopening (CMT-22).
requirements.quote: `Commenter` - can view and comment. … Comments can be replied to, reacted to, edited and resolved. Resolved threads can be reopened.
requirements.acceptance: On c:ada's deck, c:bea and si:writer are commenters, and c:cy and si:reader are viewers. c:bea resolves c:ada's thread in /decks/<id>, and si:writer runs `present resolve <thread>` on another thread. Both succeed, and GET /v1/decks/<id>/threads?state=resolved shows them resolved by c:bea and by si:writer. c:cy is offered no resolve or reopen control. si:reader's `present resolve <thread>` and `present reopen <thread>` are refused with 403, and the threads stay as they were.

requirements.requirement: A Carbon Viewer sees a deck's comment threads in the web, just as a Silicon Viewer reads them through the CLI (SIL-065), but can't post, reply, react, edit or resolve.
requirements.quote: `Viewer` - can only view. … Carbons and Silicons get exactly the same roles and the same rights. … any deck can be read as text: every slide, its elements, their positions, the speaker notes, and the comments next to what they're on.
requirements.acceptance: c:ada's deck has three threads and is shared with c:cy and si:reader as viewers. c:cy opens /decks/<id> and sees the three threads in the thread list and on their slides. She has no way to post, reply, react, edit or resolve, and the matching API calls with her token return 403. si:reader's `present comments <deck>` shows the same three threads. Google Slides hides comments from viewers; here the Reading bullet and the equal-rights line say Viewers see them. A Carbon should confirm if that is not intended.

requirements.requirement: In the web comment box, typing @ suggests matching Carbons and Silicons, shown by c:id or si:id, and picking one inserts the mention. This follows from effortless commenting and from Google Slides behaviour.
requirements.quote: commenting has to be effortless for Carbons … Anyone can mention a Carbon or Silicon in a comment with their c:id or si:id.
requirements.acceptance: c:ada types '@si:des' in a comment box in /decks/<id>. A list suggests si:designer, shown as si:designer with its pfp. Pressing Enter inserts '@si:designer', and posting sends si:designer a present.mention.received. Typing '@c:be' suggests c:bea in the same way.

requirements.requirement: No ting is lost when Silicon Ting can't be reached. Tings are kept and delivered once Ting is back, each exactly once.
requirements.quote: All notifications go through Silicon Ting; Silicon Present never sends its own. … Everything in Silicon Present is versioned, and nothing is ever lost.
requirements.acceptance: Stop the Ting stand-in. c:ada mentions si:designer, comments on c:bea's deck and shares a deck with si:writer. Restart the service once, then restart the stand-in.
