Within a minute the stand-in records exactly one present.mention.received for si:designer, one present.comment.created for c:bea and one present.deck.shared for si:writer, each with the same content as if Ting had been up. None is recorded twice.

requirements.requirement: A mention keeps pointing at the same Carbon or Silicon after their c:id or si:id changes at Silicon Accounts, and from then on it is shown with the new id.
requirements.quote: Carbons and Silicons are always stored by their Silicon Accounts uuid, and shown by their c:id or si:id.
requirements.acceptance: c:ada comments '@si:designer make this simpler'. si:designer's id is then changed to si:designer2 at Silicon Accounts. Once Present has refreshed the account (by webhook or on the next request): c:ada's thread shows the mention as @si:designer2 and links it to that account. `present comments <deck> --json` shows the same account uuid with id si:designer2, and nothing in the deck points at the old id. A new Silicon that later takes the id si:designer is not treated as mentioned in that comment.

requirements.requirement: A change the service has accepted is never lost, even if the service restarts or crashes right afterwards.
requirements.quote: There is no save button: every change is saved the moment it's made.
requirements.acceptance: c:ada types 'Durable' in /decks/<id> and waits until its POST /v1/decks/<id>/updates returns 2xx. si:designer's `present set <deck> 1 <element> x=321` exits 0, and si:writer posts a comment. The service process is killed at once (SIGKILL) and started again. `present read <deck> --comments`, a freshly opened /decks/<id> and GET /v1/decks/<id>/versions all show 'Durable', x=321 and the comment, attributed as before.

requirements.requirement: Changes that aren't slide content are also kept in the deck's history, with who made them and when: invites, role changes and removals, the public switch, moves between folders, transfers, and trashing and restoring. VER-02 covers renames only.
requirements.quote: Everything in Silicon Present is versioned, and nothing is ever lost.
requirements.acceptance: On deck D, c:ada shares it with si:designer, changes its role, turns the public switch on and off, moves D into a folder, trashes and restores it, and transfers it to si:designer, who accepts. /decks/D/history and GET /v1/decks/D/versions (with its events) list each of these, in order, with the actor's c:id or si:id and the time. They are still listed after the transfer and after further edits.

requirements.requirement: Folders are versioned too: renaming a folder, moving it, and decks or folders going in or out of it are kept with who did it and when.
requirements.quote: Everything in Silicon Present is versioned, and nothing is ever lost.
requirements.acceptance: c:ada renames folder F from 'Clients' to 'Clients 2026', moves F into folder P and moves deck D out of F, and si:designer (an editor on F) creates a deck inside F. F's history, in the web and through the CLI or API, lists each of these changes with who made it and when, and the earlier name 'Clients' can still be seen.

requirements.requirement: A Silicon that can edit a deck can render any slide as it was at an older version, the way a Carbon sees it on the history page.
requirements.quote: Anyone who can edit can open a deck exactly as it was at any version … The `present` CLI is how Silicons use Silicon Present, and it can do everything the web editor can.
requirements.acceptance: At version N, a box on slide 2 is blue. Later it is made red. si:designer (an editor) runs `present render <deck> 2 --version N -o old.png`. The box is blue in old.png and red in a render without --version, and old.png matches c:ada's view of version N on /decks/<id>/history. The same command run by a Viewer is refused (VER-23).

requirements.requirement: An HTML element whose JS hangs or keeps using more memory can't freeze or crash anything outside its own box. The editor, present mode, presenter view, follow pages and converter keep working. This reads 'never run outside its own box' as also covering the CPU and memory of the page around the element; a Carbon should confirm.
requirements.quote: never run outside its own box on the slide
requirements.acceptance: Slide 2 holds one HTML element whose JS runs `while(true){}` 1 s after load, and another that allocates memory without end. With slide 2 showing in /decks/<id>, c:ada can still type in a text box, switch slides and post a comment. In /decks/<id>/present the next-slide key still works, and c:bob's /p/<presentation> still follows each move. `present render <deck> 2` returns within its time limit, with an image or a clear error. Renders and exports of other decks made at the same time succeed.

requirements.requirement: HTML elements run sandboxed on every page that draws slides, including the history page and the version compare view, where older versions run too, and in the slide list, slide sorter and next-slide thumbnails wherever those run HTML. SLD-64 lists only the editor, present mode, presenter view, follow page and public link.
requirements.quote: Every HTML element runs sandboxed.
requirements.acceptance: The SLD-64 probe element is added at version N and later deleted. c:ada opens version N on /decks/<id>/history and compares N with the current version. She also opens the slide sorter, and the presenter view with the probe's slide next. Wherever the probe runs, it reports the same results as in SLD-64: no access to the page around it, its variables, cookies or storage.

requirements.requirement: An HTML element can't reach the viewer's device over the network: services on the viewer's own machine (localhost) and on their local network are out of its reach.
requirements.quote: never reach their account, their device or the rest of the deck
requirements.acceptance: This runs against the deployed site, or a test host that the browser treats as public. The test machine runs HTTP servers on 127.0.0.1:<port> and on its LAN address, each returning a secret with Access-Control-Allow-Origin: *. A probe HTML element tries a fetch, an img, a script tag and a WebSocket against both, in /decks/<id>, in /decks/<id>/present and on the public link. The probe reads neither secret, while the same element can still fetch a public https URL (SLD-68).

requirements.requirement: When the converter renders or exports a slide, an HTML element can't reach the private network of the machine it runs on: the service, the converter, the database, cloud metadata or anything else that isn't on the internet. SLD-78 only tries the service's deck content and the converter's /render.
requirements.quote: Every HTML element runs sandboxed. It can load anything it needs from the internet
requirements.acceptance: A probe HTML element tries a fetch, an img, a script tag and a WebSocket against http://127.0.0.1:<service port>/v1/decks, http://127.0.0.1:<converter port>/health, 127.0.0.1:<postgres port>, http://169.254.169.254/latest/meta-data/, and other asset ids under the signed asset base the converter was given. It writes what it got into its own DOM. `present render <deck> <slide> --at 3000 -o p.png` and `present export <deck> --format pdf` both show the probe reporting that nothing was reached, while a public https fetch from the same element succeeds.

requirements.requirement: The CLI is comfortable for a Silicon to work with: every command that prints data has a --json form, and every failure exits non-zero with an error saying what happened and what to do. This is implied: the matrix only checks help text (INTRO-06) and the API's error body (SIGN-06).
requirements.quote: every deck has to be a comfortable place for a Silicon to work
requirements.acceptance: For every command in `present --help` that prints data, adding --json prints valid JSON on stdout. Failures are provoked: an unknown deck, no access, a replace that finds nothing, an invalid role and no sign-in. Each one exits non-zero and prints a message naming the cause plus a hint for the next step: for example, text_not_found shows the closest passage, and sign_in_required says to run `present login`. With --json, the error is {error: {code, message, hint}}.

requirements.section: Intro paragraphs, Glossary, and Sign in
requirements.requirement: Nothing a Carbon or Silicon reads uses 'frontend', 'backend', 'AI' or 'agent' for a Silicon, 'user' or 'users' for a Carbon or Silicon, or 'org' or 'organization'. This covers pages, CLI help, output and errors, API error messages, the invite-to-join email and ting texts. GLOS-01 and GLOS-02 check only 'human', 'user account', 'AI agent', 'agent account' and 'bot'. The broader list comes from the Carbon's standing vocabulary rule (also in docs/architecture.md).
requirements.quote: Every human account is called a carbon. … Our AI Agent account is referred to as a Silicon.
requirements.acceptance: Repeat the GLOS-01 crawl, and add the invite email (email_outbox or the mock mailbox), the ting data texts, and the error states shown when the service is stopped or unreachable from the web and the CLI. No string contains 'frontend', 'backend', 'AI' as a word, 'agent', 'bot', 'user' or 'users' naming an account, 'org' or 'organization'. Errors about the service call it Silicon Present or the service.

requirements.section: Carbon's standing instruction for this build (not in UNDERSTANDING.md): minimal
requirements.requirement: Every list on the site uses the same list style: decks and folders, Shared with me, trash, transfers, the thread list and the history all look and behave as one kind of row. This comes from the Carbon's approved minimal design (2026-10-11): 'one way to list items everywhere'.
requirements.quote: the website is minimal
requirements.acceptance: At 1440x900, a reviewer compares /decks (mine and shared), /trash, /transfers, the thread list in /decks/<id> and /decks/<id>/history. All rows share one structure: the same type sizes, spacing and separators, and the same way of showing the second line and actions. No page uses cards where another uses table rows.

requirements.section: Carbon's standing instruction for this build (not in UNDERSTANDING.md): minimal
requirements.requirement: No page has broken details at desktop or phone width: no sideways scrolling, no words cut in the middle, no separators wrapped onto their own line, and no empty state shown twice. On a phone, the follow page shows the whole slide.
requirements.quote: the website is minimal
requirements.acceptance: Take full-page screenshots at 1440x900 and 390x844 of /, /decks (empty and full), /trash, /transfers, /decks/<id>, /decks/<id>/history, /decks/<id>/present and /p/<presentation>. On each page, document.documentElement.scrollWidth equals the viewport width. A reviewer finds no word cut mid-way, no separator wrapped onto its own line and no doubled empty state. At 390 wide, the follow page shows the entire slide (letterboxed) and moves with the presenter.
